# Episode 6 repair handoff: make discharge and documentation selection testable

Status: design-only. I read the inherited reference-complete proposal (candidate-9bd7a428ee4ae729076c3694) and its exact source-binding summary. I did not read patient rows, execute the full study, fit a model, or claim patient-level results. This branch reuses the parent’s frozen three-work evidence package and source-check.

## Decision

The inherited design is scientifically strong but not yet discriminating enough about two selection processes. It conditions on survival and remaining in the first ICU for at least 48 hours, then on reaching an alive ICU outtime, and it makes a dense urine-documentation restriction. It also defined a pseudo-landmark from future t0 and could treat early hospital discharge as an ordinary no-event. Those choices can make residual severity, discharge selection, or documentation propensity look like persistent renal physiology.

The substantive repair preserves:

- the exact first-ICU adult population and ICU-outtime landmark t0;
- the non-causal, 48-hour prognostic estimand;
- the exact MIMIC-IV 3.1 archive/member bindings and item IDs;
- the coverage ladder and no-absent-as-zero urine rule; and
- the held-out transparent baseline versus masked longitudinal/HMM comparison.

The repair adds an explicit discharge-survivor estimand, a competing hospital-discharge endpoint, a fixed ICU-age pseudo-landmark selection audit, and a pre-final-window observation-process sensitivity.

## Frozen population and time boundaries

Use the parent’s exact source and joins:

- archive: [private-path]/mimic-iv-3.1.zip;
- archive/catalog SHA-256: 0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09;
- first ICU per subject_id, joined to admissions on subject_id,hadm_id;
- adults patients.anchor_age >= 18;
- valid icustays.intime < outtime, icustays.los >= 2 days;
- t0 = icustays.outtime, t0 <= admissions.dischtime;
- retain only rows alive at t0: deathtime null or strictly later than t0.

The primary population is therefore conditional on surviving and reaching the first ICU outtime alive. It is not an all-ICU prognosis and does not estimate a discharge or treatment effect. The LOS >=48-hour condition is a survivor/continuation restriction; it is not an immortal-time error if every predictor is strictly pre-t0, but the report must not describe early-bin patterns as representative of all ICU admissions.

Primary features remain in [t0-24h,t0); longitudinal bins remain non-overlapping 6-hour bins from icustays.intime through t0, with partial first-bin duration recorded. No charttime, starttime, or endtime at/after the landmark may enter a predictor.

Report a source-frame flow before model fitting:

A0: adult first ICU stays with valid times and linked admission; A24: alive at 24 hours; A48: alive at 48 hours; P: the frozen primary population; D: the parent’s dense documentation stratum. Separate exclusions by death, ICU exit, linkage/time failure, and documentation threshold. Do not call P a general ICU cohort.

## Exact bound fields and item IDs

No binding changes are permitted.

- hosp/patients.csv.gz: subject_id,gender,anchor_age (parent also verified anchor-year fields and dod).
- hosp/admissions.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,admittime,dischtime,deathtime,admission_type,hospital_expire_flag.
- hosp/transfers.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,transfer_id,eventtype,careunit,intime,outtime.
- icu/icustays.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,first_careunit,last_careunit,intime,outtime,los.
- hosp/labevents.csv.gz: labevent_id,subject_id,hadm_id,specimen_id,itemid,charttime,storetime,value,valuenum,valueuom,flag; creatinine is itemid=50912, with finite positive valuenum, compatible mg/dL, and charttime before the landmark.
- hosp/d_labitems.csv.gz: itemid,label,fluid,category; verify 50912 = Creatinine/Blood/Chemistry.
- icu/outputevents.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,caregiver_id,charttime,storetime,itemid,value,valueuom; urine items are Foley 226559, Void 226560, Condom Cath 226561. Use finite nonnegative value in mL; absence is missing, never zero.
- icu/d_items.csv.gz: itemid,label,abbreviation,linksto,category,unitname,param_type,lownormalvalue,highnormalvalue; verify urine labels/units and support dictionary rows.
- icu/chartevents.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,caregiver_id,charttime,storetime,itemid,value,valuenum,valueuom,warning; MAP is itemid=220052.
- icu/inputevents.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,caregiver_id,starttime,endtime,storetime,itemid,amount,amountuom,rate,rateuom,statusdescription; pressors are 221906,221289,221749,222315.
- icu/procedureevents.csv.gz: subject_id,hadm_id,stay_id,caregiver_id,starttime,endtime,storetime,itemid,value,valueuom,statusdescription; invasive ventilation is 225792.

Lactate, platelet, RRT, complete diuretic exposure, fluid composition, validated weight, measured GFR/cystatin C, complete urine collection, and discharge rationale remain unavailable/deferred. Do not invent item IDs or add a source.

## Replacement primary outcome: account for hospital discharge

Define H=t0+48h. Order the first event in (t0,H], using admissions.dischtime only to identify observed follow-up:

- E: first in-hospital death (deathtime>t0 and <= H) or later ICU admission for the same subject_id,hadm_id with icustays.intime>t0 and <= H. Preserve separate death and ICU-readmission components.
- D: alive hospital discharge before H with no preceding E. If dischtime=t0, classify D at time zero rather than as a 48-hour non-event.
- N: no E or D by H and still hospitalized at H.

If dischtime<t0, or death timing contradicts the alive-at-t0 rule, fail/quarantine as a data-quality exception. A hospital_expire_flag=1 without usable deathtime is not assigned an event time.

The primary estimand is the standardized observational probability of E by 48 hours conditional on P, with D as a competing observed endpoint. Report probabilities for E,D,N; this is not risk after hospital discharge and not a causal discharge estimand.

B0/B1 retain the parent’s exact inputs, patient-level 70/15/15 split, train-only preprocessing, tune-only penalty selection, untouched test set, and 200 patient-bootstrap intervals, but use the three-level E/D/N target as the primary held-out analysis (multinomial landmark model or equivalent cause-specific discrete-time hazards). Report held-out E probability, standardized group risk differences/ratios, calibration for all states, Brier/log loss, and descriptive AUROC/AUPRC. The old binary logistic treatment of D as a no-event is a sensitivity only and must be labeled selection-sensitive. The masked HMM uses the same target/split and remains descriptive, not mechanistic.

## Fixed pseudo-landmark: no future t0 leakage

Replace the parent’s “24 hours before t0” pseudo-landmark with the fixed ICU-age landmark p=icustays.intime+48h. This is a diagnostic, not a second primary endpoint.

From A0, report how many reach p alive and with a valid first ICU record (A48), distinguishing death before p, ICU exit before p, and invalid timing. Among A48, construct the same 24-hour creatinine/urine discordance and 6-hour longitudinal bins in [p-24h,p), using only rows before p. In (p,p+24h], classify the first process outcome as:

- alive ICU exit: outtime in the interval and no death at/before ICU exit;
- ICU death: deathtime in the interval and deathtime <= outtime;
- still ICU/unknown.

Fit a simple held-out multinomial selection model for these process outcomes using early analog features and the same patient split. Use its pre-specified G_p score/stratum only to standardize or stratify the primary repeated-versus-final-only contrast. For primary subjects, G_p uses only observations before p; missing early fields remain missing with indicators. It is not a discharge-decision model. A signal that is comparable for early alive ICU exit/ICU death, or that disappears after G_p stratification, is adverse for the persistent-physiology interpretation.

This audit cannot remove unmeasured survivor selection, discharge rationale, or treatment confounding. It makes their measured component visible.

## Observation-process repair

Retain the parent’s coverage ladder: any valid row; >=2 final-window rows; >=1 row in each final 6-hour bin; and >=2 valid rows per final bin with a verified source. Retain volume, row count, source type, zero fraction, first/last chart time, observed span, and explicit masks.

Add O_pre from [t0-48h,t0-24h): prior urine row/source/span, creatinine count, MAP count for 220052, care unit/transfer context, pressor/ventilation exposure, and missingness flags. Fit Pr(D_dense=1|O_pre on train only, trim/choose regularization on tune only, and apply it to the untouched test set. Report overlap and standardized dense-cohort risks as a measurement sensitivity, not as recovery of unobserved urine. Also report source-specific results for 226559/226560/226561 and urine-to-MAP coverage strata. Post-t0 documentation can appear only in a descriptive data-quality table, never in prediction, weighting, matching, or outcome adjudication.

## Supportive/adverse/inconclusive criteria

Supportive requires: the held-out repeated-versus-final-only E contrast is directionally stable and calibrated in the dense ladder and O_pre-standardized analysis; it survives G_p stratification; no comparable early ICU-exit/death selection signal dominates; HMM persistence is stable and adds a held-out risk contrast beyond B0 at matched final-window discordance; and coverage, source, support, care-unit, 12/48-hour, continuous-creatinine, and permutation checks do not reverse it. This supports only an observed conditional prognostic regularity.

Adverse includes attenuation/reversal after coverage standardization; concentration in sparse documentation, one urine source, heavy support, or a final-window burst; comparable early selection-outcome association; disappearance after G_p; no held-out longitudinal contrast beyond B0/final-only; or a permutation contrast comparable to observed. These favor measurement, residual severity, or survivor/discharge selection explanations.

Inconclusive includes missing/hash/schema/item failures; invalid time order; unresolved death/discharge timestamps; inadequate D_dense/G_p overlap; fewer than 30 primary test events; unstable/calibration-failing models; HMM state failure; small selection strata; or wide uncertainty that cannot distinguish rivals. An imprecise null is not a refutation.

## Unchanged claims and deliverable

No result is claimed here. Completion requires frozen source/item manifest and flow, E/D/N outcome table, fixed split, B0/B1 held-out outputs, HMM masks/persistence/fit diagnostics if gated, G_p selection audit, O_pre coverage sensitivity, source-stratified and competing-discharge results, bootstrap uncertainty, and an interpretation table linking each conclusion to computed output.

Even supportive results cannot establish true GFR, complete urine collection, CKD/renal reserve, tubular injury, fluid balance, complete diuretic exposure, renal mechanism, causal treatment/discharge effect, clinical utility, or transportability. The inherited [K1] Kellum/KDIGO, [K2] Haines clearance, and [K3] Neumann kinetic-eGFR abstract-only receipts remain exactly the three inspected works; no new evidence claim is introduced.

## Text-level changes requested of Lead/compiler

1. Replace the parent binary outcome section with E/D/N and retain binary logistic only as sensitivity.
2. Replace future-defined t0-24h pseudo-landmark with fixed p=intime+48h.
3. Add A0 -> A24 -> A48 -> P -> D flow and explicitly name P a discharge-survivor estimand.
4. Add G_p early selection audit and O_pre documentation propensity sensitivity.
5. Preserve every parent source path, hash, join, item ID, coverage rule, HMM fit gate, reference receipt, and CPU planning estimate.

# HCC post-TACE trajectory: episode-4 endpoint-validity and competing-event child

Status: proposed Harbor experiment. No cohort count, model fit, adjudication, or clinical result has been executed in this branch. This is a substantive child of `candidate-dfcd18d98b7b9f122cc4790f`, preserving its HCC population, procedure time zero, laboratory window, days 8–90 target, all-eligible primary population, and baseline-versus-dynamic comparison.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis, and boundary

The parent’s strongest evidence-supported claim is only that an early post-TACE laboratory trajectory could carry incremental prognostic information for a later coded decompensation admission, after accounting for baseline risk and observation intensity. The unresolved clinical claim is stronger: that the trajectory reflects clinically meaningful loss of hepatic/renal reserve rather than a coding/documentation convention, a care-intensity signal, early acute-care selection, or ascertainment after discharge.

The primary hypothesis remains: in adults with HCC undergoing a first observed TACE, with no documented high-specificity decompensation before or at index, a 0–7-day trajectory showing coordinated deterioration in synthetic/renal reserve predicts a new post-discharge decompensation event during days 8–90 beyond a baseline-only model. An isolated AST/ALT flare is the leading biological rival. This episode adds two non-biological rivals:

1. discharge and early acute-care selection may determine who is observed and who receives a coded endpoint; and
2. a diagnosis code may be present without clinical decompensation, while clinically meaningful decompensation may be documented without the prespecified code.

A supportive result would therefore require more than incremental discrimination against the original code. It would require compatible timing, competing-event analyses, and a blinded endpoint-validation sample in which code-positive events are clinically credible across availability and care-regime strata. An adverse result would localize the signal to documentation or observation practice. An inconclusive result would show that the source can estimate coded prediction but not clinical validity; it would not refute a biological reserve-loss hypothesis.

Closest inspected evidence is [K1] Sanai et al., which reports post-locoregional hepatic decompensation and baseline-reserve associations but does not test this routine-laboratory trajectory or endpoint validity; [K2] Piscaglia and Ogasawara, which emphasizes TACE benefit/risk selection and preservation of hepatic reserve but does not provide a days-8–90 trajectory test; and [K3] Yang et al., a protocol documenting inconsistent post-TACE syndrome risk-factor evidence and the need for systematic endpoint definitions, not a completed validation result. All three were inspected abstract-only; no inaccessible full text or supplement is claimed. The new contribution is an endpoint-validity and competing-event test of the parent’s prediction question, not a claim that these works establish the present hypothesis.

## Frozen population, time zero, and temporal estimand

Use only the HCC dataset. Identify each patient’s first procedure row whose `手术` contains TACE, `肝动脉化疗栓塞`, `经导管肝动脉栓塞`, or `动脉化疗栓塞`, with parseable `开始时间` and a matching encounter. Require age >=18 and an HCC diagnosis (at minimum `肝细胞癌` or `肝恶性肿瘤`) before/on the index encounter. Exclude the parent’s high-specificity pre/index terms: `腹水`, `肝性脑病`, `消化道出血`, `食管胃底静脉曲张`, `肝肾综合征`, `急性肝衰竭`, `肝功能衰竭`, `自发性腹膜炎`, and `黄疸`; report broader cirrhosis/decompensation flags separately.

Time zero is the earliest qualifying `手术.开始时间`. Baseline is the closest assay-specific quantitative result in [-14, 0] days, with [-30, 0] as sensitivity analysis. Dynamic laboratory information is restricted to [0, 7] days after time zero, with raw timestamps, assay/name regime, specimen type, and duplicate status retained. The primary source-follow-up rule is unchanged: use only index dates with a verifiable 90-day observation horizon, using 2025-10-03 or a recomputed equivalent cutoff after checking source maxima.

The primary binary outcome remains the first distinct encounter after the index `出院时间` whose admission time is in [8, 90] days after time zero and whose diagnosis contains a prespecified high-specificity decompensation component. Report the composite and ascites, encephalopathy, gastrointestinal/variceal bleeding, renal/hepatic failure, and jaundice components separately. Any admission and repeat TACE remain non-equivalent secondary outcomes. Do not silently turn missing discharge into an event, censoring time, or new time zero.

The primary estimand is still the paired chronological-test-set difference in Brier score, calibration, discrimination, and decision-curve net benefit between the baseline-only and dynamic models for the all-eligible population. It is incremental prognostic value for an operational endpoint, not a treatment effect, causal effect, mechanism, or action threshold.

## Exact read-only HCC bindings

## Endpoint construction and blinded validation substudy

### Operational strata

Construct the primary diagnosis endpoint from `诊断名称` on the qualifying post-discharge encounter using frozen, component-specific lexical rules. Before looking at model predictions, create four mutually reported endpoint strata:

- diagnosis-only/clinical-document unavailable: the diagnosis rule is positive, but no linked usable clinical-document row is available for the encounter;
- document-confirmed: the diagnosis rule is positive and the same component is present in one or more of the document fields above, with document time/encounter linkage valid;
- discordant: diagnosis and an available document disagree, including a diagnosis-positive/document-negative record or a document-positive/diagnosis-negative record;
- negative/other: neither source supports the component.

The first category is intentionally called diagnosis-only rather than clinically true. A diagnosis-positive record with an available document that does not support the component belongs to discordant, not document-confirmed. Keep missing-document cases separate from discordance. Repeat this table for each component and for the composite.

### Sampling and blinding

Freeze a deterministic validation sample from the chronological test period before adjudication. Sample across coded outcome status, A0/A1/A2 laboratory availability, calendar era, department, index discharge completeness, and early acute-care status. Use a fixed cap of 30 records per nonempty cell of (coded positive/negative × availability stratum × calendar tertile × department group), include all coded-positive records when a cell has fewer than 30, and cap the total at 600 by a fixed seeded random draw if the cross-product is larger. Report sampling fractions and use inverse sampling weights for validation estimates. If a cell is too sparse, collapse only adjacent calendar strata or clinically similar departments using a rule frozen before inspecting labels; otherwise report it as unestimable.

The adjudication packet is assembled from diagnoses, encounters, clinical_documents, medications, and, when present, orders/examinations. It contains index and outcome encounter times, all relevant text fields, medication/order timing, and the component-specific code, but no model prediction, laboratory trajectory, feature importance, or model-derived risk. Adjudicators are blinded to model outputs and to the primary endpoint label; the packet’s raw source fields cannot be hidden because they are the evidence being adjudicated. A second clinician independently reviews a fixed subset, with disagreements resolved by a prespecified third review. Record agreement, missing fields, and reasons for unresolvable labels.

Adjudication labels are: (a) definite/probable new or worsening ascites, encephalopathy, bleeding, renal/hepatic failure, or jaundice; (b) no clinical support; (c) competing illness or HCC progression better explaining the encounter; (d) isolated expected/TACE-related injury without decompensation; (e) text/document invalid or temporally mislinked; and (f) indeterminate. Also label whether the episode appears planned, unplanned, or unknown. “Planned” is accepted only when explicitly supported by the encounter/document/order/procedure record; scheduling cannot be reconstructed reliably from these tables. Unknown planned status is retained, not forced into unplanned. Medication patterns are corroboration, not proof of a syndrome.

Validation outputs are sensitivity, positive predictive value, and weighted agreement of the code composite against adjudicated definite/probable decompensation, with 95% design/bootstrap intervals and separate diagnosis-only, document-confirmed, discordant, missing-document, availability, calendar, department, and planned-status-unknown results. Do not use adjudicated labels to tune the primary model. If the sample is too small for precise validation, call the endpoint clinically unvalidated rather than treating code performance as truth.

### Timing and competing early events

Preserve the primary binary target exactly, but create an independent event-history audit. From index time, derive:

- index admission discharge lag and whether `出院时间` is parseable;
- any distinct post-discharge admission/acute-care encounter in days 0–7;
- repeat TACE or another procedure in days 0–7;
- first days 8–90 decompensation encounter;
- first days 8–90 non-decompensation acute admission;
- first days 8–90 repeat TACE/procedure; and
- whether a qualifying decompensation record occurs after an earlier non-decompensation encounter.

For the primary target, earlier non-decompensation care does not erase a later qualifying decompensation: the binary estimand asks whether any qualifying decompensation occurs in the frozen days 8–90 window. For a secondary competing-risk estimand, define entry as `max(index + 8 days, discharge time)` and exit at the first days 8–90 event, end of the 90-day horizon, or the source follow-up boundary. A discharge after day 90 produces no estimable post-discharge risk interval and is reported separately. Competing first events are non-decompensation acute admission and repeat TACE/procedure; early days 0–7 acute-care return is a prespecified state/stratum before entry, not silently treated as censoring. Death is unavailable and cannot be treated as a competing risk.

Fit cause-specific discrete-time hazards and cumulative-incidence curves only as a secondary analysis. The event-history alternative must distinguish the estimand “first observed competing event” from the primary “any qualifying decompensation by day 90.” Report both rather than relabeling one as the other. Examine whether dynamic-model performance changes after stratifying by early acute-care return, discharge lag, or missing discharge. Do not use any post-day-7 observation in either prediction model.

## Baseline/dynamic model and substantive alternative

The transparent models are fit on one row per eligible index patient:

- **B0 baseline-only:** L2-regularized logistic regression for the primary binary composite using age, sex, index department, HCC/cirrhosis/portal-vein-thrombus/prior-decompensation flags, procedure context, pre-index utilization, baseline assay-specific values, and baseline missingness. A no-lab B0 is a sensitivity comparator.
- **B1 dynamic:** B0 plus prespecified day-0–7 assay features: baseline-to-last change, robust slope, extrema, last value, bin coverage, first-lab lag, observation count, and separate AST/ALT-flare blocks. Labs are transformed within training-set assay/name regimes because units are unavailable. B1 does not condition its primary score on complete trajectory, discharge, or a post-outcome record.
- **Care-intensity audit:** add pre-index and day-0–7 encounter/admission/department/lab/procedure/medication/order/examination counts, discharge lag, and early-return indicators in a locked sensitivity model. This is not the primary dynamic claim; it tests whether the gain is explained by the observation/care process.

The substantive alternative is an **observation-aware competing-risk landmark model**. It is selected because the unresolved scientific issue is endpoint timing and observation selection, which B1’s summaries cannot represent. Inputs are the same baseline variables and day-0–7 laboratory timestamps/assay regimes plus bin-level lab indicators/counts, first-lab lag, index discharge lag/completeness, early acute-care return, repeat TACE/procedure indicators, index department, calendar era, and pre-index utilization. The outcome head models discrete-time transitions from post-discharge entry to days 8–90 decompensation, non-decompensation acute admission, or repeat TACE/procedure; the observation head models laboratory availability and care encounters through day 7. Use partial pooling by department/era and assay/name regime, and a pattern-mixture sensitivity parameter for informative missingness. Generate both a predicted probability of the primary binary outcome and a cause-specific cumulative-incidence curve for first decompensation. No post-day-7 data enter the inputs.

The alternative can reveal whether the apparent trajectory gain remains after modeling who is discharged, who returns early, and who is observed, and whether a risk signal predicts a clinically specific event or simply first acute-care contact. It also exposes whether the conclusions depend on treating non-decompensation admission or repeat TACE as censoring. It cannot identify a biological mechanism. Risks are stronger assumptions about missingness, transition ordering, sparse department/era cells, and planned status; convergence or positivity failure is an informative feasibility limitation.

The neural sequence alternative is deferred. It could represent irregular timestamps, but it would add capacity without resolving whether endpoint ascertainment and early-care selection generate the association. Revisit it only if the transparent and observation-aware models show a reproducible residual pattern that is scientifically about nonlinear trajectory structure rather than data capture.

### Split, fit, and uncertainty

Freeze a patient-level chronological split before endpoint inspection: train 2010-07-27–2018-12-31, validation 2019-01-01–2021-12-31, and test 2022-01-01–2025-10-03, or recompute the terminal date from the verified source maximum while preserving the complete-follow-up rule. Tune penalties, transition regularization, state/feature choices, partial-pooling strength, and missingness sensitivity presentation on train/validation only. The test set remains untouched for primary claims. Department or era holdouts are secondary; sparse cells are reported as inconclusive rather than merged after seeing outcomes.

Fit B0, B1, the care-intensity audit, and the observation-aware alternative from the same eligible population with explicit missingness handling. Compare paired test-set Brier score, calibration intercept/slope, ROC-AUC/PR-AUC, high-sensitivity operating-point performance, and decision-curve net benefit. Use patient-cluster bootstrap uncertainty (2,000 replicates or the maximum permitted bounded equivalent), preserving the chronological test set and validation-sample weights. Report event counts, discharge completeness, early-return and competing-event frequencies, A0/A1/A2 flow, effective sample sizes, validation sensitivity/PPV, and model convergence. Do not interpret a wide null as refutation.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted B0 and B1, the care-intensity audit, and the observation-aware competing-risk model; frozen all-patient test predictions; event-history and discharge-selection flow; diagnosis/document/discordance tables; blinded adjudication labels and weighted validity estimates; component and planned-status-unknown results; paired uncertainty; and negative-control outputs. A complete package must show whether the incremental 0–7-day signal survives endpoint validation and care-timing checks. No result is claimed here.

## Decision-curve interpretation

Decision-curve net benefit is computationally checkable only as a standardized comparison under an assumed threshold probability and an assumed relative harm of false positives versus false negatives. In this dataset it is not, by itself, evidence that clinicians should act on a risk score: there is no observed intervention triggered by the score, no validated action threshold, no reliable planned/unplanned label, no adjudicated endpoint for the full cohort, no mortality linkage, and no prospective calibration or external validation.

Therefore report DCA as exploratory model-utility analysis against the operational coded endpoint and, separately, against adjudicated labels in the validation substudy. It may support a candidate triage aid only if adjudicated endpoint validity is acceptable, calibration is stable across availability/calendar/department strata, the threshold and action are specified in advance, and an expert team confirms that false-positive and false-negative consequences are clinically plausible. Even then, it would justify prospective decision-impact validation, not clinical deployment. No DCA result can establish mechanism, treatment benefit, causal TACE harm, or a safe intervention threshold.

## Falsification and interpretation

Mandatory controls are:

1. within-patient timestamp permutation preserving values, assay names, and counts;
2. a matched pre-index pseudo-window with the same feature construction;
3. measurement/care-only prediction from counts, lag, discharge/early-return, department, and era without lab values;
4. AST/ALT-only versus reserve-panel-only blocks;
5. any-admission and repeat-TACE outcomes as non-equivalent outcomes;
6. a future-observation audit proving that no post-day-7 value, document, medication, diagnosis, or encounter is used as a feature;
7. endpoint-stratum analysis comparing diagnosis-only, document-confirmed, discordant, and missing-document events;
8. competing-risk comparison with and without early days 0–7 acute-care returns; and
9. a regime-label shuffle for department/calendar observation heterogeneity.

Supportive evidence requires a non-negligible paired dynamic gain on the untouched chronological test in the all-eligible population; no material timestamp-permutation or pre-index reproduction; persistence after care-intensity adjustment and the missingness sensitivity range; compatible B0/B1 and observation-aware calibration; endpoint PPV/sensitivity and adjudication agreement that are not confined to one availability, department, or calendar stratum; and directionally consistent component results. This would support a clinically credible incremental prognostic regularity, not a mechanism or clinical decision aid.

Adverse evidence includes disappearance after care-intensity or observation-aware adjustment; dominance by discharge lag, early return, counts, or a single documentation regime; timestamp or pre-index reproduction; code-positive events judged as planned care, HCC progression, isolated TACE injury, or unsupported text; major diagnosis/document discordance; calibration failure in held-out regimes; or an effect limited to first acute-care contact rather than decompensation. This would revise the claim to a local documentation/observation association or abandon the trajectory direction if an adequately observed adjudicated test repeatedly fails.

Inconclusive evidence includes missing/late discharge, too few adjudicated records, unresolvable planned status, sparse competing-event cells, unknown assay units, high unmapped assay names, weak common support, unstable competing-risk convergence, or wide intervals. These defer clinical interpretation; they do not refute reserve loss. Continue only if the primary computation and a sufficiently informative validation sample are complete. Narrow to a prespecified regime if only that regime is estimable; defer clinical utility if adjudication or assay review is missing; require prospective/external study before acting on the score.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes/headers, composite-key joins, timing bounds, split integrity, model inputs, predictions, code/document strata, adjudication sampling and agreement calculations, calibration, paired uncertainty, competing-risk transitions, DCA under declared assumptions, and leakage/negative-control behavior. Clinical truth, planned status, mechanism, causality, mortality, action thresholds, and external validity require clinician adjudication, assay/unit review, prospective decision-impact work, or another study.

## Alternatives and resource decision

B0/B1 is the transparent baseline/dynamic comparison: inputs are the frozen baseline and [0,7] assay summaries; target is the primary days-8–90 binary composite; fit is chronological train/validation/test; uncertainty is paired patient bootstrap. It is retained as the interpretable reference and is adequate for the incremental-prognostic estimand.

The observation-aware competing-risk landmark model uses the same labs and baseline inputs plus explicit availability, discharge, early-care, and competing-event processes; fit targets are transition hazards, availability, and the primary binary risk; it uses the same split and reports transition-specific and primary-risk uncertainty. It is selected because it can distinguish a reserve trajectory from a pathway through discharge and acute-care observation, information B1 loses.

A neural sequence model using irregular assay/time tokens is deferred for the scientific reason that greater capacity would not identify whether a coded endpoint is clinically valid or whether missingness is informative. GPU use is therefore not required. B0/B1 likely fit with 4–8 CPU cores and <32 GB RAM in tens of minutes; the competing-risk/observation fit and 2,000-replicate bootstrap are estimated at 16 CPUs, 64–128 GB RAM, no GPU, and up to 4–8 hours (28,800 seconds). These are planning estimates, not measured results. A bounded train-only convergence probe may use 4 CPUs/16 GB and cannot be reported as study evidence.

## Three inspected key works

[K1] Sanai FM, Saati A, Alghamdi H, Aldosari S, Alzanbagi A, Albenmousa A, Bzeizi KI, Abaalkhail F, AlJudaibi B, Alqahtani SA. “Predictors and outcomes of hepatic decompensation following transarterial locoregional therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.” 2026. Abstract-only inspection of the Europe PMC search response. It supports post-LRT decompensation and baseline-reserve relevance; it does not establish this routine-lab trajectory, endpoint adjudication, or transportability. This proposal adds a 0–7-day, all-eligible, adjudication-aware endpoint and competing-event test.

[K2] Piscaglia F, Ogasawara S. “Patient Selection for Transarterial Chemoembolization in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Importance of Benefit/Risk Assessment.” 2018. Abstract-only inspection. It bounds the clinical question by emphasizing selection and preservation of hepatic reserve; it does not test dynamic post-TACE laboratory prediction or endpoint documentation. This proposal adds explicit discharge/early-care timing and validation strata.

[K3] Yang L, Huang S, Sheng X, Xu Q, Ding J. “Analysis of risk factors for post-transarterial chemoembolization syndrome in patients with liver cancer: a systematic review protocol.” 2026. Abstract-only inspection. It supports the existence of inconsistent post-TACE syndrome risk-factor evidence and the need for prespecified synthesis; it is a protocol, not outcome evidence and not a decompensation adjudication study. This proposal adds a computable HCC-specific endpoint-validation and competing-risk design.

These are exactly three distinct inspected works. Their frozen Europe PMC provider responses and SHA-256-linked key-references.json are attached below; no inaccessible full text is claimed.

# MIMIC-IV renal-discordance: discharge-survivor and observation-process repair

Status: planned design only. No patient rows were read, no cohort was fitted, and no clinical result is claimed.

Parent: candidate-31009d7ec73ba43965cccd19. This child preserves the parent’s exact MIMIC-IV 3.1 bindings, first-ICU-outtime landmark, non-causal renal-discordance question, B0/B1/B2 versus masked-HMM comparison, held-out evaluation, and three-work evidence package. The substantive repair is to make the population’s survivor/continuation restrictions, hospital discharge and ICU-event endpoints, and urine-observation selection jointly explicit.

## Scientific opening and claim boundary

Creatinine improvement and urine output are complementary observations in AKI assessment [K1], but a creatinine fall near ICU discharge can also reflect changing creatinine generation rather than filtration recovery [K2]. Dynamic renal measures can be useful for risk stratification, while added markers may contribute little beyond a strong dynamic baseline [K3]. None of these inspected works tests whether an EHR-defined creatinine/urine discordance in MIMIC-IV is prognostic after making discharge and documentation selection visible.

The unresolved question is:

> Among adults who reach the end of a first ICU stay alive, does a fall in creatinine without adequately observed urine-output recovery in a fixed pre-landmark 24-hour window identify a reproducible 48-hour post-ICU risk pattern, and does recurrence in the immediately preceding non-overlapping window add information beyond final-window severity and observation density once early continuation-to-discharge selection is audited?

The leading explanation is an observable persistent pattern: repeated discordance should have a stable held-out contrast with death or ICU readmission, including in dense and selection-standardized analyses. The strongest rivals are (a) discharge/survivor selection, where reaching ICU outtime and being observed near discharge is a care-process consequence of severity and recovery, and (b) urine-documentation selection, where sparse or bursty charting makes low observed urine look like physiology. Creatinine-generation, dilution, fluid balance and treatment confounding are additional measurement limitations. These explanations have different predictions, but none can be separated completely without measured GFR, complete urine collection, treatment timing and discharge rationale.

The falsifiable claim is deliberately narrower:

> Conditional on the prespecified first-ICU-outtime population and, primarily, a prespecified dense-observation regime, final-window discordance is associated with a calibrated held-out difference in the competing probabilities of death, ICU readmission/continued ICU care, hospital discharge, and remaining hospitalized by 48 hours; among final-window-discordant stays with a valid prior window, repeated discordance has a stable contrast beyond transient discordance after measured early-selection and pre-window documentation diagnostics. A masked HMM is retained as evidence only if its label-invariant transition/persistence summaries add stable held-out information beyond the transparent B2 recurrence baseline.

This is an observational prognostic estimand. It is not an effect of discharge, ICU transfer, urine output, a treatment, or changing a discharge decision. It does not establish true GFR, complete urine collection, CKD, renal reserve, fluid balance, tubular injury, mechanism, causality, clinical utility, or transportability.

The substantive advance over the parent is not a new predictor: it prevents an apparent post-discharge association from silently mixing (i) selection into an alive ICU-outtime landmark, (ii) the requirement for dense urine documentation, and (iii) the competing possibility of early hospital discharge. A result that disappears under these checks supports an ascertainment or care-process explanation; a stable result supports only an observable prognostic regularity and justifies external validation or clinical adjudication.

## Population, selection stages and fixed time boundaries

Use the first ICU stay per subject_id, linked to its admission. Define the source-frame flow before feature construction:

- A0: adults with patients.anchor_age >= 18, a first ICU stay with valid icustays.intime < icustays.outtime and a linked admission.
- A24: A0 subjects alive and still in that first ICU at p24 = icustays.intime + 24 hours.
- A48: A0 subjects alive and still in that first ICU at p48 = icustays.intime + 48 hours.
- P: A48 stays with icustays.los >= 2 days, a valid linked admission, icustays.outtime <= admissions.dischtime, and alive at t0 = icustays.outtime (admissions.deathtime is null or strictly after t0).
- P_dense: P meeting the frozen strict primary urine-observation rule below.

The primary prognostic estimand is conditional on P_dense: standardized competing-endpoint probabilities at t0, not an all-ICU or discharge-intervention estimand. P_full=P and each coverage-ladder stratum are mandatory sensitivity populations. Report the A0 -> A24 -> A48 -> P -> P_dense flow with separate counts of death, ICU exit, hospital discharge, linkage/time failures and urine-coverage exclusions. No early-bin result is described as representative of ICU admissions that did not reach A48 or P.

The primary measurement windows are fixed before any outcome review:

- Final window F = [t0 - 24 hours, t0), never including t0.
- Prior window Q = [t0 - 48 hours, t0 - 24 hours), non-overlapping with F.
- Longitudinal sequence: non-overlapping 6-hour bins from icustays.intime through t0; retain partial first-bin duration.

All charttime, starttime and endtime values used for predictors must be strictly before t0. MIMIC timestamps are subject-shifted; never align calendar time across subjects.

### Selection endpoints at fixed ICU age

To expose the selection into P, classify A0 at p48 using mutually exclusive, pre-specified states:

1. death by p48 (usable admissions.deathtime <= p48);
2. hospital discharge by p48 before death;
3. alive ICU exit before p48 without hospital discharge by p48;
4. alive and still in the first ICU at p48 (continued ICU).

Invalid or contradictory times are a data-quality exception, not a favorable category. This fixed ICU-age audit does not use future t0 and is not a second primary outcome. Fit a train-only multinomial selection model for these states using only information available before p48; export a fixed early-continuation score G_p for P. Report whether the distribution of G_p and the observed discordance differ across source-frame states. Within P, standardize or stratify the final/repeated-versus-transient contrasts by G_p using training-derived cutpoints. This makes measured survivor/continuation selection visible but cannot remove unmeasured selection or discharge rationale.

## Landmark outcomes and estimand

Set H = t0 + 48 hours. Follow each P stay only through H and admissions.dischtime; do not turn post-discharge time into observed follow-up. Define the first mutually exclusive post-t0 state:

1. Death (M): admissions.deathtime in (t0,H], before any earlier competing state.
2. Continued ICU care/readmission (R): a later icustays.intime for the same subject_id and hadm_id in (t0,H], before earlier M or D. Because t0 is the first ICU outtime, this is operationally a subsequent ICU episode/readmission, not literal uninterrupted ICU care; the fixed p48 audit separately measures literal continued ICU status.
3. Hospital discharge (D): admissions.dischtime in (t0,H] with no preceding M or R.
4. Continued hospitalization (N): no M, R or D by H and the admission remains open at H.

If dischtime <= t0, deathtime conflicts with alive-at-t0, or an event order cannot be established, quarantine the row and report the exception. Do not use hospital_expire_flag to invent an event time when deathtime is unusable. Keep M, R, D and N separate. The primary estimand is the standardized vector (Pr[M by H], Pr[R by H], Pr[D by H], Pr[N at H]) conditional on P_dense, with the binary adverse composite M or R and time-to-first-event as secondary summaries. D is not a no-event: it is a competing observed endpoint that can otherwise create discharge-selection bias.

The four-level final-window group is descriptive: improved/high-output, improved/low-output (discordant), not-improved/high-output, and not-improved/low-output. The focal repeated-versus-transient contrast is restricted to final discordance with valid Q: repeated if D_F=1 and D_Q=1; transient if D_F=1 and D_Q=0. A missing or invalid Q is never called transient.

## Exact measurement definitions

Creatinine uses only hosp/labevents itemid=50912, linked to hosp/d_labitems. Retain finite positive valuenum and verified compatible valueuom in canonical mg/dL; exclude and report incompatible or unitless rows rather than silently converting. In F and Q require at least two observations at least 6 hours apart, with the final valid observation inside the window. Let C_peak be the maximum and C_last the final valid value; improvement is C_peak - C_last >= 0.3 mg/dL. Retain continuous change, count, span and time since peak.

Urine uses only icu/outputevents itemids 226559 (Foley), 226560 (Void) and 226561 (Condom Cath), with finite nonnegative value, valueuom=mL, and charttime within the selected stay/window. Sum valid values; absent rows are missing, never zero. Retain total observed volume, row count, source indicators, zero fraction, earliest/latest charttime and observed span. Span measures documentation timing and is not complete collection.

P_dense requires at least two valid urine rows in each of the four 6-hour bins of F and at least one verified source type. The frozen coverage ladder is: any valid row; at least two final-window rows; at least one row in every final 6-hour bin; and the strict P_dense rule. Report all strata separately, without changing thresholds after seeing outcomes. Low observed output is <400 mL/24 hours, an unweighted observed-volume threshold; no weight-indexed claim is made.

## Baseline and substantive learned/mechanistic alternative

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted, leakage-safe, held-out evidence for the competing-endpoint vector and the repeated-versus-transient contrast, plus pre-specified selection and observation-process diagnostics. Completion requires the frozen source/item/unit manifest and flow; endpoint assignments; split; B0/B1/B2 coefficients and test predictions; G_p and documentation-density diagnostics; L1 emissions/masks/transitions/posteriors if gated; 200-bootstrap uncertainty; falsification outputs; and an interpretation table tying every claim to a computed output. No result is asserted here.

### B0/B1: transparent baseline

Fit penalized multinomial landmark regression for M/R/D/N, with the binary M-or-R logistic model as a secondary sensitivity. B0 inputs are the parent’s verified, pre-t0 variables: age, gender, admission_type, ICU LOS, admission-to-t0 duration, first_careunit, last_careunit, creatinine level/trajectory and observation intensity, final-window urine volume/low-output/row count/span/source/zero fraction, MAP summaries and measurement indicators, vasopressor exposure/duration/last-active status, invasive-ventilation exposure/duration/status, transfer context and explicit missingness indicators. Transfer context is a selection diagnostic, not a post-t0 predictor.

B1 adds the four-level final-window group while retaining its continuous ingredients. B1 versus B0 tests whether the thresholded discordance statement adds information beyond measured creatinine, observed urine and care/documentation covariates. Report standardized M/R/D/N probabilities, focal risk differences/ratios for M-or-R and D, multiclass Brier score, log loss, one-vs-rest calibration slope/intercept and plots; AUROC/AUPRC are descriptive only.

### B2: transparent repeated-versus-transient baseline

Construct Q with exactly the same units, observation rules and four-bin coverage definitions as F. Define D_Q only when Q has valid creatinine improvement and strict urine coverage; define D_F identically. B2 adds D_Q, a prior-window-valid indicator, prior urine row count/span/source/zero fraction, prior creatinine count/span/time-since-peak, and prior continuous urine volume/creatinine change to B1. The focal transparent contrast is repeated versus transient among D_F=1 with valid Q. B2 is the required simple baseline because it directly tests recurrence using an interpretable, non-overlapping window; the HMM must exceed it to justify latent-state complexity.

### L1: masked HMM alternative

Fit a three-state masked HMM over the 6-hour sequence from ICU intime to t0 using the same verified channels: creatinine last value and adjacent change, urine volume/row count/observed span/source/zero fraction, MAP, vasopressor and ventilation support, and explicit masks. Missing urine is a missing emission, never zero. Partial first-bin duration is retained. Fit only on train subjects; select emission family, regularization and state count on tune using unsupervised sequence likelihood and label-invariant state-stability criteria. Export only prespecified label-invariant summaries: expected adjacent transition count; posterior probability of remaining in one state across the final four bins; posterior probability of same state across the Q/F boundary; occupancy and mask summaries; and time since last inferred transition.

The outcome model is B2 plus these summaries, fit to the same M/R/D/N target and split. L1 is interpretable as a test of whether transition/persistence information lost by B2’s recurrence indicator improves prognosis—not as renal biological states. It is retained only if it adds a stable held-out proper-score result beyond B2 and a distinct repeated-versus-transient contrast. An HMM improvement over B1 alone is insufficient.

### Selection and documentation diagnostics

Freeze these diagnostics before test outcomes:

1. The A0/A24/A48/P/P_dense flow and the fixed p48 competing selection states above.
2. The coverage ladder, source-specific urine results, urine-to-MAP coverage strata, row timing/zero-fraction/observed-span summaries, and a late-charting-burst indicator.
3. O_pre documentation features from Q before F: urine rows/source/span, creatinine count/span, MAP count, care-unit/transfer context, vasopressor/ventilation exposure and missingness. Fit Pr(P_dense | O_pre) on train only, select regularization and trimming on tune only, and apply to the untouched test set. Report overlap and train-defined standardized P_full/P_dense contrasts; this is an observation-process sensitivity, not recovery of unobserved urine.
4. A no-support restriction (no pre-t0 vasopressor or invasive-ventilation exposure), care-unit and ICU-LOS strata, and continuous rather than thresholded creatinine change.
5. A permutation of final discordance within ICU-LOS, admission-type, G_p and B1-risk strata, with the permutation rule frozen before test review.
6. A fixed early ICU-age p48 diagnostic using only rows before p48; never define a pseudo-landmark relative to future t0.

Post-t0 documentation may appear only in a descriptive data-quality table, never in features, weighting, matching, outcome adjudication or model selection.

## Split, evaluation and uncertainty

Create one patient-level 70/15/15 train/tune/test split before fitting, using a recorded fixed seed/hash rule; reuse it for B0, B1, B2, L1, G_p and the documentation model. Fit all preprocessing, G_p cutpoints, density propensity, trimming and model penalties on train/tune only. Inspect test outcomes once.

Report held-out M/R/D/N probabilities and calibration, the M-or-R risk difference/ratio for final discordance versus improved/high-output, and the repeated-versus-transient contrast among valid final discordance. Standardize comparisons over B1-risk strata with train-learned cutpoints and report P_full, each coverage ladder step, G_p strata and O_pre-standardized versions. Use 200 patient-level bootstrap resamples of held-out predictions for risks, contrasts and proper-score deltas. Report test size, each endpoint count, focal-group counts and overlap/trim counts.

The HMM is not fit or interpreted if the test set has fewer than 200 subjects or 30 M-or-R events, if masks require imputation, if either repeated or transient group has fewer than 20 test subjects, or if train/tune support for a competing endpoint is absent. A fit is inconclusive if convergence fails, a state occupies <5% of training bins, median maximum posterior state probability is <0.60, or label-invariant summaries are directionally stable in fewer than 80% of prespecified stability refits. A multiclass comparison with fewer than 10 test observations in a key endpoint is endpoint-specific inconclusive.

### Alternatives and revisit criteria

B2 is selected as the simple baseline because it answers the recurrence question transparently with the same inputs, windows and missingness rules. L1 is scientifically useful because it can reveal transition timing, persistence across the Q/F boundary and mask-aware trajectory information that a binary prior-window indicator loses. The alternative is not selected for a small predictive gain: it must yield a stable temporal contrast beyond B2.

A deterministic filtration/fluid-balance model is deferred because the bound source lacks measured GFR, cystatin C, complete urine collection, validated time-aligned weight, fluid composition, complete diuretic exposure and creatinine-generation parameters. Revisit it only if those inputs are verified. A transformer/LSTM is deferred because no concrete clinical observable unavailable to B2/L1 is currently specified; revisit only with a prespecified new observable and the same held-out estimand. GPU use is not excluded in principle, but the current low-dimensional multinomial/HMM workload is planned for CPU; a GPU would not solve the selection or measurement-identification problem.

## Interpretation and falsification rules

Supportive evidence requires: a calibrated held-out final-discordance contrast in P_dense and P_full that is not explained by a sparse-coverage step; a directionally stable repeated-versus-transient M/R contrast after G_p and O_pre diagnostics; no comparable early p48 selection-state pattern that accounts for the result; and L1 transition/persistence summaries that add a paired held-out proper-score improvement beyond B2 with stable estimates across coverage, support and care-unit checks. This supports an observable conditional prognostic regularity and motivates external validation plus clinical adjudication of urine completeness. It does not support a renal mechanism or discharge intervention.

Adverse evidence is attenuation or reversal after G_p or O_pre standardization, concentration in sparse/one-source/bursty records or heavily supported stays, a comparable p48 continuation/death/discharge selection signal, a permutation contrast comparable to the observed contrast, loss of the repeated contrast in the dense/no-support strata, or L1 transitions dominated by low-density bins without incremental evidence over B2. These findings favor documentation, residual severity or survivor/discharge selection and justify stopping or revising this direction.

Inconclusive evidence includes archive/member/schema/item mismatch; invalid units or time order; unresolved death/discharge timestamps; inadequate density overlap; fewer than 30 held-out M/R events or too few endpoint/group observations; calibration failure; unstable G_p/density models; HMM nonconvergence/state instability; or wide uncertainty that cannot distinguish rivals. An imprecise null is not a refutation.

Computationally checkable claims are source/member/schema availability; leakage-free time windows and split; endpoint ordering; coverage and selection diagnostics; fitted models; held-out predictions; calibration/proper scores; bootstrap intervals; HMM stability; and whether conclusions match those outputs. Complete urine collection, true filtration, CKD/renal reserve, mechanism, discharge rationale, causal effects, clinical utility and transportability require unavailable measurements, expert adjudication, external validation or another study.

# HCC post-TACE trajectory: index-anchored timing successor

Status: proposed Harbor experiment; no cohort scan, model fit, adjudication, or scientific result has been executed. This episode repairs evidence delivery for candidate-4e26300959818e3881f07308 and preserves its population, time zero, [0,7] dynamic window, primary discharge-anchored estimand, all-eligible handling, exact HCC bindings, and no-validated-mortality limitation.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis, and advance

The inspected evidence supports three bounded points, not the present conclusion. [K1] reports clinically consequential hepatic decompensation after locoregional therapy and identifies baseline hepatic reserve as a predictor in a selected, adjudicated multicenter cohort. [K2] provides an internally validated baseline model for an acute post-TACE hepatic-dysfunction label. [K3] shows that five-day post-TACE biochemical injury patterns vary by treatment type. None tests whether a first-observed-TACE, routine-care, multianalyte trajectory during days 0–7 predicts a later clinical decompensation event beyond baseline, and none separates a reserve signal from discharge selection or the observation process.

The unresolved question is whether an early trajectory is a transportable prognostic regularity about subsequent decompensation, or mainly a consequence of index length of stay, discharge observability, early acute-care utilization, or diagnosis/documentation timing. This matters because a clinician could otherwise misread a transient post-embolization enzyme flare as evidence of impending reserve failure. Resolving the boundary would determine whether follow-up treats the trajectory as a candidate risk marker, restricts its interpretation to a discharge/observation regime, or abandons it.

Primary hypothesis:

> Among adults with HCC and a first observed TACE, a 0–7-day trajectory showing worsening synthetic/renal reserve adds held-out prognostic information beyond baseline for a new high-specificity decompensation-coded admission during days 8–90 after index discharge.

Timing-boundary hypothesis:

> If the incremental signal reflects post-TACE reserve loss rather than discharge selection or endpoint ascertainment, its direction and calibrated incremental value will remain when the same day-0–7 information is evaluated from index time without conditioning on discharge, using a prespecified index-anchored cause-specific event estimand and explicit early-care/observation strata.

Supportive evidence establishes at most incremental prediction under the observed-data regime. It does not establish TACE causality, a latent biological mechanism, treatment or mortality benefit, a safe action threshold, or clinical utility. Adverse evidence would localize the claim to discharge-conditioned observed-care prediction, or stop the trajectory direction if timing, observation, or endpoint validity explains the gain. Inconclusive evidence identifies missing endpoint timing, sparse risk sets, unstable observation weights, or unavailable terminal-event adjudication as dependencies rather than refuting the hypothesis.

## Population, time zero, and primary estimand

Use only the HCC dataset. Select each patient's first qualifying procedure row where `procedures.手术` contains TACE, `肝动脉化疗栓塞`, `经导管肝动脉栓塞`, or `动脉化疗栓塞`, with parseable `procedures.开始时间` and a matching encounter. Require age >=18 and an HCC diagnosis containing at least `肝细胞癌` or `肝恶性肿瘤` on or before the index encounter. Exclude high-specificity decompensation terms before or at index: `腹水`, `肝性脑病`, `消化道出血`, `食管胃底静脉曲张`, `肝肾综合征`, `急性肝衰竭`, `肝功能衰竭`, `自发性腹膜炎`, and `黄疸`. Report broader cirrhosis/decompensation flags separately. Missing labs, missing discharge, early return, and incomplete trajectories do not exclude anyone from the primary population.

Time zero is the earliest qualifying procedure `开始时间`. Baseline is the closest assay-specific numeric result in days [-14,0], with [-30,0] sensitivity. The dynamic window is [0,7] days, with raw timestamps, assay/name, specimen type, observation count, and encounter retained. Candidate concepts are bilirubin, albumin, platelets, PT/INR or PT ratio, creatinine, sodium, AST, ALT and AFP, subject to demonstrated presence and assay comparability. There is no lab-unit column: parse only numeric `labs.定量结果`, audit assay/name regimes in training data, and do not claim ALBI, MELD, or Child-Pugh from unverified units.

The primary event is discharge-anchored `D_D`: the first distinct encounter after the index `encounters.出院时间`, with linked `encounters.入院时间` in index days [8,90] and occurring after index discharge, whose linked diagnosis contains a prespecified high-specificity decompensation component. Report composite and components (ascites, encephalopathy, gastrointestinal/variceal bleeding, renal/hepatic failure, jaundice), plus diagnosis-only versus document-confirmed strata. The primary estimand is the paired chronological-test-set difference between baseline-only and baseline-plus-[0,7] dynamic predictions for `D_D`: Brier score, calibration, discrimination, and decision-curve net benefit. This is a prognostic comparison, not a treatment-effect estimand.

All eligible patients remain in the primary analysis. Missing `出院时间` is an explicit ascertainment stratum; it is not recoded as discharge, event-negative, censoring at an invented date, or a new time zero. If ascertainment is incomplete, report the all-eligible result and stratum-specific result; an ascertainment-weighted sensitivity may be used only with predeclared weights and diagnostics.

## Index-anchored timing sensitivity and observation rival

Define `D_I` as the first distinct post-index encounter with `入院时间` in index days [8,90], regardless of whether an index discharge exists or precedes it, and with the same high-specificity diagnosis-component rule. Its event time is `入院时间 - index 开始时间`. A continued index encounter with a newly appearing diagnosis has no independent diagnosis timestamp in this release; it is excluded from primary `D_I` or placed in an explicitly unresolvable-timing stratum. Do not invent a diagnosis date. An any-encounter analysis using `就诊时间` is secondary and never pooled with the admission endpoint.

For `D_I`, report cause-specific hazard and cumulative incidence at days 30, 60 and 90, time-dependent discrimination, IPCW Brier/integrated Brier, calibration, event counts, risk-set size, and paired uncertainty. This is a sensitivity/child estimand, not a replacement for `D_D`; it asks whether the contrast persists without the post-discharge observation gate.

Define `A_{0–7}` as the first distinct post-index acute-care encounter in days [0,7] using parseable `入院时间`; any-encounter timing is separately labeled. The source has no planned/unplanned field, so status is unknown and never inferred. Early acute care is not automatically a competing clinical endpoint: it may alter laboratory observation, discharge, and endpoint ascertainment, but does not necessarily preclude later decompensation. Use it as an availability/selection stratum, an index-to-early-care-to-`D_I` multi-state description, and a negative-control/process target. Do not adjust for it as if it were a baseline confounder.

The primary observation sensitivity estimates stabilized inverse-probability-of-observation weights from day-0 variables (baseline severity/utilization, department, calendar era, and discharge observability), with predeclared truncation and effective-sample-size diagnostics. Last observed record is a censoring proxy only in a labeled sensitivity; absent later encounter is not recovery.

A clinical terminal-event competing risk is unavailable. The HCC release has no mortality linkage, and `clinical_documents` has text but no temporal columns; a death mention is not a validated death date. Therefore `F_D^{I,CR}` with death/hospice as a mutually exclusive cause is not identified and must not be reported as a clinical competing-risk result. Only if separate blinded clinical review validates terminal-event status and a linked date from `clinical_documents.出院情况`, `出院诊断`, or `诊疗经过` plus encounter admission/discharge times may the predeclared Aalen–Johansen sensitivity be run. Last encounter, missing discharge, and lexical “death” flags cannot substitute.

The catalog also lists `vitals` and `transfers` as identifier-only, `front_page` as identifier-only/nominal, and `pathology` without a usable event timestamp for this question; they are not required inputs. No imaging, tumor burden, embolized territory, TACE drug/dose, ECOG, portal pressure, validated assay units, external follow-up, or mortality linkage is available or inferred. The configured HCC release is the sole clinical source used here; no cross-source patient matching is permitted.

## Endpoint validity and adjudication safeguards

Freeze lexical endpoint rules before model fitting. Build a ledger for every eligible index containing index/discharge times and lag, discharge missingness and timing, early acute care, lab observation density and source encounter, `D_D` time from discharge and index, `D_I` time from index, diagnosis-only/document-confirmed/discordant/missing-document/unresolvable labels, endpoint source field, and other acute diagnoses on the event encounter.

Sample events and non-events blinded to model score across discharge strata, early-event strata, calendar/department strata, assay regimes, and diagnosis/document discordance. Labels must include new/worsening decompensation, pre-existing disease, planned/unclear status, competing illness/HCC progression, isolated TACE injury, text validity, and terminal-event status only if date can be validated. The lexical rule is a computable screen, not clinical truth. This adjudication is essential to claim clinical decompensation and is not executed in discovery.

## Models, split, uncertainty, and falsification

The transparent baselines are regularized L2 logistic regression for `D_D` and a matched baseline-only cause-specific survival model for `D_I`. Inputs are time-zero age, sex, department, HCC/cirrhosis/portal-vein-thrombus/prior-decompensation flags, procedure context, pre-index utilization, baseline assay values and missingness. A no-lab baseline is a sensitivity comparator. Dynamic predictors add assay-indexed last value, baseline-to-last delta, robust slope, extrema, fixed [0,1–2,3–4,5–7] bins, timing, counts, missingness, and AST/ALT-flare versus reserve-panel blocks. Patients are not dropped for incomplete trajectories.

The substantive alternative `SS-CR` is a joint irregular-time state/observation/cause-specific survival model using the same baseline/lab inputs, timestamps, assay/name regime, observation indicators/counts, department/calendar, and process fields available by day 7. It has a slowly varying reserve factor, transient injury factor, assay-specific measurement error, observation/discharge head, early-care state head, and `D_I` cause-specific hazard head. It predicts from the day-7 posterior plus baseline and uses no post-day-7 information. Latent factors are representations, not mechanisms. If terminal-event review is unavailable, no terminal cause is added.

Freeze patient-level chronological splits before outcome inspection: train 2010-07-27–2018-12-31, validation 2019-01-01–2021-12-31, test 2022-01-01–2025-10-03, or a recomputed equivalent complete-follow-up cutoff after checking the source maximum. No patient crosses splits. Tune penalties, state dimension, observation shrinkage, and weight truncation on train/validation only.

For `D_D`, report paired test Brier, calibration, discrimination, and decision-curve net benefit, with a practically meaningful improvement threshold defined before test evaluation. For `D_I`, report cumulative incidence/risk at 30/60/90, cause-specific hazard summaries, time-dependent ROC/PR-AUC, IPCW Brier/integrated Brier, calibration, effective risk-set and event counts, observation-weight diagnostics, and paired patient-cluster bootstrap uncertainty (2,000 replicates or configured bounded equivalent). Report convergence and posterior/state uncertainty. Intervals crossing no incremental difference are inconclusive unless the predeclared precision target is met.

Falsification and boundary checks:
1. Permute laboratory timestamps within patient while preserving values and counts.
2. Fit the same machinery to a matched pre-index pseudo-trajectory.
3. Predict discharge lag and `A_{0–7}` as process-control outcomes.
4. Compare counts/lag/department/era-only models with clinical feature models.
5. Compare AST/ALT-only and reserve-panel-only blocks.
6. Report any-admission and repeat-TACE outcomes only as secondary, non-equivalent targets.
7. Shuffle discharge-stratum labels within train/validation as a selection-process control.
8. Audit feature time to prove no post-day-7 lab, encounter, discharge outcome, endpoint text, or later process variable enters dynamic features.
9. Produce diagnosis/document concordance and adjudication tables; do not report clinical terminal competing-risk results without validated timing.

Support requires improved primary `D_D` prediction on the untouched chronological test set, directionally compatible `D_I` performance, calibration not confined to discharged-by-day-7 or early-observed patients, no dominance by observation counts/discharge prediction, weak pre-index/timestamp-permutation performance, and no reversal after endpoint adjudication. Adverse evidence is disappearance under index anchoring, restriction to discharge/one care regime, prediction of care intensity rather than decompensation, pre-index reproduction, poor index calibration, or removal by adjudication. Inconclusive evidence includes sparse events, high censoring, unstable weights, missing/ambiguous timing, unresolved assay regimes, inadequate common support, or state-space nonconvergence. These defer or narrow interpretation; an imprecise null is not decisive refutation.

Computationally checkable outputs are source/header/hash integrity, within-HCC joins, cohort/timing ledgers, split/leakage audits, predictions, metrics, calibration, weights, negative-control contrasts, and adjudication-packet completeness. True decompensation, planned status, assay-unit validity, death/hospice, external validity, mechanism, causality, treatment benefit, and action thresholds require clinician review, validated linkage, or another study.

## Scientific deliverable and future budget

The solver must newly fit and freeze: (1) all-eligible `B_D` versus dynamic `D_D`; (2) baseline `B_I` and dynamic/SS-CR index-anchored predictions; (3) timing and observation ledgers; (4) endpoint diagnosis/document concordance and adjudication-ready packets; (5) observation-weight and early-care process analyses; and (6) all falsification outputs with uncertainty. Completion is established by these artifacts and their reproducible linkage to test predictions, not a favorable result.

The future-solver estimate is unmeasured and separate from discovery: 4–8 CPU cores and <32 GB RAM for selected-column parsing/L2 fits; about 16 CPUs, 64–128 GB RAM, no GPU, and up to 28,800 seconds for SS-CR plus bounded bootstrap. CPU is selected because this is low-dimensional tabular likelihood/survival fitting; an A100 is available but not needed on scientific grounds. A separate allocated GPU diagnostic may be considered only if matrix-heavy repeated fitting makes convergence infeasible. No full study is run here.

## Three key works

[K1] Sanai et al. supports the clinical consequence of post-LRT decompensation and baseline reserve; its selected, adjudicated cohort does not establish the present trajectory or timing estimands.

[K2] Xu et al. supports a baseline-only acute post-TACE dysfunction precedent; it does not test longitudinal trajectory information, discharge selection, or later decompensation.

[K3] You et al. supports a five-day biochemical injury window and the need to distinguish injury patterns from reserve loss; it does not establish later decompensation prediction.

Compact bibliography: Sanai FM et al., Scientific Reports (2026), DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-54466-4; Xu L et al., World Journal of Surgical Oncology (2025), DOI 10.1186/s12957-025-04100-w; You R et al., Discover Oncology (2025), DOI 10.1007/s12672-025-02286-9.

# Episode 5 evolution memo: index-anchored timing stress test for HCC

Status: proposed Harbor experiment only. No cohort scan, model fit, endpoint adjudication, or result has been executed.

## Repair objective and scientific boundary

The selected parent is `candidate-4e26300959818e3881f07308`. This repair preserves its primary estimand exactly:

> Among adults with HCC and a first observed TACE, does a 0–7-day laboratory trajectory add held-out prognostic information beyond baseline for a new high-specificity decompensation-coded admission during days 8–90 after index discharge?

The strongest rival is not merely “length-of-stay confounding.” The apparent trajectory signal could be generated by (1) who is discharged and therefore enters the primary risk set, (2) early acute-care encounters that increase laboratory and diagnosis observation, (3) assay/measurement intensity, or (4) diagnosis/documentation coding rather than reserve loss. The available evidence supports the importance of post-locoregional decompensation and baseline reserve [K1], but not that this HCC release’s 0–7-day trajectory predicts it. The literature also warns that TACE injury and post-TACE liver failure have heterogeneous definitions [K2], and that reserve scores and dynamic monitoring need careful interpretation [K3].

The unresolved claim is therefore narrower and falsifiable:

> If the trajectory contains prognostic information beyond discharge selection, early-care observation, assay intensity, and coding, its incremental direction and calibration should remain when the same day-0–7 features are evaluated from procedure time zero using an index-anchored observed-event estimand, with an explicit unresolvable-timing category.

A supportive result is incremental prognostic evidence only. It is not TACE causality, a biological mechanism, treatment benefit, mortality prediction, or a clinical action threshold.

## Minimal substantive revision

Keep the all-eligible primary population, baseline [−14,0] window, trajectory [0,7] window, and discharge-anchored binary outcome unchanged. Add one executable timing ledger and predeclare three outcomes:

1. `D_D`, unchanged primary: first distinct encounter after index `encounters.出院时间`, with `encounters.入院时间` in index days 8–90 and a high-specificity decompensation component in `diagnoses.诊断名称`.
2. `D_I`, index-anchored sensitivity: first distinct post-index encounter with `入院时间` in index days 8–90, regardless of discharge observability, with the same component rule. Its event time is linked encounter admission time minus the earliest qualifying procedure `procedures.开始时间`.
3. `U_T`, unresolvable timing: a candidate diagnosis attached to the continued index encounter or otherwise lacking a distinct post-index encounter anchor. Do not assign it an invented diagnosis timestamp, silently call it an event, or turn it into mortality.

The index-anchored analysis is a sensitivity, never a replacement for `D_D`. Missing discharge remains a reported ascertainment stratum, not discharge, a negative outcome, or a new time zero. Early care is represented as an observation/state transition, not an automatic competing clinical endpoint. A true terminal competing-risk analysis is not identified in this release: there is no mortality linkage, and clinical-document fields have no independent temporal column. It may be reported only after blinded clinician review validates terminal status and its linked encounter date; otherwise report the limitation and stop at observed-data cause-specific analyses.

## Population, time, and outcome construction

Use only HCC and never join patient identifiers to MIMIC or eICU.

- Select the first qualifying row in `procedures` where `手术` contains TACE, 肝动脉化疗栓塞, 经导管肝动脉栓塞, or 动脉化疗栓塞, with parseable `开始时间` and a matching `encounters` row.
- Require age >=18 from `encounters.年龄` and HCC on/before the index encounter from `diagnoses.诊断名称` (at least 肝细胞癌 or 肝恶性肿瘤).
- Exclude high-specificity decompensation terms on/before index using diagnosis rows linked to encounters: 腹水, 肝性脑病, 消化道出血, 食管胃底静脉曲张, 肝肾综合征, 急性肝衰竭, 肝功能衰竭, 自发性腹膜炎, 黄疸. Because diagnoses has no time field, use the linked encounter time and keep ambiguous same-encounter cases in an explicit ambiguity audit. Broader cirrhosis/decompensation flags remain descriptive.
- Time zero is the earliest qualifying `procedures.开始时间`; retain `结束时间` and `手术来源` for audit but do not infer procedural intensity or dose.
- Baseline is the closest assay-specific numeric `labs.定量结果` in [−14,0] days; [−30,0] is a sensitivity. Dynamic data are only [0,7] days, retained at raw `labs.检验时间`.
- The primary event component list is frozen before model performance is viewed. Report composite plus ascites, encephalopathy, bleeding, renal/hepatic failure, and jaundice components. Any admission and repeat TACE are secondary process/clinical outcomes, not substitutes for `D_D` or `D_I`.

No patient is excluded from the primary population for missing baseline, incomplete day-0–7 labs, missing discharge, or incomplete trajectory. Report availability strata and ascertainment flow.

## Exact HCC bindings and variables

All joins are within HCC on the documented composite key `(患者主索引, 就诊号)`; audit duplicate keys before aggregation. Every source is an ordinary CSV; archive member is “ordinary file.”
