| `orders` | `[private-path]/data_医嘱(非药品)_2062526727266216118.csv`; `24a6356b5c259e0573e75163e27d3eea15592c7691ed68f8e0979ac3c358c3d1` | `医嘱(非药品)`, `开立时间`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `医嘱期限`, `医嘱状态`, `频次`; observation/utilization process |

The full catalog was inspected. `vitals` and `transfers` contain identifiers only, `front_page` is identifiers only, and `pathology` lacks a usable event timestamp for this question. There is no imaging, tumor burden, ECOG, portal pressure, embolized territory, procedural drug/dose, validated lab-unit column, external follow-up, or mortality linkage.

For the lab panel, candidate concepts are bilirubin, albumin, platelets, PT/INR or PT ratio, creatinine, sodium, AST, ALT and AFP only if present. Freeze a train-only assay/name dictionary; parse numeric `定量结果` within assay/name regimes; preserve `定性结果`, `标本类型`, raw names, timestamps and counts. Since no lab-unit column exists, do not pool raw thresholds or claim ALBI/MELD/Child-Pugh without expert unit review.

## Observation and coding stress test

Create a pre-outcome timing/ascertainment ledger for every eligible index:

- discharge missingness and discharge lag; discharge before day 8, on/after day 8, and no observable discharge;
- first distinct post-index admission in days 0–7, whether it is the index encounter, and a separately labeled `就诊时间` any-encounter process;
- lab counts, assay counts, first-lab lag, last observed day, encounter/department counts, examination counts, order counts, medication counts, and whether observations came from index or later encounters;
- `D_D` time from discharge and `D_I` time from index;
- diagnosis-only, document-confirmed, discordant, missing-document and `U_T` timing labels.

The main endpoint rule is lexical/computable screening, not clinical truth. Require a blinded clinician sample across endpoint strata, discharge strata, early-care strata, calendar/departments, assay regimes and diagnosis/document discordance. Labels should include true new/worsening decompensation, pre-existing disease, competing illness/HCC progression, isolated TACE injury, planned/unclear status, text validity, and terminal-event status/date if a competing-risk quantity is proposed. The release does not provide planned/unplanned fields, so unknown status is retained.

## Matched methods and scientific alternatives

### Simple baseline

Fit `B_D`: L2-regularized logistic regression for unchanged `D_D`, using only time-zero age, sex, department, HCC/cirrhosis/portal-vein-thrombus/prior-decompensation flags, procedure context, pre-index utilization, assay-specific baseline values and missingness. Fit matched `B_I`: the same baseline covariates in a regularized cause-specific survival model for `D_I`, without post-index variables.

The primary comparison is the paired chronological-test-set difference between baseline-only and baseline-plus-[0,7] trajectory features for `D_D`: Brier score, calibration, discrimination and decision-curve net benefit. Survival metrics are supplementary and cannot replace this primary estimand.

### Substantive alternative: SS-CR state-space/observation model

Fit a two-factor irregular-time state-space model on the same assay-specific labs: a slowly varying reserve factor and a transient injury factor, with assay-regime measurement error, irregular timestamps, missingness/observation indicators, and process features available by day 7. A cause-specific hazard head predicts `D_I` days 8–90 from the day-7 posterior state and baseline covariates. Separate observation/early-care heads model lab and encounter observation; they do not use post-day-7 data. Add a terminal cause only if clinically adjudicated dates exist; otherwise state that clinical competing-risk inference is unavailable.

SS-CR can reveal whether a robustly shared trajectory differs from a slope/extreme-value summary, whether the apparent signal is concentrated in measurement intensity, whether reserve and transient injury separate, and whether early acute-care patients have different state uncertainty. Latent factors are representations, not mechanisms. The model’s state-evolution, missingness and partial-pooling assumptions are sensitivity assumptions.

The methods were selected because the baseline tests the clinically relevant incremental claim transparently, while SS-CR directly targets the observation/timing rival. A neural sequence model is deferred: it could learn ordering but would not by itself identify discharge selection, coding validity, missing mortality or assay units. Revisit only after an independent temporal test shows residual, stable ordering information not explained by the observation/state checks. This is a scientific deferral, not a complexity prohibition.

## Split, uncertainty, falsification, and no-results interpretation

Freeze patient-level chronological partitions before outcome inspection: train 2010-07-27–2018-12-31, validation 2019-01-01–2021-12-31, test 2022-01-01–2025-10-03, or the same rule recomputed from the verified source maximum. No patient crosses partitions. Tune penalties, state dimension, observation model, and weight truncation on train/validation only.

For `D_D`, report paired test Brier, calibration, discrimination, net benefit and uncertainty. For `D_I`, report cause-specific hazard summaries, risks at 30/60/90, time-dependent ROC/PR-AUC, IPCW Brier/integrated Brier, calibration, and paired patient-cluster bootstrap (2,000 replicates or a prespecified bounded equivalent). Report event counts, effective risk-set size, missing-discharge and early-care strata, censoring/weight diagnostics, state uncertainty and convergence. An interval crossing no meaningful incremental difference is inconclusive unless precision was prespecified as adequate.

Predeclared falsifications:

1. Permute lab timestamps within patient while preserving values and observation counts.
2. Apply the same model to a matched pre-index pseudo-trajectory.
3. Predict `D_D`/`D_I` from counts, lags, departments and calendar era without lab values.
4. Predict process outcomes (discharge lag and early acute care) to quantify observation association.
5. Compare AST/ALT-only, reserve-panel-only and combined blocks.
6. Repeat with any-admission and repeat-TACE outcomes, clearly secondary.
7. Shuffle discharge-stratum labels within train/validation as a selection-process control.
8. Audit that no post-day-7 lab, encounter, discharge outcome, endpoint text or later process variable enters features.
9. Reconcile diagnosis components with clinical-document fields and blinded adjudication.

Support means: the dynamic model improves untouched `D_D`; `D_I` gives directionally compatible incremental value; calibration is not confined to discharged or early-observed patients; counts-only/process outcomes do not dominate; pre-index and timestamp-permuted controls are weak; and endpoint concordance is acceptable. This supports an incremental observed-data prognostic regularity, not reserve mechanism or causality.

Adverse evidence means: the gain disappears under index anchoring, is confined to discharge/early-care regimes, is explained by counts or discharge prediction, reproduces pre-index/timestamp permutation, loses calibration, or disappears under document/adjudication review. Revise the claim to discharge-conditioned observed-care association or abandon the trajectory direction after adequately supported failure.

Inconclusive evidence means sparse index-anchored events, unstable weights or convergence, high missingness, unresolved assay units, poor common support, diagnosis/document discordance, or non-identifiable terminal timing. Narrow or defer interpretation; do not treat an imprecise null as refutation.

Computationally checkable: source hashes/headers, joins, timing ledger, cohort flow, split/leakage integrity, feature availability, fitted predictions, calibration, survival metrics, weight diagnostics, uncertainty and falsification outputs. Requiring clinician adjudication: true decompensation, assay units, planned status, competing illness, terminal events/death/hospice, mechanism, causal effect, external validity and action thresholds.

## Scientific deliverable and budget

The solver must newly produce: one all-eligible `D_D` ledger; one index-anchored `D_I/U_T` ledger; assay and observation audits; fitted `B_D`, `B_I` and SS-CR models; paired held-out predictions and uncertainty; discharge/early-care/process contrasts; diagnosis/document concordance tables; adjudication packets; and all falsification outputs. These outputs, not a favorable direction, establish completion.

Discovery did not fit models. The future workload estimate is unmeasured: 4–8 CPU cores and <32 GB RAM for selected-column parsing, ledgers and L2/Cox fits; approximately 16 CPU cores and 64–128 GB RAM for SS-CR plus bounded bootstrap, up to roughly 8 hours. GPU: 0 selected because this is low-dimensional likelihood/survival fitting; A100 availability does not make a GPU scientifically necessary. If repeated state-space linear algebra is demonstrably matrix-bound, a separate allocated one-GPU diagnostic may be considered, using `cuda:0` only inside an allocated job. This estimate is separate from the discovery budget and is not a claim that the solver has run.

## Reference-complete delivery

This child carries exactly three distinct abstract-only inspected works in `key-references.json` and the attached UTF-8 excerpts `hcc_K1_Sanai_excerpt.txt`, `hcc_K2_Sun_excerpt.txt`, and `hcc_K3_Decraecker_excerpt.txt`. The excerpts are provider-response snapshots, not full texts; no unavailable full text or supplementary methods is claimed.

[K1] Sanai et al., 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-54466-4: post-LRT decompensation and reserve importance; does not establish this estimand.

[K2] Sun et al., 2026, DOI 10.1016/j.clinre.2026.102874: heterogeneous TACE injury/decompensation definitions and dynamic reserve indicators; abstract-only review evidence.

[K3] Decraecker et al., 2026, DOI 10.2147/JHC.S579537: limitations of Child-Pugh, ALBI and dynamic monitoring in fragile HCC; abstract-only review evidence.

These references support, challenge and bound the question; they are not evidence of results for this proposed Harbor experiment.

# MIMIC-IV renal discordance: discharge- and observation-selection repair

Status: planned design only. I audited candidate-31009d7ec73ba43965cccd19 (the selected, valid, reference-complete parent) and candidate-4d74dcc7d306c36c4235c9f9 (the sibling's valid but reference-incomplete discharge repair). No patient rows were read, no cohort was fitted, and no patient-level result is claimed.

## Repair decision and scientific opening

The parent has a consequential remaining estimand flaw. It conditions on adults who survive at least 48 hours and reach an alive first-ICU outtime, then makes a dense final-window urine-documentation restriction. It models ICU readmission/death after t0 but can treat an early alive hospital discharge as an ordinary no-event. Thus residual severity, the decision to leave ICU/hospital, and the intensity of charting can be mistaken for a persistent renal pattern. The sibling correctly identified the flaw, but its handoff did not carry a complete evidence package.

The smallest substantive repair is to preserve the renal-discordance question, first-ICU-outtime landmark, repeated-versus-transient discriminator, exact MIMIC bindings, and held-out B0/B1/B2-versus-HMM comparison while making two selection processes part of the estimand:

1. define the target population as a conditional discharge-survivor landmark population and analyze alive hospital discharge as a competing observed endpoint; and
2. define the dense urine cohort as a measurement-supported stratum, report the full landmark flow, and standardize the dense-cohort contrast to the eligible landmark population using only pre-final-window observation-process information when overlap supports that transport.

This is not a treatment or discharge intervention effect. It asks whether an observed, time-aligned creatinine/urine pattern has conditional prognostic information that remains after measured discharge-process and observation-density checks.

### Evidence-supported versus unresolved claims

[K1] supports the clinical premise that AKI assessment and risk evaluation use complementary renal observations, but does not test this EHR phenotype. [K2] shows, in a small selected critical-illness cohort with measured clearance, that creatinine-based estimates can overestimate kidney function and be affected by muscle loss; this bounds interpretation of creatinine improvement. [K3] supports dynamic renal-function assessment for risk stratification while finding limited/inconsistent incremental value for extra biomarkers; it motivates a direct temporal-persistence comparison but does not establish this MIMIC question. These are abstract-only inspections; no full text or supplement is claimed.

The strongest available evidence supports only that creatinine and urine output are clinically relevant but imperfect, and that dynamic renal features can be prognostic in other cohorts. The unresolved, falsifiable claim is:

> Among adults who survive to an alive first-ICU outtime after at least 48 hours, a final 24-hour observed creatinine fall without observed urine recovery is associated with a higher probability of event E (in-hospital death or ICU readmission) within 48 hours than the improved/high-output group, after measured severity, support, discharge-process and observation-density adjustment; among final-window discordant patients with a valid prior window, repeated discordance has a different held-out E/D/N risk profile from transient discordance; a masked HMM adds information beyond the transparent recurrence baseline only if its label-invariant persistence/transition summaries yield a stable held-out contrast.

Here “E/D/N” means event, alive hospital discharge before the horizon, or no event/discharge by the horizon while still hospitalized. Supportive results establish an observed conditional prognostic regularity, not true filtration, complete urine collection, renal recovery, mechanism, causality, discharge utility, or transportability.

## Clinical importance and rival explanations

A clinically meaningful result would tell investigators whether a creatinine–urine discordance near ICU exit merits validation as a warning phenotype, or whether its apparent signal is mostly created by who survives to ICU exit, who is discharged early, or who receives dense urine charting. The closest rival is not simply “no renal effect.” It is a composite of:

- survivor/discharge selection: patients with different severity or care trajectories both reach t0 and have different short-term outcomes;
- informative documentation: urine rows, source type, and measurement span reflect Foley use, nursing workflow, or concern rather than complete physiologic urine output; and
- creatinine measurement artifact: muscle loss or changing creatinine generation makes a fall look like recovery.

Persistent observed physiology predicts a repeated final/prior pattern whose E risk contrast remains in dense and full-coverage analyses, after pre-final observation and fixed-ICU-age selection standardization, with stable temporal summaries. Selection/documentation predicts that discordance and recurrence concentrate in sparse/burst-like records, vary by source and support, predict D or early ICU-exit processes more strongly than E, or attenuate after those restrictions. Neither outcome identifies a renal mechanism.

## Population, temporal boundaries and joint estimand

Use only the frozen MIMIC-IV 3.1 archive and subject-specific shifted times. The unit is a first ICU stay per subject_id, linked to one admission. Let t0 = icustays.outtime.

Construct the flow before modeling:

- A0: adults with patients.anchor_age >=18, valid icustays.intime < outtime and los >=2 days, and a linked admissions row;
- A24: A0 alive and still in the ICU at 24 hours when applicable;
- A48: A0 with at least 48 hours of valid ICU time and alive at ICU age 48 hours;
- P: the primary conditional landmark population, with first ICU per subject_id, linked hadm_id, t0 >= intime + 48h, t0 <= admissions.dischtime, and deathtime null or strictly later than t0;
- D_dense: the subset of P satisfying the frozen final-window urine coverage rule and valid creatinine/urine measurements.

Report deaths before 24/48 hours, ICU exit before 48 hours, linkage/time failures, survival-to-t0 failures, and D_dense exclusions separately. P is not a general ICU cohort and is not an all-admission prognosis population.

The primary horizon is H=t0+48 hours. Define the first observed state using event/discharge times, with all timestamps compared within the same subject/admission:

- E: the earliest qualifying in-hospital death with admissions.deathtime in (t0,H], or later icustays.intime for the same subject_id, hadm_id with intime in (t0,H] and no preceding discharge;
- D: alive hospital discharge at admissions.dischtime in [t0,H] with no preceding E; discharge exactly at t0 is D at time zero, not a 48-hour non-event;
- N: no E or D by H and still hospitalized at H.

A later ICU admission after admissions.dischtime, an impossible death/discharge ordering, dischtime < t0, or death at/before t0 in P is a data-quality quarantine, not silently recoded. Tied discharge/readmission or death times are reported and quarantined unless a source-defined ordering is available. hospital_expire_flag never supplies an event time when deathtime is unusable. Keep death and ICU readmission as E components.

The primary estimand is the standardized observational state probability vector Pr(E,D,N | P, g), where g is a final-window renal-discordance group, plus risk differences and ratios for E. The primary group contrast is improved/high-output versus improved/low-output (discordant); the repeated-versus-transient contrast is among D_F=1 subjects with a valid prior window. This is a conditional discharge-survivor estimand, not risk after discharge and not a causal discharge estimand.

Because D_dense is selected by final-window documentation, report two related estimands rather than calling the dense estimate population-wide:

- measurement-supported estimand: Pr(E,D,N | P,D_dense=1,g);
- target-standardized sensitivity: standardize dense-cohort predictions over pre-final observation-process strata S observed in P, using Pr(S|P) and only if every focal group has adequate overlap. If overlap is inadequate, retain the dense result as conditional and mark target standardization inconclusive.

## Measurements and exact discordance

Primary final window F=[t0-24h,t0). The prior non-overlapping window is Q=[t0-48h,t0-24h). All predictor rows must be strictly before t0; observations at or after t0 are excluded from feature construction.

Creatinine uses hosp/labevents itemid=50912, linked to hosp/d_labitems. Retain finite positive valuenum with verified compatible valueuom, canonical mg/dL; exclude and report incompatible or unitless values. In each 24-hour window require at least two observations at least six hours apart and a final valid observation in the window. Let C_peak be the maximum and C_last the final value; improvement is C_peak-C_last >=0.3 mg/dL. Retain count, span and time from peak.

Urine uses icu/outputevents itemid 226559 (Foley), 226560 (Void), or 226561 (Condom Cath), joined by subject_id, hadm_id, stay_id. Retain finite nonnegative value with valueuom=mL and charttime within the selected stay/window. Sum valid values; absent rows are missing, never zero. Retain row count, source indicators, zero fraction, earliest/latest charttime and observed span. Span is documentation timing, not proof of complete collection. Low output is observed total <400 mL/24h, deliberately unweighted because no validated time-aligned weight field is bound.

D_dense requires at least two valid urine rows in each of four final six-hour bins and at least one verified source type. Report the frozen ladder: any valid row, >=2 final-window rows, >=1 row in every final bin, and >=2 rows per final bin with a verified source. Do not alter the ladder after test review. Final groups are improved/high-output, improved/low-output, not-improved/high-output, and not-improved/low-output; they are observed groups, not diagnoses.

The recurrence discriminator is defined identically in Q and F. D_F is final discordance and D_Q is prior discordance only when Q has the same creatinine validity and strict four-bin urine coverage. Define repeated=D_F=1 and D_Q=1; transient=D_F=1, D_Q=0 with Q valid; never call a missing/invalid Q window transient. Retain Q row count/span/source/zero fraction and creatinine count/span/time-from-peak.

## Discharge and observation-process audits

### Fixed ICU-age selection audit

Use p=icustays.intime+48h, computed from the ICU admission and never from future t0. Among A48, classify the first process state in (p,p+24h] as alive ICU exit, ICU death, or still ICU/unknown, using icustays.outtime and admissions.deathtime with data-quality checks. This audit is not a second primary outcome.

Fit G_p, a simple multinomial selection/process model on A48 using only features observed before p: age, gender, admission type, ICU care unit, early creatinine/urine observation counts and masks, MAP, support, transfer context and missingness indicators. The same patient split is used; preprocessing/fitting is train-only. Use G_p risk strata to standardize or stratify the P repeated-versus-transient and final-group contrasts. A comparable early exit/death association or disappearance after G_p is adverse to a persistent-physiology interpretation. G_p cannot remove unmeasured survivor selection, discharge rationale or treatment confounding.

### Pre-final observation selection

Define O_pre in Q: urine row count/span/source, creatinine count/span, MAP count, care unit/transfer fields, vasopressor/ventilation exposure, and missingness flags. Fit Pr(D_dense=1 | O_pre) on training P only, tune regularization on the tuning split, and apply to untouched test data. Use stabilized inverse-odds/standardization only with pre-specified overlap and positivity diagnostics; do not use post-t0 documentation. Report source-specific results (Foley, Void, Condom Cath), urine-to-MAP coverage strata, and the full P missingness/coverage flow. This is a measurement sensitivity, not recovery of unobserved urine.

## Baseline and substantive learned alternative

The scientific deliverable is not a leaderboard. It must produce a frozen manifest/flow, E/D/N outcomes, leakage-safe fits, held-out standardized contrasts, uncertainty, selection/coverage diagnostics, and an interpretation table that links each claim to those outputs.

B0 is the transparent penalized multinomial logistic baseline for E/D/N. Inputs are age, gender, admission_type, ICU LOS, admission-to-t0 duration, first_careunit, last_careunit, creatinine level/change/count/span/time-from-peak and missingness, final urine volume/low-output/row count/span/source/zero fraction and missingness, MAP item 220052 summaries/masks, vasopressor exposure/duration/last-active status from itemids 221906, 221289, 221749 and 222315, invasive ventilation exposure/duration/status from procedureevents itemid 225792, and missingness indicators. Pre-t0 transfer context is a selection diagnostic.

B1 adds the four-level F renal group while retaining continuous ingredients and documentation measures. B1 versus B0 tests whether the thresholded clinical grouping adds information beyond its measured components. B2 adds D_Q, prior-window validity, Q urine/creatinine coverage and continuous summaries. B1-to-B2 tests whether transparent recurrence adds information beyond the final snapshot and its observation fields. Report group contrasts standardized over fixed B1-risk strata whose cutpoints are learned on training predictions; no matching criterion is selected after test review.

L1 is a three-state masked HMM over non-overlapping six-hour bins from icustays.intime to t0. Channels are creatinine last/change, urine volume, urine row count, observed span, source indicators, zero fraction, MAP, pressor/ventilation support, and explicit masks. Unobserved urine is a missing emission, never zero; partial first bins retain duration. Fit only on training subjects, tune emission/regularization on tune, and export label-invariant summaries: expected adjacent transition count, posterior persistence through the final four bins, persistence across Q/F boundary, occupancy/mask summaries and time since inferred transition. Use B2 plus these summaries in the E/D/N outcome model. L1 is retained only if it adds a stable held-out transition/persistence contrast beyond B2; HMM improvement over B1 alone is insufficient.

The baseline is scientifically useful because it makes the estimand and documentation adjustment auditable. The HMM can reveal persistence, transition timing and mask-aware trajectories that the baseline's aggregates lose. It is not allowed to convert latent states into biological renal labels.

## Split, uncertainty and fit/no-fit gates

Create one patient-level 70/15/15 train/tune/test split before any fit, using a recorded fixed seed/hash rule, and reuse it for B0/B1/B2, L1, G_p and the observation-selection model. Fit preprocessing and standardization parameters on train only; select penalties/HMM settings on tune only; inspect test outcomes once.

On untouched test predictions report E/D/N probabilities, calibration for all states, Brier score, log loss, calibration slope/intercept, descriptive AUROC/AUPRC, standardized E risks, risk differences/ratios, and paired proper-score deltas B1-B0, B2-B1 and L1-B2. Report primary and component event counts, D and N counts, P/D_dense sizes, repeated/transient sizes, overlap and effective sample size. Use 200 patient-level bootstrap resamples of held-out predictions for uncertainty in probabilities, contrasts and score deltas.

Do not fit or interpret L1 if the test set has <200 subjects, <30 E events, <20 repeated or <20 transient subjects, absent E/D/N support, nonrepresentable masks, or missing train/tune coverage. A fit is inconclusive if convergence fails, a state occupies <5% of training bins, median maximum posterior state probability is <0.60, or label-invariant transition/persistence summaries remain directionally stable in <80% of pre-specified stability refits. Do not use a weak or imprecise null as refutation.

The target-standardized D_dense sensitivity is not reported as identified if focal groups lack overlap in O_pre selection scores, effective sample size is too small, or weighting is dominated by a pre-specified tail. G_p standardization is similarly marked inconclusive when early process strata are too small or positivity fails.

## Falsification, interpretation and stopping rules

Freeze before test-outcome review: archive/member/schema/item checks; A0/A24/A48/P/D_dense flow; coverage ladder; 12-hour and 48-hour horizons; continuous creatinine change; source and measurement-density strata; care-unit and support strata; O_pre overlap; G_p selection audit; no-support restriction; creatinine-only and urine-only models; permutation of final discordance within ICU-LOS/admission/B1-risk strata; and a fixed p=intime+48h pseudo-landmark diagnostic.

Supportive evidence requires a calibrated held-out E contrast in D_dense and, where overlap permits, the O_pre-standardized target; a repeated-versus-transient E/D/N contrast that survives G_p and coverage/source/support checks; and a stable L1 transition/persistence contrast with incremental proper-score evidence beyond B2. This supports an observed conditional prognostic regularity and justifies external or clinically adjudicated validation.

Adverse evidence is attenuation/reversal after O_pre standardization or support restriction, concentration in sparse/burst documentation or one source type, a strong D or early ICU-exit/death signal without E separation, disappearance after G_p, a permutation contrast comparable to observed, or no stable held-out L1 contrast beyond B2. This favors ascertainment, residual severity, creatinine artifact, or survivor/discharge selection and stops the complexity branch.

Inconclusive evidence includes missing or mismatched archive/schema/items, invalid units/times, unresolved death/discharge order, inadequate events/groups/overlap, calibration failure, unstable HMM states, or wide uncertainty. Report the exact limitation and do not relabel it as a favorable or null clinical result.

Computationally checkable claims are archive/member/schema/item availability; cohort flow; no post-t0 predictors; split integrity; fits; held-out predictions; proper scores; bootstrap intervals; state/selection summaries; and whether conclusions follow from those outputs. Complete urine collection, true GFR, CKD/renal reserve, fluid balance, treatment or discharge causality, mechanism, clinical utility and transportability require adjudication, richer measurements, external validation or another study.

## Exact source binding

Configured source (read-only): [private-path]/mimic-iv-3.1.zip, 10,551,747,784 bytes, SHA-256 0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09; catalog snapshot 5126591f768df4f9d981d97d94329fd65f78a1a0e1eb7cab0332454f888ab8b6. Stage only through binding-template.json as /data/baidu_downloads/eicu_mimic/mimic数据库/mimic-iv-3.1.zip/mimic-iv-3.1.zip.

Required archive member bindings, verified source schemas, joins and times are:

The bounded parent verification checked archive existence, all 11 members, schemas and dictionary rows for 50912, 226559/226560/226561, 220052, 221906/221289/221749/222315 and 225792 without scanning patient rows. ## Alternatives, resource budget and revisit evidence

The selected simple comparator is B0/B1/B2 because it directly exposes threshold, recurrence, severity and documentation contributions. The selected learned alternative is L1 because mask-aware transition timing may reveal information lost by window aggregates; its extra complexity is justified only by a distinct held-out temporal contrast beyond B2. Both use the exact same P, F/Q measurements, E/D/N outcome and patient split. Fit targets are multinomial E/D/N probabilities and repeated-versus-transient standardized contrasts; uncertainty is 200 patient bootstrap resampling of held-out predictions.

A mechanistic filtration/fluid-balance model is deferred because the bound archive lacks measured GFR, validated time-aligned weight, fluid composition, complete diuretic exposure and adjudicated urine collection. A transformer/LSTM is deferred because it adds opaque capacity without a pre-specified clinical observable beyond L1 persistence/transition summaries. These are question-specific deferrals, not blanket exclusions of neural networks or GPUs. Revisit the mechanistic branch when validated weight, fluid composition, complete diuretic exposure and filtration/urine adjudication are available; revisit a neural model only when it yields a defined observable unavailable to B2/L1 and is tested on the same held-out split. If CPU extraction/HMM fitting exceeds the envelope, complete B0-B2 and the selection/coverage audits and defer L1; do not change the estimand.

Future solver estimate: CPU 8 cores, 64 GiB RAM, up to 4 hours for streaming extraction, B0-B2/G_p/selection fits, HMM, bootstrap and diagnostics. Campaign planning envelope: up to 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds. These full-study timings are unmeasured; the only measured parent probe was archive/dictionary verification (0.55 seconds). GPU is not needed for these low-dimensional models; no GPU feasibility claim is made.

## Three inspected works and evidence delivery

Exactly three distinct works are highlighted: [K1] Kellum/Lameire/KDIGO (2013), [K2] Haines et al. (2023), and [K3] Neumann et al. (2026). Each was inspected through a frozen Europe PMC metadata/abstract response; full text and supplements were not inspected or claimed. Their claims, limitations, locators, retrieval receipts and hashes are in key-references.json. Attached UTF-8 evidence files are K1_kellum_kdigo_abstract_excerpt.txt, K2_haines_clearance_abstract_excerpt.txt and K3_neumann_kinetic_egfr_abstract_excerpt.txt.

## Completion deliverable

The future study is complete only when it produces: byte/schema/item manifest; A0/A24/A48/P/D_dense flow; E/D/N event table and component timing exceptions; frozen F/Q feature tables and coverage ladder; G_p process audit; O_pre selection overlap/standardization diagnostics; fixed patient split; B0/B1/B2 and held-out risks/calibration/score outputs; L1 masks/emissions/transitions/persistence and gate results if fit; 200-bootstrap intervals; all falsification outputs; and an interpretation table linking every conclusion to a computed output. No patient result is asserted here.

# Episode 6 generation memo: endpoint-validity and decision-relevance repair

Status: proposed Harbor experiment only. No cohort scan, adjudication, model fit, or result has been executed.

Parent: candidate-c82b7c59f3d2d8bb7b448a5d. This child is a bounded interpretive repair. It preserves the parent population, earliest-procedure time zero, baseline and dynamic windows, primary estimand, and D_I sensitivity.

## Scientific deliverable

The solver must newly produce, from the frozen HCC snapshot:

1. an all-eligible population and timing ledger;
2. the unchanged discharge-anchored primary outcome `D_D), the index-anchored sensitivity `D_I), and explicit unresolvable-timing `U_T`;
3. a blinded, stratified endpoint-adjudication packet and design-weighted validity estimates;
4. matched held-out predictions from an L2 baseline and a substantive state-space/observation alternative;
5. a capacity-indexed post-discharge clinical-review evaluation that reports what can be learned without inventing treatment thresholds;
6. process, coding, timing, assay-regime, and leakage falsifications.

Completion is established by these auditable ledgers, packets, adjudication agreement/uncertainty, frozen splits, held-out predictions, uncertainty intervals, and interpretation table—not by a favorable result.

## Opening, evidence boundary, and hypothesis

The strongest evidence already supports is narrower than the parent’s predictive claim. [K1] reports clinically important post-locoregional hepatic decompensation and an association with baseline hepatic reserve in a selected multicenter cohort. [K2] distinguishes transient biochemical injury/post-embolization effects from clinically meaningful decompensation and emphasizes heterogeneous definitions. [K3] bounds reserve interpretation: commonly used reserve scores are subjective or interrelated, and dynamic liver-function monitoring is clinically relevant. None validates this HCC release’s coding, diagnosis timing, assay units, discharge process, or post-TACE trajectory.

The unresolved claim is:

> Among adults with HCC and a first observed TACE, does information in the day-0–7 laboratory trajectory add reproducible prognostic information beyond the parent’s time-zero baseline for a clinically credible new/worsening decompensation event in days 8–90, when the event is tested under both discharge-anchored and index-anchored timing and when observation intensity and endpoint validity are explicitly audited?

The primary estimand remains:

> In the all-eligible first-observed-TACE population, compare baseline-only with baseline-plus-day-0–7 trajectory predictions for a new high-specificity decompensation-coded admission whose encounter admission time is days 8–90 after the index encounter’s observed discharge (`D_D`).

`D_I` remains a sensitivity, not a replacement:

> the same high-specificity coded component on the first distinct post-index encounter whose admission time is index days 8–90, regardless of whether discharge is observed.

This is prognostic/descriptive evidence about observed care, not TACE causality, biological mechanism, treatment benefit, mortality, or an action threshold.

## What the endpoint can and cannot establish

The computational screen freezes a high-specificity lexical component list before model inspection: ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, gastrointestinal bleeding, esophageal/gastric variceal bleeding, hepatorenal syndrome, acute hepatic failure, hepatic failure, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, and jaundice in `diagnoses.诊断名称`. HCC and prior disease flags use the same field. Diagnosis rows are linked to an encounter by `(患者主索引, 就诊号)`; they do not have an independent diagnosis date. `诊断类型` is retained as a descriptive field, not treated as timing or truth.

A candidate is a coded event only when the diagnosis row links to a distinct qualifying encounter whose `encounters.入院时间` supplies the event anchor. A diagnosis attached to the continuing index encounter, a missing encounter anchor, or a candidate whose timing cannot be separated from the index encounter is `U_T`. It is never assigned an invented diagnosis date, silently treated as a positive/negative event, or turned into a terminal event.

The clinical-document packet can strengthen or contradict the lexical screen, but cannot by itself create a date. It can support explicit narrative evidence of new/worsening symptoms, an admission/discharge condition, treatment course, or procedure context. It cannot establish complete physiologic severity, causal relation to TACE, treatment appropriateness, death, hospice, or an unrecorded event. There is no mortality linkage. The fields do not contain an explicit planned/unplanned indicator: planned status is `planned-supported`, `unplanned-supported`, or `unknown` only when the wording unambiguously supports it; otherwise it is unknown and retained in the primary analysis.

## Population, time, and outcomes

Use HCC only; never join patient identifiers to MIMIC or eICU.

- Population: age `>=18` in `encounters.年龄`, HCC diagnosis on or before the index encounter, and a parseable matching procedure row containing a frozen TACE synonym rule in `procedures.手术`. Select the earliest qualifying `procedures.开始时间`; retain `结束时间` and `手术来源` for audit but do not infer dose, embolized territory, or procedural intensity.
- Join key: every HCC table is joined only on the documented composite key `(患者主索引, 就诊号)`. Audit duplicate keys before aggregation; do not use name, identity-card, phone, or cross-dataset identifiers.
- Time zero: earliest qualifying procedure `开始时间`; retain linked index encounter `就诊时间`, `入院时间`, `出院时间`, and `就诊科室`.
- Baseline: closest assay-specific numeric result in `labs.定量结果` in [-14, 0] days relative to procedure start, with a predeclared [-30, 0] sensitivity. Preserve raw assay name, qualitative result, sample type and timestamp.
- Dynamic window: only labs with `labs.检验时间` in [0, 7] days, represented by assay-specific values, slopes/changes, irregular timestamps, missingness and counts. Do not pool raw values across assay/name regimes. No ALBI, MELD, Child-Pugh, INR, bilirubin, creatinine or other clinical unit claim is made without expert review because the source has no lab-unit column.
- `D_D`: first distinct encounter after the observed index `出院时间`, with `入院时间` in index days 8–90 after that discharge and at least one frozen decompensation component in linked diagnoses. If discharge is missing, retain the patient in the all-eligible cohort and report a missing-discharge ascertainment stratum; do not call missing discharge a discharge or a negative outcome.
- `D_I`: first distinct post-index encounter with `入院时间` in index days 8–90 and the same component rule, including patients without an observable discharge.
- `U_T`: component diagnosis attached to the continuing index encounter or lacking a distinct encounter admission anchor. Do not impute its event time.
- Report component-specific ascites, encephalopathy, bleeding/varices, renal/hepatic failure, and jaundice results. Repeat TACE and any admission are secondary process/clinical outcomes, never substitutes for `D_D` or `D_I`.
- No eligibility exclusion for missing baseline, incomplete day-0–7 labs, missing discharge, or incomplete trajectory. Report flow and availability.

## Blinded endpoint adjudication packet

This is a validation substudy over the same all-eligible cohort, not a change in the primary estimand.

### Sampling and blinding

Before model fitting and without model scores, sample packets using a frozen random seed and retain design weights. The main cross-classification is coded event (positive/negative) by diagnosis-document concordance (diagnosis-only, document-confirmed, discordant, missing document), with quotas to preserve discharge observed/missing, early acute care in days 0–7, department/era, assay regime, and repeat-TACE strata. Sample all cases when a populated cell is smaller than its quota and randomly sample non-cases within cell; record the sampling fraction. The target is 30 packets per populated main cell, with a hard maximum of 360 packets. If that target cannot be reached or a required stratum has no independent reviewer, report sparse/incomplete evidence rather than silently collapsing it.

Each packet contains only source-derived information: index and candidate encounter identifiers/times (`encounters`), all linked diagnosis rows and `诊断类型`, the index and candidate `clinical_documents` rows including both admission-diagnosis occurrences, admission/discharge conditions, diagnoses, treatment course, procedure name/course, relevant `procedures` rows, and a compact ledger of early-care encounters and utilization from `examinations`, `orders`, and `medications`. It does not contain model scores, predicted risk, or a trajectory-derived label. Reviewers are blinded to exposure block and model performance but necessarily see the encounter time anchors needed to judge whether “new” can be supported.

Two independent hepatology-trained clinical reviewers assign labels; disagreements are resolved by a third reviewer or consensus, with the unresolved fraction reported. The packet includes a reviewer statement for each field: explicit, inferred, absent, or contradictory.

### Required labels

- endpoint truth: `definite_new_or_worsening_decompensation`, `probable_new_or_worsening_decompensation`, `preexisting_or_no_support`, `competing_illness_or_HCC_progression`, `isolated_TACE_injury_or_postembolization_effect`, `invalid_or_uninterpretable_text`, or `indeterminate`;
- component: ascites, encephalopathy, gastrointestinal/variceal bleeding, renal/hepatic failure, jaundice, or other/none;
- status: `planned-supported`, `unplanned-supported`, or `unknown`;
- timing: distinct encounter-anchored, continuing-index/ambiguous, or missing anchor;
- document concordance: diagnosis-only, document-confirmed, discordant, or missing document;
- terminal status: not adjudicable from this release; if a reviewer notes terminal language, store it as a note/unknown field and do not use it as death or competing-risk time.

The primary coded outcome is not relabeled by reviewer opinion. Report raw `D_D`/`D_I`, design-weighted PPV and negative-stratum estimates for definite-or-probable decompensation, component-specific agreement, reviewer agreement (weighted kappa or raw agreement with confidence interval), and the fraction planned/unknown, ambiguous, and indeterminate. Use the adjudication overlay to quantify endpoint validity; do not silently replace the original endpoint.

Predeclared endpoint interpretation: supportive validity requires a majority of weighted coded positives to be definite/probable, a 95% interval for that PPV that is not compatible with a majority of coded positives being unsupported, and at least moderate reviewer agreement (kappa 0.60 or higher where estimable). These are validation-quality criteria, not patient-treatment thresholds. Adverse validity is a majority unsupported/competing/injury label or agreement below 0.40. Sparse packets, wide intervals, unresolved reviewer disagreement, or inadequate coverage of key strata are inconclusive. No result is claimed in this proposal.

## Matched methods and why both are needed

### Matched simple baseline

For the unchanged primary `D_D`, fit an L2-regularized logistic model `B_D`. Use only time-zero variables: age, sex, department, HCC/cirrhosis and prior-decompensation lexical flags, procedure context, pre-index utilization, assay-specific baseline values, and baseline missingness. Fit the matched `B_I` cause-specific survival/logistic landmark model with the same covariates and no post-index variables. Compare each baseline model with a baseline-plus-[0,7] trajectory block; every model uses the same cohort and patient-level split.

The trajectory block contains only assay-specific, unit-free within-assay transformations: last/first observed value, within-person change or slope where at least two timed values exist, number and timing of observations, missingness, and assay-regime indicators. Raw thresholds and clinical composite scores are prohibited unless an expert unit review first establishes comparability.

### Substantive learned/mechanistic alternative

Fit an irregular-time two-factor state-space/observation model (`SS-CR`) to the same assay-specific observations. One latent factor is a slowly varying reserve-like state and one is a transient post-procedure injury-like state; these are statistical representations, not established mechanisms. The observation submodel uses lab counts/timing, encounter/department observation, examination/order/medication counts, and missingness. The outcome head predicts `D_D` and the index-anchored `D_I` from information available by day 7. No post-day-7 data, adjudication label, discharge outcome, or later utilization may enter a feature.

This alternative can reveal information the L2 summary loses: whether a shared trajectory is stable after irregular sampling, whether transient injury separates from a slower reserve-like pattern, whether posterior uncertainty tracks early-care/observation intensity, and whether the apparent laboratory signal is mostly an observation process. It does not make the latent factors biological proof or solve endpoint misclassification.

The comparison is scientific, not a contest for a small AUC gain. If SS-CR adds no stable information after observation and endpoint checks, the simpler baseline is preferred for the next study. A transformer sequence model is deferred because a short, low-dimensional [0,7] window and unresolved endpoint/units make a black-box ordering gain uninterpretable; this is a scientific deferral, not a ban on neural methods. The Delphi demonstration’s long dated diagnosis histories and scale are not reproduced. The Bayesian latent-signature demonstration’s genetic inputs and multi-disease horizon are not available or needed; an HCC-only state-space adaptation is the bounded alternative.

## Split, analysis, decision relevance, and uncertainty

Freeze a patient-level chronological split before outcome inspection: train 2010-07-27–2018-12-31, validation 2019-01-01–2021-12-31, and test 2022-01-01–2025-10-03, or recompute these cut points from verified source extrema if the catalog maximum differs. No patient crosses partitions. Tune penalties, state dimension, observation model, and any weighting on train/validation only.

Primary held-out comparison: paired test-set Brier score, calibration intercept/slope/curve, discrimination with uncertainty, and calibration after the adjudication-weighted endpoint overlay. For `D_I`, report 30/60/90-day risks, time-dependent ROC/PR-AUC, IPCW Brier/integrated Brier, calibration, effective risk set, censoring/weight diagnostics, convergence, and state uncertainty. Use patient-cluster bootstrap (2,000 replicates or a bounded equivalent declared before fitting). Report estimates and intervals, not only p-values.

The decision object is explicitly limited to prioritizing a post-discharge clinical chart-review/follow-up queue at day 7. It is not a medication, repeat-TACE, admission, transplant, or mortality decision. To make relevance testable without inventing an action threshold, predeclare capacity fractions of 5%, 10%, and 20% of the eligible queue. At each fraction compare baseline versus dynamic models on sensitivity, positive predictive value, number needed to review, calibration within selected and unselected groups, and the fraction of definite/probable adjudicated events captured. These are workload scenarios, not clinical thresholds. Report decision curves only as cost-free ranking curves; do not assign benefit, harm, or net-benefit weights that the source does not contain. If adjudicated validity is absent, the queue analysis is coded-event prioritization only and cannot be called clinically useful.

Supportive decision-relevance evidence requires endpoint validity to be supportive, a directionally concordant dynamic gain on untouched `D_D` and `D_I`, no material calibration failure, and higher validated event capture than the matched baseline at at least one prespecified capacity fraction without the gain being confined to a single discharge/early-care/department/assay stratum. This supports a decision to seek prospective clinical validation of review prioritization, not deployment or treatment selection.

Adverse evidence includes dynamic gain disappearing under `D_I`, being explained by counts/lags/departments or discharge/early-care prediction, reproducing in timestamp-permuted or pre-index pseudo-trajectories, failing document adjudication, or selecting mostly planned/unsupported/injury labels. Revise the claim to observed-care association or abandon the trajectory direction after adequately powered failure.

Inconclusive evidence includes too few index-anchored events, unstable IPCW weights, nonconvergence, insufficient adjudication coverage, wide validity intervals, substantial timing ambiguity, unresolved assay units, poor common support, or no independent clinical reviewers. An imprecise null is not refutation. Continue only to an independently reviewed prospective endpoint/units study; defer or stop if the same limitations persist.

### Falsification and leakage checks

1. Permute lab timestamps within patient while preserving values and observation counts.
2. Apply the same pipeline to a matched pre-index pseudo-trajectory.
3. Fit counts/lags/departments/calendar-only models and compare their performance with value-bearing models.
4. Predict discharge lag and early acute care as process outcomes to quantify observation association.
5. Compare AST/ALT-only, reserve-panel-only, and combined assay blocks without pooling units.
6. Repeat coded secondary outcomes for any admission and repeat TACE, clearly not the primary endpoint.
7. Verify that no post-day-7 lab, encounter, diagnosis/document adjudication, discharge outcome, or later utilization enters prediction.
8. Audit diagnosis/document concordance, planned-status unknown retention, `U_T`, missing discharge, duplicate keys, and assay regimes.
9. Shuffle discharge-stratum labels in train/validation as a selection-process control.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes/headers, joins, timing ledger, cohort flow, split/leakage integrity, feature availability, predictions, calibration, survival metrics, capacity curves, bootstrap intervals, and falsification outputs. Clinical adjudication is required for true decompensation, new/worsening status, planned intent, competing illness, and unit interpretation. Mechanism, causal effect, external validity, mortality, treatment benefit, and action thresholds require expert review, linked outcomes, or another study.

## Demonstration dispositions

- D1, “Learning the natural history of human disease with generative transformers” (Shmatko et al., Nature 2025): the full local XML and readable extraction were inspected, including the continuous-time trajectory, chronological held-out evaluation, and external Danish validation claims. Disposition: use only as a rationale for patient-level temporal splits and a warning about learned missingness; do not reproduce its UKB/Danish scale, diagnosis vocabulary, death token, or generative claims in HCC.
- D2, “Advancing cancer detection and treatment using longitudinal routine clinical data” (Oncoformer, Cell 2026): the README and supplementary PDF/text were inspected. The main article and complete STAR Methods were unavailable, and images are absent locally. The supplement supports explicit lab-only/utilization baselines and modality ablations. Disposition: do not claim to have read the main paper or reproduce the multimodal experiment; retain only the comparison principle, with SS-CR chosen because it addresses observation and latent reserve in the available HCC fields.
- D3, “A Bayesian framework for longitudinal EHR and genetic discovery” (ALADYNOULLI, Nature 2026): the local article readable text and relevant longitudinal-prediction/method passages were inspected. It uses longitudinal diagnosis trajectories, latent signatures and genetic inputs with dynamic held-out prediction. Disposition: genetics, multi-disease scale and long horizon are absent or unnecessary here; adapt the scientific idea only as a bounded HCC state-space/observation model, not as reproduction or a claim of genetic discovery.

These demonstrations are method/context references, not evidence that the HCC hypothesis is true.

## Compute and revisit rule

Discovery has not fitted the models. The future solver envelope is estimated, not measured: 4–8 CPU cores and <32 GiB for selected-column parsing, ledgers, L2 fits and adjudication sampling; approximately 16 CPU cores and 64–128 GiB for SS-CR and bounded bootstrap, up to about 8 hours. CPU is selected because the proposed models are low-dimensional survival/state-space fits; the configured A100 GPUs are not a scientific requirement. If a bounded matrix diagnostic shows repeated state-space linear algebra is the limiting step, a separate allocated one-GPU job may request `gpus=1` and use `cuda:0` inside the allocation; ordinary shell CUDA absence is not evidence of hardware absence. These estimates are separate from discovery and no solver run is claimed.

Revisit the deferred transformer/complex latent-signature directions only if (a) a blinded adjudication packet supports endpoint validity, (b) a chronological test shows residual dynamic information beyond observation counts and discharge/early-care strata, and (c) unit review establishes a defensible assay registry. Defer or abandon the trajectory direction if endpoint validity is adverse or if the apparent gain is entirely a process/coding artifact. Seek prospective expert adjudication and externally anchored outcomes before any clinical deployment claim.

## Key references

Exactly three distinct abstract-only works are attached in `work/key-references.json` with the inspected UTF-8 provider-response snapshots:

[K1] Sanai FM et al. “Predictors and outcomes of hepatic decompensation following transarterial locoregional therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma.” Scientific Reports, 2026. DOI: 10.1038/s41598-026-54466-4. Abstract-only; supports clinical importance and reserve association, but not this dataset’s endpoint validity or timing.

[K2] Sun K et al. “TACE-induced liver injury in hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms, prediction, and prevention in the era of gut microbiota and inflammasome research.” Clinical Research in Hepatology and Gastroenterology, 2026. DOI: 10.1016/j.clinre.2026.102874. Abstract-only; supports separating transient injury from decompensation and definition audits.

[K3] Decraecker M et al. “Impact of Child Pugh B Stage for the Treatment of Advanced HCC.” Journal of Hepatocellular Carcinoma, 2026. DOI: 10.2147/JHC.S579537. Abstract-only; bounds reserve and dynamic-monitoring interpretation.

The attached reference JSON preserves the original receipts and hashes; no inaccessible full text or supplementary methods is claimed.

# Episode 6 evolution: internally transportable HCC post-TACE trajectory with endpoint-validity gate

Status: proposed Harbor experiment only. No cohort scan, model fit, adjudication, calibration, decision curve, or result was executed.

Parent: candidate-c82b7c59f3d2d8bb7b448a5d. This child preserves the parent's population, procedure time zero, baseline window, dynamic window, primary endpoint, and primary estimand. Its substantive repair is to make transportability and clinical decision relevance testable without treating a coded diagnosis as a clinical gold standard.

## Scientific opening, evidence-supported claim, and unresolved claim

The strongest available evidence supports the clinical importance of hepatic reserve and post-locoregional decompensation [K1], and supports separating transient post-TACE biochemical injury from clinically meaningful decompensation [K2]. It also bounds reserve scores and dynamic liver monitoring as interpretable but imperfect constructs [K3]. These inspected works do not test this release's first-observed-TACE routine-care population, do not establish its discharge-versus-index timing, and do not validate its diagnosis or document fields.

The parent supports a computable prognostic opening only: a day 0–7 laboratory trajectory may add information about a later high-specificity decompensation-coded encounter beyond baseline, while discharge selection, early care, observation intensity, assay regime and coding remain serious rivals. It does not establish that the code is true clinical decompensation, that the pattern transports across care/assay regimes, or that a risk score would change monitoring.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> In the fixed all-eligible HCC population below, a day 0–7 trajectory that adds held-out prognostic information beyond time-zero baseline will retain its direction, calibration and incremental value when evaluated in later calendar bands, departments and observed assay/name/sample-type regimes, and this pattern will not be explained by endpoint-document discordance or observation intensity.

“Transportable” here means internal transportability across prespecified regimes in this HCC release, not external validity to another hospital or population. A supportive result would justify a future prospective monitoring-and-adjudication study. It would not establish TACE causality, a reserve mechanism, mortality prediction, treatment benefit, or a patient-care threshold. Latent reserve and injury factors are statistical representations, not mechanisms.

## What changes and what does not

Unchanged primary estimand:

> Among adults with HCC and a first observed TACE, does a 0–7-day laboratory trajectory add held-out prognostic information beyond baseline for a new high-specificity decompensation-coded admission during days 8–90 after index discharge?

Keep:

- all eligible patients, including missing baseline, incomplete trajectory, missing discharge and early acute-care returns;
- earliest qualifying TACE procedures.开始时间 as time zero;
- baseline laboratory window [-14,0] days and dynamic window [0,7] days;
- primary discharge-anchored binary outcome D_D;
- index-anchored sensitivity D_I, and explicit unresolvable-timing category U_T;
- no patient joins to MIMIC or eICU.

The repair adds a prespecified endpoint-validity gate, regime-held-out transportability analysis and an exploratory decision-curve handoff. It does not replace D_D with D_I, convert missing discharge into discharge, assign diagnosis timestamps, or create mortality.

## Fixed population and temporal construction

Select the first qualifying procedure row within HCC whose procedures.手术 contains TACE, 肝动脉化疗栓塞, 经导管肝动脉栓塞 or 动脉化疗栓塞, with parseable procedures.开始时间 and a matching encounter. Require age >=18 in encounters.年龄 and HCC (肝细胞癌 or 肝恶性肿瘤) on or before the index encounter through diagnosis rows linked by the composite key. Exclude high-specificity decompensation terms linked to an encounter on or before index: 腹水, 肝性脑病, 消化道出血, 食管胃底静脉曲张, 肝肾综合征, 急性肝衰竭, 肝功能衰竭, 自发性腹膜炎 and 黄疸. Because diagnoses has no independent time field, the linked encounter time is only a timing proxy and same-encounter ambiguity remains in an audit.

Time zero is the earliest qualifying procedures.开始时间; retain procedures.结束时间 and procedures.手术来源 for audit only. Do not infer dose, embolized territory, intensity or treatment response.

For each eligible index:

1. D_D is the first distinct post-index encounter whose encounters.入院时间 is in index days 8–90 and whose linked diagnoses.诊断名称 has a frozen high-specificity component. It must be a post-discharge encounter under the unchanged primary definition; missing discharge is its own ascertainment stratum.
2. D_I is the first distinct post-index encounter with encounters.入院时间 in index days 8–90 and the same component, regardless of observable discharge. Its time is encounter admission minus procedure-start time.
3. U_T is a candidate component attached only to the continued index encounter or lacking a distinct post-index encounter anchor. It is not assigned an invented date, silently promoted to an event, or interpreted as death.

Report composite, ascites, encephalopathy, bleeding, renal/hepatic failure and jaundice components separately. Any admission and repeat TACE remain secondary process outcomes. There is no mortality linkage and no independent clinical-document timestamp, so no mortality, hospice, terminal competing risk or death date may be inferred. A terminal label can be collected by clinicians only as a separately adjudicated, date-qualified fact; until then it is unavailable.

Baseline is the closest assay-specific numeric labs.定量结果 in [-14,0] days; [-30,0] is sensitivity. Dynamic observations use raw labs.检验时间 in [0,7]. Preserve labs.检验, labs.定性结果, labs.定量结果, labs.标本类型 and timestamps. There is no lab-unit column: no raw cross-assay threshold, ALBI, MELD, Child-Pugh, or other unit-dependent score may be claimed unless a clinician separately verifies units.

## New endpoint-validity experiment

Before looking at fitted test predictions, draw an adjudication sample from all eligible test records, stratified by:

- D_D, D_I-only, U_T, and no computable event;
- diagnosis-only, document-confirmed, discordant and missing-document status;
- discharge missingness, an early day 0–7 acute-care encounter, calendar band, index department and assay regime;
- positive/negative components, repeat TACE and observation-intensity strata.

The packet contains the index procedure and encounter context; index and follow-up encounter admission/discharge fields; raw diagnosis names/types; the relevant clinical-document fields; raw labs with assay names, sample types, qualitative/numeric results and 检验时间; and bounded medications, examinations and orders used to describe care intensity. It contains no model score, predicted risk, selected threshold or post hoc stratum label visible to reviewers. Reviewers are blinded to model and baseline-versus-trajectory status.

Two clinicians independently label each packet, with a third adjudicator resolving disagreement. The label set is: definite new/worsening decompensation; probable but date-uncertain decompensation; pre-existing disease; isolated TACE injury/post-embolization syndrome; competing illness or HCC progression; planned/unclear status; no support; text insufficient; and terminal-event status/date only if evidence and a linked encounter date support it. Planned/unplanned is not available in the source and remains unknown unless the packet supplies explicit clinical evidence; it must not be inferred from admission or order fields.

For each computable endpoint, report blinded inter-rater agreement, adjudication agreement, component-specific positive predictive value and negative agreement, timing-uncertain fraction, document/diagnosis discordance and regime-specific validity. A date-uncertain label is not used to manufacture D_D or D_I. If the packet cannot establish new/worsening status or a linked date, the result is an explicit validity limitation, not a negative outcome. This is a validation sample and cannot turn a diagnosis code into a population-wide clinical gold standard.

Endpoint-validity support requires an adjudication report with acceptable expert agreement and no material, unexplained concentration of coding errors in a regime used for the transportability claim. The exact clinical acceptability judgment belongs to the blinded clinicians; an automated verifier can check sampling, blinding, label completeness and calculations but cannot certify clinical truth. If adjudication is not performed, the solver may report computable-code performance only and must defer all clinical-validity and clinical-utility language.

## Regime-held-out transportability experiment

Freeze all regime definitions and the chronology before outcome inspection.

Calendar split: train indices 2010-07-27–2018-12-31, validation 2019-01-01–2021-12-31, and untouched test 2022-01-01–2025-10-03, recomputed from the verified source maximum if necessary. Report the full test and two predeclared test calendar bands (2022–2023 and 2024–2025-10-03) without tuning on either. No patient crosses a split.

Department regime: raw index encounters.就诊科室, with a missing category. Assay regime: exact train-observed pair (labs.检验, labs.标本类型) among the predeclared candidate panel (bilirubin, albumin, platelets, PT/INR or PT ratio, creatinine, sodium, AST and ALT, plus AFP only if present), with an explicit unseen-in-train category. A name/sample-type regime is an observation regime, not proof that two assays measure the same analyte. Numeric values are parsed and standardized within train-fitted regime dictionaries; no unit conversion is invented. Report all nonempty strata and their support; do not drop inconvenient regimes.

The primary transportability output is the paired held-out difference between baseline-only and trajectory models for D_D: Brier score, calibration intercept/slope, calibration plot, discrimination and exploratory net benefit, globally and by calendar, department and assay regime. D_I supplies index-anchored survival sensitivity: cause-specific risk at 30/60/90 days, time-dependent discrimination, IPCW Brier/integrated Brier, calibration and weight diagnostics. It does not replace the primary D_D comparison.

Predeclare a transportability decision rule:

- Supportive: the trajectory increment has the same favorable direction in the global untouched test and every regime with prespecified adequate support (at least 100 patients and 20 adjudication-independent computable events where applicable), calibration does not materially deteriorate in a regime, and no single observation-count/process model explains the gain. The adjudication packet does not show a regime-specific endpoint failure that changes the interpretation.
- Adverse/falsifying: the gain reverses with a bootstrap interval excluding zero in an adequately supported calendar, department or assay regime; or the apparent gain disappears after endpoint discordance review and observation-only controls; or calibration is confined to a discharge/early-care regime while the index-anchored sensitivity loses the direction. This falsifies the internal transportability claim, not necessarily every local prognostic association.
- Inconclusive: sparse events, insufficient common support, unstable censoring weights, convergence failure, unresolved assay units, large timing-uncertain or text-insufficient fractions, or adjudication disagreement that prevents a clinical endpoint interpretation. An imprecise null is not refutation.

If some regimes are underpowered, report them as unresolved rather than averaging them away. A favorable global number cannot override an adverse well-supported regime. Conversely, a noisy small-stratum result does not refute the claim. This is descriptive/prognostic transportability, not causal transportability.

## Matched simple baseline and substantive learned/mechanistic alternative

### B0/B1 simple baseline

Fit an L2-regularized logistic model for primary D_D.

- B0 uses only time-zero inputs: age, sex, index department, HCC/cirrhosis/portal-vein-thrombus/prior-decompensation flags, procedure context, pre-index utilization, assay-specific baseline values and baseline missingness.
- B1 adds fixed, transparent [0,7] summaries for exactly the same candidate assay inputs: baseline, last observed value, change from baseline, within-window min/max, observation count, last-observation day and missingness. Each numeric summary is assay/name/sample-type-specific; no cross-unit pool is allowed. B1 is the matched baseline-plus-trajectory comparator for the primary estimand.

Use train-only preprocessing, penalties and any feature dictionary; validation tunes them; test is untouched. Fit the same B0/B1 inputs in a regularized cause-specific survival form for D_I as a sensitivity. The baseline is clinically auditable and exposes whether any apparent value is only a missingness or observation-count signal.

### SS-Obs learned/mechanistic alternative

Fit a two-factor irregular-time state-space model using the same B0 baseline variables and the same raw [0,7] assay-specific observations as B1: a slowly varying reserve representation and a transient injury representation, each with train-fitted assay-regime measurement error, irregular timestamps, missingness indicators and partial pooling. A day-7 posterior-state head predicts D_D; a cause-specific hazard head predicts D_I through days 8–90. Separate observation heads model lab-observation counts/timing and early-care encounters, but cannot use data after day 7 or endpoint text. The alternative is substantive because it tests whether ordered, irregular observations separate persistent coordinated change from transient injury and observation intensity; B1 loses that temporal/state decomposition.

Compare B0, B1 and SS-Obs on the same chronological test patients, with identical primary outcome and input availability. Report paired test differences, calibration, discrimination, Brier score, state uncertainty, convergence and regime contrasts. Use patient-level bootstrap (2,000 replicates or a bounded prespecified equivalent) for global and supported-stratum uncertainty; use stratified bootstrap summaries where event support permits. The verifier must check that no post-day-7 lab, encounter, discharge, diagnosis/document text or later utilization enters a feature.

A neural sequence model is not chosen now. The question is whether observation-aware state separation and regime stability explain the trajectory signal, not whether a larger predictor wins a small score margin. Revisit a neural sequence model only if SS-Obs and B1 show stable residual ordering information on an independent temporal test, endpoint validity is acceptable, and a new proposal specifies what ordering question the neural model can answer. Otherwise defer it.

## Falsification and observation controls

Predeclare and run:

1. Within-patient permutation of lab timestamps, preserving values and observation counts.
2. A matched pre-index pseudo-trajectory with the same summaries and model class.
3. Counts/lags/departments/calendar-only models without lab values.
4. Models of discharge lag and early acute care as process outcomes.
5. AST/ALT-only, reserve-panel-only and combined blocks.
6. Any-admission and repeat-TACE outcomes as secondary process checks.
7. Calibration and rank-order contrasts by missing-discharge and early-care strata.
8. Document/diagnosis concordance and adjudication-stratum contrasts.
9. Leakage audit covering post-day-7 labs, encounter, discharge, endpoint text, repeat procedures and later utilization.

A supportive result means B1 and/or SS-Obs improves untouched D_D, SS-Obs adds interpretable state/observation information beyond B1, D_I is directionally compatible, regime calibration is not confined to discharge or early-care strata, counts-only and timestamp/pre-index controls are weak, and endpoint review does not show regime-specific invalidity. It remains an observed-data prognostic regularity.

An adverse result means the gain is only a care-intensity proxy, reproduces under timestamp permutation or pre-index pseudo-trajectories, reverses in a supported regime, is lost under index anchoring, or fails blinded endpoint review. The next decision is to narrow to a discharge-conditioned coding/observation association or abandon the trajectory direction after adequate precision; no treatment recommendation follows.

## Exploratory decision relevance, not a treatment recommendation

Only after the endpoint adjudication packet is complete, plot decision curves for B0, B1 and SS-Obs on D_D across a prespecified mathematical risk-probability grid and by supported regime, alongside treat-none and treat-all reference curves. Do not select a cutoff, claim a monitoring benefit, or recommend treatment. Repeat only as a sensitivity for adjudication-supported labels if the clinicians establish a usable event/date definition; with unresolved validity, label DCA non-actionable and defer it.

The concrete clinical deliverable is a go/no-go package for a future monitoring-and-adjudication study: regime-specific held-out predictions and calibration, an endpoint-validity packet with expert labels and disagreement, observation-process diagnostics, and an exploratory DCA showing where a prospectively tested monitoring trigger might be worth evaluating. The package can justify continuing to a prospective adjudication/monitoring design, revising the endpoint or assay registry, deferring for missing units or sparse regimes, or abandoning the trajectory direction. It cannot justify changing care in this retrospective release.

Freeze the primary component list and all preprocessing before viewing test outcomes. Report cohort flow, duplicate-key audit, availability strata, event counts, discharge/early-care strata, assay regimes, common support, censoring/weight diagnostics, convergence, state uncertainty and paired confidence intervals. All model and DCA outputs must be linked to saved held-out predictions and a manifest of feature availability.

Computationally checkable: source hashes and headers, joins, time windows, cohort flow, split integrity, leakage, regime definitions, fitted predictions, Brier/calibration/discrimination, process controls, bootstrap calculations, DCA arithmetic, adjudication sampling/blinding metadata and result linkage. Requires clinical experts or another study: truth of new/worsening decompensation, planned status, assay units, competing illness, terminal events/death/hospice, mechanism, causal effect, external transportability, prospective monitoring benefit and any action threshold.

## Alternative-method record and compute

The simple alternative is B0/B1 logistic plus cause-specific survival: exact baseline and trajectory summary inputs above; fit on train, tune on validation, predict the chronological test; evaluate paired Brier, calibration, discrimination, survival metrics, regime heterogeneity, bootstrap uncertainty and DCA. It is CPU-feasible and selected as the transparent decision comparator.

The substantive alternative is SS-Obs: same raw inputs and split; fit the reserve/injury state evolution, observation model and D_D/D_I heads; evaluate the same held-out outputs plus latent-state uncertainty and observation-process separation. Its added information is irregular ordering and partial pooling, which B1 discards. It is selected because it directly tests the observation/timing rival, not because it is complex.

A neural sequence model and any causal treatment model are deferred: the available release cannot identify treatment effect, mortality, unit equivalence or clinical mechanisms, and a larger predictor would not repair those gaps. Revisit only with stable held-out residual ordering, acceptable endpoint adjudication and a specified new scientific target. Evidence against revisiting includes a null or unstable SS-Obs/B1 comparison, regime-specific reversal, endpoint invalidity, or unresolved assay units.

The discovery episode performed no fitting. Future planning estimate, not measured execution: 4–8 CPU cores and under 32 GiB for selected-column parsing, ledgers and B0/B1; approximately 16 CPU cores and 64–128 GiB for SS-Obs and bounded bootstrap, up to about 8 hours. CPU is selected because the proposed state dimension and tabular inputs are low-dimensional; an A100 is not scientifically necessary. The hardware inventory has A100-SXM4-80GB devices, but ordinary shell CUDA visibility is intentionally empty and no GPU probe was needed. If an implementation benchmark demonstrates matrix-bound repeated state updates, a separate one-GPU job may use only allocated cuda:0; that would be a measured infrastructure diagnostic, not evidence for the hypothesis.
