# Independent, source-specific triangulation of context-selective MerTK harm

Status: substantive successor of candidate-e2c88fac21f4420df13909b9. Planned Harbor experiment only; no screening or scientific result has been executed.

## Opening and hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports a broad starting claim: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission/repair and MerTK perturbation has been associated with increased FLS inflammatory transcripts [K1]. It does not establish that inhibitor harm is larger in MerTK/CD206-positive than MerTK/CD206-negative context, or that the observation transfers to an independently designed paired perturbation assay.

Primary hypothesis: in E-MTAB-8873 type-B synovial-cell cocultures, exact macrophage MerTK-inhibitor exposure produces a larger FLS harm response in MerTK/CD206pos than MerTK/CD206neg coculture after accounting for contributing FLS and macrophage memberships. Secondary triangulation hypothesis: within E-MTAB-8316, paired UNC106238 response in synovial monocyte preparations is directionally compatible with the primary perturbation response when summarized with a frozen verified gene map and nested donor-aware units. The secondary is not a claim that E-MTAB-8316 contains Mpos/Mneg contexts or FLS coculture harm.

The strongest rivals are generic inflammatory/stress signaling or composition, and timing/protocol mismatch. They predict similar perturbation direction in LPS controls, FLS-only samples, or all macrophage contexts; and they predict that any E-MTAB-8316 disagreement could reflect its different compound, monocyte label and absent time field. [K2] makes the macrophage-state rival consequential; [K3] shows why heterogeneous, niche-linked FLS programs must not be reduced to one transcript. The advance over [K1] is a prespecified identifiability gate plus a directional source-specific transfer check, not pooled external validation.

## Data bindings and population

All source files are read-only. Prepared matrices and designs are analysis tables; archive members are provenance, not extra observations.

Primary E-MTAB-8873:

- Matrix: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f. Verified header has 33 sample columns and 445 feature rows. Measured rows include MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end, SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end, IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end, IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end, MMP12|NM_002426.5|Reference_end, MMP13|NM_002427.3|Reference_end and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end.
- Design: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json, SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4. Fields are sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata and cells. Join only design.sample_id to counts header. Comma-separated donor memberships are dependence annotations, not independent donors.
- Registry: [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab1bd1a31c77b7f70f. It records 33 samples, 445 measured features, no verified single donors and disables ordinary donor t-tests.
- Provenance: E-MTAB-8873/E-MTAB-8873.sdrf.txt and registered R1, R2 and R5 R*_SA*_..._RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz members listed in configured metadata.

Eligible rows have tissue=synovial membrane, cell_type=type B synovial cell and documented coculture. Context is the design label co-cultured with MerTK/CD206pos macrophages versus co-cultured with MerTK/CD206neg macrophages. Exact primary treatment is macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor. Exact treated rows are R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor, R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor and R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos_Inhibitor. The last has no unambiguous untreated counterpart. R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor and R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor remain a separate tier and are not silently pooled. R1_SA256A_FLS_SA260R_Mpos has conflicting donor metadata and is sensitivity-only. Mixed-composition, not-cocultured and six FLS-only rows are controls or descriptive strata. There is no clinical time field.

Secondary E-MTAB-8316 is source-specific and is never joined to E-MTAB-8873:

- Matrix: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645. It has 12 sample columns and 58,302 Ensembl-indexed feature rows; header IDs are MK11, MK12, MK15, MK16, MK19, MK20, MK23, MK24, MK3, MK4, MK7 and MK8.
- Design: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.design.json, SHA-256 ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81. Fields are sample_id, donor_id, other_donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata and unit_definition. Labels are verified none versus UNC106238; no time field and no Mpos/Mneg label. Unit definition is FLS donor cluster; monocyte donors nested and balanced across compound conditions.
- Registry: same assay-registry path; it records 12 samples, 58,302 features, independent donors not assumed, verified single donors SA049, SA051, SA104 and SA114, four FLS donor clusters and six nested monocyte donors.
- Provenance: E-MTAB-8316/MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz and E-MTAB-8316/E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt, source hashes 510b69e449ed424adfbf225b8eeaf9faff1f8a973c76951612caf7ae69103228 and 3e304fc612102181c9106532d42b010554f342b8529f6542c04169e50093ce74.

The six verified within-source pairs are MK11/MK12 (SA114, other_donor_id 1533), MK15/MK16 (SA114, 1534), MK19/MK20 (SA051, 1601), MK23/MK24 (SA104, 1602), MK3/MK4 (SA049, 1462), and MK7/MK8 (SA049, 1463), first none and second UNC106238. No identifier, donor, specimen or row may be joined across assays. E-MTAB-8316 cells are monocyte; FLS donor cluster is a nesting unit, not evidence that its readout is FLS harm.

The feature-header inspection found no rows named MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, SPP1, IL1B, IL6, MMP1, MMP3, MMP12, MMP13, MMP14, TNF or CXCL8 in E-MTAB-8316. It is Ensembl-only. A target-module claim is gated on a named frozen Ensembl-to-transcript map and protocol reconciliation. If absent, secondary status is mapping_blocked, not zero.

## Estimands, baseline and identifiability

Normalize each prepared matrix independently to log2(CPM + pseudocount), preserve identifiers and do not impute absent genes. Emit a manifest with source, sample ID, treatment tier, context, round, FLS membership, macrophage membership, nested donor unit, mapping status and exclusions.

Primary harm score H is the mean of feature-standardized IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14, standardized using eligible untreated coculture references only. Secondary outcomes are IL1B, MMP12 and MMP13 plus each component. MERTK, MRC1, TREM2 and SPP1 are a descriptive context panel, not proof of target engagement.

Primary estimand:
Delta = [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mpos) - E(H | untreated, Mpos)] - [E(H | exact inhibitor, Mneg) - E(H | untreated, Mneg)].

First report the rank/overlap gate: exposure-by-context cells, matched counterpart availability, FLS/macrophage membership incidence overlap, and whether Delta is estimable without the ambiguous untreated row or preInhibitor tier. Only the R1 SA256A/SA259A Mneg and Mpos pairs provide complete same-membership exact comparisons; one Mneg treated cluster and conflicting Mpos metadata mean a population-level interaction may be non-identifiable. Failure returns inconclusive, not zero.

Transparent baseline: construct within matched same-membership H differences, then fit a small fixed-effects model with context, exact exposure and interaction, adding assay round only when rank permits. Represent every FLS and macrophage donor as a membership incidence matrix. Use crossed random effects or penalized membership effects only after documenting rank. Report effects, intervals, component effects, donor-membership bootstrap, leave-one-round-out, leave-one-membership-out and admissible mapping sensitivities. Donor t-tests, cell counts as replication, random row splits, confounded age/sex adjustment and pooling exact/preInhibitor are prohibited.

Secondary estimand is not pooled with Delta. Conditional on the annotation gate, compute within-source log-expression differences for the six none/UNC106238 pairs, average repeated context measurements within each verified donor/condition as the registry directs, retain four FLS-cluster and six nested-monocyte strata, and fit a paired donor-aware response summary with no twelve-independent-donor claim. Compare direction and module coherence only. Without the map, output secondary_mapping_blocked.json with the missing dependency and stop that branch.

## Same-input alternative and compute

The substantive alternative uses the same E-MTAB-8873 matrix, manifest, rows and outcomes: a cross-classified multivariate partial-pooling model with feature-specific intercepts, exposure, context, exposure-by-context, round and crossed FLS/macrophage membership effects. A shared latent FLS-harm factor loads IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14; MERTK/MRC1/TREM2 form a descriptive context factor; SPP1 and IL1B remain an inflammatory contrast. Its target is the distribution of the same Delta, context effects, loading coherence and probability that Delta exceeds a material threshold, not predictive accuracy. Compare sign, uncertainty width, marker coherence and membership/mapping stability. The baseline loses correlated-program information; the alternative can reveal a coherent multi-marker program or appropriately widen uncertainty.

Fit only after the primary rank gate; otherwise record alternative_deferred. A conditional E-MTAB-8316 alternative, only after an Ensembl map, is a low-dimensional paired latent perturbation score within source, not a pooled meta-analysis. Held-out unit is assay round or donor-membership cluster for stability diagnostics, not external validation. Planned future cost is 4–8 CPU cores, less than 16 GiB RAM and minutes for the 33-by-11 primary target table plus a 12-sample secondary check; this is an estimate, not a measured runtime. GPU is deferred because design identifiability, not scale, limits the study. Neural prediction, ordinary t-tests, pooling the two compounds, E-MTAB-8322 scoring without its missing map and GSE95588 validation with unresolved mapping are deferred.

## Falsification and interpretation

Fix material threshold delta=0.5 SD of H before fitting. Supportive primary evidence requires positive Delta with uncertainty supporting Delta > delta (or posterior probability at least 0.90), coherent components, stable sign across mapping and membership/round holdouts, and no selective mimicry in LPS or FLS-only controls. A gated E-MTAB-8316 result is directionally concordant only if its mapped target/module response has the prespecified compatible sign across donor strata; it cannot rescue a failed primary rank gate.

Adverse evidence is nonpositive Delta, Mneg harm at least as large, generic LPS/FLS-only mimicry, or clearly discordant gated secondary direction. This weakens context-selective prioritization and favors generic inflammation, composition or timing.

Inconclusive evidence includes rank/overlap failure, missing Ensembl map, unreconciled secondary protocol/labels, uncertainty spanning zero or delta, sign changes across mappings, one cluster driving the effect, exact/preInhibitor disagreement or a non-identifiable alternative. Next test: balanced matched Mpos/Mneg perturbation across multiple FLS/macrophage donor pairs with dose, time, viability, MerTK protein/phosphorylation, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS invasion or matrix-degradation readouts.

Harbor can check source joins, feature selection, paired units, estimand arithmetic, rank reports, mapping gates, uncertainty and conclusion compliance. It cannot establish direct mechanism, viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window, patient selection, clinical benefit or independent biological validity. Those require expert review, orthogonal agonism/genetic loss-of-function, protein/functional assays and an independent cohort. Clinical outcomes, medication response, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, viability, dose-response and longitudinal time course are unavailable.

## Completion deliverable and references

The deliverable is newly fitted primary Delta and context-specific effects with uncertainty, rank/overlap report, exposure-tier and LPS/FLS-only controls, donor/mapping sensitivity, fitted-or-deferred alternative, and separate E-MTAB-8316 status concordant, discordant or mapping_blocked. Required outputs are effects.csv, controls.csv, sensitivity.csv, analysis_manifest.json, results.json and, when needed, secondary_mapping_blocked.json. Readiness and a planned analysis are not a result.

[K1] supports MerTK-positive resolution/repair and inhibitor-associated FLS-response evidence; this proposal adds the state-by-perturbation estimand and transferability gate. [K2] supplies the inflammatory macrophage/HBEGF rival; this proposal uses generic controls and refuses to call a generic response MerTK-selective. [K3] bounds the FLS endpoint by showing heterogeneity and niche-linked states; this proposal requires a multi-marker score and does not infer mechanism from one gene.

The exact parent key-reference receipts and three inherited work excerpts are preserved in the support package. Local files are concise UTF-8 evidence notes; no unavailable full text or supplementary methods are claimed.

# Source-local benefit–harm gate for context-selective MerTK prioritization

Status: substantive successor of `candidate-f5f1c5b4afb7ffad9717f432`; planned Harbor experiment only. No screening or scientific fitting has been executed. “Observed” below means registry, schema and source-file inspection, not biological results.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and decision

The three inspected works establish a bounded prior, not the proposed conclusion. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce fibroblast repair [K1]. An inflammatory macrophage state can drive fibroblast invasiveness through tissue cross-talk [K2]. Fibroblast inflammatory programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked [K3]. The unresolved decision is whether the configured data can support a next-stage target-prioritization decision that weighs a remission-associated macrophage benefit proxy against MerTK-perturbation FLS harm.

Falsifiable hypothesis:

> A state-stratified MerTK follow-up is justified only if two source-local findings jointly pass independent identifiability gates: (1) E-MTAB-8322 remission macrophages have a stable, preregistered MerTK-associated benefit proxy above the naive/resistant reference; and (2) the exact E-MTAB-8873 MerTK-inhibitor interaction remains materially harmful in the Mpos context relative to Mneg after membership-aware controls and sensitivities. If either axis fails, these data do not support a context-selective MerTK strategy.

This is a conjunctive advancement gate, not a patient-level net-benefit estimand. The sources have no shared donor, perturbation, time field, cell composition, endpoint or verified common biological unit. No `benefit - harm` arithmetic, cross-source pooling or donor-ID matching is allowed.

The clinically important decision is whether to invest in state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation, balanced loss-of-function and orthogonal functional assays, or abandon selective MerTK reasoning in favor of generic inflammation/composition explanations. Supportive results justify follow-up only; they do not establish clinical efficacy, direct target engagement, a therapeutic window or a patient-selection rule.

## Evidence, leading explanation and rivals

[K1] supports remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophages and fibroblast repair, but not the configured benefit proxy, inhibitor interaction or clinical efficacy. [K2] is the consequential rival: inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast cross-talk could explain FLS harm without MerTK selectivity. [K3] limits any four-transcript FLS harm score because fibroblast programs are niche-linked and heterogeneous.

The leading explanation is that a remission-associated MerTK program identifies a protective macrophage context whose perturbation exposes FLS harm. Plausible alternatives are:

- Disease-state selection, treatment history, cell composition, capture depth or donor biology may generate the 8322 state score without protective MerTK biology.
- Generic stress, LPS response, assay round, composition, exposure tier or FLS baseline may generate the 8873 interaction; HBEGF-like cross-talk is a substantive rival [K2].
- The targeted FLS panel may miss invasion, matrix degradation, viability and other niche-specific functions [K3].
- Concordant source-local axes would remain descriptive and non-causal; they cannot establish direct MerTK action or a shared patient-level benefit-harm effect.

## Exact data bindings and observed availability

The full catalog is `[private-path]/catalog.json`, catalog SHA-256 `162ddf0148975035ee641ae75a2666bf44a7b458b050d79370ee9f550953312f`. Snapshot: `core-molecular-20261003`. The read-only registry is `[private-path]/assay-registry.json`, SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`.

### E-MTAB-8322: benefit proxy

Inputs and joins:

- Counts: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz`; 27 sample-ID columns and 33,694 Ensembl feature rows.
- Design: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json`; join only `design.sample_id = counts` header ID. Required fields: `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_name`, `source_metadata`, `cells`.
- Repository: `[private-path]/repository.json`, SHA-256 `a9ef0d1103b3afd790db0dee089e62e03dbde4b1b8e889625f09c94dbdb160f3`; source SDRF `E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt`, SHA-256 `b87005a9eefff1beb2d12de2e9f945e2a0b6330aa59207f61f0ecaba180fa237`.
- Source feature map: `[private-path]/SA220.genes.tsv`, SHA-256 `920b9e836ae82aeabe5b95932ac8a7795c6f03decff45381749e1e3cdad1f1fa`. It explicitly maps MERTK `ENSG00000153208`, MRC1 `ENSG00000260314`, TREM2 `ENSG00000095970`, C1QA/B/C `ENSG00000173372/ENSG00000173369/ENSG00000159189`, APOE `ENSG00000130203`, SPP1 `ENSG00000118785`, HBEGF `ENSG00000113070`, IL1B `ENSG00000125538`, IL6 `ENSG00000136244`, and MMP1/3/12/13/14 `ENSG00000196611/ENSG00000149968/ENSG00000262406/ENSG00000137745/ENSG00000157227`. ## Baseline versus substantive alternative

Both methods use the same exact source-local inputs, targets, split and uncertainty criteria.

The transparent baseline computes fixed `B) and its state contrasts in 8322, and the parent’s paired score/interaction model for `Delta) in 8873 using the incidence matrix only when rank permits. It reports component effects, controls, exact versus preInhibitor tiers, leave-round-out and leave-membership-out results. Its advantage is auditable behavior under sparse designs; it loses correlated marker structure and uncertainty sharing.

The substantive alternative is a source-stratified multivariate/mechanistic model. In 8322, fit the same seven benefit transcripts with a shared latent macrophage-state factor, gene-specific loadings, state effects and donor-level residual covariance. In 8873, fit the same 11 measured target/context/harm transcripts with feature-specific exposure/context/interaction effects, crossed FLS/macrophage membership terms and a shared harm factor. It must output the same `B) contrasts and `Delta), components, controls and uncertainty—not a surrogate prediction. The alternative can reveal whether each signal is a coherent program or a one-marker artifact; it cannot establish direct mechanism. If either source gate fails, defer that multivariate fit and report why.

The fixed split is generated once from frozen IDs: five-fold donor/sample holdout stratified by state in 8322 and by admissible membership cluster/round in 8873, reused by both methods. In 8322, this is a stability diagnostic because groups are small, not external validation. Fit any learned loadings or nuisance adjustments inside training folds; evaluate held-out contrasts/rank stability. Primary uncertainty is a cluster bootstrap over 8322 donor IDs and 8873 contributing membership clusters, with bounded sign/permutation and leave-cluster-out sensitivity. Cells and matrix entries are never replicates.

CPU is selected: planned future solver use is 4–8 cores, <16 GiB and minutes for 19 samples/33 samples and 7/11 features; this is an estimate, not measured runtime. GPU is deferred because the bottleneck is identifiability, not matrix scale. A neural predictor is not selected because predictive gain would not distinguish donor/composition selection from MerTK biology or answer the target decision.

## Falsification and interpretation

Freeze a material threshold of 0.5 SD of `B) and 0.5 SD of `H) before fitting. These are within-source thresholds and must not be subtracted.

Supportive requires the 8322 feature/state gate to pass, remission `B) contrast above its threshold with uncertainty supporting it, stable held-out/leave-donor signs and no single marker/donor driving it; the 8873 exact gate to pass, `Delta) above its threshold with uncertainty supporting it, coherent components and stable admissible sensitivities; and no Mpos-selective LPS/FLS-only mimicry. This supports orthogonal MerTK perturbation, protein/phospho-MerTK, viability, efferocytosis, secreted mediators and direct FLS invasion/matrix-degradation testing, not clinical efficacy.

Adverse means the 8322 proxy is nonpositive/unstable, the 8873 `Delta) is nonpositive or at least as large in Mneg, a control reproduces selectivity, or the multivariate model reveals a single-marker/membership artifact. This favors generic inflammation, composition, treatment history or assay-specific explanations.

Inconclusive means a feature, state, rank, overlap or holdout gate fails; uncertainty spans zero or threshold; an admissible mapping/tier changes sign; one cluster drives the result; or state selection cannot be separated from protective biology. Do not interpret an imprecise null as refutation. The next study needs balanced matched Mpos/Mneg FLS–macrophage donors, dose/exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, spatial localization and direct FLS functional endpoints.

Harbor can check joins, exact feature presence, state counts, rank, split reproducibility, uncertainty, controls and conclusion-to-output linkage. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct mechanism, viability, spatial localization, therapeutic window or biological validity of labels without expert review and another study.

## Actual scientific deliverable and evidence limits

Completion requires newly fitted source-specific outputs:

- `benefit_effects.csv`: 8322 score contrasts, components, donor counts and uncertainty;
- `harm_effects.csv`: 8873 `Delta), components and membership-aware uncertainty;
- `controls.csv`, `holdout_sensitivity.csv`, `source_compatibility.json`, `method_comparison.json` and `results.json`, with every conclusion linked to computed rows and a supportive/adverse/inconclusive rule.

The benefit axis is only a remission-associated macrophage expression proxy. 8322 lacks FLS, perturbation, dose, time, protein, spatial and functional repair measures. 8873 lacks clinical outcomes, dose-response, exposure time, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, spatial localization, direct FLS invasion/matrix degradation and an independent balanced validation cohort. The three works are abstract-level inspected excerpts; no unavailable full text or supplementary methods is claimed. Screening remains planned.

## Alternatives and selection record

The fixed-score baseline is primary because its signs and missingness are transparent under the sparse interaction and small atlas strata. The multivariate model is retained because it can expose program coherence and uncertainty sharing that a score loses; it is not a complexity bonus and is deferred on failed gates. A neural/high-dimensional predictor is not selected because it targets prediction rather than the scientific advancement decision and risks donor/composition leakage. The inherited E-MTAB-8316 branch is deferred: its six source-local none/UNC106238 pairs are monocyte measurements with no Mpos/Mneg field and no configured feature map, so they cannot repair the missing common benefit-harm estimand.

## Key references

[K1] establishes the remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophage and repair prior; this proposal adds a bounded E-MTAB-8322 benefit proxy and keeps it separate from 8873 harm.

[K2] supplies the inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast rival; this proposal uses control and component falsification rather than treating MerTK expression as mechanism.

[K3] bounds the FLS harm endpoint as heterogeneous and niche-linked; this proposal reports components and refuses to call 8322 an FLS validation cohort.

Attached are exactly three distinct inspected works: `key-references.json`, `evidence-K1-alivernini-2020.txt`, `evidence-K2-kuo-2019.txt` and `evidence-K3-korsunsky-2022.txt`.

# A benefit-axis identifiability gate for context-selective MerTK perturbation

Status: substantive evolution of `candidate-f5f1c5b4afb7ffad9717f432`; planned Harbor experiment only. No molecular screening, model fitting, or scientific result has been executed in this episode.

## Scientific opening, supported claim, and unresolved claim

The inspected evidence supports a bounded biological prior: MerTK-positive/TREM2-high or LYVE1-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with rheumatoid-arthritis remission and can induce synovial-fibroblast repair [K1]. A distinct HBEGF-positive inflammatory macrophage state can promote fibroblast invasiveness through tissue cross-talk [K2]. Fibroblast inflammatory programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked [K3]. These observations motivate target prioritization, but they do not show that inhibiting MerTK selectively harms the resolution-like context, nor that the same context carries a measurable clinical benefit in the configured assays.

The parent made the harm estimand explicit: in E-MTAB-8873, exact MerTK-inhibitor exposure might increase an FLS inflammatory harm program more in the unambiguous MerTK/CD206-positive than in the negative coculture. Its consequential limitation is that this is harm-only. A target can have a selective harm signal without a demonstrated benefit axis, and the available remission/resistant atlas might be mistaken for an external validation if incompatible units are forced together.

The smallest scientifically meaningful evolution is therefore not to add an arbitrary net-benefit score. It is to add a prespecified benefit-axis identifiability gate:

> Exact MerTK-inhibitor exposure has a larger FLS inflammatory harm effect in the eligible Mpos than Mneg coculture, but a MerTK-specific benefit-versus-harm prioritization is supportable only if an independently fitted remission-versus-resistant macrophage state axis is reproducible under donor holdout, has a verified target annotation, and can be linked to the measured Mpos/Mneg context without cross-assay donor or unit substitution.

The executable primary hypothesis is the narrowed harm claim. The benefit clause is a falsifiable gate and a required decision condition, not an established conclusion. With the currently frozen files, the benefit gate is expected to be blocked by feature namespace and context incompatibility; that is a planned identifiability outcome, not a screening result.

Clinical importance: deciding whether to preserve or activate MerTK-like resolution states requires evidence that perturbation harm is context-selective and that the selected context is clinically relevant. A supportive harm result alone justifies orthogonal target-engagement and functional experiments; it does not justify a patient-selection rule, treatment, direct mechanism, or clinical benefit claim. A benefit gate that remains blocked prevents over-prioritizing a target on a one-sided expression endpoint.

The source lineage is `GSE95588/GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz` (`334255c7635fecc72d50e57adcfd242c938970442a85aae80339ef7519a3aa46`), `GSE95588/GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz` (`285d27bcd669004c575479722ab229e9cca7ec4ef30302fabb632a339edd741e`), `samples.soft` (`d003ec183a255f8a01f9ced519f1aabfc5e454f84b880a951a1f4db2fb4719c5`), and `series.soft` (`1de3446c18ec7fcacc47cc7cb74a56fb166233ed07866a940c5544f9e0f2674a`). The registry also states that the coculture r1/r2 material includes earlier GSE57723 data and cannot be counted as independent validation of that study. The source metadata describes one-day TNF exposure, but there is no verified donor/time field in the prepared design; no longitudinal inference is permitted.

GSE95588 is used only for descriptive concordance and negative-control planning after a GSM/donor gate. It cannot repair the 8873 rank deficiency, demonstrate MerTK perturbation, or serve as independent validation. Duplicate/date-like feature labels must be resolved by the frozen feature maps; no guessed correction or row merging is allowed.

## Estimands and identifiability gates

Normalize each source separately to log2(CPM+1), preserving feature IDs and never imputing absent genes.

Primary harm outcome is
`H_s = mean(z(IL6), z(MMP1), z(MMP3), z(MMP14))`,
where z parameters are frozen from eligible unambiguous untreated exact-context co-culture rows. The primary estimand is
`Delta_H = [E(H | exact inhibitor,Mpos)-E(H | untreated,Mpos)] - [E(H | exact inhibitor,Mneg)-E(H | untreated,Mneg)]`.
Report each component, plus MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 and IL1B/MMP12/MMP13 contrasts. This is a descriptive/associational perturbation interaction under a pseudobulk assay, not a clinical or causal treatment effect.

Before fitting, emit `harm_gate.json` with: row counts for each treatment/context cell; exact counterpart availability; donor-membership incidence matrix rank; whether any cell requires mixed, preInhibitor, metadata-conflicted, or random-split rows; and model estimability. The gate fails if it relies on ambiguous mixed rows, preInhibitor rows, the conflicted SA260R untreated row, random row split, or independent-donor assumptions. With the verified design, only one same-membership R1 pair supplies all four exact cells, so a population-level interaction is not automatically identified. Rank failure or a non-estimable interaction returns inconclusive, never a zero.

The secondary atlas estimand is a source-local remission-versus-resistant state contrast, not a target effect:
`B_f = mean(log2CPM_f | verified remission donors) - mean(log2CPM_f | verified resistant donors)`,
with uncertainty clustered at donor and with the two related/unresolved SA149 rows excluded. B is a state-association axis, not a treatment benefit or transition effect. The benefit gate requires: (a) the Ensembl feature map is present and frozen; (b) target genes and a prespecified resolution module are actually measured; (c) a donor-holdout model/contrast is stable; and (d) an explicit bridge to the 8873 Mpos/Mneg context is available. Current files fail (a) and (d), so the full benefit-versus-harm estimand is not identified.

For 8316, estimate source-local paired d-vectors only after compound/protocol and feature-map checks. For GSE95588, produce a mapping/feature-quality report and descriptive contrasts only unless donor and GSM identity are independently verified. Neither source is pooled with 8873 or 8322.

## Baseline and substantive alternative

Both alternatives use the same prepared inputs, frozen row filters, normalization, biological-unit definitions, donor/cluster holdouts, and prespecified outcomes.

Simple baseline:

1. On 8873, calculate the paired four-cell `Delta_H` and component contrasts with an incidence-matrix paired-score model. Use membership-cluster bootstrap only when at least two admissible clusters exist; otherwise report the exact contrast, rank, and an honest non-population uncertainty status. Use leave-one-round and leave-one-membership sensitivity only as applicable. This baseline is transparent and auditable, but loses correlated marker structure.
2. On 8322, estimate feature-wise `B_f` and a nearest-centroid remission-versus-resistant score after a training-only variance filter, only if the annotation/measurement gate passes. Fit target is the remission versus resistant label; hold out one verified donor at a time and report held-out balanced accuracy/log loss, donor-bootstrap intervals, and sign stability. This is a feasibility state axis, not a benefit outcome.
3. On 8316, report paired within-cluster d-vectors and on GSE95588 report only gated descriptive contrasts. No donor t-tests, pooled coefficients, or cross-source donor matches.

Substantive alternative:

- On 8873, fit a cross-classified multivariate partial-pooling model to IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 with shared harm factor, feature-specific treatment/context/interaction effects, and FLS/macrophage membership effects represented by an incidence matrix. Retain target/context marker features as contrasts. The fitted target remains `Delta_H`; the alternative asks whether the harm signal is a coherent multivariate program and whether uncertainty widens when membership dependence is respected.
- On 8322, if the feature-map and measurement gates pass, fit a sparse multivariate remission-versus-resistant model (elastic-net logistic or a low-rank factor model selected before fitting) to the same Ensembl matrix. Target is the same remission/resistant label, not drug response. Use leave-one-verified-donor-out validation, donor-cluster bootstrap, held-out log loss/AUROC/balanced accuracy, feature-sign stability, and calibration. The alternative can reveal a correlated state program that nearest-centroid scoring loses; it cannot establish a MerTK mechanism without annotation and context bridge.
- On 8316, a multivariate paired response is secondary and source-local only after the same protocol/feature gates. GSE95588 is not used to rescue a result with unresolved donor mapping.

The alternative is scientifically useful because it tests whether a putative harm or remission state is a coherent biological program rather than a single marker or one row. It is deferred automatically when the relevant gate fails; complexity cannot repair missing units, labels, or features. A neural predictor is not selected: predictive gain would not identify a MerTK interaction or clinical benefit. Revisit a hierarchical cross-assay model only after a named common feature map, same endpoint, verified context, intervention identity, and compatible biological units are obtained.

Approximate future solver resources: CPU only, 4-8 cores and <16 GiB RAM for 8873; 8-16 cores and 16-64 GiB RAM for repeated sparse/low-rank fits on 27 x 33,694 atlas data; approximately minutes for the baseline and 10-60 minutes for donor-held-out alternatives, unmeasured in this episode. GPU is deferred because the limiting issue is identifiability, not matrix scale. This is a planning estimate, not an executed benchmark. The configured planning envelope is 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds; no GPU or screening job is required here.

## Controls, falsification, and interpretation

Controls are fixed before fitting:

- FLS-only untreated/inhibitor rows test whether an apparent signal is a direct FLS or capture effect rather than macrophage-context interaction.
- LPS-pretreated Mpos/Mneg rows test whether generic macrophage activation reproduces the context pattern.
- Mixed-cell-composition rows test composition sensitivity but never define a clean context.
- Exact versus preInhibitor and R1/R2/R5 round/tier comparisons are sensitivity analyses, not pooled replication.
- MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1 and IL1B/MMP12/MMP13 components test coherence and competing inflammatory programs.
- 8316 paired none/UNC106238 and GSE95588 drug/TNF labels are source-local perturbation or timing comparators only; they are not MerTK validation.

Freeze a material harm threshold of 0.5 SD of H before fitting. A harm-supportive result requires positive `Delta_H` above that threshold with uncertainty supporting the threshold, coherent components, stable admissible mapping/round sensitivities, and no matching selective pattern in LPS or FLS-only controls. It supports follow-up with balanced donor pairs, orthogonal MerTK protein/phospho-readouts, genetic perturbation, viability, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, and direct FLS invasion/matrix-degradation assays. It does not establish direct target engagement or clinical benefit.

A full target-prioritization-supportive result additionally requires a non-blocked benefit gate: a reproducible donor-held-out remission-versus-resistant atlas axis, verified annotation including the target, and a separately obtained context bridge. Even then, it supports a next experiment, not a net clinical benefit estimate. Under the current files, the honest expected status is harm result plus benefit-gate blocked/inconclusive.

Adverse evidence includes a nonpositive harm interaction, Mneg harm at least as large as Mpos harm, generic LPS/FLS-only mimicry, instability driven by one membership, or discordance after a valid source-local 8316 gate. This weakens the selective-harm rationale and favors generic inflammation, composition, assay, timing, or off-target explanations. A weak or non-reproducible atlas state axis is adverse to the *benefit* claim but does not refute the harm interaction.

Inconclusive evidence includes rank/overlap failure, dependence on mixed/preInhibitor/conflicted rows, uncertainty spanning zero or the material threshold, unresolved donor/GSM mapping, missing Ensembl annotation, absent Mpos/Mneg bridge, or a cross-source estimand that must be invented. Inconclusive means obtain balanced matched Mpos/Mneg donor pairs with dose, exposure time, viability, target engagement, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, and FLS functional endpoints; it is not evidence for or against a drug.

Harbor can check source-local joins, required feature presence, exact row filters, incidence rank, held-out split integrity, paired contrasts, uncertainty calculations, gate status, and rule-consistent conclusion links. It cannot establish clinical benefit, direct molecular mechanism, spatial localization, viability, therapeutic window, or independent biological validity; these require expert adjudication, missing measurements, orthogonal experiments, or another study.

## Scientific deliverable

Newly fitted or computed outputs must include:

- `analysis_manifest.json`: catalog and input hashes, source-local filters, exact included/excluded rows, and temporal boundaries.
- `harm_gate.json`: cell counts, incidence matrix/rank, estimability, and reasons for any failure.
- `effects.csv`: `Delta_H`, component effects, marker contrasts, and uncertainty status.
- `controls.csv` and `sensitivity.csv`: FLS-only, LPS, mixed-composition, tier, round, and membership checks.
- `atlas_benefit_gate.json`, `atlas_effects.csv`, and `atlas_holdout.csv`: remission/resistant state contrast, map/measurement status, donor-holdout metrics, and explicit blocked status where required.
- `source_compatibility.json`: 8316 and GSE95588 protocol, feature, donor, context, and pooling decisions.
- `method_comparison.json`: baseline versus multivariate alternative, targets, splits, uncertainty, resource timing, and fit/defer reason.
- `results.json`: every conclusion linked to computed output rows and tagged supportive, adverse, or inconclusive.

Completion is not a readiness report. It requires the primary harm estimand or a formal non-identifiability report, the benefit-axis gate result, controls/sensitivities, method comparison, and conclusions that preserve uncertainty. No result is claimed in this proposal.

## Evidence limits and alternatives not selected

Unavailable or inadequate evidence remains explicit: no clinical outcomes, remission transition data, dose-response, exposure-time field in the prepared assays, viability, protein/phospho-MerTK, efferocytosis, secreted mediators, spatial localization, direct FLS invasion/matrix-degradation readout, verified common annotation across all assays, or balanced independent Mpos/Mneg FLS-macrophage cohort.

The atlas extension is retained as a bounded feasibility branch because remission/resistant donor labels are present and can test whether a state axis is reproducible. It is not promoted to a benefit claim because the required feature map and context bridge are absent. GSE95588 is retained as an artifact/timing comparator because its feature maps and rich treatment labels may inform controls, but it is not selected as validation because donor identities are unresolved and coculture r1/r2 includes GSE57723 material. A pooled hierarchical cross-assay model is deferred because the endpoints, feature namespaces, contexts, and units differ. A neural model is deferred because no added information would distinguish mechanism from assay structure at this sample size. Evidence that would justify revisiting these decisions is a frozen Ensembl-to-gene map, verified target/intervention identity, balanced matched contexts, donor/GSM mapping, and orthogonal protein/functional data.

## Key inspected works

[K1] establishes a remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophage state and fibroblast repair association; it does not establish the interaction or benefit axis tested here.

[K2] supplies a consequential inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast rival; it does not establish MerTK specificity or equivalence of the configured assay units.

[K3] bounds the FLS harm endpoint as heterogeneous and niche-linked; it does not validate the targeted score, atlas bridge, or clinical benefit.

Exactly three distinct inspected works are attached as UTF-8 excerpts in `evidence-K1-alivernini-2020.txt`, `evidence-K2-kuo-2019.txt`, and `evidence-K3-korsunsky-2022.txt`. They are reused unchanged from the parent’s inspected evidence; no inaccessible full text or supplementary method is claimed.

# MerTK context-selectivity gate with an explicit perturbation-control residual

Status: substantive child of `candidate-decab21ae0a9e3a872d2c42f`; planned Harbor experiment only. No screening, fitting, or biological result has been executed. The audit below is observed metadata/source inspection, not an observed biological finding.

## Decision and falsifiable hypothesis

[K1] supports a remission-associated synovial macrophage/TAM-MerTK program and reports MerTK perturbation in primary macrophage–fibroblast co-culture. [K2] supplies a consequential rival: inflammatory macrophage–fibroblast cross-talk can drive fibroblast invasiveness through HBEGF/EGFR, without a MerTK-specific explanation. [K3] shows why a small fibroblast transcript panel cannot stand in for the heterogeneous stromal, matrix, spatial, viability, and invasion phenotypes.

The unresolved target-prioritization question is narrower than a benefit-minus-harm claim:

> Within E-MTAB-8873, does exact MerTK-inhibitor exposure produce a larger FLS harm response in the MerTK/CD206-positive than the MerTK/CD206-negative macrophage context, and is that context selectivity greater than the selectivity produced by the registered LPS perturbation control?

The primary estimand remains the exact source-local interaction
`Delta_I = [H(I,Mpos)-H(U,Mpos)] - [H(I,Mneg)-H(U,Mneg)]`.
The new control estimand is
`Delta_LPS = [H(L,Mpos)-H(U,Mpos)] - [H(L,Mneg)-H(U,Mneg)]`,
using the same-round R1 Mpos/Mneg LPS rows. A descriptive residual
`S = Delta_I - Delta_LPS` is reported only as “inhibitor context selectivity beyond this generic perturbation control.” It is not a target-specificity proof: LPS is not a matched non-MerTK inhibitor, the perturbations have no recorded time field, and off-target pharmacology remains possible.

The separate E-MTAB-8322 axis stays a source-local descriptive benefit proxy:
`B_remission - 0.5*(B_naive+B_resistant)`. It is not joined, subtracted, pooled, or donor-matched to E-MTAB-8873. The advancement decision is conjunctive: stable 8322 state association plus a discriminating—but still non-causal—8873 harm/control pattern. A positive result justifies an expert perturbation study, not clinical efficacy, direct mechanism, a therapeutic window, or a patient-selection rule.

## Full metadata and exact compatibility audit

The catalog is the read-only source catalog at `[private-path]/catalog.json`, SHA-256 `162ddf0148975035ee641ae75a2666bf44a7b458b050d79370ee9f550953312f`, snapshot `core-molecular-20261003`. The registry is `[private-path]/assay-registry.json`, SHA-256 `e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f`. The registry exposes four configured assay families, but this child uses only E-MTAB-8322 and E-MTAB-8873; E-MTAB-8316 and GSE95588 remain accessible and are not used to repair the missing target comparator.

### E-MTAB-8322: source-local benefit

- Analysis table: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz`, 33,694 Ensembl feature rows and 27 sample-ID columns; source SHA-256 `95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36`.

Required fields verified in the design are `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_name`, `source_metadata`, and `cells`.
- The source gene map `[private-path]/SA220.genes.tsv`, SHA-256 `920b9e836ae82aeabe5b95932ac8a7795c6f03decff45381749e1e3cdad1f1fa`, maps the Ensembl rows used here: MERTK `ENSG00000153208`, MRC1 `ENSG00000260314`, TREM2 `ENSG00000095970`, C1QA/B/C `ENSG00000173372/ENSG00000173369/ENSG00000159189`, and APOE `ENSG00000130203`. There is no perturbation, FLS endpoint, time field, protein, spatial, or functional-repair measure. The states are cross-sectional labels, not transitions.

### E-MTAB-8873: primary harm and control design

- Analysis table: `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz`, 445 measured feature rows and 33 sample columns; SHA-256 `d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f`. All 33 rows require a contributing-donor model; no verified single-donor inference is available. Composite `donor_id` values are membership labels, not independent donors.

  These are source members under `[private-path]/E-MTAB-8873`; the prepared table is the analysis input and the raw members are lineage/provenance, not extra observations.
- Control tiers are not interchangeable. Same-round R1 LPS members exist in both contexts—`R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_preLPS_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (SHA-256 `98ac568cd83db21e687b32b45000998e331ffe55b99d5f8fd051c1a3f2d3d3eb`) and `R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_preLPS_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` (SHA-256 `00fb2700ece4f1533ab963abfca91eed5651bc2d1a57badb9afbc1c19fada37d`). They support Delta_LPS, not a matched target-negative drug control. Mixed 1Mpos/3Mneg and 3Mpos/1Mneg untreated rows test composition sensitivity. FLS-only rows are untreated controls. The raw member named `R1_SA256A_FLS_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz` has `treatment=none` in the registered design, so it is not a valid FLS-only inhibitor control. R2/R5 preInhibitor rows are Mpos-only and sensitivity-only; they cannot provide a balanced exact inhibitor contrast. The R1 SA260R untreated row has a metadata conflict and is excluded from primary inference.
- No 8873 time field is present. Round is an assay/design grouping, not a biological time axis. No source contains a matched non-MerTK inhibitor, vehicle-controlled alternative inhibitor, genetic MerTK perturbation, protein/phospho-MerTK, viability, efferocytosis, secreted mediator, direct FLS invasion/matrix-degradation, spatial, or clinical outcome measurement.

No donor ID, sample ID, feature ID, treatment, endpoint, or time field may be joined across E-MTAB-8322 and E-MTAB-8873. Although both assays contain labels such as MERTK, their feature namespaces and biological units differ; any cross-source “benefit minus harm” arithmetic is illegal.

## Computable analysis

### Fixed score/interaction baseline

1. Freeze eligibility, features, thresholds, and partitions before fitting. In 8322, fit no cross-source quantities: compute B and its three state contrasts. In 8873, standardize IL6, MMP1, MMP3, and MMP14 using eligible untreated unambiguous co-culture rows and define H as their mean. Preserve all four components.
2. Estimate Delta_I from the exact R1 quartet. Estimate Delta_LPS from the same-round R1 LPS rows. Report S only with its formula, input rows, and the explicit label “perturbation-control residual; not target specificity.”
3. Report MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/SPP1/IL1B/MMP12/MMP13 components and the 8873 composition, LPS, FLS-only, preInhibitor, metadata-conflict, and leave-round/membership sensitivities. Do not promote a sensitivity tier into the primary estimand.
4. Use a fixed 0.5 within-source SD materiality threshold for B and H and freeze it before analysis. Report exact treatment/context cell counts, counterpart availability, feature rank, and whether each contrast is estimable. The exact R1 interaction is an assay-level contrast supported by one contributing FLS/macrophage membership cluster, not an independent-donor population estimate.
5. Primary uncertainty is donor/membership-cluster bootstrap where clusters exist, supplemented by leave-cluster-out and sign/permutation diagnostics. If the primary interaction has only one contributing cluster, report the descriptive contrast and the degeneracy of cluster uncertainty rather than manufacturing a confidence interval. Cells and matrix entries are never replicates.

### Same-input multivariate/mechanistic alternative

Fit a source-stratified, feature-wise partial-pooling model only if the pre-fit rank and counterpart gates pass:

- In 8322, fit the same seven Ensembl features with a shared latent macrophage-state factor, gene-specific loadings, condition effects, and donor-level residual covariance. The model must return B, its state contrasts, all loadings, and donor/holdout stability.
- In 8873, fit the same exact 11 measured transcript features with feature-specific treatment, context, treatment-by-context, round/membership terms and a shared harm factor. It must return Delta_I, Delta_LPS, S, component effects, control contrasts, and uncertainty. HBEGF is not an input.
- The alternative is scientifically useful because the fixed score can hide correlated program structure or let one transcript dominate; the multivariate output can reveal coherent harm/selectivity versus a one-marker artifact. It cannot identify direct MerTK mechanism.
- Use the same predeclared partitions for both methods: five donor/sample holdouts stratified by state in 8322, and fixed round/admissible membership leave-outs in 8873. No random row split is allowed. The 8873 primary exact inhibitor interaction has no independent held-out round, so no held-out confirmation claim is permitted for it. Any learned loadings or nuisance terms are fit within the relevant training partition.
- Estimated future solver budget: CPU, 4–8 cores, less than 16 GiB, minutes to tens of minutes for 19 eligible 8322 samples, 33 8873 samples, and 7/11 features. This is an estimate from dimensions, not a measured solver runtime. GPU is deferred because the scientific bottleneck is donor/control identifiability, not matrix scale.

The fixed baseline is primary for auditability in the sparse design. The multivariate alternative is retained as a secondary coherence/measurement check. A neural predictor is not selected: predictive performance would not distinguish a generic context response from MerTK biology or answer the target-specificity decision. E-MTAB-8316 and GSE95588 are not substituted: their documented donor/assay structures do not supply the missing balanced Mpos/Mneg exact MerTK comparator in this question.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive, still planned, requires all of the following: the 8322 feature/state gate passes with a materially positive remission contrast that is stable across donor holdouts and not one component/donor; the 8873 exact quartet is rank-identifiable; Delta_I is materially positive with coherent components; Delta_LPS is not comparably Mpos-selective and S is positive; composition, FLS-only, leave-round, and leave-membership checks do not reproduce the pattern; and the multivariate model does not reduce it to one transcript. This supports advancing a balanced orthogonal MerTK perturbation experiment. It does not establish target specificity, direct action, clinical benefit, or a therapeutic window.

Adverse means Delta_I is nonpositive, Mneg-selective, no larger than Delta_LPS, or reproduced by composition/FLS-only controls; the 8322 proxy is unstable/nonpositive; or the multivariate model shows a marker/membership artifact. That favors generic activation, FLS/macrophage composition, treatment-history selection, assay-round effects, or off-target explanations and argues against a context-selective MerTK strategy.

Inconclusive means an exact counterpart, feature namespace, rank, donor/membership, or control gate fails; cluster uncertainty is degenerate; the sign changes across admissible tiers; the residual is imprecise; or the only available comparator remains LPS rather than a target-negative perturbation. An imprecise null is not evidence that MerTK has no role. Harbor can verify joins, measured features, row eligibility, rank, fixed partitions, computed contrasts, uncertainty bookkeeping, and conclusion-to-output linkage. It cannot adjudicate whether labels represent biologically pure Mpos/Mneg cells, establish direct target engagement, or validate clinical relevance.

## Smallest expert-ready follow-up if the comparator gap remains

The smallest decisive experiment is a balanced, matched human RA FLS–macrophage co-culture with the same FLS donor paired across Mpos and Mneg macrophage contexts and the same pre-specified exposure schedule. It must include vehicle, exact MerTK inhibition, an orthogonal MerTK perturbation (genetic or independently validated pharmacologic), and LPS as a generic activation control. The independent donor-pair count must be powered for the treatment-by-context interaction; cells and technical replicates cannot replace donor units. Before advancing the target, expert review should require protein/phospho-MerTK target engagement, viability, efferocytosis or another MerTK function, secreted mediators, and direct FLS invasion/matrix readouts alongside the transcript panel. This is a proposed acquisition, not available evidence and not an executed result.

## Actual deliverable

Completion of the Harbor experiment requires newly estimated, source-local files:

- `benefit_effects.csv`: B, components, remission/naive/resistant contrasts, donor counts, holdout and cluster uncertainty;
- `harm_effects.csv`: H components, Delta_I, Delta_LPS, S, exact row/member IDs, and membership-aware diagnostics;
- `controls.csv`: LPS, mixed-composition, FLS-only, preInhibitor, conflicted-row, and leave-round/membership results;
- `source_compatibility.json`: namespace, feature presence, joins, eligible counts, counterpart/rank gates, and explicit no-cross-source status;
- `method_comparison.json`: baseline versus multivariate estimates, coherence/marker diagnostics, fit partitions, and resource logs;
- `results.json`: supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification with every conclusion linked to computed output rows and uncertainty.

# Episode 5 evolution: specificity and negative-control hierarchy for the source-local MerTK gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. The bounded source audit below was executed; no biological fitting, screening, or hypothesis result was executed. “Observed” means schema/design/registry availability, not a biological result.

## Scientific change from the parent

The parent’s two-axis gate is clinically relevant but its 8873 harm axis is not yet target-specific. The strongest remaining rival is not merely generic stress: the registered Mpos/Mneg labels jointly encode MerTK and CD206, so a Mpos-versus-Mneg inhibitor interaction cannot separate MerTK from CD206 co-expression. The exact inhibitor interaction is concentrated in the R1 quartet: one Mneg untreated/inhibitor pair and one Mpos untreated/inhibitor pair. R2 and R5 contain Mpos `preInhibitor` rows, not independent exact inhibitor replications, and there is no time field.

This child changes the scientific deliverable from “an inhibitor interaction consistent with MerTK-context harm” to a staged specificity gate:

1. determine whether an exact, source-local Mpos-selective harm interaction is estimable without pooling incompatible exposure labels;
2. test whether it survives generic-activation, composition, marker-coherence, round, and contributing-donor sensitivities;
3. state explicitly that the molecular data cannot identify MerTK-specific action when MerTK and CD206 are co-defined; require an orthogonal MerTK-versus-CD206 perturbation as the smallest decision-changing follow-up.

A supportive computational result therefore advances a MerTK/CD206-context-consistent follow-up, not a MerTK-specific therapeutic claim.

[K1] supports remission-associated synovial macrophage states containing MerTK-positive biology and repair-associated effects. [K3] shows that stromal/fibroblast programs are heterogeneous and niche-linked. None establishes the configured benefit proxy, the configured inhibitor interaction, direct MerTK engagement in these matrices, or a clinical therapeutic window.

The strongest available data-supported premise is thus only that (a) a MerTK-associated remission state is biologically plausible, and (b) inflammatory macrophage–FLS cross-talk is a plausible harm mechanism. The unresolved claim is:

> In a source-local 8873 coculture assay, does MerTK/CD206-positive macrophage context show an inhibitor-associated FLS harm interaction that is not explained by generic macrophage activation, mixture/composition, round or contributing-donor selection, or a single measured transcript—and can the available data identify MerTK rather than CD206 as the responsible target?

Answering this matters because it determines whether to invest in state-stratified MerTK preservation/activation and orthogonal target experiments, or redirect effort toward generic inflammatory/macrophage-context mechanisms. R2/R5 `Mpos_preInhibitor` members are sensitivity-only.

The 8873 targeted panel directly contains transcript rows for MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, APOE, C1QA/B, SPP1, HBEGF, IL1B, IL6, MMP1, MMP3, MMP12, MMP13, and MMP14. Because the table is FLS/coculture pseudobulk and not cell-resolved, these rows do not provide direct macrophage target engagement. Mpos and Mneg are metadata-defined MerTK/CD206 states, not orthogonal MerTK and CD206 measurements.

The primary population requires `tissue=synovial membrane`, `cell_type=type B synovial cell`, non-mixed coculture, and exact treatment labels. The exact primary quartet is:

`Delta_exact = (H_Mpos,inhibitor-H_Mpos,none) - (H_Mneg,inhibitor-H_Mneg,none)`.
Do not interpret this as MerTK-specific unless the wet-lab orthogonal test is positive.

## Falsifiable hierarchy and interpretation

All thresholds are frozen before fitting at 0.5 within-source SD for `B` and `H`; they are never subtracted across assays.

1. Compatibility/estimability gate: exact feature IDs, design-to-count joins, non-mixed status, exact counterpart availability, incidence-matrix rank, and contributing-donor dependence must pass. A failure is inconclusive, not zero.
2. Exact interaction gate: estimate `Delta_exact` from the R1 quartet only, with paired/contributor-aware uncertainty. Treat it as one exact round, not independent replication.
3. Generic-activation negative control: estimate the analogous Mpos-minus-Mneg interaction for matched LPS-pretreated rows only when both Mpos and Mneg counterparts are present. The R1 LPS pair is available; R2/R5 have Mneg LPS only. If the LPS interaction is similar in sign and material magnitude to `Delta_exact`, generic activation is favored. Absence of a complete pair is inconclusive, not evidence of no generic response.
4. Composition control: use R2/R5 `1Mpos_3Mneg` and `3Mpos_1Mneg` rows only as non-inhibitor composition checks. A monotone H change tracking mixture ratio without a perturbation contrast supports composition/context confounding, not target specificity.
5. Baseline and FLS controls: FLS-only rows and `R1_SA256A_FLS_Inhibitor` are `treatment=none` and not a valid macrophage-inhibitor toxicity control. They can bound FLS baseline only. Do not relabel them as vehicle or inhibitor controls.
6. Marker-coherence control: report MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, SPP1, HBEGF, IL1B, IL6, MMP12, MMP13 and the four H components. A one-feature effect or an HBEGF/IL1B-driven pattern is adverse for target-specific interpretation. Target transcript changes in this FLS/coculture matrix are not direct target engagement.
7. Donor/round sensitivity: report leave-R1/R2/R5-out where estimable, leave-contributing-membership-cluster-out, and an analysis excluding conflicted/reused contributors. Because exact inhibition is R1-only, a failed leave-round-out stability check is expected to be inconclusive, not a refutation.

Supportive computational outcome: both source-local axes meet their own gates; `Delta_exact` exceeds its within-source threshold with coherent H components; no complete LPS control mimics it; composition and marker sensitivities do not explain it; and no single contributing cluster drives the sign. This supports a MerTK/CD206-context-consistent, not MerTK-specific, orthogonal follow-up. It does not support cross-source arithmetic, direct mechanism, efficacy, or a patient rule.

Adverse outcome: `Delta_exact` is nonpositive, Mneg is as harmful or more harmful, LPS reproduces the selectivity, mixture composition explains the H pattern, a single marker/cluster drives the result, or the multivariate analysis removes the apparent interaction. Redirect toward generic inflammation, HBEGF/IL1B cross-talk, composition, or assay context.

Inconclusive outcome: any compatibility/rank/overlap gate fails; uncertainty spans zero or the threshold; the R1-only effect cannot survive dependence sensitivity; an exposure-tier choice changes its sign; or the available labels cannot separate MerTK from CD206. This is the expected interpretation for target specificity without orthogonal perturbation.

## Smallest follow-up that can change the decision

Run a matched, donor-blocked coculture factorial experiment using the same FLS donor and macrophage donor pair:

- macrophage contexts: MERTK+/CD206+ and MERTK+/CD206−, with orthogonal surface/protein verification;
- perturbations: vehicle, a MerTK-selective perturbation, and a CD206-selective perturbation or matched CD206 blockade; include non-targeting/isotype controls;
- generic control: matched LPS activation;
- outcomes: viability plus a direct FLS invasion or matrix-degradation endpoint, with IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 and HBEGF/IL1B as molecular secondary outcomes;
- use at least two biological donor blocks and a prespecified exposure/time grid, because 8873 has neither dose nor time.

The decision-changing pattern is MerTK-perturbation harm in MERTK+/CD206+ coculture that is absent under CD206 perturbation and not reproduced by LPS, with direct functional harm and preserved viability. If MerTK and CD206 perturbations are indistinguishable, or LPS reproduces the effect, the MerTK-specific direction is abandoned. If all effects are imprecise or viability-confounded, the result is inconclusive and another matched study is required. This wet-lab dependency is essential because 8873 cannot identify it computationally.

## Baseline versus substantive alternative

Both alternatives use identical source-local inputs, outcomes, controls, split logic, and uncertainty criteria.

Baseline: a fixed molecular score computes `B` and `H` from the prespecified gene sets and estimates `Delta_exact` plus the LPS, composition, marker, round, and contributing-cluster sensitivities. It is primary because every sign, missing counterpart, and dependence assumption is auditable in this sparse design. It loses correlation sharing and a formal separation of coherent programs from one-marker effects.

Substantive alternative: a source-stratified multivariate hierarchical model fits the same seven 8322 benefit transcripts and the same 8873 12 target/context/harm transcripts, with gene-specific effects, a shared benefit/harm factor, treatment-by-context interaction, explicit composition terms, and contributing-donor random effects. The 8873 feature set is exactly MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, SPP1, HBEGF, IL1B, MMP12, MMP13, IL6, MMP1, MMP3, and MMP14. It outputs the same `B`, `H`, `Delta_exact`, every component, and the same negative controls; it is not a surrogate prediction model. It can reveal whether the apparent interaction is a coherent program or one-marker artifact and whether residual harm remains after composition terms. It cannot manufacture MerTK/CD206 identifiability.

Use a fixed split generated once from frozen sample IDs: five-fold donor holdout stratified by state in 8322, and admissible membership-cluster/round holdout in 8873. Fit loadings and nuisance parameters inside training folds. For the exact R1 contrast, report that no independent held-out inhibitor round exists; if rank or fold support fails, defer the multivariate fit rather than changing the estimand. Primary uncertainty is donor bootstrap in 8322 and contributing-membership-cluster bootstrap plus sign/permutation sensitivity in 8873; cells and matrix entries are not replicates.

CPU is selected for the future solver envelope: 4–8 cores, under 16 GiB, minutes for the 19-sample benefit and 33-sample targeted assay. This is a planning estimate, not a measured full fit. GPU is deferred because the scientific bottleneck is target identifiability and sparse replication, not matrix scale. A neural predictor is not selected because predictive improvement would not distinguish MerTK from CD206 or generic stress.

## Actual planned deliverable

Completion requires newly fitted, source-local outputs:

- `benefit_effects.csv`: B contrast, seven components, donor counts, and uncertainty;
- `harm_effects.csv`: `Delta_exact`, four H components, and contributor-aware uncertainty;
- `specificity_controls.csv`: exact R1, complete LPS if estimable, mixture, FLS baseline, marker, round, and contributor sensitivities;
- `source_compatibility.json`: paths, hashes, feature IDs, labels, rank, counterpart and overlap gates;
- `method_comparison.json`: fixed-score versus hierarchical multivariate outputs under identical splits;
- `results.json`: each conclusion linked to computed rows with supportive/adverse/inconclusive status.

The source audit and registry checks are complete, but screening status remains planned. Harbor can verify joins, feature presence, rank, control availability, uncertainty computation, and whether conclusions follow from outputs. It cannot adjudicate direct target engagement, cell identity, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, spatial localization, clinical benefit, or the MerTK-versus-CD206 wet-lab result.

## Key references

[K1] Alivernini et al. supports the remission-associated MerTK macrophage prior; this proposal adds source-local proxy discipline and a specificity gate.

[K2] Kuo et al. supplies the HBEGF inflammatory macrophage–FLS rival; this proposal uses LPS, HBEGF, IL1B, component and composition controls.

[K3] Floudas et al. bounds the FLS endpoint as heterogeneous immune–stromal biology; this proposal refuses to call the four-transcript H score invasion and requires direct functional follow-up.

Attached exactly three distinct abstract-only inspected works: `key-references.json`, `evidence-K1-alivernini-2020.txt`, `evidence-K2-kuo-2019.txt`, and `evidence-K3-floudas-2022.txt`.

# Episode 6 evolution: namespace-corrected, source-local escalation gate

Status: planned Harbor computation plus a completed source/namespace audit. No molecular screening, biological fitting, or wet-lab result was executed. The audit jobs only inspected immutable hashes, headers, feature identifiers, design rows and registered exposure labels.

Parent: `candidate-b158db9dbd9a3a296a6a1c3c`.

## Substantive change

The parent’s scientific direction is retained: determine whether a remission-associated macrophage context proxy and an inhibitor-associated FLS harm contrast justify an orthogonal MerTK-versus-CD206 experiment. This child repairs two grounding problems and sharpens the decision rule.

1. The E-MTAB-8322 benefit proxy is explicitly bound to the registered Ensembl namespace. The unusual map value `MRC1 -> ENSG00000260314` is not silently replaced with an external annotation.
2. The E-MTAB-8873 panel is explicitly bound to its measured `SYMBOL|RefSeq.version|assay-end` feature strings. HBEGF and C1QC are absent from the 445 measured features and are removed from computational scores; HBEGF remains a future orthogonal measurement, not an imputed covariate.
3. The R1 exact interaction is one sparse source-local contrast, not independent replication and not a cross-source decision gate. A qualitative escalation matrix may use the two source-local statuses to decide what experiment to fund, but no benefit-minus-harm arithmetic, cross-source join, clinical utility, or target-specific conclusion is permitted.

The scientific deliverable is newly estimated source-local quantities and a predeclared escalation state: a namespace/rank report; the E-MTAB-8322 remission-state proxy and uncertainty; the E-MTAB-8873 exact R1 interaction, component effects and dependence sensitivities; and a baseline-versus-hierarchical comparison whose conclusions are linked to those outputs. Completion is not a favorable result.

## Opening, evidence-supported claim, and unresolved claim

[K1] reports remission-associated MerTK-positive/TREM2-high or MerTK-positive/LYVE1-positive synovial macrophage states, including fibroblast-repair observations. That supports biological plausibility for a resolution-associated macrophage context, not the configured seven-gene score or a MerTK therapeutic window.

[K2] reports HBEGF-positive macrophages associated with fibroblast invasiveness. This is a consequential non-MerTK inflammatory rival. It motivates generic activation and inflammatory-marker controls, but HBEGF is not measured in the configured 8873 panel.

[K3] reports heterogeneous FLS states driven by local cytokine exposures and spatial signaling. Thus a four-transcript FLS score can be a reproducible assay proxy, but it is not invasion, matrix degradation, viability, or clinical harm.

The unresolved, falsifiable claim is:

> In E-MTAB-8873, does the exact R1 MerTK-inhibitor contrast produce a materially larger FLS inflammatory transcript response in the metadata-defined Mpos than Mneg context, after source-local composition, LPS, marker, round and contributing-donor sensitivities; and, independently, does E-MTAB-8322 show a remission-associated seven-gene macrophage state proxy? If both source-local statuses are supportive, is the rational next action an orthogonal MerTK-versus-CD206 experiment rather than a target-specific conclusion?

The data cannot identify MerTK versus CD206 because Mpos/Mneg are jointly defined MerTK/CD206 labels, not orthogonal target measurements. Nor can they establish direct inhibitor engagement, dose response, time course, viability, invasion, spatial localization, or clinical benefit.

## Estimability, falsification and decision rule

All thresholds are frozen before fitting at 0.5 within-source SD; they are not cross-source quantities.

1. Namespace gate: every requested feature resolves exactly, counts/design sample IDs are bijective, and no feature is substituted by a symbol or external annotation.
2. Design gate: non-mixed primary rows, exact untreated counterparts, exposure-tier labels, rank of the R1 design, and contributor membership are recorded. Failure is inconclusive and stops inferential interpretation.
3. Benefit status: supportive only if the 8322 remission proxy is positive and material for the prespecified contrasts with donor-aware uncertainty; adverse if it is nonpositive or clearly inconsistent across the two contrasts; otherwise inconclusive. This is not evidence of clinical benefit.
4. Harm status: supportive only if `Delta_exact` exceeds the frozen within-8873 materiality threshold with coherent IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 components, no complete LPS control mimics it, no mixture/composition pattern explains it, and no single contributor cluster determines the sign. Adverse includes a nonpositive interaction, Mneg at least as harmful, LPS selectivity of similar magnitude, composition explanation, a single-marker effect, or removal by the multivariate sensitivity. Any rank/uncertainty failure is inconclusive.
5. Dependence status: use donor/contributing-membership cluster bootstrap and sign/permutation sensitivity. Cells, matrix entries and repeated sample rows are not independent replicates. Leave-round-out is reported as unavailable for the exact R1 interaction because exact inhibitor exposure occurs in R1 only; that absence is inconclusive, not refutation.

Qualitative escalation matrix:

| 8322 state proxy | 8873 R1 harm interaction | permitted next decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| supportive | supportive | Commission the smallest orthogonal MerTK-versus-CD206 factorial experiment; do not claim MerTK specificity or net benefit. |
| supportive | adverse | Do not pursue a MerTK-protective direction from these data; redirect to generic inflammation, CD206/state composition, or HBEGF biology, with HBEGF measured in the next assay. |
| adverse | supportive | No cross-source benefit conclusion is allowed; treat the apparent harm as a context signal only and require expert justification before any wet-lab escalation. |
| either status inconclusive | any | Repair/adjudicate mapping, contributor metadata, or matched exposure evidence; no target prioritization. |
| namespace/design gate fails | any | Stop the computational gate and correct the source binding; do not classify as a null. |

This table is a research triage rule, not a cross-source estimand. A supportive pair does not establish a clinical decision, direct mechanism, efficacy, or patient-selection rule.

The decision-changing wet-lab test is donor-blocked coculture with MERTK+/CD206+ and MERTK+/CD206− contexts, orthogonal surface/protein verification, vehicle, a MerTK-selective perturbation, a CD206-selective perturbation or matched blockade, non-targeting/isotype controls, matched LPS, viability, direct invasion or matrix-degradation measurement, and IL6/MMP1/MMP3/MMP14 plus HBEGF/IL1B secondary outcomes. Use at least two biological donor blocks and a prespecified time/exposure grid. MerTK-specific support requires MerTK perturbation harm in the positive context, absent or materially smaller CD206 perturbation harm, no LPS mimic, preserved viability and direct functional harm. Indistinguishable MerTK/CD206 effects, LPS reproduction, or viability confounding abandons or defers the MerTK-specific direction.

## Baseline and substantive learned alternative

Both methods use identical source-local inputs, outcomes, split logic, and uncertainty rules.

Baseline (primary): compute the fixed seven-gene 8322 score and four-gene 8873 H score, then estimate the prespecified contrasts and controls. Fit within-split z parameters only on training data. Preserve every component, missing counterpart, rank result, exposure tier, and contributor cluster. This is auditable and appropriate for a 19-primary-row 8322 state comparison and a four-sample exact R1 interaction.

Substantive alternative (secondary): fit a source-stratified, cross-classified hierarchical multivariate model using the same seven Ensembl features in 8322 and the same 12 measured 8873 features (MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, APOE, C1QA, C1QB, SPP1, IL1B, IL6, MMP1, MMP3 and MMP14). Include gene-specific effects, a shared state/harm covariance structure, the prespecified condition or treatment-by-Mpos/Mneg interaction, composition terms for mixture controls, and random effects for donor/contributor membership. It must emit the same B, H, Delta_exact, components and controls. It can reveal whether a score is a coherent program or one-marker artifact and whether residual harm remains after composition adjustment. It cannot create MerTK/CD206 identifiability or an independent R1 inhibitor replicate; if rank fails, defer rather than change the estimand.

Generate one frozen split assignment: donor-blocked, state-stratified five-fold holdout in 8322 where each fold is estimable; in 8873 use round/membership-cluster holdouts only for estimable sensitivity outcomes and explicitly mark exact R1 as having no held-out inhibitor round. Use donor bootstrap for 8322 and contributor-cluster bootstrap plus sign/permutation sensitivity for 8873. Report interval width and estimability, not only p-values.

CPU is selected: 4–8 cores, less than 16 GiB, expected minutes for these small matrices; this is an unmeasured planning estimate. GPU is deferred because the bottleneck is sparse replication, contributor dependence and target identifiability, not matrix throughput. A neural predictor is not selected: there is no independent clinical outcome to predict, and incremental prediction cannot distinguish MerTK from CD206 or generic stress. A mechanistic pathway model is deferred until protein, HBEGF, viability and functional endpoints exist; fitting it now would encode unavailable biology rather than test it.

## Planned outputs and interpretation limits

The future Harbor run must create:

- `source_compatibility.json`: exact paths, hashes, feature IDs, namespace resolution, sample/design joins, row counts, rank, counterpart availability and exposure tiers;
- `benefit_effects.csv`: B contrasts, seven components, donor counts and uncertainty;
- `harm_effects.csv`: Delta_exact, four H components, 10 measured secondary components and contributor-aware uncertainty;
- `specificity_controls.csv`: LPS, composition, FLS baseline, marker, round and contributor sensitivities, with unavailable HBEGF/C1QC explicitly listed;
