## Fixed estimands, controls and temporal/split rules

Apply one prespecified log1p transform only when a prepared matrix is raw nonnegative abundance; fit feature-wise mean/SD within the applicable source calibration partition and record the transform and feature availability in `source_compatibility.json`.

Define (H=mean[z(IL6),z(MMP1),z(MMP3),z(MMP14)]). The primary exact interaction is:

[
Delta_{R1,exact}=(H_{Mpos,Inhibitor}-H_{Mpos})-(H_{Mneg,Inhibitor}-H_{Mneg}).
]

Positive Delta means a larger inhibitor-associated increase in the jointly Mpos/CD206pos-labelled context, not MerTK-specific harm.

Report separately:

- (A_{R2,pre}=H[R2\_Mpos\_preInhibitor]-H[R2\_Mpos]).
- (A_{R5,pre}=H[R5\_Mpos\_preInhibitor]-H[R5\_Mpos]).
- (L_{R1}=(H_{Mpos,preLPS}-H_{Mpos})-(H_{Mneg,preLPS}-H_{Mneg})), using the exact R1 preLPS rows and same-context untreated rows.
- Every H component effect, the macrophage marker/context panel, FLS-only rows (R1 SA256A, R2 SA257A, R2 SA258R, R5 SA263R and R5 SA266A), mixed R2/R5 rows against the predeclared 1/4 and 3/4 pure-row weighted means, cells sensitivity, and the conflict/reuse-sensitive R1 SA260R rows.

The exact four R1 inhibitor rows are a locked estimand partition: they are excluded from nuisance calibration and are never described as held-out replication. R2/R5 and LPS families stay grouped by round/contributor. E-MTAB-8316 folds keep each donor/specimen pair together. E-MTAB-8322 folds keep donor and repeated/related flags together, with unresolved related donors excluded from independent-donor inference. No cross-source fold, donor join or arithmetic is allowed.

Freeze materiality at 0.5 within-source SD before fitting. Uncertainty for the fixed score uses contributor-aware sign permutations and/or donor/cluster bootstrap; cells never provide replication. Report intervals and estimability, not ordinary donor t-tests or p-value-based rescue.

## Method comparison: fixed score versus hierarchical decomposition

### A. Fixed auditable baseline

The baseline computes H, the exact R1 Delta, A_R2_pre, A_R5_pre, L_R1, C_8316 and B_8322 directly from the recorded source scales after the prespecified transform. It fits only source-local z parameters. Its strengths are transparent row-level auditability, no unidentifiable cross-source pooling and a decision that remains interpretable when the R1 design is sparse. Its weakness is that averaging H can hide whether one gene or one contributor drives the signal.

### B. Same-input hierarchical/mechanistic alternative

Fit a source-stratified multivariate decomposition on exactly the same selected rows, features, calibration partitions and split groups. No latent variable, donor effect or parameter is shared across datasets.

For E-MTAB-8873, model each available H gene as a gene-specific intercept plus a shared latent FLS inflammatory factor, gene-specific residual loading, Mpos/Mneg context, treatment, round/tier and contributor/context effect. Estimate the treatment-by-context contrast gene by gene and recombine it with the prespecified H weights. Contributor effects are random or fixed only when their levels are estimable; the R1 SA256A/SA259A interaction remains explicitly flagged as one contributing-donor configuration. R2/R5 can inform round/tier variability but cannot identify a MerTK-only coefficient.

For E-MTAB-8316, fit a paired marker-response model with gene-specific effects and specimen-pair/donor-cluster variation. For E-MTAB-8322, fit a donor-aware macrophage-state model with gene-specific variance and the B contrast. These are separate models; there is no cross-source latent factor and no donor matching across assays.

The hierarchy can reveal whether H coherence survives residual covariance, whether one component drives Delta, and whether donor/context variation dominates the fixed contrast. It cannot create independent R1 donors, MerTK/CD206 separation, target engagement or transferability. If the random-effect variance or latent factor is rank-unstable, return an identifiability warning and retain the fixed score as the primary result.

Use source-local fitting only. The hierarchical sensitivity uses parametric bootstrap or posterior simulation conditional on the frozen grouping, with sensitivity over weakly informative variance priors/regularization fixed before looking at Delta. Compare the two methods on the same Delta, A_R2_pre, A_R5_pre, L_R1, C_8316 and B contrasts; component concordance, interval width, donor/context variance share, rank/estimability and gate status are the scientific outputs. Do not select a model for a smaller p-value or prediction gain.

The planned resource envelope is 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU and at most 1,200 seconds for tabular fitting/resampling. This is an unmeasured planning estimate; no diagnostic was run. The structured panel is small enough that a GPU is not scientifically useful. A future high-dimensional functional assay could change that resource decision.

## Falsification and interpretation

Structural failure (bad paths/hashes, non-bijective counts/design join, missing exact feature IDs or absent counterparts) is a packaging/design failure, not a biological null.

The molecular gate is supportive only when all structural checks pass; Delta is material; all four H components are directionally concordant; A_R2_pre and A_R5_pre share the R1 Mpos direction with at least 3/4 components concordant where estimable; |L_R1| is below materiality or materially smaller/opposite; C_8316 lacks a coherent same-direction marker response; no contributor, mixed-row, FLS-only, cells or sensitivity audit reverses Delta; and baseline and hierarchy agree, or hierarchy instability is itself transparently reported as the bound. This supports only “a source-local context-associated transcript pattern warrants orthogonal testing.”

Adverse results are LPS/context or generic perturbation at least as compatible as Delta, both tier checks reverse, or composition/contributor/component audits remove the signal. Do not prioritize MerTK-specific harm.

Inconclusive results are missing exact counterparts, only one tier estimable, intervals spanning materiality, non-comparable controls, or hierarchical rank/variance instability. Preserve the observation and defer the target decision; an imprecise null is not refutation.

A supportive result still requires an independent, donor-blocked factorial experiment: MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle crossed with measured CD206-high/low macrophage preparations, plus target-negative matched perturbation control. Measure MerTK and CD206 protein independently, direct engagement or validated proximal readout, viability, FLS H as secondary transcript readout, and invasion or matrix degradation as a functional endpoint. The target-by-CD206 interaction in functional endpoint Y is:

[
Tau=[Y(MerTK,CD206high)-Y(vehicle,CD206high)]-[Y(MerTK,CD206low)-Y(vehicle,CD206low)].
]

A target-specific functional claim requires matched CD206, engagement, no viability explanation, concordant functional change and no target-negative effect. If only H changes, the result remains a transcript proxy. If the response follows CD206, co-encoding is favored; if target-negative or generic, perturbation/measurement is favored. Clinical safety, efficacy and benefit require another translational study.

## Alternatives not chosen and revisit evidence

Pooling R1 inhibitor with R2/R5 preInhibitor is rejected because exposure labels and matched contexts differ; revisit only after exposure-equivalence and matched-Mneg curation. Calling Delta MerTK-specific is rejected because the labels jointly encode MerTK/CD206; revisit after independent protein measurement and perturbation. FLS-only rows are untreated handling baselines, not inhibitor toxicity controls; revisit with matched treated FLS-only samples and viability. A neural predictor is deferred because there is no independent clinical or functional endpoint and it cannot resolve target specificity; revisit with a validated held-out functional outcome. Cross-source B-H arithmetic is prohibited because assays, namespaces, donors and estimands differ. GSE95588 remains deferred pending verified feature-map and GSM/donor lineage.

# Episode 10 child: a GSE95588 source-local transferability gate for the MerTK/CD206 hypothesis

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No biological screening, fitting of biological effects, or result has been executed. Parent: candidate-f375506334f96c9a014ada81.

## Decision and scientific opening

The episode-9 question remains whether the E-MTAB-8873 R1 inhibitor interaction is informative enough to justify an orthogonal MerTK-by-CD206 experiment. Its exact estimand is a single sparse, contributing-donor FLS contrast whose context labels jointly encode MerTK and CD206. E-MTAB-8316 adds six paired UNC106238-versus-none monocyte contrasts, but has no Mpos/Mneg context and no FLS endpoint. The unresolved issue is therefore not whether more transcript rows can be pooled; it is whether a genuinely separate assay can show a related, source-local context pattern and whether ordinary perturbations produce the same pattern.

[K1] supports the leading biological prior: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce repair-associated FLS responses, while the relevant published state labels co-describe MerTK and CD206. [K2] supplies a consequential rival: fibroblast/TNF-shaped HBEGF-positive macrophages can promote FLS invasiveness. [K3] bounds interpretation of the E-MTAB-8873 H score: FLS states respond to local cytokine context, so an inflammatory transcript change is not target engagement or functional harm. These works motivate a context-transferability check; none establishes MerTK specificity in the configured data. The three inspected works and evidence limits are attached in key-references.json and evidence-K1-alivernini.txt, evidence-K2-kuo.txt and evidence-K3-smith.txt.

The actual deliverable is newly estimated source-local GSE95588 context and drug-by-context contrasts, with component-level outputs, block-aware uncertainty/sensitivity, identifiability diagnostics, and a prespecified gate linked to those outputs. The deliverable is complete only when both GSE matrices pass structural checks and the report states supportive, adverse, or inconclusive status for transferability and generic perturbation. It is not complete from a favorable transcript result and cannot establish clinical benefit.

## Hypothesis and competing explanations

Falsifiable hypothesis: in GSE95588, the macrophage program recorded in fibroblast-plus-TNF context will show a coherent, round-repeated context response across the MerTK/CD206 marker panel B_GSE and the inflammatory transcript panel H_GSE, while the exact same source will not show an equally coherent context-selective response for unrelated matched drug perturbations (A77 and naproxen). If this pattern is observed, it supports only that a macrophage/FLS/TNF context-associated transcript state is transferable enough to motivate an orthogonal MerTK-by-CD206 test; it does not support MerTK-specific action, target engagement, functional harm, or benefit.

The strongest rival explanations are:

1. Context and severity: fibroblast/TNF exposure itself drives the macrophage and inflammatory panels, with no MerTK-specific mechanism.
2. Generic drug or assay response: ordinary anti-inflammatory perturbations produce similar context contrasts, making the E-MTAB-8873 inhibitor interaction non-specific.
3. Co-encoding and measurement: MERTK and MRC1/CD206 state labels are correlated and source feature labels are not independently re-annotated; a marker transcript pattern need not imply protein abundance or engagement.
4. Donor/round and protocol structure: public GSE95588 labels identify P1–P4/round-like blocks but the prepared design has donor_id=null and donor_status=unresolved for every row. Apparent replication may be repeated or reused material.

The observation that separates these explanations is a prespecified comparison of the same exact context contrast across B_GSE and H_GSE components, across the two coculture rounds, against A77/naproxen context contrasts, and against the separate E-MTAB-8316 paired UNC106238 marker response. No result is currently assumed.

### Existing configured gates retained

Retain E-MTAB-8873 exact R1 Delta_R1_exact, R2/R5 preInhibitor direction checks, L_R1, component/contributor/composition audits and E-MTAB-8316 C_8316 exactly as frozen by the parent. E-MTAB-8316 bindings are its prepared counts/design, 12 rows MK11, MK12, MK15, MK16, MK19, MK20, MK23, MK24, MK3, MK4, MK7, MK8, with six specimen-paired UNC106238-versus-none contrasts keyed by donor_id plus other_donor_id. All rows are synovial membrane monocytes exposed to LPS 1 ng/mL; UNC106238 dose metadata is 250. Its counts namespace is Ensembl IDs (first row ENSG00000223972), while GSE95588 uses gene symbols; there is no cross-source feature join. E-MTAB-8316 has no MerTK/CD206 context, no FLS endpoint and no clinical outcome. It remains a generic perturbation gate whose coherent marker response weakens target-specific interpretation, while a null cannot prove specificity.

## Analysis, baseline and substantive alternative

Use recorded assay scales. For each matrix, apply one prespecified log1p only if values are raw nonnegative abundance, then fit feature-wise means/SDs within that source's selected calibration partition. Do not calibrate GSE scores using E-MTAB-8873 or E-MTAB-8316. Report feature availability, transforms and raw selected rows.

Primary auditable baseline:

- Compute B_GSE and H_GSE from source-local z scores.
- Estimate I_B,1, I_B,2, I_H,1, I_H,2 and all component contrasts.
- Estimate J_q,p,d for q in {B_GSE,H_GSE}, p in P1–P4 and d in {A77,Nap}.
- Use P1–P4 and r1/r2 only as structural blocks. Report block-wise ranges and sign concordance; use exact sign permutations over the four P blocks for J and a two-block descriptive range for I. Do not call unresolved sample labels independent donors and do not use cells as replication.
- Keep all GSE results separate from E-MTAB-8873 Delta and E-MTAB-8316 C_8316. Compare qualitative gate status, not effect-size arithmetic across assay scales.

Substantive same-input alternative:

Fit a source-stratified multivariate hierarchical sensitivity model on exactly the same selected rows and source-specific feature IDs. Use gene-specific intercepts/variances, a latent B_GSE factor for the seven state markers, a latent H_GSE factor for the four inflammatory genes, fixed context terms and P/round block terms, and gene-specific residuals. For the drug matrix, fit paired drug-by-context terms for A77 and Nap with P block effects; do not share a latent factor across matrices or join donors. Evaluate posterior/parametric uncertainty, component loadings, block influence, rank/estimability and whether the sign of I or J survives residual covariance. The alternative reveals whether a score-level contrast is driven by one gene or measurement covariance, which the fixed score baseline hides.

Freeze the analysis split before fitting: the eight coculture rows are a locked source-local descriptive partition; the 28 drug rows are grouped by P block with all conditions for a block kept together. There is no held-out clinical outcome and no predictive accuracy estimand. The hierarchical model is selected only as a sensitivity analysis if it is identifiable and changes the transferability/generic gate; it is deferred as a primary estimator because two coculture blocks and four unresolved P blocks cannot support stable donor-level random effects. A neural predictor is not scientifically useful here because no independent functional outcome exists; revisit only if a validated held-out functional endpoint is added. No GPU is indicated. Planned resource envelope is 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, at most 1,200 seconds.

## Decision rules and falsification

Structural failure (missing path/hash, header/design mismatch, missing feature row, nonunique sample IDs or use of the four unprepared Donor2 rows) invalidates the packaging, not the biology.

Supportive transferability gate requires: structural checks pass; I_B,1 and I_B,2 have the same direction with at least 5/7 B components concordant in each estimable block; the corresponding I_H components are directionally coherent in both blocks or are explicitly inconclusive due to sparse values; hierarchical sensitivity does not assign the result to one marker alone; and the pattern is not completely explained by an equally large generic J_A77/J_Nap context effect. This means “source-local macrophage/FLS/TNF context pattern compatible with proceeding to orthogonal testing,” not “MerTK-specific.”

Adverse gate means the GSE context effect is absent/reversed across rounds, the result is driven by one component, or A77/naproxen produces a comparable or larger context interaction across blocks. It also means treating the E-MTAB-8873 Delta as non-specific enough that MerTK prioritization should be deferred. A coherent response in E-MTAB-8316 further supports the generic explanation.

Inconclusive means donor identity remains essential to the requested claim, the two coculture blocks disagree, block intervals span materiality, the selected drug counterpart is absent, the hierarchy is rank-unstable, or the raw feature labels cannot be curated. Inconclusive is not a null. Preserve the source-local descriptive output and seek curation or an orthogonal assay.

Even a supportive result cannot establish:

- MerTK-specific target engagement or occupancy;
- CD206-independent action;
- FLS viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair or other functional harm/benefit;
- causal treatment effect, clinical efficacy, safety or patient benefit.

## Minimum orthogonal follow-up and revisit criteria

The dependency is not resolvable from the configured transcript matrices. The minimum follow-up is an independent-donor, randomized and blinded MerTK-by-CD206 factorial macrophage–FLS assay. Cross MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle with a target-negative matched perturbation control and CD206-high versus CD206-low preparations. Measure MerTK and CD206 protein independently; verify direct MerTK engagement or a validated proximal readout; record viability; prespecify H as a secondary transcript outcome and measure a functional endpoint such as FLS invasion or matrix degradation.

For functional outcome Y, estimate:
Tau_MerTK×CD206 = [Y(MerTK perturbation, CD206-high)-Y(vehicle, CD206-high)] - [Y(MerTK perturbation, CD206-low)-Y(vehicle, CD206-low)].
A target-specific functional claim requires comparable measured CD206, direct engagement, no viability explanation, a concordant functional change and no matching target-negative effect. If the effect follows CD206, co-encoding is favored; if it follows target-negative perturbation or transcript only, generic/measurement explanations are favored. Clinical benefit requires another translational study.

Revisit GSE as an independent gate only after donor/contributor lineage is curated and source labels are independently mapped. Revisit pooling R1 with R2/R5 only after exposure equivalence and matched Mneg contrasts are available. Revisit a neural or high-dimensional model only with a held-out functional outcome; complexity cannot solve target specificity.

## Key references

[K1] Alivernini et al., Nature Medicine (2020): MerTK-positive macrophage remission/repair prior and MerTK/CD206 co-labeling; no configured MerTK-specific effect.

[K2] Kuo et al., Science Translational Medicine (2019): HBEGF/TNF/fibroblast macrophage–FLS rival route; abstract-only inspection and no configured MerTK claim.

[K3] Smith et al., Nature Immunology (2023): cytokine/context-dependent FLS heterogeneity; no target engagement or functional validation of H.

# Episode 11: an estimand-and-decision gate for the MerTK/CD206 source-local signal

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No screening, biological fitting, or bounded result was executed in Episode 11. Parent: candidate-62a1af5137ebbfa438046cf0.

## Scientific question and advance

The strongest evidence-supported claim is descriptive. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission/repair biology [K1], macrophage–FLS communication can promote an invasive FLS program through a non-MerTK route [K2], and local cytokine exposure produces heterogeneous FLS states [K3]. None of those claims establishes that the configured R1 inhibitor contrast is MerTK-specific, donor-generalizable, target-engaging, functionally harmful, or clinically beneficial.

The unresolved question is narrower and falsifiable: in the frozen E-MTAB-8873 source, does the exact macrophage-pre-treatment interaction in the FLS inflammatory transcript proxy H exceed a predeclared assay-level materiality threshold with uncertainty small enough to justify the smallest independent MerTK-by-CD206 target-specific test, after accounting for component coherence, LPS/context handling, generic perturbation, contributor composition, and model instability?

The substantive Episode-11 advance is an executable decision contract. It fixes (i) the estimand and units, (ii) the calibration partition and uncertainty rule, (iii) the donor/contributor interpretation, (iv) the output row that can authorize the next action, and (v) the minimum follow-up after supportive, adverse, or inconclusive molecular evidence. A positive gate remains a source-local transcript decision; it never becomes a MerTK-specific or clinical conclusion.

## Hypothesis and competing explanations

Hypothesis: the R1 Mpos-versus-Mneg inhibitor interaction in H is a material, component-coherent context-associated FLS response that is more compatible with the jointly MerTK/CD206-labelled context than with LPS handling, generic perturbation, composition, contributor reuse, or one-gene measurement artifact.

The labels are not independent MerTK and CD206 measurements. Mpos and Mneg jointly encode both markers and a broader macrophage state. The R1 quartet is one SA256A/SA259A contributing-donor configuration, not four independent donors. Thus the test can estimate a finite source-local contrast but cannot estimate a population-level MerTK-specific effect or clinical benefit. The principal rival is CD206/broader-state encoding; other rivals are FLS cytokine response, LPS handling, mixed-cell composition, contributor reuse, UNC106238 response, and nonfunctional transcript variation.

A supportive molecular gate means only: proceed to the specified orthogonal assay. An adverse gate means the source-local pattern is better explained by a rival or fails the fixed coherence rule, so MerTK should not be prioritized from this evidence. An inconclusive gate means the data do not discriminate; it does not refute the hypothesis.

## Actual scientific deliverable

The future solver must produce newly estimated, source-local quantities and a decision record, not a prediction score:

1. A locked fixed-score estimate of Delta_R1_exact and its four component effects.
2. Auxiliary, non-pooled checks: A_R2_pre, A_R5_pre, L_R1, the E-MTAB-8316 paired marker response, and the E-MTAB-8322 descriptive macrophage-state contrasts.
3. A same-input hierarchical sensitivity decomposition of the same quantities, including gene/residual, contributor/context, and round/tier variance shares where estimable.
4. A machine-readable output/decision_row.json containing one row for gate_id R1_MerTK_CD206_source_local, the exact estimate and interval, threshold, structural status, coherence flags, rival-check flags, estimability status, decision, and next_action.
5. A source_compatibility.json recording every transform, feature identifier, selected sample, calibration partition, grouping key, join result, and missing feature/counterpart. The experiment is complete only when these files are produced and the decision row is reproducible from the declared inputs.

No biological result is asserted here.

## Exact data binding and population

All source data are read-only. Use the catalog at [private-path]/catalog.json, SHA-256 162ddf0148975035ee641ae75a2666bf44a7b458b050d79370ee9f550953312f, and the prepared assay registry at [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f. The complete table relationships and source-file inventory are in the workspace datasets/therapeutic_targets/metadata.json and README.md.

For each assay, read the prepared counts table and prepared design JSON. Join only counts.header.sample_id = design.sample_id, require a bijection for selected samples, and preserve the source-specific donor/specimen namespace. There is no usable longitudinal time field. The temporal boundary is the frozen 2026-10-03 source snapshot and the recorded condition/treatment/exposure labels. Do not join donor IDs across assays.

### Primary E-MTAB-8873 population

Use E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f, and E-MTAB-8873.design.json, SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4. The prepared table has 33 samples and 445 measured feature rows/columns as cataloged; retain the feature identifiers exactly. Filter design rows to tissue=synovial membrane and cell_type=type B synovial cell. Required design columns are sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, other_donor_id, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata, and cells. cells is metadata only, never a replicate count.

The locked primary partition is the four exact archive members:

- E-MTAB-8873/R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz, SHA-256 ef435ca4a16bb535f74ad077297861f2f9672827c2d2a4e7f9e65171bea2b0d7
- E-MTAB-8873/R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz, SHA-256 144b62d01db3f4635bdd19ecc599ce7670770ddf79b7e72e846c46a3cf732e9e
- E-MTAB-8873/R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz, SHA-256 1dafc0a646fc9cdc1101803cf9d36802a1775844a85877930341ebe6edcf2176
- E-MTAB-8873/R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz, SHA-256 e3d6554a4e6c262fca98ce8263fb3c1d86d2c47c5f7e3e1fe5aa516367b3f599

Their exact design labels are co-cultured with MerTK/CD206neg or MerTK/CD206pos macrophages, crossed with macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor or none. All four are donor_status=requires_contributing_donor_model with the FLS and macrophage identifiers SA256A and SA259A. The exact interaction is therefore one contributing-donor context, not a four-donor study.

The four H features must be exactly IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end, and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end. Context audit features are MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, TREM2|NM_018965.3|Reference_end, APOE|NM_000041.3|Reference_end, C1QA|NM_015991.2|Reference_end, C1QB|NM_000491.3|Reference_end, and SPP1|NM_000582.2|Reference_end. Do not substitute symbols, merge duplicate rows, or zero-fill HBEGF or C1QC; neither has a matching E-MTAB-8873 feature row.

Use the two Mpos preInhibitor families only as tier/round checks: R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor versus R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos (archive hashes e14006cefdb3b642c3f280d3e888b3e16767e2b36288bb7029ce2e52d36c6a85 and 9868244d7d0171f5b994e1685111619a77d817fc54737b7aac98391931b0f98d), and R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor versus R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos (hashes 09bb1e81c247f251930c10ea8bfc25e651c01a8746a2fbe630d27dce4cb064a8 and 031a9813265d611f76eb2cfd787ced65208eedf544e79af4f8d4952f369673a3). They lack matched Mneg preInhibitor cells and are not exact inhibitor replications.

### E-MTAB-8316 generic-perturbation bound

Use [private-path]/E-MTAB-8316.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 9ceb4b7cf3d52d7f6e3800c827d491b174b646826fae9c6d1433c5d64b219645, and E-MTAB-8316.design.json, SHA-256 ca011580853bbea30b4f68f21bb5b017721c3e47bfefee6e9083b44da04c4c81. Required design columns are sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, other_donor_id, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata, and unit_definition. Use all 12 synovial membrane/monocyte rows, paired by donor_id plus other_donor_id specimen, giving six none/UNC106238 pairs nested in six monocyte donors and four FLS donor clusters. UNC106238 dose is 250 and all rows carry LPS 1 ng/mL. The archive lineage is MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz, SHA-256 510b69e449ed424adfbf225b8eeaf9faff1f8a973c76951612caf7ae69103228, and E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt, SHA-256 3e304fc612102181c9106532d42b010554f342b8529f6542c04169e50093ce74.

Use only the verified Ensembl feature IDs MERTK ENSG00000153208, MRC1 ENSG00000260314, TREM2 ENSG00000095970, C1QA ENSG00000173372, C1QB ENSG00000173369, C1QC ENSG00000159189, and APOE ENSG00000130203. Estimate C_8316(g)=log(UNC106238)-log(none) within each paired specimen, then summarize with pair/donor-cluster uncertainty. This source has no Mpos/Mneg context and no FLS H endpoint; it is a generic/state-marker bound, not an H-equivalent control.

### E-MTAB-8322 descriptive state proxy

Use [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36, E-MTAB-8322.design.json, SHA-256 4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da, and the source feature map [private-path]/SA220.genes.tsv, SHA-256 920b9e836ae82aeabe5b95932ac8a7795c6f03decff45381749e1e3cdad1f1fa. Required design columns are sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, other_donor_id, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata, source_name, and cells. Restrict to synovial membrane/macrophage rows and exact naive, remission, and resistant condition labels. Keep donor and repeated/related flags; exclude SA149/SA149P-type unresolved related rows from independent-donor inference. Use the seven verified Ensembl-to-symbol map entries for MERTK, MRC1, TREM2, C1QA, C1QB, C1QC, and APOE to form B_8322 as the mean source-local z-score, with remission-naive and remission-resistant contrasts. This is descriptive and cross-sectional, never efficacy and never joined arithmetically to H.

GSE95588 is explicitly deferred because its prepared GSM/donor lineage is not independently resolved. It contributes no output to this gate.

## Fixed primary estimand and decision thresholds

For each source, first verify that the prepared abundance matrix is nonnegative. Apply log1p once if and only if that check identifies raw abundance; otherwise use the documented prepared scale and record the decision. Fit feature-wise calibration mean and SD within the source calibration partition, excluding the four locked R1 primary samples from nuisance calibration. If any required feature, exact counterpart, or one-to-one counts/design join is missing, return structural_blocked and do not call that condition biological.

For E-MTAB-8873 define H_s=(z_IL6,s+z_MMP1,s+z_MMP3,s+z_MMP14,s)/4. The primary estimand is the finite source-local R1 interaction:

Delta_R1_exact = (H_Mpos,Inhibitor - H_Mpos,None) - (H_Mneg,Inhibitor - H_Mneg,None).

Positive Delta means a larger inhibitor-associated increase in the jointly MerTK/CD206-labelled Mpos context. It does not mean MerTK-specific harm.

Fix the assay-level materiality threshold before fitting at M_R1=0.5 source-local SD of H, where the SD is computed in the declared E-MTAB-8873 calibration partition. This is a practical assay signal threshold, not a clinical minimal important difference. Use a 95% contributor-aware conditional interval for Delta: parametric bootstrap of the declared source-local model, clustered by the available contributor/donor grouping, with the same variance regularization in every replicate. Because R1 has only one SA256A/SA259A contributor configuration, label this interval source-conditional and set donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; do not replace the interval with a donor t-test or treat cells as independent. The hierarchical sensitivity must repeat the gate under two predeclared weakly informative variance specifications. Support cannot be claimed if the two interval calculations disagree on materiality.

Define the primary flags:
- material_positive iff the fixed estimate is positive and the lower endpoint of both 95% intervals is greater than +M_R1;
- material_negative iff the upper endpoint of both intervals is less than -M_R1;
- component_coherent iff all four gene-specific Delta_g have the Delta sign and none is structurally missing;
- tier_coherent iff each estimable R2 and R5 Mpos preInhibitor component has the Delta sign, with at least 3 of 4 H components concordant in each tier; a missing counterpart is not concordance;
- rival_clear iff L_R1 or the generic-marker response C_8316 has a same-direction material interval at least as large as Delta, or a composition/contributor/FLS-only/cells sensitivity reverses the Delta sign;
- method_stable iff the fixed and hierarchical estimates have the same sign, both exceed M in the same direction, and the hierarchical fit has full required rank and no variance-boundary warning.

The decision is fixed as follows. supportive requires all structural checks, material_positive, component_coherent, tier_coherent, |L_R1| below M or materially smaller/opposite, rival_clear=false, and method_stable=true. Supportive authorizes only the orthogonal test described below. adverse requires structural checks plus material_negative, or rival_clear=true with the rival material and at least as compatible as Delta, or both tier checks materially reverse Delta, or a composition/contributor/component audit reverses Delta. adverse authorizes no MerTK-specific prioritization from this package. Every other case is inconclusive, including an interval spanning M, a missing counterpart, only one estimable tier, hierarchy rank/variance instability, or a source-conditional result that is not stable under the declared variance specifications. An imprecise null is not refutation.

The one authorization row must contain:
gate_id=R1_MerTK_CD206_source_local; estimate=Delta_R1_exact; interval_fixed and interval_hierarchical; threshold=M_R1; donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; component_coherent; tier_coherent; rival_clear; method_stable; structural_status; estimability; decision in {supportive, adverse, inconclusive}; and next_action in {run_orthogonal_factorial, do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals, resolve_curation_or_defer}. No prose conclusion may override this row.

## Donor-aware grouping and temporal/split rules

The primary R1 quartet is a locked estimand partition. It is never used for nuisance calibration, model selection, or claimed held-out replication. The exact quartet is grouped as one SA256A/SA259A contributor configuration; the SA260R conflict/reuse-sensitive rows remain a sensitivity audit and cannot create an independent R1 replicate. R2 and R5 remain grouped by round and contributing donor pair. FLS-only rows are handling baselines, not treated inhibitor controls. Mixed 1/4 and 3/4 rows are checked against predeclared weighted pure-row means, not refit to rescue the gate.

For E-MTAB-8316, keep each donor_id plus other_donor_id pair together in every fit and leave-one-pair-out sensitivity; repeated measurements within donor are averaged only at the declared pair level. For E-MTAB-8322, keep donor and related/repeated flags together, and exclude unresolved related donors from independent-donor inference. No source has a usable time field, so no temporal prediction split is claimed. The only cross-source operation is qualitative comparison of predeclared flags; no donor join, feature-scale pooling, or B_8322-H arithmetic is allowed.

## Matched alternatives before method selection

### Fixed-score baseline

Target: the exact Delta_R1_exact, A_R2_pre, A_R5_pre, L_R1, C_8316, and B_8322 contrasts. Inputs are the same selected counts/design rows and exact feature IDs above. Fit only source-local transform and z parameters using the declared calibration partition; preserve the R1 quartet as locked. Uncertainty is the fixed 95% conditional interval plus contributor/pair-grouped sensitivity. There is no independent donor holdout for R1; the auxiliary leave-one-pair/donor grouping is a sensitivity, not validation.

This baseline is primary because it is row-auditable, does not invent independent units, and leaves the estimand interpretable under sparse design. It can hide whether one gene or contributor drives H.

### Same-input hierarchical alternative

Target: the same Delta_g and H contrasts, with a decomposition of gene covariance, shared FLS inflammatory state, treatment-by-context effect, round/tier and contributor/context variance. Inputs, feature IDs, calibration rows, locked partition and group splits are identical to the fixed baseline. Fit separate source-stratified models: an E-MTAB-8873 multivariate partial-pooling model, a paired E-MTAB-8316 gene-specific model, and a donor-aware E-MTAB-8322 state model. No latent factor, donor effect, or parameter is shared across assays.

Estimate gene-specific treatment-by-context effects and recombine with the fixed H weights. Use parametric bootstrap/posterior simulation with variance specifications frozen before reading Delta. Return rank, variance-boundary, interval-width, contributor-variance share, and estimability flags. This alternative can reveal whether H coherence survives residual covariance and whether a contributor/context component dominates; it cannot separate MerTK from CD206, create independent R1 donors, prove engagement, or provide a functional endpoint.

Selection: retain the fixed score as the primary decision rule and the hierarchy as a predeclared scientific sensitivity, because the question is whether the gate is stable and interpretable, not whether a model predicts better. Defer neural or high-dimensional predictors: this package has no independent functional or clinical outcome, and extra predictive complexity cannot resolve target specificity. Revisit only after a validated held-out functional endpoint and independently measured MerTK/CD206 are available.

Resource estimate: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, at most 1,200 seconds for tabular fits and resampling. This is an unmeasured planning estimate. The panel and grouped models are small; a GPU is not scientifically useful for this design. A future high-dimensional functional assay may warrant a new resource estimate.

## Smallest orthogonal target-specific test

If the decision row is supportive, the minimum next experiment is one independent-donor-blocked FLS coculture factorial: MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle crossed with independently measured CD206-high versus CD206-low macrophage preparations, with a matched target-negative perturbation control. The minimum unit is the within-donor 2x2 contrast; donor number must be set by a pre-study power calculation and must not be represented by technical cells. Measure MerTK protein and CD206 protein independently, a direct MerTK engagement or validated proximal readout, viability, FLS H as a secondary transcript endpoint, and a functional FLS endpoint (invasion or matrix degradation) as the primary consequence endpoint. The target-by-context interaction is Tau=[Y(MerTK,CD206high)-Y(vehicle,CD206high)]-[Y(MerTK,CD206low)-Y(vehicle,CD206low)]. A target-specific functional claim requires engagement, a nonzero prespecified functional Tau with uncertainty excluding zero, no viability explanation, and no comparable target-negative effect. If only H changes, the conclusion remains transcript-proxy evidence.

If adverse, do not run a target-specific prioritization experiment on this package. The smallest follow-up is either expert-reviewed abandonment, or—only if external evidence justifies retaining the target—an independent measurement/curation check: MerTK and CD206 protein on the archived R1 material plus a matched Mpos/Mneg inhibitor/vehicle contrast. A generic or rival-dominated result cannot authorize the factorial.

If inconclusive, the smallest next action is to resolve the blocking item before functional escalation: verify exact counterparts and counts/design joins, obtain independent MerTK/CD206 measurements, and repeat the matched Mpos/Mneg inhibitor/vehicle contrast in donor-blocked material. If that resolves to supportive, run the same factorial; if not, defer or abandon. No missing value, unverified donor lineage, or model instability may be converted into a positive result.

Clinical safety, efficacy, target engagement, and treatment benefit require the orthogonal assay plus additional translational/clinical evidence. Automatic computation can check source binding, transforms, exact contrasts, thresholds, flags, intervals, and whether a conclusion matches the decision row. It cannot adjudicate protein identity, engagement, invasion assay validity, clinical benefit, or mechanistic causality.

## Falsification and interpretation

Structural failure is a packaging/design failure, not a biological null. The hypothesis is falsified as a useful source-local gate by a material adverse result, rival equivalence or dominance, reversal under composition/contributor/component audit, or failure of the exact estimand to be stable under the declared hierarchy. A supportive result supports only the next orthogonal test. An adverse result supports deprioritization or revision toward the rival explanation. An inconclusive result preserves uncertainty and specifies the missing evidence.

The principal unresolved limitation remains exact: the four R1 cells are one contributing-donor configuration and the Mpos/Mneg labels co-encode MerTK and CD206. E-MTAB-8316 lacks separated context and E-MTAB-8322 is a cross-sectional macrophage-state proxy. No configured source has protein, direct engagement, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, dose-response, time, or clinical outcome data. GSE95588 remains deferred because its GSM/donor lineage is unresolved.

## Three inspected works

# Episode 11: an orthogonal MerTK-by-CD206 decision gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment and planned follow-up assay. No biological fitting, screening, or result was executed in this episode. This is a complementary child of `candidate-62a1af5137ebbfa438046cf0`.

## Scientific opening and clinical decision

The strongest evidence-supported prior is that MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce a repair response in synovial fibroblasts [K1]. That prior makes MerTK clinically consequential: a MerTK-antagonist strategy could remove a protective macrophage–FLS interaction, whereas preservation or activation could be useful. The configured molecular source does not establish either direction.

The unresolved claim is narrower and falsifiable: in the exact E-MTAB-8873 R1 coculture, does macrophage pre-treatment labelled “MerTK inhibitor” produce a materially larger FLS inflammatory-transcript response in the jointly Mpos/CD206pos-labelled context than in the jointly Mneg/CD206neg-labelled context, after generic, LPS/context, component, composition and contributor checks? Even a positive answer is not a MerTK-specific causal or functional result because the context labels co-encode MerTK and CD206 and the R1 interaction is one contributing-donor configuration.

The important rival explanations are:

1. CD206 or a broader macrophage state, rather than MerTK, drives the interaction.
2. LPS/context handling, contributor composition, generic perturbation, or a treatment/measurement artifact drives it.
3. FLS-intrinsic cytokine heterogeneity produces the transcript pattern without functional damage. Local cytokine exposures are known to create distinct FLS states and matrix-metalloproteinase programs [K3]. A separate HBEGF-positive macrophage–FLS route can promote fibroblast invasiveness [K2], so a functional endpoint is needed before a target-specific prioritization decision.

The substantive advance is an operational bridge from a source-local transcript gate to the smallest independent target-specific test. It does not relabel the existing expression association as mechanism. It asks whether the molecular result is strong enough to spend experimental effort on MerTK, and specifies exactly what that next assay must show.

## Falsifiable hypothesis and estimand

### Molecular Harbor estimand

For each eligible E-MTAB-8873 sample, transform the prepared nonnegative abundance with one prespecified `log1p) transform. Within E-MTAB-8873, standardize each available FLS feature using the non-primary source calibration rows; do not use the locked R1 primary quartet to tune the score. Define

[
H = operatorname{mean}{z(IL6),z(MMP1),z(MMP3),z(MMP14)}.
]

The exact primary estimand is

[
Delta_{R1,exact} =
(H_{Mpos,Inhibitor}-H_{Mpos}) -
(H_{Mneg,Inhibitor}-H_{Mneg}).
]

Positive (Delta_{R1,exact}) means a larger inhibitor-associated increase in this FLS inflammatory-transcript proxy in the jointly Mpos/CD206pos-labelled context. It does not mean MerTK-specific harm.

The assay-level materiality threshold is fixed before fitting at (delta_H=0.5) within-source SD of (H). The primary molecular gate is:

- supportive only if the exact R1 estimand is structurally valid, (Delta_{R1,exact}geq 0.5), its contributor-aware 95% interval lies above (0), all four H components point in the same direction, the LPS/context contrast is below the materiality threshold, the generic perturbation bound is not comparably context-selective, and no composition, FLS-only, contributor or mixed-row audit reverses it;
- adverse if the exact interaction is at most (-0.5) with a 95% interval below (0), or if a generic/LPS/composition/component audit is at least as compatible with the observed direction;
- inconclusive otherwise, including an interval spanning the materiality region, non-identifiability, missing exact counterparts, or hierarchical instability.

For decision safety, a point estimate near 0.5 with a wide interval is not supportive. This threshold is a planning materiality rule, not a biological constant; its clinical relevance requires expert assay review.

Report, but do not pool into the primary estimand:

- (A_{R2,pre}=H[R2_Mpos_preInhibitor]-H[R2_Mpos]);
- (A_{R5,pre}=H[R5_Mpos_preInhibitor]-H[R5_Mpos]);
- the exact R1 pre-LPS context contrast;
- every H component;
- macrophage context markers;
- FLS-only rows, mixed-composition rows and cells-count sensitivity;
- donor/contributor and round/tier sensitivity.

R2/R5 preInhibitor rows are coherence checks only. They are not exact inhibitor replications and do not provide a matched Mneg interaction.

### Orthogonal target-specific estimand

After a supportive molecular gate, run an independent human RA synovial macrophage/type-B FLS assay with donor blocks. For each independent donor block, classify macrophage preparations by measured CD206-high versus CD206-low status and cross that context with a MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle. The minimal target-negative control receives the same perturbation in matched MerTK-negative or MerTK-below-assay-LOD macrophages; if that material cannot be obtained and verified, the target-specific claim is unavailable.

Let (Y) be a prespecified FLS functional endpoint such as viable-cell-normalized invasion or matrix degradation, with larger values meaning more damage, and standardize within donor to the pooled vehicle SD. Define

[
	au =
[Y(MerTK perturbation,CD206high)-Y(vehicle,CD206high)]
-
[Y(MerTK perturbation,CD206low)-Y(vehicle,CD206low)].
]

Use (delta_Y=0.5) pooled within-donor SD as the fixed functional materiality threshold. A target-specific functional result requires:

- (|hat	au|geq 0.5) and a donor-blocked 95% interval excluding (0);
- perturbation engagement shown by a validated MerTK protein/proximal pharmacodynamic readout in the intended cells;
- target-negative matched perturbation effect bounded within ([-0.2,0.2]) SD, or its 95% interval contained in that nuisance band;
- viability and cell-composition differences bounded by the same 0.2-SD nuisance rule (plus no expert-defined unacceptable absolute viability loss);
- concordance of the functional endpoint with, but not substitution by, the secondary FLS H transcript readout.

If (	au>0.5), MerTK inhibition selectively worsens FLS function in the CD206-high context: this argues against MerTK antagonism and supports preserving or activating the pathway, subject to further translational work. If (	au<-0.5), it supports an inhibitory direction in that context. If (|	au|<0.5), the interaction is not materially target-selective. None of these outcomes establishes clinical efficacy or safety.

## Analysis, splits and uncertainty

The locked R1 quartet is a primary estimand partition: it is excluded from nuisance calibration and is never described as held-out replication. R2/R5 and LPS families remain grouped by round/contributor. E-MTAB-8316 keeps each donor/specimen pair together. E-MTAB-8322 keeps donor and related/repeated flags together and excludes unresolved related rows from independent-donor inference. There is no cross-source fold or cross-source donor join.

The fixed baseline computes H, (Delta_{R1,exact}), the R2/R5 checks, LPS contrast, C8316 and B8322 directly on source-local scales. Uncertainty uses contributor-aware sign permutations and/or donor/cluster bootstrap; cells are never replicates. Report point estimates, 95% intervals, component effects, materiality status and an estimability flag. The primary output must include the exact row IDs, feature availability, transform, calibration partition, split groups and hashes.

### Same-input mechanistic/hierarchical alternative

Fit a source-stratified, cross-classified model to exactly the same rows, features, transforms, calibration partitions and grouping:

- E-MTAB-8873: gene-specific intercepts plus a shared FLS inflammatory factor, gene-specific residual loadings, context, treatment, round/tier and contributor/context effects; recombine gene-specific interaction estimates using the fixed H weights.
- E-MTAB-8316: gene-specific paired marker effects with specimen-pair and donor-cluster variation.
- E-MTAB-8322: gene-specific donor-aware state contrasts.

No latent factor, donor effect or parameter is shared across datasets. Random effects are used only where levels are estimable. The single-contributor R1 interaction remains flagged as one configuration; hierarchy cannot create independent donors or separate MerTK from CD206.

The fixed score is selected as primary because it is auditable and remains interpretable under sparse design. The hierarchical model is a substantive sensitivity analysis because it can reveal whether one H gene, contributor, residual covariance or context component drives the score and can quantify variance/identifiability. It is not chosen for a smaller p-value or prediction gain. Use parametric bootstrap or posterior simulation with weakly informative variance priors fixed before looking at (Delta); return a rank/variance instability warning rather than a forced decomposition.

Report method comparison on the same (Delta), R2/R5, LPS, C8316 and B8322 contrasts: component concordance, interval width, contributor/context variance share, rank/estimability and gate status. A planned output set is `source_compatibility.json`, `fixed_contrasts.csv`, `hierarchical_contrasts.csv`, `uncertainty.json`, `identifiability.json` and `decision.json`.

## Harbor compute and scientific deliverable

The future Harbor fitting target is the newly estimated source-local contrasts and their uncertainty, plus a same-input decomposition and explicit decision row. Completion requires all structural checks, both method outputs, the locked estimand, uncertainty intervals, component/control audits and one of supportive/adverse/inconclusive decisions. It does not require or claim a biological discovery.

The planned envelope is 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, and at most 1,200 seconds for tabular fitting and resampling. This is a planning estimate, not a measured runtime. The assay has 33/12/27 rows and a 445-feature panel for the primary source; GPU use is not scientifically useful for this small source-local model. The deployment has A100 GPUs available only through explicit allocation, but no GPU is requested here. A future high-dimensional imaging or functional assay would require a separate feasibility assessment; it is not silently substituted into this Harbor experiment.

The smallest scientifically useful check is therefore the fixed-score gate with the prespecified controls and an estimability report. If supportive, it changes the next action to the independent factorial below; if adverse, it stops target-specific prioritization; if inconclusive, it preserves the uncertainty and requests curation or expert assay review.

## Orthogonal decision matrix and interpretation

The future assay is not a replacement for Harbor computation. It needs independent donor blocks, measured CD206-high/low strata, target-negative matched material, MerTK engagement, viability/composition QC and a functional FLS endpoint. At least six independent RA donor blocks is a planning minimum for a donor-blocked pilot; final number, sorting strategy and target-negative availability require expert review and power assessment. Technical wells are nested within donor and cannot be counted as independent donors.

Interpret results as follows:

- Molecular supportive: authorize only this orthogonal factorial. It does not justify a clinical or target-specific claim by itself.
- Molecular adverse: if generic perturbation, LPS/context, composition, component or target-negative effects meet/exceed the pattern, do not prioritize MerTK-specific harm or inhibition. Seek a different target or curation.
- Molecular inconclusive: no change in target priority. If exact rows, control comparability or the hierarchical rank are unavailable, the correct conclusion is non-identifiability; a wide interval is not refutation.
- Orthogonal supportive for MerTK specificity: engagement passes, target-negative and viability nuisance bounds pass, and (|	au|geq0.5) with a donor-blocked interval excluding zero. The sign chooses preservation/activation versus inhibition as the next target direction, but clinical translation needs another study.
- Orthogonal adverse: no material (	au), target-negative/generic response, failed engagement, or viability/composition explanation. Abandon or revise the MerTK-specific direction.
- Orthogonal inconclusive: failed or unavailable target-negative material, failed engagement, insufficient independent donors, interval spanning ([-0.5,0.5]), or conflicting functional and transcript outcomes. Do not convert it into a null or a clinical recommendation.

Automatic computation can check source paths/hashes, exact joins, feature availability, estimands, split integrity, contrasts, intervals and whether a conclusion follows the declared decision table. It cannot establish clinical adjudication, direct molecular engagement, target specificity when controls are unavailable, functional harm if the assay is invalid, or clinical benefit. Those require expert assay review and a separate translational study.

## Alternatives not chosen and revisit criteria

Pooling exact R1 inhibitor with R2/R5 preInhibitor is rejected because exposure labels and matched contexts differ; revisit only after exposure-equivalence and matched Mneg curation. Calling the R1 interaction MerTK-specific is rejected because Mpos/Mneg jointly encode MerTK/CD206; revisit only after independent protein measurement, perturbation and target-negative controls. Cross-source B-H arithmetic is prohibited because assays, namespaces, donors and estimands differ. A neural predictor is deferred because the available sources lack an independent clinical or functional outcome and a predictor cannot resolve MerTK specificity; revisit with a validated held-out functional outcome. GSE95588 is deferred until GSM/donor lineage is independently resolved. The hierarchical alternative is retained as a scientific sensitivity model, not promoted to the primary decision.

## Three inspected works

[K1] Alivernini S, MacDonald L, Elmesmari A, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020. DOI: 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text provider response was inspected for the abstract and relevant article passages. It supports the remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophage prior and bounds, rather than proves, the present target-specific claim.

[K2] Kuo D, Ding J, Cohn IS, Zhang F, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019. DOI: 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587; PMID: 31068444. Europe PMC metadata/abstract only was inspected; publisher full text and supplementary methods are not claimed here. It supplies a consequential macrophage–FLS functional rival.

[K3] Smith MH, Gao VR, Periyakoil PK, et al. “Drivers of heterogeneity in synovial fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Immunology, 2023. DOI: 10.1038/s41590-023-01527-9. Full-text provider response passages were inspected. It supports cytokine/context-driven FLS heterogeneity and bounds H as a transcript proxy.

The exact three evidence attachments are `evidence-k1-inspected.json`, `evidence-k2-inspected.json` and `evidence-k3-inspected.json`; their hashes and receipts are bound in `key-references.json`. No other work is used as a key reference.

### Same-input mechanistic/hierarchical alternative

Fit a source-stratified, cross-classified model to exactly the same rows, features, transforms, calibration partitions and grouping:

- E-MTAB-8873: gene-specific intercepts plus a shared FLS inflammatory factor, gene-specific residual loadings, context, treatment, round/tier and contributor/context effects; recombine gene-specific interaction estimates using the fixed H weights.
- E-MTAB-8316: gene-specific paired marker effects with specimen-pair and donor-cluster variation.
- E-MTAB-8322: gene-specific donor-aware state contrasts.

No latent factor, donor effect or parameter is shared across datasets. Random effects are used only where levels are estimable. The single-contributor R1 interaction remains flagged as one configuration; hierarchy cannot create independent donors or separate MerTK from CD206.

The fixed score is selected as primary because it is auditable and remains interpretable under sparse design. The hierarchical model is a substantive sensitivity analysis because it can reveal whether one H gene, contributor, residual covariance or context component drives the score and can quantify variance/identifiability. It is not chosen for a smaller p-value or prediction gain. Use parametric bootstrap or posterior simulation with weakly informative variance priors fixed before looking at (Delta); return a rank/variance instability warning rather than a forced decomposition.

The future Harbor fitting target is the newly estimated source-local contrasts and their uncertainty, plus a same-input decomposition and explicit decision row. Completion requires all structural checks, both method outputs, the locked estimand, uncertainty intervals, component/control audits and one of supportive/adverse/inconclusive decisions. It does not require or claim a biological discovery.

The planned envelope is 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, and at most 1,200 seconds for tabular fitting and resampling. This is a planning estimate, not a measured runtime. The assay has 33/12/27 rows and a 445-feature panel for the primary source; GPU use is not scientifically useful for this small source-local model. The deployment has A100 GPUs available only through explicit allocation, but no GPU is requested here. A future high-dimensional imaging or functional assay would require a separate feasibility assessment; it is not silently substituted into this Harbor experiment.

The smallest scientifically useful check is therefore the fixed-score gate with the prespecified controls and an estimability report. If supportive, it changes the next action to the independent factorial below; if adverse, it stops target-specific prioritization; if inconclusive, it preserves the uncertainty and requests curation or expert assay review.

## Orthogonal decision matrix and interpretation

The future assay is not a replacement for Harbor computation. It needs independent donor blocks, measured CD206-high/low strata, target-negative matched material, MerTK engagement, viability/composition QC and a functional FLS endpoint. At least six independent RA donor blocks is a planning minimum for a donor-blocked pilot; final number, sorting strategy and target-negative availability require expert review and power assessment. Technical wells are nested within donor and cannot be counted as independent donors.

Interpret results as follows:

- Molecular supportive: authorize only this orthogonal factorial. It does not justify a clinical or target-specific claim by itself.
- Molecular adverse: if generic perturbation, LPS/context, composition, component or target-negative effects meet/exceed the pattern, do not prioritize MerTK-specific harm or inhibition. Seek a different target or curation.
- Molecular inconclusive: no change in target priority. If exact rows, control comparability or the hierarchical rank are unavailable, the correct conclusion is non-identifiability; a wide interval is not refutation.
- Orthogonal supportive for MerTK specificity: engagement passes, target-negative and viability nuisance bounds pass, and (|tauau|>=0.5) with a donor-blocked interval excluding zero. The sign chooses preservation/activation versus inhibition as the next target direction, but clinical translation needs another study.
- Orthogonal adverse: no material (tauau), target-negative/generic response, failed engagement, or viability/composition explanation. Abandon or revise the MerTK-specific direction.
- Orthogonal inconclusive: failed or unavailable target-negative material, failed engagement, insufficient independent donors, interval spanning ([-0.5,0.5]), or conflicting functional and transcript outcomes. Do not convert it into a null or a clinical recommendation.

Automatic computation can check source paths/hashes, exact joins, feature availability, estimands, split integrity, contrasts, intervals and whether a conclusion follows the declared decision table. It cannot establish clinical adjudication, direct molecular engagement, target specificity when controls are unavailable, functional harm if the assay is invalid, or clinical benefit. Those require expert assay review and a separate translational study.

## Alternatives not chosen and revisit criteria

Pooling exact R1 inhibitor with R2/R5 preInhibitor is rejected because exposure labels and matched contexts differ; revisit only after exposure-equivalence and matched Mneg curation. Calling the R1 interaction MerTK-specific is rejected because Mpos/Mneg jointly encode MerTK/CD206; revisit only after independent protein measurement, perturbation and target-negative controls. Cross-source B-H arithmetic is prohibited because assays, namespaces, donors and estimands differ. A neural predictor is deferred because the available sources lack an independent clinical or functional outcome and a predictor cannot resolve MerTK specificity; revisit with a validated held-out functional outcome. GSE95588 is deferred until GSM/donor lineage is independently resolved. The hierarchical alternative is retained as a scientific sensitivity model, not promoted to the primary decision.

[K1] Alivernini S, MacDonald L, Elmesmari A, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020. DOI: 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text provider response was inspected for the abstract and relevant article passages. It supports the remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophage prior and bounds, rather than proves, the present target-specific claim.

[K2] Kuo D, Ding J, Cohn IS, Zhang F, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019. DOI: 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587; PMID: 31068444. Europe PMC metadata/abstract only was inspected; publisher full text and supplementary methods are not claimed here. It supplies a consequential macrophage–FLS functional rival.

[K3] Smith MH, Gao VR, Periyakoil PK, et al. “Drivers of heterogeneity in synovial fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Immunology, 2023. DOI: 10.1038/s41590-023-01527-9. Full-text provider response passages were inspected. It supports cytokine/context-driven FLS heterogeneity and bounds H as a transcript proxy.

## Scientific opening and clinical decision

The strongest evidence-supported prior is that MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce a repair response in synovial fibroblasts [K1]. That prior makes MerTK clinically consequential: a MerTK-antagonist strategy could remove a protective macrophage–FLS interaction, whereas preservation or activation could be useful. The configured molecular source does not establish either direction.

The unresolved claim is narrower and falsifiable: in the exact E-MTAB-8873 R1 coculture, does macrophage pre-treatment labelled “MerTK inhibitor” produce a materially larger FLS inflammatory-transcript response in the jointly Mpos/CD206pos-labelled context than in the jointly Mneg/CD206neg-labelled context, after generic, LPS/context, component, composition and contributor checks? Even a positive answer is not a MerTK-specific causal or functional result because the context labels co-encode MerTK and CD206 and the R1 interaction is one contributing-donor configuration.

The important rival explanations are:

1. CD206 or a broader macrophage state, rather than MerTK, drives the interaction.
2. LPS/context handling, contributor composition, generic perturbation, or a treatment/measurement artifact drives it.
3. FLS-intrinsic cytokine heterogeneity produces the transcript pattern without functional damage. Local cytokine exposures are known to create distinct FLS states and matrix-metalloproteinase programs [K3]. A separate HBEGF-positive macrophage–FLS route can promote fibroblast invasiveness [K2], so a functional endpoint is needed before a target-specific prioritization decision.

The substantive advance is an operational bridge from a source-local transcript gate to the smallest independent target-specific test. It does not relabel the existing expression association as mechanism. It asks whether the molecular result is strong enough to spend experimental effort on MerTK, and specifies exactly what that next assay must show.

The donor/GSM lineage is not independently resolved enough for an independent transferability claim; deferral is not evidence of absence.

## Analysis, splits and uncertainty

The locked R1 quartet is a primary estimand partition: it is excluded from nuisance calibration and is never described as held-out replication. R2/R5 and LPS families remain grouped by round/contributor. E-MTAB-8316 keeps each donor/specimen pair together. E-MTAB-8322 keeps donor and related/repeated flags together and excludes unresolved related rows from independent-donor inference. There is no cross-source fold or cross-source donor join.

The fixed baseline computes H, (Delta_{R1,exact}), the R2/R5 checks, LPS contrast, C8316 and B8322 directly on source-local scales. Uncertainty uses contributor-aware sign permutations and/or donor/cluster bootstrap; cells are never replicates. Report point estimates, 95% intervals, component effects, materiality status and an estimability flag. The primary output must include the exact row IDs, feature availability, transform, calibration partition, split groups and hashes.

### Same-input mechanistic/hierarchical alternative

Fit a source-stratified, cross-classified model to exactly the same rows, features, transforms, calibration partitions and grouping:

- E-MTAB-8873: gene-specific intercepts plus a shared FLS inflammatory factor, gene-specific residual loadings, context, treatment, round/tier and contributor/context effects; recombine gene-specific interaction estimates using the fixed H weights.
- E-MTAB-8316: gene-specific paired marker effects with specimen-pair and donor-cluster variation.
- E-MTAB-8322: gene-specific donor-aware state contrasts.

No latent factor, donor effect or parameter is shared across datasets. Random effects are used only where levels are estimable. The single-contributor R1 interaction remains flagged as one configuration; hierarchy cannot create independent donors or separate MerTK from CD206.

The fixed score is selected as primary because it is auditable and remains interpretable under sparse design. The hierarchical model is a substantive sensitivity analysis because it can reveal whether one H gene, contributor, residual covariance or context component drives the score and can quantify variance/identifiability. It is not chosen for a smaller p-value or prediction gain. Use parametric bootstrap or posterior simulation with weakly informative variance priors fixed before looking at (Delta); return a rank/variance instability warning rather than a forced decomposition.

Report method comparison on the same (Delta), R2/R5, LPS, C8316 and B8322 contrasts: component concordance, interval width, contributor/context variance share, rank/estimability and gate status. A planned output set is `source_compatibility.json`, `fixed_contrasts.csv`, `hierarchical_contrasts.csv`, `uncertainty.json`, `identifiability.json` and `decision.json`.

## Harbor compute and scientific deliverable

The future Harbor fitting target is the newly estimated source-local contrasts and their uncertainty, plus a same-input decomposition and explicit decision row. Completion requires all structural checks, both method outputs, the locked estimand, uncertainty intervals, component/control audits and one of supportive/adverse/inconclusive decisions. It does not require or claim a biological discovery.

The planned envelope is 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, and at most 1,200 seconds for tabular fitting and resampling. This is a planning estimate, not a measured runtime. The assay has 33/12/27 rows and a 445-feature panel for the primary source; GPU use is not scientifically useful for this small source-local model. The deployment has A100 GPUs available only through explicit allocation, but no GPU is requested here. A future high-dimensional imaging or functional assay would require a separate feasibility assessment; it is not silently substituted into this Harbor experiment.

The smallest scientifically useful check is therefore the fixed-score gate with the prespecified controls and an estimability report. If supportive, it changes the next action to the independent factorial below; if adverse, it stops target-specific prioritization; if inconclusive, it preserves the uncertainty and requests curation or expert assay review.

## Orthogonal decision matrix and interpretation

The future assay is not a replacement for Harbor computation. It needs independent donor blocks, measured CD206-high/low strata, target-negative matched material, MerTK engagement, viability/composition QC and a functional FLS endpoint. At least six independent RA donor blocks is a planning minimum for a donor-blocked pilot; final number, sorting strategy and target-negative availability require expert review and power assessment. Technical wells are nested within donor and cannot be counted as independent donors.

Interpret results as follows:

- Molecular supportive: authorize only this orthogonal factorial. It does not justify a clinical or target-specific claim by itself.
- Molecular adverse: if generic perturbation, LPS/context, composition, component or target-negative effects meet/exceed the pattern, do not prioritize MerTK-specific harm or inhibition. Seek a different target or curation.
- Molecular inconclusive: no change in target priority. If exact rows, control comparability or the hierarchical rank are unavailable, the correct conclusion is non-identifiability; a wide interval is not refutation.
- Orthogonal supportive for MerTK specificity: engagement passes, target-negative and viability nuisance bounds pass, and (|tau|>=0.5) with a donor-blocked interval excluding zero. The sign chooses preservation/activation versus inhibition as the next target direction, but clinical translation needs another study.
- Orthogonal adverse: no material (tau), target-negative/generic response, failed engagement, or viability/composition explanation. Abandon or revise the MerTK-specific direction.
- Orthogonal inconclusive: failed or unavailable target-negative material, failed engagement, insufficient independent donors, interval spanning ([-0.5,0.5]), or conflicting functional and transcript outcomes. Do not convert it into a null or a clinical recommendation.

Automatic computation can check source paths/hashes, exact joins, feature availability, estimands, split integrity, contrasts, intervals and whether a conclusion follows the declared decision table. It cannot establish clinical adjudication, direct molecular engagement, target specificity when controls are unavailable, functional harm if the assay is invalid, or clinical benefit. Those require expert assay review and a separate translational study.

## Alternatives not chosen and revisit criteria

Pooling exact R1 inhibitor with R2/R5 preInhibitor is rejected because exposure labels and matched contexts differ; revisit only after exposure-equivalence and matched Mneg curation. Calling the R1 interaction MerTK-specific is rejected because Mpos/Mneg jointly encode MerTK/CD206; revisit only after independent protein measurement, perturbation and target-negative controls. Cross-source B-H arithmetic is prohibited because assays, namespaces, donors and estimands differ. A neural predictor is deferred because the available sources lack an independent clinical or functional outcome and a predictor cannot resolve MerTK specificity; revisit with a validated held-out functional outcome. GSE95588 is deferred until GSM/donor lineage is independently resolved. The hierarchical alternative is retained as a scientific sensitivity model, not promoted to the primary decision.

## Three inspected works

[K1] Alivernini S, MacDonald L, Elmesmari A, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020. DOI: 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text provider response was inspected for the abstract and relevant article passages. It supports the remission-associated MerTK-positive macrophage prior and bounds, rather than proves, the present target-specific claim.

[K2] Kuo D, Ding J, Cohn IS, Zhang F, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019. DOI: 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587; PMID: 31068444. Europe PMC metadata/abstract only was inspected; publisher full text and supplementary methods are not claimed here. It supplies a consequential macrophage–FLS functional rival.

[K3] Smith MH, Gao VR, Periyakoil PK, et al. “Drivers of heterogeneity in synovial fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Immunology, 2023. DOI: 10.1038/s41590-023-01527-9. Full-text provider response passages were inspected. It supports cytokine/context-driven FLS heterogeneity and bounds H as a transcript proxy.

The exact three evidence attachments are `evidence-k1-inspected.json`, `evidence-k2-inspected.json` and `evidence-k3-inspected.json`; their hashes and receipts are bound in `key-references.json`. No other work is used as a key reference.
