# Episode 12 crossover: assay-structured transferability of the MerTK/CD206 gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No source scan, biological fitting, screening, or result was executed in this branch. Parents: candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 and candidate-ba3ec15ac0a3e2c458d36ef3.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and advance

The leading evidence-supported claim is bounded: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states can accompany remission/repair biology [K1], macrophage-to-FLS communication has a consequential HBEGF/invasiveness rival [K2], and FLS inflammatory states are strongly shaped by local cytokine context [K3]. In the configured E-MTAB-8873 data, the R1 inhibitor contrast is a source-local interaction in an Mpos/Mneg label that jointly encodes MerTK/CD206 and uses one SA256A/SA259A contributing-donor configuration. The GSE95588 assay has two coculture rounds and P-block labels but unresolved donor identity. E-MTAB-8316 has paired UNC106238/none monocyte samples but no Mpos/Mneg context or FLS endpoint.

The unresolved claim is not “the signal predicts elsewhere.” It is: does the R1 context-associated perturbation pattern have assay-structured transferability that survives a distinct fibroblast-plus-TNF coculture design and is not equally represented by matched generic drug/context effects or a marker response in a separate monocyte assay? Resolution would change whether the next target-specific experiment is run, deferred for curation, or abandoned in favor of generic/context explanations.

Falsifiable hypothesis: conditional on a structurally estimable, material, component-coherent E-MTAB-8873 R1 anchor, GSE95588 will show a same-direction, component-coherent fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in the source-local MerTK/CD206 marker panel B_GSE and an interpretable relation to H_GSE across both recorded rounds, while A77 and naproxen will not produce an equally coherent context interaction. The E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238-versus-none response will not show a stronger generic, same-direction marker-panel response that makes the anchor less target-specific. A failure of either transferability coherence, generic-perturbation separation, or method stability falsifies this as a useful gate; it does not prove MerTK absence.

The substantive advance over both parents is an assay-specific estimand and a staged authorization rule. “Transferable” means a predeclared source-local fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in GSE95588, not pooled effect-size agreement, donor generalization, or predictive performance. GSE rounds/P blocks are explicitly descriptive because donor_id is null/unresolved. No donor IDs or feature rows are joined across sources.

## Competing explanations and discriminating observations

The strongest rival is assay/context composition: TNF and fibroblast exposure may create the marker and inflammatory pattern without any MerTK-specific action. A second is generic perturbation: A77, naproxen, or UNC106238 may alter the same state markers through broad assay effects. A third is measurement/co-encoding: MERTK and MRC1/CD206 labels may be correlated state annotations rather than independently measured target and context. A fourth is contributor reuse or assay mismatch: apparent repeated rounds/P blocks may be the same biological material, and the GSE macrophage RNA endpoint is not the E-MTAB-8873 FLS endpoint. K2 adds a biologically consequential HBEGF/macrophage-FLS rival, but HBEGF is unavailable in E-MTAB-8873 and is not imputed.

The observations are separated as follows.

- A coherent R1 Delta with four H components, stable contributor-aware uncertainty, and no LPS/composition reversal is an anchor observation only.
- Same-direction I_B and I_H in both GSE95588 coculture rounds, with at least 5/7 B components and 3/4 H components concordant per round, is compatible with assay-structured context transfer. It is not independent-donor replication because all eight donor IDs are unresolved.
- A comparable or stronger matched A77/naproxen J interaction in the same GSE treatment matrix favors generic/context perturbation.
- A coherent E-MTAB-8316 C_8316 response across the seven state markers is a generic/state-marker warning, not a negative control for MerTK specificity; a null there does not establish specificity.
- A reversal in one component, round, P block, contributor audit, or hierarchical sensitivity makes the gate adverse or inconclusive according to the staged rules below.
- No configured result establishes target engagement, CD206 independence, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, causal treatment effect, or clinical benefit.

## Exact data binding, population and temporal boundary

All source files are read-only. Use the catalog at [private-path]/catalog.json, SHA-256 162ddf0148975035ee641ae75a2666bf44a7b458b050d79370ee9f550953312f, and the prepared assay registry at [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f. The snapshot boundary is core-molecular-20261003. No bound design has a usable longitudinal time field; recorded treatment, condition, LPS/TNF and protocol labels define assay exposure, not a clinical time course.

For every prepared matrix, join only counts.header.sample_id = design.sample_id, require one-to-one selected header/design membership, and retain source-specific donor/specimen namespaces. Never join donor IDs across sources. Never join or pool the E-MTAB-8316 Ensembl namespace with the GSE95588 gene-symbol namespace or the E-MTAB-8873 RefSeq-like feature namespace.

### Anchor: E-MTAB-8873

Use prepared counts [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz (SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f) and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json (SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4). Stage 0 — structural and namespace gate. Verify all declared paths/hashes, nonnegative matrix/transform decisions, exact feature availability, no duplicated feature rows, selected header/design bijections, exact sample membership, and no use of excluded GSE Donor2 rows. Structural failure is a packaging/design failure, not a biological null.

Stage 1 — anchor gate. Estimate Delta_R1_exact and its four component effects with the parent’s locked threshold M_8873=0.5 source-local SD and contributor-aware fixed plus hierarchical 95% intervals. Require component coherence and no reversal by the predeclared R2/R5 tier, LPS, mixed/composition, or contributor audits. If the anchor is adverse, do not authorize transferability as support for MerTK; if anchor is inconclusive, report the transferability result descriptively but set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer.

Stage 2 — transferability estimand. Within the GSE coculture matrix, fit source-local scores and estimate I_B,1/I_B,2, I_H,1/I_H,2 plus all component effects. Adverse requires structural validity plus a material anchor reversal, transferability reversal/component failure, or a generic rival that is material and at least as compatible within its own assay. Set next_action=do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals. Inconclusive includes missing counterparts/features, interval spanning materiality, r1/r2 disagreement, unresolved rank/variance, only one estimable block, or unresolved donor identity being essential to the requested claim. gate_id=MerTK_CD206_assay_transferability_v1; anchor_status; I_B_1/I_B_2 and I_H_1/I_H_2 estimates and intervals; J_A77/J_Nap block flags; C_8316 component flag; component_coherent; assay_block_consistent; donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; generic_rival_clear; method_stable; structural_status; estimability; decision in {supportive, adverse, inconclusive}; and next_action in {run_orthogonal_factorial, do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals, resolve_curation_or_defer}. ## Baseline and substantive same-input alternative

The simple baseline is the primary auditable estimator. Inputs are exactly the selected rows/features above, with source-local log/scale handling and z parameters fitted within each source matrix. It computes Delta_R1_exact, I_q,r, J_q,p,d and C_8316 directly; uncertainty is contributor/pair/block-aware bootstrap or exact block sign sensitivity, never cell-level replication. Its advantage is transparent estimands under unresolved donors; it can conceal whether one gene or covariance drives the score.

The substantive alternative fits source-stratified multivariate hierarchical sensitivities on exactly the same rows, features, joins, grouping and outcomes: gene-specific effects plus a B_GSE factor and H_GSE factor in the eight-row coculture block model; paired gene-specific J terms with P-block effects in the 28-row drug model; and paired gene-specific C terms with donor/specimen effects in E-MTAB-8316. The future solver must newly fit/estimate source-local transforms, feature/component effects, Delta_R1_exact, I_B/I_H, J_A77/J_Nap, C_8316, uncertainty and method diagnostics, then write source_compatibility.json, output/transferability_gate.json and a reproducible decision row. # Episode 12 crossover: assay-structured transferability of the MerTK/CD206 gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No source scan, biological fitting, screening, or result was executed in this branch. Parents: candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 and candidate-ba3ec15ac0a3e2c458d36ef3.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and advance

The leading evidence-supported claim is bounded: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states can accompany remission/repair biology [K1], macrophage-to-FLS communication has a consequential HBEGF/invasiveness rival [K2], and FLS inflammatory states are strongly shaped by local cytokine context [K3]. In the configured E-MTAB-8873 data, the R1 inhibitor contrast is a source-local interaction in an Mpos/Mneg label that jointly encodes MerTK/CD206 and uses one SA256A/SA259A contributing-donor configuration. The GSE95588 assay has two coculture rounds and P-block labels but unresolved donor identity. E-MTAB-8316 has paired UNC106238/none monocyte samples but no Mpos/Mneg context or FLS endpoint.

The unresolved claim is not “the signal predicts elsewhere.” It is: does the R1 context-associated perturbation pattern have assay-structured transferability that survives a distinct fibroblast-plus-TNF coculture design and is not equally represented by matched generic drug/context effects or a marker response in a separate monocyte assay? Resolution would change whether the next target-specific experiment is run, deferred for curation, or abandoned in favor of generic/context explanations.

Falsifiable hypothesis: conditional on a structurally estimable, material, component-coherent E-MTAB-8873 R1 anchor, GSE95588 will show a same-direction, component-coherent fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in the source-local MerTK/CD206 marker panel B_GSE and an interpretable relation to H_GSE across both recorded rounds, while A77 and naproxen will not produce an equally coherent context interaction. The E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238-versus-none response will not show a stronger generic, same-direction marker-panel response that makes the anchor less target-specific. A failure of either transferability coherence, generic-perturbation separation, or method stability falsifies this as a useful gate; it does not prove MerTK absence.

The substantive advance over both parents is an assay-specific estimand and a staged authorization rule. “Transferable” means a predeclared source-local fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in GSE95588, not pooled effect-size agreement, donor generalization, or predictive performance. GSE rounds/P blocks are explicitly descriptive because donor_id is null/unresolved. No donor IDs or feature rows are joined across sources.

## Competing explanations and discriminating observations

The strongest rival is assay/context composition: TNF and fibroblast exposure may create the marker and inflammatory pattern without any MerTK-specific action. A second is generic perturbation: A77, naproxen, or UNC106238 may alter the same state markers through broad assay effects. A third is measurement/co-encoding: MERTK and MRC1/CD206 labels may be correlated state annotations rather than independently measured target and context. A fourth is contributor reuse or assay mismatch: apparent repeated rounds/P blocks may be the same biological material, and the GSE macrophage RNA endpoint is not the E-MTAB-8873 FLS endpoint. K2 adds a biologically consequential HBEGF/macrophage-FLS rival, but HBEGF is unavailable in E-MTAB-8873 and is not imputed.

The observations are separated as follows.

- A coherent R1 Delta with four H components, stable contributor-aware uncertainty, and no LPS/composition reversal is an anchor observation only.
- Same-direction I_B and I_H in both GSE95588 coculture rounds, with at least 5/7 B components and 3/4 H components concordant per round, is compatible with assay-structured context transfer. It is not independent-donor replication because all eight donor IDs are unresolved.
- A comparable or stronger matched A77/naproxen J interaction in the same GSE treatment matrix favors generic/context perturbation.
- A coherent E-MTAB-8316 C_8316 response across the seven state markers is a generic/state-marker warning, not a negative control for MerTK specificity; a null there does not establish specificity.
- A reversal in one component, round, P block, contributor audit, or hierarchical sensitivity makes the gate adverse or inconclusive according to the staged rules below.
- No configured result establishes target engagement, CD206 independence, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, causal treatment effect, or clinical benefit.

Supportive transferability requires: Stage 0 passes; Stage 1 is supportive; Stage 2 passes; the GSE hierarchy does not overturn the block pattern; Stage 3 generic_rival_clear=false; and all missing evidence is explicitly recorded. This authorizes only the smallest independent MerTK-by-CD206 functional assay, not target prioritization as a clinical conclusion.

Adverse requires structural validity plus a material anchor reversal, transferability reversal/component failure, or a generic rival that is material and at least as compatible within its own assay. Set next_action=do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals. Inconclusive includes missing counterparts/features, interval spanning materiality, r1/r2 disagreement, unresolved rank/variance, only one estimable block, or unresolved donor identity being essential to the requested claim. Set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer. An imprecise null is not refutation.

The machine-readable output must contain one gate row:
gate_id=MerTK_CD206_assay_transferability_v1; anchor_status; I_B_1/I_B_2 and I_H_1/I_H_2 estimates and intervals; J_A77/J_Nap block flags; C_8316 component flag; component_coherent; assay_block_consistent; donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; generic_rival_clear; method_stable; structural_status; estimability; decision in {supportive, adverse, inconclusive}; and next_action in {run_orthogonal_factorial, do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals, resolve_curation_or_defer}. Conclusions must be linked to this row and computed outputs.

## Baseline and substantive same-input alternative

The simple baseline is the primary auditable estimator. Inputs are exactly the selected rows/features above, with source-local log/scale handling and z parameters fitted within each source matrix. It computes Delta_R1_exact, I_q,r, J_q,p,d and C_8316 directly; uncertainty is contributor/pair/block-aware bootstrap or exact block sign sensitivity, never cell-level replication. Its advantage is transparent estimands under unresolved donors; it can conceal whether one gene or covariance drives the score.

The substantive alternative fits source-stratified multivariate hierarchical sensitivities on exactly the same rows, features, joins, grouping and outcomes: gene-specific effects plus a B_GSE factor and H_GSE factor in the eight-row coculture block model; paired gene-specific J terms with P-block effects in the 28-row drug model; and paired gene-specific C terms with donor/specimen effects in E-MTAB-8316. No latent factor, donor effect, or scale is shared across sources. Use two predeclared weakly informative variance specifications and parametric bootstrap/posterior simulation. Return gene loadings, residual covariance, block/contributor variance share, interval width, rank, variance-boundary and estimability flags. This alternative can reveal a measurement/co-encoding or single-gene driver hidden by the score baseline; it cannot create donor identity, separate MerTK from CD206, or add a functional endpoint.

Freeze the split before fitting: R1 is a locked estimand partition excluded from nuisance calibration and never held out replication; GSE r1/r2 stay grouped by round; GSE P blocks keep all paired conditions together; E-MTAB-8316 keeps donor_id+other_donor_id specimen pairs together. There is no predictive accuracy estimand or clinical outcome. Retain the baseline as primary because the scientific question is transferability and rival discrimination, not prediction. Defer neural/high-dimensional models: without a held-out functional outcome they add complexity but cannot resolve target specificity. Revisit only after independent MerTK/CD206 protein and functional measurements exist.

Planned resource envelope: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, at most 1,200 seconds for tabular transforms, grouped resampling and hierarchical sensitivity. This is an unmeasured planning estimate. A GPU is not scientifically useful for these small structured matrices; that is a resource judgment, not a blanket method exclusion.

## Actual scientific deliverable and unavailable evidence

The future solver must newly fit/estimate source-local transforms, feature/component effects, Delta_R1_exact, I_B/I_H, J_A77/J_Nap, C_8316, uncertainty and method diagnostics, then write source_compatibility.json, output/transferability_gate.json and a reproducible decision row. Completion is these computed outputs plus a conclusion that matches the row—not a favorable hypothesis result. No screening job was run here.

Unavailable or essential evidence includes independent GSE donor identity, MerTK/CD206 protein or direct engagement, CD206-independent perturbation, target-negative matched perturbation, FLS viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, dose-response, time, spatial context and clinical outcomes. HBEGF is absent from the E-MTAB-8873 feature panel despite being a literature rival. E-MTAB-8316 has no FLS endpoint and GSE95588 measures macrophage RNA, so neither is an H-equivalent replication. No automatic verifier can establish protein identity, target engagement, mechanism or clinical benefit; it can check joins, transforms, exact contrasts, thresholds, flags, uncertainty plumbing and conclusion-row consistency.

If supportive, run an independent-donor randomized/blinded factorial of MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle crossed with independently measured CD206-high/low macrophages and a matched target-negative perturbation. Measure MerTK/CD206 protein, direct engagement or validated proximal readout, viability, FLS H as secondary, and invasion or matrix degradation as primary functional outcome. If adverse, stop MerTK-specific prioritization from this package and review generic/context rival evidence. If inconclusive, resolve curation or repeat a donor-blocked assay before escalation. None of these configured matrices can support a clinical treatment claim.

[K2] Kuo et al., Science Translational Medicine (2019): inspected Europe PMC metadata/abstract response only; full text and supplementary methods were not inspected. It supplies the HBEGF/FLS invasiveness rival, while HBEGF is unavailable in the configured panel.

[K3] Smith et al., Nature Immunology (2023): inspected provider full-text response passages including abstract; cytokine/context-driven FLS heterogeneity bounds H as a transcript proxy.

The attached key-references.json has exactly these three distinct works, and the attached UTF-8 evidence snapshots preserve the inspected source excerpts and hashes.

# Episode 12 crossover: assay-structured transferability of the MerTK/CD206 gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No source scan, biological fitting, screening, or result was executed in this branch. Parents: candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 and candidate-ba3ec15ac0a3e2c458d36ef3.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and advance

The leading evidence-supported claim is bounded: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states can accompany remission/repair biology [K1], macrophage-to-FLS communication has a consequential HBEGF/invasiveness rival [K2], and FLS inflammatory states are strongly shaped by local cytokine context [K3]. In the configured E-MTAB-8873 data, the R1 inhibitor contrast is a source-local interaction in an Mpos/Mneg label that jointly encodes MerTK/CD206 and uses one SA256A/SA259A contributing-donor configuration. The GSE95588 assay has two coculture rounds and P-block labels but unresolved donor identity. E-MTAB-8316 has paired UNC106238/none monocyte samples but no Mpos/Mneg context or FLS endpoint.

The unresolved claim is not “the signal predicts elsewhere.” It is: does the R1 context-associated perturbation pattern have assay-structured transferability that survives a distinct fibroblast-plus-TNF coculture design and is not equally represented by matched generic drug/context effects or a marker response in a separate monocyte assay? Resolution would change whether the next target-specific experiment is run, deferred for curation, or abandoned in favor of generic/context explanations.

Falsifiable hypothesis: conditional on a structurally estimable, material, component-coherent E-MTAB-8873 R1 anchor, GSE95588 will show a same-direction, component-coherent fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in the source-local MerTK/CD206 marker panel B_GSE and an interpretable relation to H_GSE across both recorded rounds, while A77 and naproxen will not produce an equally coherent context interaction. The E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238-versus-none response will not show a stronger generic, same-direction marker-panel response that makes the anchor less target-specific. A failure of either transferability coherence, generic-perturbation separation, or method stability falsifies this as a useful gate; it does not prove MerTK absence.

The substantive advance over both parents is an assay-specific estimand and a staged authorization rule. “Transferable” means a predeclared source-local fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in GSE95588, not pooled effect-size agreement, donor generalization, or predictive performance. GSE rounds/P blocks are explicitly descriptive because donor_id is null/unresolved. No donor IDs or feature rows are joined across sources.

## Competing explanations and discriminating observations

The strongest rival is assay/context composition: TNF and fibroblast exposure may create the marker and inflammatory pattern without any MerTK-specific action. A second is generic perturbation: A77, naproxen, or UNC106238 may alter the same state markers through broad assay effects. A third is measurement/co-encoding: MERTK and MRC1/CD206 labels may be correlated state annotations rather than independently measured target and context. A fourth is contributor reuse or assay mismatch: apparent repeated rounds/P blocks may be the same biological material, and the GSE macrophage RNA endpoint is not the E-MTAB-8873 FLS endpoint. K2 adds a biologically consequential HBEGF/macrophage-FLS rival, but HBEGF is unavailable in E-MTAB-8873 and is not imputed.

The observations are separated as follows.

- A coherent R1 Delta with four H components, stable contributor-aware uncertainty, and no LPS/composition reversal is an anchor observation only.
- Same-direction I_B and I_H in both GSE95588 coculture rounds, with at least 5/7 B components and 3/4 H components concordant per round, is compatible with assay-structured context transfer. It is not independent-donor replication because all eight donor IDs are unresolved.
- A comparable or stronger matched A77/naproxen J interaction in the same GSE treatment matrix favors generic/context perturbation.
- A coherent E-MTAB-8316 C_8316 response across the seven state markers is a generic/state-marker warning, not a negative control for MerTK specificity; a null there does not establish specificity.
- A reversal in one component, round, P block, contributor audit, or hierarchical sensitivity makes the gate adverse or inconclusive according to the staged rules below.
- No configured result establishes target engagement, CD206 independence, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, causal treatment effect, or clinical benefit.

## Staged estimands, analysis and decision gate

Stage 0 — structural and namespace gate. Verify all declared paths/hashes, nonnegative matrix/transform decisions, exact feature availability, no duplicated feature rows, selected header/design bijections, exact sample membership, and no use of excluded GSE Donor2 rows. Output source_compatibility.json with source, path/hash, selected samples, selected features, design columns, join key/result, transform, calibration partition, missing counterparts and donor grouping. Structural failure is a packaging/design failure, not a biological null.

Stage 1 — anchor gate. Estimate Delta_R1_exact and its four component effects with the parent’s locked threshold M_8873=0.5 source-local SD and contributor-aware fixed plus hierarchical 95% intervals. Require component coherence and no reversal by the predeclared R2/R5 tier, LPS, mixed/composition, or contributor audits. If the anchor is adverse, do not authorize transferability as support for MerTK; if anchor is inconclusive, report the transferability result descriptively but set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer.

Stage 2 — transferability estimand. Within the GSE coculture matrix, fit source-local scores and estimate I_B,1/I_B,2, I_H,1/I_H,2 plus all component effects. Set M_GSE=0.5 within-matrix source-local SD before fitting. Use block-aware intervals/sensitivity, not donor t-tests. A transferability-positive pattern requires both blocks to share direction, at least 5/7 B components concordant in each block, and at least 3/4 H components concordant in each block. Because donor IDs are unresolved, call assay_block_consistent=true but donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; no pooled cross-source estimate is allowed.

Stage 3 — generic/context rival gate. For each GSE P block, estimate J_A77 and J_Nap with block-preserving uncertainty. A generic rival is clear if either drug has a same-direction, material, component-coherent context interaction in at least 3/4 P blocks, or if the hierarchical decomposition shows the candidate transferability pattern is attributable to shared drug/context or one component. Separately, a coherent same-direction C_8316 marker-panel response in at least 5/7 genes across the six paired specimens is a generic/state-marker warning. These are qualitative rival flags; effect magnitudes are never pooled across GSE, E-MTAB-8873 or E-MTAB-8316 scales.

Stage 4 — method-stability and staged authorization. The baseline and hierarchical sensitivity must agree on the sign and materiality status of I_B and I_H, with full required rank, no variance-boundary warning, and no single-marker explanation. Supportive transferability requires: Stage 0 passes; Stage 1 is supportive; Stage 2 passes; the GSE hierarchy does not overturn the block pattern; Stage 3 generic_rival_clear=false; and all missing evidence is explicitly recorded. This authorizes only the smallest independent MerTK-by-CD206 functional assay, not target prioritization as a clinical conclusion.

Adverse requires structural validity plus a material anchor reversal, transferability reversal/component failure, or a generic rival that is material and at least as compatible within its own assay. Set next_action=do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals. Inconclusive includes missing counterparts/features, interval spanning materiality, r1/r2 disagreement, unresolved rank/variance, only one estimable block, or unresolved donor identity being essential to the requested claim. Set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer. An imprecise null is not refutation.

The machine-readable output must contain one gate row:
gate_id=MerTK_CD206_assay_transferability_v1; anchor_status; I_B_1/I_B_2 and I_H_1/I_H_2 estimates and intervals; J_A77/J_Nap block flags; C_8316 component flag; component_coherent; assay_block_consistent; donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; generic_rival_clear; method_stable; structural_status; estimability; decision in {supportive, adverse, inconclusive}; and next_action in {run_orthogonal_factorial, do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals, resolve_curation_or_defer}. Conclusions must be linked to this row and computed outputs.

## Baseline and substantive same-input alternative

The simple baseline is the primary auditable estimator. Inputs are exactly the selected rows/features above, with source-local log/scale handling and z parameters fitted within each source matrix. It computes Delta_R1_exact, I_q,r, J_q,p,d and C_8316 directly; uncertainty is contributor/pair/block-aware bootstrap or exact block sign sensitivity, never cell-level replication. Its advantage is transparent estimands under unresolved donors; it can conceal whether one gene or covariance drives the score.

The substantive alternative fits source-stratified multivariate hierarchical sensitivities on exactly the same rows, features, joins, grouping and outcomes: gene-specific effects plus a B_GSE factor and H_GSE factor in the eight-row coculture block model; paired gene-specific J terms with P-block effects in the 28-row drug model; and paired gene-specific C terms with donor/specimen effects in E-MTAB-8316. No latent factor, donor effect, or scale is shared across sources. Use two predeclared weakly informative variance specifications and parametric bootstrap/posterior simulation. Return gene loadings, residual covariance, block/contributor variance share, interval width, rank, variance-boundary and estimability flags. This alternative can reveal a measurement/co-encoding or single-gene driver hidden by the score baseline; it cannot create donor identity, separate MerTK from CD206, or add a functional endpoint.

Freeze the split before fitting: R1 is a locked estimand partition excluded from nuisance calibration and never held out replication; GSE r1/r2 stay grouped by round; GSE P blocks keep all paired conditions together; E-MTAB-8316 keeps donor_id+other_donor_id specimen pairs together. Planned resource envelope: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, at most 1,200 seconds for tabular transforms, grouped resampling and hierarchical sensitivity. This is an unmeasured planning estimate. A GPU is not scientifically useful for these small structured matrices; that is a resource judgment, not a blanket method exclusion.

The future solver must newly fit/estimate source-local transforms, feature/component effects, Delta_R1_exact, I_B/I_H, J_A77/J_Nap, C_8316, uncertainty and method diagnostics, then write source_compatibility.json, output/transferability_gate.json and a reproducible decision row. Completion is these computed outputs plus a conclusion that matches the row—not a favorable hypothesis result. No screening job was run here.

Unavailable or essential evidence includes independent GSE donor identity, MerTK/CD206 protein or direct engagement, CD206-independent perturbation, target-negative matched perturbation, FLS viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, dose-response, time, spatial context and clinical outcomes. HBEGF is absent from the E-MTAB-8873 feature panel despite being a literature rival. E-MTAB-8316 has no FLS endpoint and GSE95588 measures macrophage RNA, so neither is an H-equivalent replication. # Episode 12 crossover: assay-structured transferability of the MerTK/CD206 gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No source scan, biological fitting, screening, or result was executed in this branch. Parents: candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 and candidate-ba3ec15ac0a3e2c458d36ef3.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and advance

The leading evidence-supported claim is bounded: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states can accompany remission/repair biology [K1], macrophage-to-FLS communication has a consequential HBEGF/invasiveness rival [K2], and FLS inflammatory states are strongly shaped by local cytokine context [K3]. In the configured E-MTAB-8873 data, the R1 inhibitor contrast is a source-local interaction in an Mpos/Mneg label that jointly encodes MerTK/CD206 and uses one SA256A/SA259A contributing-donor configuration. The GSE95588 assay has two coculture rounds and P-block labels but unresolved donor identity. E-MTAB-8316 has paired UNC106238/none monocyte samples but no Mpos/Mneg context or FLS endpoint.

The unresolved claim is not “the signal predicts elsewhere.” It is: does the R1 context-associated perturbation pattern have assay-structured transferability that survives a distinct fibroblast-plus-TNF coculture design and is not equally represented by matched generic drug/context effects or a marker response in a separate monocyte assay? Resolution would change whether the next target-specific experiment is run, deferred for curation, or abandoned in favor of generic/context explanations.

Falsifiable hypothesis: conditional on a structurally estimable, material, component-coherent E-MTAB-8873 R1 anchor, GSE95588 will show a same-direction, component-coherent fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in the source-local MerTK/CD206 marker panel B_GSE and an interpretable relation to H_GSE across both recorded rounds, while A77 and naproxen will not produce an equally coherent context interaction. The E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238-versus-none response will not show a stronger generic, same-direction marker-panel response that makes the anchor less target-specific. A failure of either transferability coherence, generic-perturbation separation, or method stability falsifies this as a useful gate; it does not prove MerTK absence.

The substantive advance over both parents is an assay-specific estimand and a staged authorization rule. “Transferable” means a predeclared source-local fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in GSE95588, not pooled effect-size agreement, donor generalization, or predictive performance. GSE rounds/P blocks are explicitly descriptive because donor_id is null/unresolved. No donor IDs or feature rows are joined across sources.

## Competing explanations and discriminating observations

The strongest rival is assay/context composition: TNF and fibroblast exposure may create the marker and inflammatory pattern without any MerTK-specific action. A second is generic perturbation: A77, naproxen, or UNC106238 may alter the same state markers through broad assay effects. A third is measurement/co-encoding: MERTK and MRC1/CD206 labels may be correlated state annotations rather than independently measured target and context. A fourth is contributor reuse or assay mismatch: apparent repeated rounds/P blocks may be the same biological material, and the GSE macrophage RNA endpoint is not the E-MTAB-8873 FLS endpoint. K2 adds a biologically consequential HBEGF/macrophage-FLS rival, but HBEGF is unavailable in E-MTAB-8873 and is not imputed.

The observations are separated as follows.

- A coherent R1 Delta with four H components, stable contributor-aware uncertainty, and no LPS/composition reversal is an anchor observation only.
- Same-direction I_B and I_H in both GSE95588 coculture rounds, with at least 5/7 B components and 3/4 H components concordant per round, is compatible with assay-structured context transfer. It is not independent-donor replication because all eight donor IDs are unresolved.
- A comparable or stronger matched A77/naproxen J interaction in the same GSE treatment matrix favors generic/context perturbation.
- A coherent E-MTAB-8316 C_8316 response across the seven state markers is a generic/state-marker warning, not a negative control for MerTK specificity; a null there does not establish specificity.
- A reversal in one component, round, P block, contributor audit, or hierarchical sensitivity makes the gate adverse or inconclusive according to the staged rules below.
- No configured result establishes target engagement, CD206 independence, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, causal treatment effect, or clinical benefit.

## Staged estimands, analysis and decision gate

Stage 0 — structural and namespace gate. Verify all declared paths/hashes, nonnegative matrix/transform decisions, exact feature availability, no duplicated feature rows, selected header/design bijections, exact sample membership, and no use of excluded GSE Donor2 rows. Output source_compatibility.json with source, path/hash, selected samples, selected features, design columns, join key/result, transform, calibration partition, missing counterparts and donor grouping. Structural failure is a packaging/design failure, not a biological null.

Stage 1 — anchor gate. Estimate Delta_R1_exact and its four component effects with the parent’s locked threshold M_8873=0.5 source-local SD and contributor-aware fixed plus hierarchical 95% intervals. Require component coherence and no reversal by the predeclared R2/R5 tier, LPS, mixed/composition, or contributor audits. If the anchor is adverse, do not authorize transferability as support for MerTK; if anchor is inconclusive, report the transferability result descriptively but set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer.

Stage 2 — transferability estimand. Within the GSE coculture matrix, fit source-local scores and estimate I_B,1/I_B,2, I_H,1/I_H,2 plus all component effects. Set M_GSE=0.5 within-matrix source-local SD before fitting. Use block-aware intervals/sensitivity, not donor t-tests. A transferability-positive pattern requires both blocks to share direction, at least 5/7 B components concordant in each block, and at least 3/4 H components concordant in each block. Because donor IDs are unresolved, call assay_block_consistent=true but donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; no pooled cross-source estimate is allowed.

Stage 3 — generic/context rival gate. For each GSE P block, estimate J_A77 and J_Nap with block-preserving uncertainty. A generic rival is clear if either drug has a same-direction, material, component-coherent context interaction in at least 3/4 P blocks, or if the hierarchical decomposition shows the candidate transferability pattern is attributable to shared drug/context or one component. Separately, a coherent same-direction C_8316 marker-panel response in at least 5/7 genes across the six paired specimens is a generic/state-marker warning. These are qualitative rival flags; effect magnitudes are never pooled across GSE, E-MTAB-8873 or E-MTAB-8316 scales.

Stage 4 — method-stability and staged authorization. The baseline and hierarchical sensitivity must agree on the sign and materiality status of I_B and I_H, with full required rank, no variance-boundary warning, and no single-marker explanation. Supportive transferability requires: Stage 0 passes; Stage 1 is supportive; Stage 2 passes; the GSE hierarchy does not overturn the block pattern; Stage 3 generic_rival_clear=false; and all missing evidence is explicitly recorded. This authorizes only the smallest independent MerTK-by-CD206 functional assay, not target prioritization as a clinical conclusion.

Adverse requires structural validity plus a material anchor reversal, transferability reversal/component failure, or a generic rival that is material and at least as compatible within its own assay. Set next_action=do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals. Inconclusive includes missing counterparts/features, interval spanning materiality, r1/r2 disagreement, unresolved rank/variance, only one estimable block, or unresolved donor identity being essential to the requested claim. Set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer. An imprecise null is not refutation.

The machine-readable output must contain one gate row:
gate_id=MerTK_CD206_assay_transferability_v1; anchor_status; I_B_1/I_B_2 and I_H_1/I_H_2 estimates and intervals; J_A77/J_Nap block flags; C_8316 component flag; component_coherent; assay_block_consistent; donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; generic_rival_clear; method_stable; structural_status; estimability; decision in {supportive, adverse, inconclusive}; and next_action in {run_orthogonal_factorial, do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals, resolve_curation_or_defer}. Conclusions must be linked to this row and computed outputs.

## Baseline and substantive same-input alternative

The simple baseline is the primary auditable estimator. Inputs are exactly the selected rows/features above, with source-local log/scale handling and z parameters fitted within each source matrix. It computes Delta_R1_exact, I_q,r, J_q,p,d and C_8316 directly; uncertainty is contributor/pair/block-aware bootstrap or exact block sign sensitivity, never cell-level replication. Its advantage is transparent estimands under unresolved donors; it can conceal whether one gene or covariance drives the score.

The substantive alternative fits source-stratified multivariate hierarchical sensitivities on exactly the same rows, features, joins, grouping and outcomes: gene-specific effects plus a B_GSE factor and H_GSE factor in the eight-row coculture block model; paired gene-specific J terms with P-block effects in the 28-row drug model; and paired gene-specific C terms with donor/specimen effects in E-MTAB-8316. No latent factor, donor effect, or scale is shared across sources. Use two predeclared weakly informative variance specifications and parametric bootstrap/posterior simulation. Return gene loadings, residual covariance, block/contributor variance share, interval width, rank, variance-boundary and estimability flags. This alternative can reveal a measurement/co-encoding or single-gene driver hidden by the score baseline; it cannot create donor identity, separate MerTK from CD206, or add a functional endpoint.

Freeze the split before fitting: R1 is a locked estimand partition excluded from nuisance calibration and never held out replication; GSE r1/r2 stay grouped by round; GSE P blocks keep all paired conditions together; E-MTAB-8316 keeps donor_id+other_donor_id specimen pairs together. There is no predictive accuracy estimand or clinical outcome. Retain the baseline as primary because the scientific question is transferability and rival discrimination, not prediction. Defer neural/high-dimensional models: without a held-out functional outcome they add complexity but cannot resolve target specificity. Revisit only after independent MerTK/CD206 protein and functional measurements exist.

Planned resource envelope: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, at most 1,200 seconds for tabular transforms, grouped resampling and hierarchical sensitivity. This is an unmeasured planning estimate. A GPU is not scientifically useful for these small structured matrices; that is a resource judgment, not a blanket method exclusion.

## Actual scientific deliverable and unavailable evidence

The future solver must newly fit/estimate source-local transforms, feature/component effects, Delta_R1_exact, I_B/I_H, J_A77/J_Nap, C_8316, uncertainty and method diagnostics, then write source_compatibility.json, output/transferability_gate.json and a reproducible decision row. Completion is these computed outputs plus a conclusion that matches the row—not a favorable hypothesis result. No screening job was run here.

Unavailable or essential evidence includes independent GSE donor identity, MerTK/CD206 protein or direct engagement, CD206-independent perturbation, target-negative matched perturbation, FLS viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, dose-response, time, spatial context and clinical outcomes. # Episode 12 crossover: assay-structured transferability of the MerTK/CD206 gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No source scan, biological fitting, screening, or result was executed in this branch. Parents: candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 and candidate-ba3ec15ac0a3e2c458d36ef3.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and advance

The leading evidence-supported claim is bounded: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states can accompany remission/repair biology [K1], macrophage-to-FLS communication has a consequential HBEGF/invasiveness rival [K2], and FLS inflammatory states are strongly shaped by local cytokine context [K3]. In the configured E-MTAB-8873 data, the R1 inhibitor contrast is a source-local interaction in an Mpos/Mneg label that jointly encodes MerTK/CD206 and uses one SA256A/SA259A contributing-donor configuration. The GSE95588 assay has two coculture rounds and P-block labels but unresolved donor identity. E-MTAB-8316 has paired UNC106238/none monocyte samples but no Mpos/Mneg context or FLS endpoint.

The unresolved claim is not “the signal predicts elsewhere.” It is: does the R1 context-associated perturbation pattern have assay-structured transferability that survives a distinct fibroblast-plus-TNF coculture design and is not equally represented by matched generic drug/context effects or a marker response in a separate monocyte assay? Resolution would change whether the next target-specific experiment is run, deferred for curation, or abandoned in favor of generic/context explanations.

Falsifiable hypothesis: conditional on a structurally estimable, material, component-coherent E-MTAB-8873 R1 anchor, GSE95588 will show a same-direction, component-coherent fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in the source-local MerTK/CD206 marker panel B_GSE and an interpretable relation to H_GSE across both recorded rounds, while A77 and naproxen will not produce an equally coherent context interaction. The E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238-versus-none response will not show a stronger generic, same-direction marker-panel response that makes the anchor less target-specific. A failure of either transferability coherence, generic-perturbation separation, or method stability falsifies this as a useful gate; it does not prove MerTK absence.

The substantive advance over both parents is an assay-specific estimand and a staged authorization rule. “Transferable” means a predeclared source-local fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in GSE95588, not pooled effect-size agreement, donor generalization, or predictive performance. GSE rounds/P blocks are explicitly descriptive because donor_id is null/unresolved. No donor IDs or feature rows are joined across sources.

## Competing explanations and discriminating observations

The strongest rival is assay/context composition: TNF and fibroblast exposure may create the marker and inflammatory pattern without any MerTK-specific action. A second is generic perturbation: A77, naproxen, or UNC106238 may alter the same state markers through broad assay effects. A third is measurement/co-encoding: MERTK and MRC1/CD206 labels may be correlated state annotations rather than independently measured target and context. A fourth is contributor reuse or assay mismatch: apparent repeated rounds/P blocks may be the same biological material, and the GSE macrophage RNA endpoint is not the E-MTAB-8873 FLS endpoint. K2 adds a biologically consequential HBEGF/macrophage-FLS rival, but HBEGF is unavailable in E-MTAB-8873 and is not imputed.

The observations are separated as follows.

- A coherent R1 Delta with four H components, stable contributor-aware uncertainty, and no LPS/composition reversal is an anchor observation only.
- Same-direction I_B and I_H in both GSE95588 coculture rounds, with at least 5/7 B components and 3/4 H components concordant per round, is compatible with assay-structured context transfer. It is not independent-donor replication because all eight donor IDs are unresolved.
- A comparable or stronger matched A77/naproxen J interaction in the same GSE treatment matrix favors generic/context perturbation.
- A coherent E-MTAB-8316 C_8316 response across the seven state markers is a generic/state-marker warning, not a negative control for MerTK specificity; a null there does not establish specificity.
- A reversal in one component, round, P block, contributor audit, or hierarchical sensitivity makes the gate adverse or inconclusive according to the staged rules below.
- No configured result establishes target engagement, CD206 independence, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, causal treatment effect, or clinical benefit.

## Staged estimands, analysis and decision gate

Stage 0 — structural and namespace gate. Verify all declared paths/hashes, nonnegative matrix/transform decisions, exact feature availability, no duplicated feature rows, selected header/design bijections, exact sample membership, and no use of excluded GSE Donor2 rows. Output source_compatibility.json with source, path/hash, selected samples, selected features, design columns, join key/result, transform, calibration partition, missing counterparts and donor grouping. Structural failure is a packaging/design failure, not a biological null.

Stage 1 — anchor gate. Estimate Delta_R1_exact and its four component effects with the parent’s locked threshold M_8873=0.5 source-local SD and contributor-aware fixed plus hierarchical 95% intervals. Require component coherence and no reversal by the predeclared R2/R5 tier, LPS, mixed/composition, or contributor audits. If the anchor is adverse, do not authorize transferability as support for MerTK; if anchor is inconclusive, report the transferability result descriptively but set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer.

Stage 2 — transferability estimand. Within the GSE coculture matrix, fit source-local scores and estimate I_B,1/I_B,2, I_H,1/I_H,2 plus all component effects. Set M_GSE=0.5 within-matrix source-local SD before fitting. Use block-aware intervals/sensitivity, not donor t-tests. A transferability-positive pattern requires both blocks to share direction, at least 5/7 B components concordant in each block, and at least 3/4 H components concordant in each block. Because donor IDs are unresolved, call assay_block_consistent=true but donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; no pooled cross-source estimate is allowed.

Stage 3 — generic/context rival gate. For each GSE P block, estimate J_A77 and J_Nap with block-preserving uncertainty. A generic rival is clear if either drug has a same-direction, material, component-coherent context interaction in at least 3/4 P blocks, or if the hierarchical decomposition shows the candidate transferability pattern is attributable to shared drug/context or one component. Separately, a coherent same-direction C_8316 marker-panel response in at least 5/7 genes across the six paired specimens is a generic/state-marker warning. These are qualitative rival flags; effect magnitudes are never pooled across GSE, E-MTAB-8873 or E-MTAB-8316 scales.

Stage 4 — method-stability and staged authorization. The baseline and hierarchical sensitivity must agree on the sign and materiality status of I_B and I_H, with full required rank, no variance-boundary warning, and no single-marker explanation. Supportive transferability requires: Stage 0 passes; Stage 1 is supportive; Stage 2 passes; the GSE hierarchy does not overturn the block pattern; Stage 3 generic_rival_clear=false; and all missing evidence is explicitly recorded. This authorizes only the smallest independent MerTK-by-CD206 functional assay, not target prioritization as a clinical conclusion.

Adverse requires structural validity plus a material anchor reversal, transferability reversal/component failure, or a generic rival that is material and at least as compatible within its own assay. Set next_action=do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals. Inconclusive includes missing counterparts/features, interval spanning materiality, r1/r2 disagreement, unresolved rank/variance, only one estimable block, or unresolved donor identity being essential to the requested claim. Set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer. An imprecise null is not refutation.

The machine-readable output must contain one gate row:
gate_id=MerTK_CD206_assay_transferability_v1; anchor_status; I_B_1/I_B_2 and I_H_1/I_H_2 estimates and intervals; J_A77/J_Nap block flags; C_8316 component flag; component_coherent; assay_block_consistent; donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; generic_rival_clear; method_stable; structural_status; estimability; decision in {supportive, adverse, inconclusive}; and next_action in {run_orthogonal_factorial, do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals, resolve_curation_or_defer}. Conclusions must be linked to this row and computed outputs.

## Baseline and substantive same-input alternative

The simple baseline is the primary auditable estimator. Inputs are exactly the selected rows/features above, with source-local log/scale handling and z parameters fitted within each source matrix. It computes Delta_R1_exact, I_q,r, J_q,p,d and C_8316 directly; uncertainty is contributor/pair/block-aware bootstrap or exact block sign sensitivity, never cell-level replication. Its advantage is transparent estimands under unresolved donors; it can conceal whether one gene or covariance drives the score.

The substantive alternative fits source-stratified multivariate hierarchical sensitivities on exactly the same rows, features, joins, grouping and outcomes: gene-specific effects plus a B_GSE factor and H_GSE factor in the eight-row coculture block model; paired gene-specific J terms with P-block effects in the 28-row drug model; and paired gene-specific C terms with donor/specimen effects in E-MTAB-8316. No latent factor, donor effect, or scale is shared across sources. Use two predeclared weakly informative variance specifications and parametric bootstrap/posterior simulation. Return gene loadings, residual covariance, block/contributor variance share, interval width, rank, variance-boundary and estimability flags. This alternative can reveal a measurement/co-encoding or single-gene driver hidden by the score baseline; it cannot create donor identity, separate MerTK from CD206, or add a functional endpoint.

Freeze the split before fitting: R1 is a locked estimand partition excluded from nuisance calibration and never held out replication; GSE r1/r2 stay grouped by round; GSE P blocks keep all paired conditions together; E-MTAB-8316 keeps donor_id+other_donor_id specimen pairs together. There is no predictive accuracy estimand or clinical outcome. Retain the baseline as primary because the scientific question is transferability and rival discrimination, not prediction. Defer neural/high-dimensional models: without a held-out functional outcome they add complexity but cannot resolve target specificity. Revisit only after independent MerTK/CD206 protein and functional measurements exist.

Planned resource envelope: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, at most 1,200 seconds for tabular transforms, grouped resampling and hierarchical sensitivity. This is an unmeasured planning estimate. A GPU is not scientifically useful for these small structured matrices; that is a resource judgment, not a blanket method exclusion.

## Actual scientific deliverable and unavailable evidence

The future solver must newly fit/estimate source-local transforms, feature/component effects, Delta_R1_exact, I_B/I_H, J_A77/J_Nap, C_8316, uncertainty and method diagnostics, then write source_compatibility.json, output/transferability_gate.json and a reproducible decision row. Completion is these computed outputs plus a conclusion that matches the row—not a favorable hypothesis result. No screening job was run here.

Unavailable or essential evidence includes independent GSE donor identity, MerTK/CD206 protein or direct engagement, CD206-independent perturbation, target-negative matched perturbation, FLS viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, dose-response, time, spatial context and clinical outcomes. HBEGF is absent from the E-MTAB-8873 feature panel despite being a literature rival. E-MTAB-8316 has no FLS endpoint and GSE95588 measures macrophage RNA, so neither is an H-equivalent replication. No automatic verifier can establish protein identity, target engagement, mechanism or clinical benefit; it can check joins, transforms, exact contrasts, thresholds, flags, uncertainty plumbing and conclusion-row consistency.

If supportive, run an independent-donor randomized/blinded factorial of MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle crossed with independently measured CD206-high/low macrophages and a matched target-negative perturbation. Measure MerTK/CD206 protein, direct engagement or validated proximal readout, viability, FLS H as secondary, and invasion or matrix degradation as primary functional outcome. If adverse, stop MerTK-specific prioritization from this package and review generic/context rival evidence. If inconclusive, resolve curation or repeat a donor-blocked assay before escalation. # Episode 12 crossover: assay-structured transferability of the MerTK/CD206 gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment and source audit. No biological fitting, screening, or effect result has been executed. Parents: candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 and candidate-ba3ec15ac0a3e2c458d36ef3. This branch makes one source-design correction to the Episode-10 transferability child: the complete generic-drug comparison is 6 A77 pairs plus 4 naproxen pairs, not 28 complete pairs.

## Scientific opening, claim boundary, and deliverable

The strongest available claim is descriptive and source-bounded. The configured E-MTAB-8873 R1 matrix contains a sparse MerTK/CD206-labelled macrophage-context inhibitor contrast in a targeted 445-feature assay; its labels jointly encode MerTK and CD206 and its R1 inhibitor quartet is one contributing-donor configuration. GSE95588 contains a separately prepared coculture matrix with fibroblast/TNF context conditions and a second matrix with ordinary drug perturbations. The registry and dataset guide warn that GSE95588 donor identities are unresolved and that its r1/r2 material includes earlier GSE57723 data. The literature supports a repair-associated MerTK-positive macrophage state [K1], a competing HBEGF/TNF/fibroblast route to FLS invasiveness [K2], and cytokine-driven FLS heterogeneity [K3]. None establishes MerTK-specific engagement, a functional harm endpoint, donor-generalizability, or clinical benefit.

The unresolved question is narrower: does the GSE95588 assay show a repeatable fibroblast-by-TNF context interaction in a macrophage state/inflammatory transcript program, while complete same-source A77 and naproxen drug-by-context controls fail to reproduce an equally coherent interaction? A supportive answer would establish only an assay-structured context pattern worth testing in an independent MerTK-by-CD206 functional assay. It would not transfer a MerTK effect, clinical effect, or expression effect size to E-MTAB-8873.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly computed, source-local output: exact feature- and score-level estimates for the GSE95588 coculture interaction on both rounds; complete-pair A77 and naproxen interactions on the same source scale; component coherence, block/sign concordance, uncertainty and identifiability flags; a frozen gate status linked to those outputs; and a continue/revise/defer/abandon decision. A favorable score alone does not complete the deliverable.

## Hypothesis and competing explanations

Falsifiable hypothesis: the GSE95588 coculture interaction

I[q,r] = [q(mtf_r) - q(mf_r)] - [q(mt_r) - q(m_r)], for r in {r1,r2},

will have a coherent direction in the seven-gene macrophage-state panel B_GSE and the four-gene inflammatory panel H_GSE across both recorded rounds, while the matched complete A77 and naproxen interactions

J[q,p,d] = [q(Pp_MTF_d) - q(Pp_MTF)] - [q(Pp_MT_d) - q(Pp_MT)]

will not show a comparably coherent context-selective pattern. Here d is A77 or Nap and p is restricted to blocks with both MTF and MT drug rows.

This tests transferability of an assay-structured context regularity, not target specificity. The leading non-MerTK explanations are: fibroblast/TNF exposure or cell composition drives both panels; generic drug or assay response produces a similar interaction; MERTK and MRC1/CD206 labels are correlated and source-label-preserved RNA is not protein abundance or engagement; r1/r2 and P1-P4 are protocol blocks or reused material rather than independent donors; and measurement covariance or one dominant gene creates a score-level contrast.

The discriminating observation is the joint pattern of exact context contrasts, all component contrasts, complete-pair generic controls, and the same-input hierarchical sensitivity. A coherent result in the separate E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238-versus-none monocyte assay remains a generic-perturbation bound; it cannot prove or disprove MerTK specificity because that assay has no MerTK/CD206 context and uses an Ensembl namespace.

## Exact data bindings and units

All source data are read-only. Catalog: [private-path]/catalog.json, SHA-256 162ddf0148975035ee641ae75a2666bf44a7b458b050d79370ee9f550953312f. Assay registry: [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f. The exact source audit and complete-pair audit are attached.

### GSE95588 coculture context source

Use all and only these eight prepared sample columns: m_r1, mf_r1, mt_r1, mtf_r1, m_r2, mf_r2, mt_r2, mtf_r2.

Bindings:

- counts: [private-path]/GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 f6ec16014f3adcadc223a4082620ee32347a5a9bdf4ee7f30903d7a7d258b9b5;
- design: [private-path]/GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.design.json, SHA-256 b324aeb435525132ba231663fd863faae6b676b8301d8ded18f4301a1ee45981;
- feature map: [private-path]/GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json, SHA-256 9c3af22472f6bea36ab2e66ab998ca83c944cb0e96f26a811ce5cf5739b80087.

The counts key is feature; the sample header/design join key is sample_id and source_metadata.matrix_column. Design fields are sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, condition, source_metadata, and mapping_note. All eight donor_id values are null and all donor_status values are unresolved; there is no usable time/date field. Protocol metadata describes primary CD14+-derived macrophages, TNF 20 ng/mL for one day, and m/mf/mt/mtf condition meanings. That is a protocol condition, not a longitudinal observation and not donor replication.

The feature map has 23,710 rows with feature_id, source_label, source_row, and mapping_status. Required source-label-preserved rows are B_GSE: MERTK row 11798; MRC1 13458; TREM2 21610; C1QA 2076; C1QB 2077; C1QC 2079; APOE 918. H_GSE: IL6 8584; MMP1 13340; MMP3 13360; MMP14 13345. Contextual/rival reporting: MMP12 13343; MMP13 13344; HBEGF 7740. All are present and not zero-filled; mapping_status is source_label_preserved_not_independently_annotated. Do not merge duplicate/date-like labels or infer protein identity.

### GSE95588 complete-pair generic source

The full prepared matrix has 70 samples and 71 columns including feature, with the same 23,710 source-label-preserved feature namespace.

Bindings:

- counts: [private-path]/GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 41c16047ab7e1c8ad2ace7e9b0c6f376fee00afe9bd6b6f360001ed52755eeb0;
- design: [private-path]/GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.design.json, SHA-256 54fb86625bd5982310e14feddb17247ea2daca6ffae2e4c67c7528a1776b6bdc;
- feature map: [private-path]/GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz.feature-map.json, SHA-256 745f4fb65a6fb643b3edc1a0c6e2d237be38c029e8ade99415061f068a49859a.

The design has sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, condition, source_metadata, and mapping_note; all 70 donor IDs are null, statuses unresolved, and there is no time/date field. Complete-pair analysis uses:

- baseline rows, for each p in P1,P2,P3,P4: Pp_M, Pp_MT, Pp_MTF (12 rows);
- A77: P1_MT_A77, P1_MTF_A77, P2_MT_A77, P2_MTF_A77, P3_MT_A77, P3_MTF_A77 (6 rows; P4 has no complete A77 pair);
- naproxen: P1_MT_Nap, P1_MTF_Nap, P3_MT_Nap, P3_MTF_Nap (4 rows).

Thus 22 rows are analyzed for complete generic interactions. P2_MT_Nap is excluded because P2_MTF_Nap is absent; all other drug-labelled rows, including P4, are excluded unless they form a complete prespecified pair. No row is imputed, renamed, or backfilled from the 74-row public GSM metadata. P1-P4 are blocks, not verified donors.

Raw GSE95588 lineage members are retained by the catalog:

- GSE95588/GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz, SHA-256 334255c7635fecc72d50e57adcfd242c938970442a85aae80339ef7519a3aa46;
- GSE95588/GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz, SHA-256 285d27bcd669004c575479722ab229e9cca7ec4ef30302fabb632a339edd741e;
- GSE95588/samples.soft, SHA-256 d003ec183a255f8a01f9ced519f1aabfc5e454f84b880a951a1f4db2fb4719c5;
- GSE95588/series.soft, SHA-256 1de3446c18ec7fcacc47cc7cb74a56fb166233ed07866a940c5544f9e0f2674a.

The prepared header/design bijections and feature map were rechecked in managed job job-501e0697bedc08d802873449, whose output is attached. The earlier source checksum/header audit is job-63e03246e729be3c712a0371.

### What is comparable to E-MTAB-8873, and what is not

E-MTAB-8873 binds to [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz and [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json (design SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae). Its design join key is sample_id, with fields including donor_id, other_donor_id, condition, treatment, cell_type, tissue, age, and sex; it has 33 samples, a targeted 445-feature transcript namespace, no usable time/date field, and no verified single-donor set. Exact R1 Delta_R1_exact, R2/R5 preInhibitor direction checks, contributor/component/composition checks, and LPS/FLS-only controls remain inherited from the frozen gate.

Comparable: both sources contain macrophage-context condition labels, support within-source contrasts, and report MerTK/CD206-related transcript labels or proxies.

Not comparable: GSE95588 records macrophage RNA in fibroblast/TNF context and has unresolved donor identity; E-MTAB-8873 includes FLS/coculture targeted pseudobulk and an inhibitor-labelled R1 quartet with contributing donors. GSE95588 has gene symbols and 23,710 source-label-preserved rows; E-MTAB-8873 has 445 preserved transcript identifiers. There is no cross-source feature arithmetic, common donor key, common time field, or pooling of I, J, or Delta_R1_exact. GSE context is not a replication of MerTK inhibition.

For the retained E-MTAB-8316 generic bound, use its prepared counts/design and 12 samples MK11, MK12, MK15, MK16, MK19, MK20, MK23, MK24, MK3, MK4, MK7, MK8, paired by documented donor/specimen keys. It has four verified donor IDs, LPS 1 ng/mL and UNC106238 versus none, but an Ensembl namespace and no MerTK/CD206 context or FLS endpoint. Never join its feature or donor IDs to either GSE95588 or E-MTAB-8873.

## Analysis contract

### Fixed-contrast baseline

1. Read only bound matrix columns and rows. Confirm unique feature/sample_id keys, header/design bijection, nonnegative numeric abundance, and required feature-map status.
2. Apply one log1p only if the selected matrix is raw nonnegative abundance; record the decision and do not transform already normalized values. Within each source separately, standardize each selected feature using a prespecified source-local calibration across selected matrix rows. Never calibrate on another assay.
3. Compute B_GSE = mean[z(MERTK), z(MRC1), z(TREM2), z(C1QA), z(C1QB), z(C1QC), z(APOE)] and H_GSE = mean[z(IL6), z(MMP1), z(MMP3), z(MMP14)].
4. Report I[B,r], I[H,r], every component I[g,r], direct context contrasts q(mtf_r)-q(mt_r) and q(mf_r)-q(m_r), and source-local score scale.
5. Report J[q,p,A77] for p=P1,P2,P3 and J[q,p,Nap] for p=P1,P3, plus all component J values. Do not use incomplete P2 naproxen or P4 drug rows.
6. Treat r1/r2 and P1-P4 as descriptive assay blocks, not independent donors. Use exact sign enumeration over the four complete P blocks for J and a two-block descriptive range for I. If intervals are reported, use block-aware/bootstrap or parametric sensitivity that never resamples cells as donors.

### Same-input substantive alternative

Fit a source-stratified multivariate measurement model on exactly the same selected rows and feature IDs. For B and H, use gene-specific intercepts and residual variances, fixed fibroblast/TNF terms, block terms for r or P, and partial pooling only across the seven or four components within that source. For the drug matrix include paired A77/Nap drug-by-context terms and P-block effects; do not share latent factors across matrices or donors. Report posterior or parametric intervals, component loadings, block influence, rank/estimability, and whether sign and gate status survive residual covariance.

This alternative can reveal whether a fixed-score result is driven by one marker or correlated measurement noise. The baseline is preferable for primary communication because it is auditable with two unresolved coculture blocks and few complete drug blocks. The hierarchy is a sensitivity, not a donor-generalizing model; if rank-unstable, report failure rather than select a favorable fit. A neural predictor is deferred because there is no held-out functional outcome and predictive gain would not resolve target specificity.

Planned solver envelope is CPU-only: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, at most 1,200 seconds. This is a planning estimate, not a measured biological fit. No GPU is indicated. Discovery audits used 2 CPUs/4,096 MiB and completed in under one second; that does not validate the future solver workload.

## Frozen decision and falsification rules

Define M_GSE = 0.5 source-local SD of H_GSE, with the SD estimator and calibration partition recorded before fitting. Rules are qualitative within GSE; no cross-assay effect-size threshold is used.

Supportive transferability requires: all structural checks pass; both I[B,r] have the same sign and at least 5 of 7 B components concordant in each round; both I[H,r] have the same sign and at least 3 of 4 H components concordant in each round, with the block-aware interval not spanning materiality in the claimed direction; the hierarchical sensitivity is estimable and does not attribute the result to one component; and neither complete A77 nor complete naproxen pattern is comparably coherent and material in the same direction. Label this source_local_context_transferability_supportive, never MerTK_specific.

Adverse transferability is a coculture reversal between rounds, failed component coherence, an equally or more coherent/material complete A77 or naproxen pattern, or a one-feature artifact in the sensitivity model. It means defer MerTK prioritization and treat the E-MTAB-8873 interaction as insufficiently specific; it does not prove MerTK irrelevant.

Inconclusive means missing/mismatched bindings, missing features, nonunique keys, uncurated duplicate labels, donor/block structure essential to the requested generalization, interval spanning materiality, block disagreement, rank instability, or an absent complete counterpart. It is not a null; preserve the descriptive output and seek donor/GSM curation or an independent assay.

Computationally checkable claims are source bindings, feature/sample availability, exact contrast arithmetic, component coherence, block-aware uncertainty, and gate assignment. Clinical or mechanistic adjudication requires independent protein measurements, direct target engagement, viability, and a functional endpoint. Additional evidence is required for causal effect, FLS invasion/matrix degradation, clinical safety/benefit, CD206-independent action, and patient transportability.

## Next decision and minimum follow-up

Supportive output justifies the smallest independent-donor randomized and blinded MerTK-by-CD206 factorial macrophage-FLS experiment: MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle, target-negative matched perturbation, CD206-high versus CD206-low preparations, independent MerTK/CD206 protein measurements, direct engagement/proximal readout, viability, and a functional endpoint such as FLS invasion or matrix degradation. Its interaction is

Tau = [Y(MerTK perturbation, CD206-high)-Y(vehicle, CD206-high)] - [Y(MerTK perturbation, CD206-low)-Y(vehicle, CD206-low)].

Adverse output defers this experiment and prioritizes donor/protocol curation or generic-mechanism controls. Inconclusive output preserves the source-local result but does not authorize MerTK-specific prioritization. Revisit the GSE gate after verified donor/GSM mapping and independent feature curation; do not pool incompatible namespaces.

## Key works

[K1] Alivernini et al., “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis,” Nature Medicine (2020). The inspected frozen evidence supports a remission/repair-associated MerTK-positive macrophage state and bounds interpretation because configured labels co-encode MerTK and CD206; it does not establish GSE transferability or target engagement.

[K2] Kuo et al., “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness,” Science Translational Medicine (2019). The inspected evidence was abstract-only and supports a consequential HBEGF/TNF/fibroblast rival route; it does not establish MerTK specificity or provide the configured functional endpoint.

[K3] Smith et al., “Drivers of heterogeneity in synovial fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis,” Nature Immunology (2023). The inspected evidence supports cytokine/context-driven FLS heterogeneity and bounds H as a transcript proxy; it does not provide target engagement, donor-generalizable GSE evidence, or functional validation here.

The frozen package must attach exactly these three distinct inspected works through the inherited hash-linked evidence snapshots and key-references.json. Publication year/version and original receipts remain unchanged; no inaccessible full text or supplementary method is claimed.
