# Episode 12 crossover: assay-structured transferability of the MerTK/CD206 gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No source scan, biological fitting, screening, or result was executed in this branch. Parents: candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 and candidate-ba3ec15ac0a3e2c458d36ef3.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and advance

The leading evidence-supported claim is bounded: MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states can accompany remission/repair biology [K1], macrophage-to-FLS communication has a consequential HBEGF/invasiveness rival [K2], and FLS inflammatory states are strongly shaped by local cytokine context [K3]. In the configured E-MTAB-8873 data, the R1 inhibitor contrast is a source-local interaction in an Mpos/Mneg label that jointly encodes MerTK/CD206 and uses one SA256A/SA259A contributing-donor configuration. The GSE95588 assay has two coculture rounds and P-block labels but unresolved donor identity. E-MTAB-8316 has paired UNC106238/none monocyte samples but no Mpos/Mneg context or FLS endpoint.

The unresolved claim is not “the signal predicts elsewhere.” It is: does the R1 context-associated perturbation pattern have assay-structured transferability that survives a distinct fibroblast-plus-TNF coculture design and is not equally represented by matched generic drug/context effects or a marker response in a separate monocyte assay? Resolution would change whether the next target-specific experiment is run, deferred for curation, or abandoned in favor of generic/context explanations.

Falsifiable hypothesis: conditional on a structurally estimable, material, component-coherent E-MTAB-8873 R1 anchor, GSE95588 will show a same-direction, component-coherent fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in the source-local MerTK/CD206 marker panel B_GSE and an interpretable relation to H_GSE across both recorded rounds, while A77 and naproxen will not produce an equally coherent context interaction. The E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238-versus-none response will not show a stronger generic, same-direction marker-panel response that makes the anchor less target-specific. A failure of either transferability coherence, generic-perturbation separation, or method stability falsifies this as a useful gate; it does not prove MerTK absence.

The substantive advance over both parents is an assay-specific estimand and a staged authorization rule. “Transferable” means a predeclared source-local fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in GSE95588, not pooled effect-size agreement, donor generalization, or predictive performance. GSE rounds/P blocks are explicitly descriptive because donor_id is null/unresolved. No donor IDs or feature rows are joined across sources.

## Competing explanations and discriminating observations

The strongest rival is assay/context composition: TNF and fibroblast exposure may create the marker and inflammatory pattern without any MerTK-specific action. A second is generic perturbation: A77, naproxen, or UNC106238 may alter the same state markers through broad assay effects. A third is measurement/co-encoding: MERTK and MRC1/CD206 labels may be correlated state annotations rather than independently measured target and context. A fourth is contributor reuse or assay mismatch: apparent repeated rounds/P blocks may be the same biological material, and the GSE macrophage RNA endpoint is not the E-MTAB-8873 FLS endpoint. K2 adds a biologically consequential HBEGF/macrophage-FLS rival, but HBEGF is unavailable in E-MTAB-8873 and is not imputed.

The observations are separated as follows.

- A coherent R1 Delta with four H components, stable contributor-aware uncertainty, and no LPS/composition reversal is an anchor observation only.
- Same-direction I_B and I_H in both GSE95588 coculture rounds, with at least 5/7 B components and 3/4 H components concordant per round, is compatible with assay-structured context transfer. It is not independent-donor replication because all eight donor IDs are unresolved.
- A comparable or stronger matched A77/naproxen J interaction in the same GSE treatment matrix favors generic/context perturbation.
- A coherent E-MTAB-8316 C_8316 response across the seven state markers is a generic/state-marker warning, not a negative control for MerTK specificity; a null there does not establish specificity.
- A reversal in one component, round, P block, contributor audit, or hierarchical sensitivity makes the gate adverse or inconclusive according to the staged rules below.
- No configured result establishes target engagement, CD206 independence, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, causal treatment effect, or clinical benefit.

## Exact data binding, population and temporal boundary

All source files are read-only. Use the catalog at [private-path]/catalog.json, SHA-256 162ddf0148975035ee641ae75a2666bf44a7b458b050d79370ee9f550953312f, and the prepared assay registry at [private-path]/assay-registry.json, SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f. The snapshot boundary is core-molecular-20261003. No bound design has a usable longitudinal time field; recorded treatment, condition, LPS/TNF and protocol labels define assay exposure, not a clinical time course.

For every prepared matrix, join only counts.header.sample_id = design.sample_id, require one-to-one selected header/design membership, and retain source-specific donor/specimen namespaces. Never join donor IDs across sources. Never join or pool the E-MTAB-8316 Ensembl namespace with the GSE95588 gene-symbol namespace or the E-MTAB-8873 RefSeq-like feature namespace.

### Anchor: E-MTAB-8873

Use prepared counts [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.counts.tsv.gz (SHA-256 d218d3c46b652d533673c9ffc7876585bc51a39371f036e92d3ce568f28a4c0f) and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8873.design.json (SHA-256 fd2ae05bd0e31a8ba72454b97e22a48f5e53c179370e5f4b5343f5382b217ae4). Required design columns are sample_id, donor_id, donor_status, other_donor_id, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata and cells. Restrict to tissue=synovial membrane and cell_type=type B synovial cell; cells is metadata only.

The locked primary rows are the four archive members R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz (SHA-256 ef435ca4a16bb535f74ad077297861f2f9672827c2d2a4e7f9e65171bea2b0d7), R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mneg_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz (144b62d01db3f4635bdd19ecc599ce7670770ddf79b7e72e846c46a3cf732e9e), R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz (1dafc0a646fc9cdc1101803cf9d36802a1775844a85877930341ebe6edcf2176), and R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_RSEC_MolsPerCell.txt.gz (e3d6554a4e6c262fca98ce8263fb3c1d86d2c47c5f7e3e1fe5aa516367b3f599). Their labels are co-cultured with MerTK/CD206neg or MerTK/CD206pos macrophages crossed with inhibitor/none. All four are donor_status=requires_contributing_donor_model with FLS/macrophage identifiers SA256A/SA259A; they are one contributing-donor configuration, not four donors.

Use exact H features IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end. ## Staged estimands, analysis and decision gate

Stage 0 — structural and namespace gate. Verify all declared paths/hashes, nonnegative matrix/transform decisions, exact feature availability, no duplicated feature rows, selected header/design bijections, exact sample membership, and no use of excluded GSE Donor2 rows. Output source_compatibility.json with source, path/hash, selected samples, selected features, design columns, join key/result, transform, calibration partition, missing counterparts and donor grouping. Structural failure is a packaging/design failure, not a biological null.

Stage 1 — anchor gate. Estimate Delta_R1_exact and its four component effects with the parent’s locked threshold M_8873=0.5 source-local SD and contributor-aware fixed plus hierarchical 95% intervals. Require component coherence and no reversal by the predeclared R2/R5 tier, LPS, mixed/composition, or contributor audits. If the anchor is adverse, do not authorize transferability as support for MerTK; if anchor is inconclusive, report the transferability result descriptively but set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer.

Stage 2 — transferability estimand. Within the GSE coculture matrix, fit source-local scores and estimate I_B,1/I_B,2, I_H,1/I_H,2 plus all component effects. Set M_GSE=0.5 within-matrix source-local SD before fitting. Use block-aware intervals/sensitivity, not donor t-tests. A transferability-positive pattern requires both blocks to share direction, at least 5/7 B components concordant in each block, and at least 3/4 H components concordant in each block. Because donor IDs are unresolved, call assay_block_consistent=true but donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; no pooled cross-source estimate is allowed.

Stage 3 — generic/context rival gate. For each GSE P block, estimate J_A77 and J_Nap with block-preserving uncertainty. A generic rival is clear if either drug has a same-direction, material, component-coherent context interaction in at least 3/4 P blocks, or if the hierarchical decomposition shows the candidate transferability pattern is attributable to shared drug/context or one component. Separately, a coherent same-direction C_8316 marker-panel response in at least 5/7 genes across the six paired specimens is a generic/state-marker warning. These are qualitative rival flags; effect magnitudes are never pooled across GSE, E-MTAB-8873 or E-MTAB-8316 scales.

Stage 4 — method-stability and staged authorization. The baseline and hierarchical sensitivity must agree on the sign and materiality status of I_B and I_H, with full required rank, no variance-boundary warning, and no single-marker explanation. Supportive transferability requires: Stage 0 passes; Stage 1 is supportive; Stage 2 passes; the GSE hierarchy does not overturn the block pattern; Stage 3 generic_rival_clear=false; and all missing evidence is explicitly recorded. This authorizes only the smallest independent MerTK-by-CD206 functional assay, not target prioritization as a clinical conclusion.

Adverse requires structural validity plus a material anchor reversal, transferability reversal/component failure, or a generic rival that is material and at least as compatible within its own assay. Set next_action=do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals. Inconclusive includes missing counterparts/features, interval spanning materiality, r1/r2 disagreement, unresolved rank/variance, only one estimable block, or unresolved donor identity being essential to the requested claim. Set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer. An imprecise null is not refutation.

The machine-readable output must contain one gate row:
gate_id=MerTK_CD206_assay_transferability_v1; anchor_status; I_B_1/I_B_2 and I_H_1/I_H_2 estimates and intervals; J_A77/J_Nap block flags; C_8316 component flag; component_coherent; assay_block_consistent; donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; generic_rival_clear; method_stable; structural_status; estimability; decision in {supportive, adverse, inconclusive}; and next_action in {run_orthogonal_factorial, do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals, resolve_curation_or_defer}. Conclusions must be linked to this row and computed outputs.

## Baseline and substantive same-input alternative

The simple baseline is the primary auditable estimator. Inputs are exactly the selected rows/features above, with source-local log/scale handling and z parameters fitted within each source matrix. It computes Delta_R1_exact, I_q,r, J_q,p,d and C_8316 directly; uncertainty is contributor/pair/block-aware bootstrap or exact block sign sensitivity, never cell-level replication. Its advantage is transparent estimands under unresolved donors; it can conceal whether one gene or covariance drives the score.

The substantive alternative fits source-stratified multivariate hierarchical sensitivities on exactly the same rows, features, joins, grouping and outcomes: gene-specific effects plus a B_GSE factor and H_GSE factor in the eight-row coculture block model; paired gene-specific J terms with P-block effects in the 28-row drug model; and paired gene-specific C terms with donor/specimen effects in E-MTAB-8316. No latent factor, donor effect, or scale is shared across sources. Use two predeclared weakly informative variance specifications and parametric bootstrap/posterior simulation. Return gene loadings, residual covariance, block/contributor variance share, interval width, rank, variance-boundary and estimability flags. This alternative can reveal a measurement/co-encoding or single-gene driver hidden by the score baseline; it cannot create donor identity, separate MerTK from CD206, or add a functional endpoint.

Freeze the split before fitting: R1 is a locked estimand partition excluded from nuisance calibration and never held out replication; GSE r1/r2 stay grouped by round; GSE P blocks keep all paired conditions together; E-MTAB-8316 keeps donor_id+other_donor_id specimen pairs together. There is no predictive accuracy estimand or clinical outcome. Retain the baseline as primary because the scientific question is transferability and rival discrimination, not prediction. Defer neural/high-dimensional models: without a held-out functional outcome they add complexity but cannot resolve target specificity. Revisit only after independent MerTK/CD206 protein and functional measurements exist.

Planned resource envelope: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, at most 1,200 seconds for tabular transforms, grouped resampling and hierarchical sensitivity. This is an unmeasured planning estimate. A GPU is not scientifically useful for these small structured matrices; that is a resource judgment, not a blanket method exclusion.

## Actual scientific deliverable and unavailable evidence

The future solver must newly fit/estimate source-local transforms, feature/component effects, Delta_R1_exact, I_B/I_H, J_A77/J_Nap, C_8316, uncertainty and method diagnostics, then write source_compatibility.json, output/transferability_gate.json and a reproducible decision row. Completion is these computed outputs plus a conclusion that matches the row—not a favorable hypothesis result. No screening job was run here.

Unavailable or essential evidence includes independent GSE donor identity, MerTK/CD206 protein or direct engagement, CD206-independent perturbation, target-negative matched perturbation, FLS viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, dose-response, time, spatial context and clinical outcomes. HBEGF is absent from the E-MTAB-8873 feature panel despite being a literature rival. E-MTAB-8316 has no FLS endpoint and GSE95588 measures macrophage RNA, so neither is an H-equivalent replication. No automatic verifier can establish protein identity, target engagement, mechanism or clinical benefit; it can check joins, transforms, exact contrasts, thresholds, flags, uncertainty plumbing and conclusion-row consistency.

If supportive, run an independent-donor randomized/blinded factorial of MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle crossed with independently measured CD206-high/low macrophages and a matched target-negative perturbation. Measure MerTK/CD206 protein, direct engagement or validated proximal readout, viability, FLS H as secondary, and invasion or matrix degradation as primary functional outcome. If adverse, stop MerTK-specific prioritization from this package and review generic/context rival evidence. If inconclusive, resolve curation or repeat a donor-blocked assay before escalation. None of these configured matrices can support a clinical treatment claim.

[K1] Alivernini et al., Nature Medicine (2020): inspected provider full-text response, including abstract; MerTK-positive STM remission/repair prior. It does not establish the configured interaction as MerTK-specific.

[K2] Kuo et al., Science Translational Medicine (2019): inspected Europe PMC metadata/abstract response only; full text and supplementary methods were not inspected. It supplies the HBEGF/FLS invasiveness rival, while HBEGF is unavailable in the configured panel.

[K3] Smith et al., Nature Immunology (2023): inspected provider full-text response passages including abstract; cytokine/context-driven FLS heterogeneity bounds H as a transcript proxy.

# Episode 12 crossover: assay-structured transferability of the MerTK/CD206 gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment and source audit. No biological fitting, screening, or effect result has been executed. Parents: candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 and candidate-ba3ec15ac0a3e2c458d36ef3. This branch makes one source-design correction to the Episode-10 transferability child: the complete generic-drug comparison is 6 A77 pairs plus 4 naproxen pairs, not 28 complete pairs.

## Scientific opening, claim boundary, and deliverable

The strongest available claim is descriptive and source-bounded. The configured E-MTAB-8873 R1 matrix contains a sparse MerTK/CD206-labelled macrophage-context inhibitor contrast in a targeted 445-feature assay; its labels jointly encode MerTK and CD206 and its R1 inhibitor quartet is one contributing-donor configuration. GSE95588 contains a separately prepared coculture matrix with fibroblast/TNF context conditions and a second matrix with ordinary drug perturbations. The registry and dataset guide warn that GSE95588 donor identities are unresolved and that its r1/r2 material includes earlier GSE57723 data. The literature supports a repair-associated MerTK-positive macrophage state [K1], a competing HBEGF/TNF/fibroblast route to FLS invasiveness [K2], and cytokine-driven FLS heterogeneity [K3]. None establishes MerTK-specific engagement, a functional harm endpoint, donor-generalizability, or clinical benefit.

The unresolved question is narrower: does the GSE95588 assay show a repeatable fibroblast-by-TNF context interaction in a macrophage state/inflammatory transcript program, while complete same-source A77 and naproxen drug-by-context controls fail to reproduce an equally coherent interaction? A supportive answer would establish only an assay-structured context pattern worth testing in an independent MerTK-by-CD206 functional assay. It would not transfer a MerTK effect, clinical effect, or expression effect size to E-MTAB-8873.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly computed, source-local output: exact feature- and score-level estimates for the GSE95588 coculture interaction on both rounds; complete-pair A77 and naproxen interactions on the same source scale; component coherence, block/sign concordance, uncertainty and identifiability flags; a frozen gate status linked to those outputs; and a continue/revise/defer/abandon decision. A favorable score alone does not complete the deliverable.

## Hypothesis and competing explanations

Falsifiable hypothesis: the GSE95588 coculture interaction

I[q,r] = [q(mtf_r) - q(mf_r)] - [q(mt_r) - q(m_r)], for r in {r1,r2},

will have a coherent direction in the seven-gene macrophage-state panel B_GSE and the four-gene inflammatory panel H_GSE across both recorded rounds, while the matched complete A77 and naproxen interactions

J[q,p,d] = [q(Pp_MTF_d) - q(Pp_MTF)] - [q(Pp_MT_d) - q(Pp_MT)]

will not show a comparably coherent context-selective pattern. Here d is A77 or Nap and p is restricted to blocks with both MTF and MT drug rows.

This tests transferability of an assay-structured context regularity, not target specificity. The leading non-MerTK explanations are: fibroblast/TNF exposure or cell composition drives both panels; generic drug or assay response produces a similar interaction; MERTK and MRC1/CD206 labels are correlated and source-label-preserved RNA is not protein abundance or engagement; r1/r2 and P1-P4 are protocol blocks or reused material rather than independent donors; and measurement covariance or one dominant gene creates a score-level contrast.

The discriminating observation is the joint pattern of exact context contrasts, all component contrasts, complete-pair generic controls, and the same-input hierarchical sensitivity. A coherent result in the separate E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238-versus-none monocyte assay remains a generic-perturbation bound; it cannot prove or disprove MerTK specificity because that assay has no MerTK/CD206 context and uses an Ensembl namespace.

## Analysis contract

### Fixed-contrast baseline

1. Read only bound matrix columns and rows. Confirm unique feature/sample_id keys, header/design bijection, nonnegative numeric abundance, and required feature-map status.
2. Apply one log1p only if the selected matrix is raw nonnegative abundance; record the decision and do not transform already normalized values. Within each source separately, standardize each selected feature using a prespecified source-local calibration across selected matrix rows. Never calibrate on another assay.
3. Compute B_GSE = mean[z(MERTK), z(MRC1), z(TREM2), z(C1QA), z(C1QB), z(C1QC), z(APOE)] and H_GSE = mean[z(IL6), z(MMP1), z(MMP3), z(MMP14)].
4. Report I[B,r], I[H,r], every component I[g,r], direct context contrasts q(mtf_r)-q(mt_r) and q(mf_r)-q(m_r), and source-local score scale.
5. Report J[q,p,A77] for p=P1,P2,P3 and J[q,p,Nap] for p=P1,P3, plus all component J values. Do not use incomplete P2 naproxen or P4 drug rows.
6. Treat r1/r2 and P1-P4 as descriptive assay blocks, not independent donors. Use exact sign enumeration over the four complete P blocks for J and a two-block descriptive range for I. If intervals are reported, use block-aware/bootstrap or parametric sensitivity that never resamples cells as donors.

### Same-input substantive alternative

Fit a source-stratified multivariate measurement model on exactly the same selected rows and feature IDs. For B and H, use gene-specific intercepts and residual variances, fixed fibroblast/TNF terms, block terms for r or P, and partial pooling only across the seven or four components within that source. For the drug matrix include paired A77/Nap drug-by-context terms and P-block effects; do not share latent factors across matrices or donors. Report posterior or parametric intervals, component loadings, block influence, rank/estimability, and whether sign and gate status survive residual covariance.

This alternative can reveal whether a fixed-score result is driven by one marker or correlated measurement noise. The baseline is preferable for primary communication because it is auditable with two unresolved coculture blocks and few complete drug blocks. The hierarchy is a sensitivity, not a donor-generalizing model; if rank-unstable, report failure rather than select a favorable fit. A neural predictor is deferred because there is no held-out functional outcome and predictive gain would not resolve target specificity.

Planned solver envelope is CPU-only: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, at most 1,200 seconds. This is a planning estimate, not a measured biological fit. No GPU is indicated. Discovery audits used 2 CPUs/4,096 MiB and completed in under one second; that does not validate the future solver workload.

## Frozen decision and falsification rules

Define M_GSE = 0.5 source-local SD of H_GSE, with the SD estimator and calibration partition recorded before fitting. Rules are qualitative within GSE; no cross-assay effect-size threshold is used.

Supportive transferability requires: all structural checks pass; both I[B,r] have the same sign and at least 5 of 7 B components concordant in each round; both I[H,r] have the same sign and at least 3 of 4 H components concordant in each round, with the block-aware interval not spanning materiality in the claimed direction; the hierarchical sensitivity is estimable and does not attribute the result to one component; and neither complete A77 nor complete naproxen pattern is comparably coherent and material in the same direction. Label this source_local_context_transferability_supportive, never MerTK_specific.

Adverse transferability is a coculture reversal between rounds, failed component coherence, an equally or more coherent/material complete A77 or naproxen pattern, or a one-feature artifact in the sensitivity model. It means defer MerTK prioritization and treat the E-MTAB-8873 interaction as insufficiently specific; it does not prove MerTK irrelevant.

Inconclusive means missing/mismatched bindings, missing features, nonunique keys, uncurated duplicate labels, donor/block structure essential to the requested generalization, interval spanning materiality, block disagreement, rank instability, or an absent complete counterpart. It is not a null; preserve the descriptive output and seek donor/GSM curation or an independent assay.

Computationally checkable claims are source bindings, feature/sample availability, exact contrast arithmetic, component coherence, block-aware uncertainty, and gate assignment. Clinical or mechanistic adjudication requires independent protein measurements, direct target engagement, viability, and a functional endpoint. Additional evidence is required for causal effect, FLS invasion/matrix degradation, clinical safety/benefit, CD206-independent action, and patient transportability.

## Next decision and minimum follow-up

Supportive output justifies the smallest independent-donor randomized and blinded MerTK-by-CD206 factorial macrophage-FLS experiment: MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle, target-negative matched perturbation, CD206-high versus CD206-low preparations, independent MerTK/CD206 protein measurements, direct engagement/proximal readout, viability, and a functional endpoint such as FLS invasion or matrix degradation. Its interaction is

Tau = [Y(MerTK perturbation, CD206-high)-Y(vehicle, CD206-high)] - [Y(MerTK perturbation, CD206-low)-Y(vehicle, CD206-low)].

Adverse output defers this experiment and prioritizes donor/protocol curation or generic-mechanism controls. Inconclusive output preserves the source-local result but does not authorize MerTK-specific prioritization. Revisit the GSE gate after verified donor/GSM mapping and independent feature curation; do not pool incompatible namespaces.

# Episode 13 crossover: assay-blocked transferability as a conditional MerTK/CD206 authorization gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment. No screening, fitting, or biological result was executed for this branch. Parents: candidate-22602b66d735b53cc3f94b36 (transferability design) and candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 (source-local authorization gate).

## Scientific opening, claim boundary, and clinical importance

The strongest available evidence supports three bounded observations, not a treatment conclusion. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states have remission-associated transcriptional and fibroblast-repair associations [K1]. Macrophage–fibroblast communication can instead promote invasive fibroblast behavior through an HBEGF/TNF context [K2]. FLS inflammatory programs vary with local cytokine exposure, including TNF, IFN-gamma and IL-1beta [K3]. The configured E-MTAB-8873 R1 inhibitor contrast is therefore a plausible source-local interaction, but its Mpos/Mneg labels jointly encode MerTK/CD206 and broader state, and the four cells are one SA256A/SA259A contributing-donor configuration.

The unresolved claim is narrower: should this source-local MerTK/CD206-labelled inhibitor interaction advance to an orthogonal target-specific experiment only if it is coherent in a distinct, assay-structured context and is not equally explained by generic perturbations? This matters because advancing a context marker as a target could misdirect expensive functional work or promote an intervention that changes a protective macrophage state while leaving fibroblast harm unexplained.

Hypothesis: conditional on a structurally valid, material and component-coherent E-MTAB-8873 R1 interaction, the pattern will recur as a same-direction fibroblast-by-TNF interaction in both recorded GSE95588 assay blocks, across a predeclared macrophage-state panel and FLS-harm proxy panel, while matched A77 and naproxen interactions will not be equally material and coherent. A coherent pattern would support only a conditional orthogonal experiment. It would not be validation, donor replication, MerTK target engagement, mechanism, or clinical benefit. Failure of block coherence, generic-rival separation, or method stability falsifies the signal as an advancement gate; an imprecise null remains inconclusive.

The substantive Episode-13 choice is a two-part authorization contract. The source-local gate is necessary, and assay-block consistency plus rival separation is also necessary. GSE95588 donor identity remains unresolved and its endpoint is macrophage RNA rather than E-MTAB-8873 FLS RNA; these limitations are represented as donor_generalizability=not_identifiable and endpoint_equivalence=not_identifiable, rather than silently upgraded to validation. A positive result authorizes only a new donor-blocked factorial with direct protein/engagement and functional readouts.

## Competing explanations and what can discriminate them

1. MerTK/CD206-linked biology: R1 and both GSE blocks show material, same-direction, multi-component interactions.
2. CD206 or broader macrophage-state encoding: Mpos/Mneg jointly label MerTK and CD206/state; component coherence cannot separate them. Direct independent protein measurements are unavailable and required next.
3. TNF/fibroblast assay composition: FLS and TNF may generate the observed pattern without target-specific action. K3 makes block-specific context a live rival; a round reversal or matched generic interaction favors this explanation.
4. Generic drug/context response: A77, naproxen, or UNC106238 may move state markers without MerTK-specific action. Matched GSE P-block interactions and E-MTAB-8316 paired marker contrasts are explicit rival bounds.
5. Macrophage–FLS communication through HBEGF or another pathway: K2 makes HBEGF/invasion a consequential rival. HBEGF is unavailable in the E-MTAB-8873 feature panel; it is not imputed.
6. Contributor reuse, label uncertainty, or measurement artifact: R1 has one contributing-donor configuration; GSE donor IDs are null and may represent reused material; a single-gene or block-specific effect is not evidence of transferability.

The experiment can check exact joins, selected rows and features, source-local contrasts, group-aware uncertainty, component/block coherence, rival flags, and whether the conclusion matches the decision row. It cannot establish MerTK protein identity, engagement, CD206 independence, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, causal mechanism, or patient benefit.

## Staged analysis and exact decision contract

### Stage 0: structural and namespace gate

Before any biological estimate, verify declared paths and hashes, nonnegative/scale status, feature uniqueness, exact selected membership, bijective header/design joins, required columns, exact archive-member labels, excluded GSE Donor2 rows, and source-specific grouping. Write source_compatibility.json containing source, path/hash, selected samples/features, design columns, join result, transform, calibration partition, missing counterparts, endpoint type, and donor grouping. Structural failure is a packaging/design failure, not a biological null.

### Stage 1: source-local anchor

Fit source-local transforms only. If the selected abundance matrix is verified nonnegative, apply log1p once; otherwise use the documented prepared scale and record the choice. Define H_8873 as the mean of the four exact H features after feature-wise calibration. Exclude the locked R1 quartet from nuisance calibration. Estimate:
Delta_R1_exact = (H_Mpos,Inhibitor-H_Mpos,None) - (H_Mneg,Inhibitor-H_Mneg).

Fix M_8873=0.5 source-local H SD before fitting. Use a fixed-score 95% contributor-aware conditional interval and a hierarchical sensitivity interval under two predeclared weakly informative variance specifications. The R1 quartet is grouped as one SA256A/SA259A configuration; no cell-level or four-donor inference is permitted. Require all four component Delta values to share the estimate sign and no material reversal in the predeclared R2/R5 tier checks. A materially positive anchor requires the estimate to be positive and the lower endpoints of both interval specifications to exceed +M_8873. A negative interval below -M_8873 is adverse; otherwise anchor status is inconclusive.

### Stage 2: assay-blocked transferability

Within the eight GSE coculture rows, standardize B_GSE and H_GSE source-locally and set M_GSE=0.5 within-GSE SD before reading the interaction outputs. Estimate I and its component effects separately for r1 and r2. Use block-preserving sign sensitivity and a grouped parametric bootstrap/hierarchical sensitivity; never use donor t-tests or treat eight rows as independent biological replicates.

A pass requires both recorded blocks to have the same direction for I_B and I_H, at least 5/7 B components concordant and at least 3/4 H components concordant in each block, and both baseline and hierarchical sensitivity to agree on sign and materiality status. Return assay_block_consistent=true, donor_generalizability=not_identifiable, and endpoint_equivalence=not_identifiable. A pass means “the configured pattern is compatible with two assay blocks”; it cannot be called validation or external donor replication. A material reversal, component failure, round disagreement, only one estimable block, or hierarchy instability is adverse if precision supports the reversal and otherwise inconclusive.

### Stage 3: generic/context rival gates

For each P block, estimate J_A77 and J_Nap with block-preserving uncertainty, returning all components. Set generic_rival_clear=true if either drug has a same-direction material, component-coherent J in at least 3/4 P blocks, or if the hierarchy shows the apparent I pattern is explained by one component/shared drug-context variance. Separately flag state_marker_rival=true when the E-MTAB-8316 paired C_8316 response is same-direction and coherent in at least 5/7 genes across six donor/specimen pairs. A state-marker warning does not by itself prove genericity; it prevents a target-specific interpretation and is recorded in the gate. E-MTAB-8322 is descriptive context only and cannot enter a cross-source effect comparison.

### Stage 4: authorization

Write exactly one row in output/transferability_gate.json:

gate_id=MerTK_CD206_assay_transferability_v2; anchor_status; I_B_1; I_B_2; I_H_1; I_H_2; fixed_and_hierarchical_intervals; J_A77/J_Nap block flags; C_8316 state_marker_rival; component_coherent; assay_block_consistent; donor_generalizability=not_identifiable; endpoint_equivalence=not_identifiable; generic_rival_clear; method_stable; structural_status; estimability; decision; next_action.

Decision rules:

- supportive requires structural pass, supportive Stage 1 anchor, supportive Stage 2 in both blocks, no generic-rival-clear flag, stable baseline/hierarchy, complete missingness record, and no component/single-marker explanation. It authorizes only run_orthogonal_factorial; it does not authorize a clinical or MerTK-specific conclusion.
- adverse requires structural validity plus a material anchor reversal, a supported material transferability reversal/component failure, or a material generic rival at least as compatible in its own assay. Next action: do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals.
- inconclusive covers structural incompleteness, interval spanning materiality, r1/r2 disagreement without precise reversal, only one estimable block, unresolved rank/variance, or missing evidence needed to distinguish the competing explanations. Next action: resolve_curation_or_defer.

The unresolved GSE donor identity is never converted into a donor count. Because the intended claim is assay-block consistency rather than donor generalizability, it does not automatically block a descriptive Stage 2 pass; it permanently blocks the words “validation,” “replication,” and “population transfer.” If a solver reports those stronger claims, the verifier must mark the interpretation unsupported even if all computations are correct.

## Baseline, substantive alternative, and selection

The auditable baseline computes source-local log/scale handling, exact H/B scores, Delta_R1_exact, I by block, J by P block, C_8316 by pair, and B_8322 descriptive contrasts. It uses fixed score weights and grouped uncertainty: R1 contributor grouping, GSE r1/r2 blocks, P blocks, E-MTAB-8316 donor/specimen pairs, and E-MTAB-8322 donor/related grouping. It is selected as primary because every number maps directly to a declared contrast and it cannot create independence from sparse data. It may conceal whether one component or covariance drives a score.

The substantive same-input alternative is source-stratified multivariate hierarchical modeling. For E-MTAB-8873 fit gene-specific interaction effects plus H-factor and contributor/context variance; for GSE fit gene-specific I effects with separate r1/r2 block effects; for the 28-row GSE rival fit paired gene-specific J terms with P-block effects; for E-MTAB-8316 fit paired gene-specific C terms with donor/specimen effects; and for E-MTAB-8322 fit only source-local descriptive state contrasts. No latent factor, donor effect, scale, or parameter is shared across sources. Use two frozen weakly informative variance specifications and parametric bootstrap/posterior simulation. Return gene loadings, residual covariance, block/contributor variance shares, interval widths, rank, variance-boundary flags, and estimability.

The alternative can reveal a single-gene driver, residual covariance, or block/contributor component that the fixed score hides. It cannot recover donor identity, separate MerTK from CD206, harmonize endpoint types, prove mechanism, or add a functional outcome. Neural/high-dimensional prediction is deferred: there is no independent functional or clinical outcome, so predictive improvement would not resolve the scientific uncertainty. Revisit only after direct MerTK/CD206 measurements and an independent functional endpoint are available.

Planning estimate for the future Harbor solver: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, at most 1,200 seconds for parsing, transforms, grouped resampling and small hierarchical fits. This is an unmeasured planning estimate, not an executed run and not a discovery budget. The matrices are small and structured; GPU use is not scientifically necessary for this design. A future functional assay receives a new estimate.

## Actual scientific deliverable and interpretation

The solver must newly estimate the source-local effects, both uncertainty specifications, all required component/block/rival diagnostics, source compatibility record, and one reproducible gate row in output/transferability_gate.json. Completion is these outputs plus a conclusion that follows the row, including supportive, adverse, or inconclusive interpretation. No favorable result is assumed.

If supportive, the smallest next study is an independent-donor-blocked factorial: MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle crossed with independently measured CD206-high versus CD206-low macrophages, with matched target-negative perturbation. Measure MerTK and CD206 protein independently, direct engagement or a validated proximal readout, viability, FLS H as secondary, and invasion or matrix degradation as the primary functional consequence. A target-specific functional claim requires engagement, a predeclared nonzero target-by-context interaction with uncertainty excluding zero, no viability explanation, and no comparable target-negative effect.

If adverse, do not prioritize MerTK from this package; review generic/context and HBEGF rivals. If inconclusive, resolve the exact missing join/feature/donor evidence or repeat a donor-blocked matched assay before escalation. None of these configured data can establish clinical safety, efficacy, mechanism, or benefit. Clinical adjudication, protein validation, assay-quality review and another donor-blocked study remain necessary.

## Key literature and evidence limits

[K1] supports a remission-associated MerTK-positive STM state and in-vitro FLS repair association, but not this R1 interaction or MerTK specificity. [K2] supplies the consequential HBEGF macrophage–FLS invasiveness rival; only its Europe PMC abstract/metadata was inspected. [K3] supports cytokine/context-driven FLS heterogeneity and limits H as a functional proxy. The attached key-references.json contains exactly these three distinct works, and the attached UTF-8 excerpts preserve the inspected evidence and hashes.

# Episode 13 crossover: a conservative benefit–harm gate for the MerTK/CD206 inhibitor signal

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No screening, source scan, fitting, or biological result was executed in this branch.

Parents: candidate-22602b66d735b53cc3f94b36 (assay-structured transferability parent) and candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 (complete narrow-gate parent). Seed context: D2-T2, candidate-ead723193c7cc7e11842325d. D2-T1/D2-T2 are context inputs, not executable instructions.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis and clinical importance

The closest inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. MerTK-positive synovial tissue macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce a synovial-fibroblast repair response [K1]. A distinct HBEGF-positive macrophage program can promote FLS invasiveness through fibroblast/TNF context and EGFR-dependent cross-talk [K2]. Local TNF, IFN-gamma and IL-1beta exposure drives distinct FLS states, including inflammatory and MMP-linked states [K3]. These findings motivate a benefit–harm question but do not establish that the configured inhibitor acts through MerTK, that Mpos is independent of CD206, or that a transcript change is a functional clinical benefit or harm.

The unresolved claim is narrower and consequential: does the exact E-MTAB-8873 R1 inhibitor interaction reduce an FLS harm program preferentially in the MerTK/CD206-labelled Mpos context while leaving a protective macrophage-linked state unperturbed, and is that signal sufficiently transferable and rival-resistant to justify an orthogonal target-specific experiment? A positive answer would change target-prioritization from descriptive association to a justified next experiment. A negative or rival-dominated answer would prevent escalation of a potentially generic context effect.

### Falsifiable hypothesis

For the exact R1 four-cell design, define the primary harm interaction

  Delta_H_R1 = (H_Mpos,Inhibitor - H_Mpos,None)
                - (H_Mneg,Inhibitor - H_Mneg,None),

where H is the mean of IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end, MMP1|NM_002421.3|Reference_end, MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end and MMP14|NM_004995.3|Reference_end on the verified prepared scale or one prespecified log1p transform if raw nonnegative abundance is verified.

The hypothesis predicts a material negative Delta_H_R1, with coherent component directions, and no incompatible source-local change in the seven-gene protective-state bound in paired E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238-versus-none samples. E-MTAB-8322 should provide only cross-sectional context consistent with a remission-associated macrophage state; it cannot test the intervention. The hypothesis further requires a future assay-structured transfer test against a donor-resolved, endpoint-comparable design and matched generic perturbations. GSE95588 is explicitly deferred in this package, so that necessary transfer condition is not met and the candidate must not be advanced here regardless of a favorable R1 result.

Failure of materiality, component coherence, preservation-bound compatibility, or later transfer/rival separation falsifies the useful target-prioritization claim. It does not prove MerTK absence.

## What changed in this crossover

The transferability parent made GSE95588 an executable gate. The narrow parent made the R1 estimand auditable. This child makes the scientific decision between them: R1 is the primary estimand; 8316 and 8322 are source-local bounds; GSE95588 is not used to manufacture a cross-assay result because its donor identity and endpoint equivalence are unresolved. This is a substantive deferral, not a filename repair.

“Protective-state preservation” is not claimed to be directly measured in R1. R1 is type B synovial-cell expression under a macrophage label and inhibitor contrast. The 8316 marker panel is monocyte expression under LPS and UNC106238, and 8322 is cross-sectional macrophage pseudobulk. They can constrain a decision but cannot establish a preserved macrophage function. No cross-source score, donor, feature row, or effect size is pooled.

## Competing explanations and discriminating observations

1. MerTK/CD206-linked context effect: Delta_H_R1 is materially negative and coherent, while the protective-state bound is not adversely shifted. This is compatible with a selective source-local harm reduction, not proof of target engagement.
2. Label co-encoding or state composition: the Mpos/Mneg label captures a broader macrophage state, with no independent MerTK measurement. A favorable Delta_H_R1 cannot separate MerTK from CD206 or other state components.
3. Generic perturbation: UNC106238 can alter state markers without target-specific action; A77 and naproxen in GSE95588 would be useful matched generic rivals, but their comparison is deferred.
4. Alternative macrophage–FLS mechanism: HBEGF/EGFR cross-talk can produce FLS invasiveness [K2]. HBEGF is absent from E-MTAB-8873 and is not imputed.
5. Cytokine/assay composition: FLS transcript states vary with local cytokines and spatial context [K3]. The R1 four-cell comparison is not a functional invasion or repair assay.
6. Contributor reuse and namespace error: R1 is one SA256A/SA259A contributing-donor configuration, not four independent donors; 8316 has six paired donor/specimen units, not 12 donors; 8322 includes related/repeated specimens; GSE rounds may reuse material.

The strongest result this package can support is a source-local association in the exact R1 contrast, bounded by source-local state observations. It cannot support mechanism, clinical benefit, target engagement, or cross-assay transfer.

## Actual future scientific deliverables

The future solver must newly compute and save:

- source_compatibility.json with paths/hashes, table names, selected rows/features, joins, transform decisions, missing features and donor grouping;
- output/r1_benefit_harm_effects.tsv with Delta_H_R1, component effects, audit sensitivities and uncertainty fields;
- output/source_local_bounds.json with 8316 paired marker results and 8322 descriptive state context;
- output/benefit_harm_gate.json with the single decision row above;
- output/method_sensitivity.json with baseline/alternative agreement and diagnostics;
- output/decision_trace.md linking every conclusion to computed output fields.

Completion is these computed outputs and an appropriately uncertain decision. A favorable output is not required. No output may claim screening, target engagement, functional repair/invasion, clinical efficacy or cross-assay transfer.

## Outcome-dependent next actions

Supportive_provisional: retain the R1 signal as a source-local candidate, record that protective function is unmeasured, and curate the GSE donor/sample mapping and endpoint comparability before running the separate transfer/rival gate. If that later gate is supportive, perform an independent-donor, randomized/blinded MerTK-selective perturbation crossed with independently measured CD206-high/low macrophages, a target-negative perturbation, MerTK/CD206 protein and engagement/proximal readouts, viability, FLS inflammatory output, invasion or matrix degradation, and repair readouts. Expert review is required.

Adverse: if the R1 harm interaction reverses materially, the preservation bound is materially adverse and coherent, or a generic explanation is at least as compatible, set next_action=do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals. Do not rescue it with GSE or 8322 state differences.

Inconclusive: if the one-contributor uncertainty is not identifiable, a required feature/join is missing, components disagree, or GSE curation remains unresolved, set next_action=resolve_curation_or_defer. An imprecise null is not refutation.

## Unavailable evidence and verifier boundary

Unavailable or essential evidence includes independent R1 donor replication, independent GSE donor identity, MerTK/CD206 protein measurements, direct target engagement, CD206-independent perturbation, target-negative matched perturbation, viability, invasion, matrix degradation, repair, dose-response, usable longitudinal time, spatial context, HBEGF in R1, and clinical outcomes. GSE macrophage RNA is not an R1 FLS endpoint. 8316 lacks the Mpos/Mneg context and FLS harm endpoint. 8322 is cross-sectional macrophage pseudobulk.

An automatic verifier can check paths/hashes, joins, namespaces, exact sample and feature selection, transforms, contrasts, donor/pair grouping, thresholds, deferred status, uncertainty plumbing and conclusion-to-output linkage. It cannot establish protein identity, mechanism, functional harm/benefit, clinical utility, donor generalizability, or whether a future assay is clinically relevant. Those require expert adjudication and another study.

## Three inspected works

[K1] Alivernini S, MacDonald L, Elmesmari A, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020. DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text provider response, abstract and relevant passages inspected. It supports the remission-associated MerTK-positive/repair prior but not the configured inhibitor's specificity.

[K2] Kuo D, Ding J, Cohn IS, Zhang F, Zhang F, Wei K, Rao DA, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019. DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587; PMID 31068444; PMCID PMC6726376. Europe PMC metadata/abstract only; publisher full text and supplementary methods were not inspected. It supplies the HBEGF/EGFR macrophage–FLS rival and an unavailable functional endpoint.

[K3] Smith MH, Gao VR, Periyakoil PK, et al. “Drivers of heterogeneity in synovial fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Immunology, 2023. DOI 10.1038/s41590-023-01527-9. Full-text provider response, abstract and relevant passages inspected. It bounds the FLS transcript endpoint as cytokine/context-sensitive rather than functional proof.

The attached key-references.json contains exactly these three works. K1-inspected.txt, K2-inspected.txt and K3-inspected.txt are UTF-8 excerpts with byte hashes recorded in that JSON.

# Episode-14 successor: a source-local MerTK/CD206 interaction gate with an identifiability audit

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. No source scan, screening, fitting, or biological result was executed in this branch.

## Scientific opening and falsifiable hypothesis

The closest inspected evidence supports a useful but non-specific prior: MerTK-positive synovial tissue macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce an FLS repair response [K1]. A different macrophage state can promote FLS invasiveness through fibroblast/TNF/EGFR cross-talk [K2], and local TNF, IFN-gamma and IL-1beta exposures produce distinct, context-sensitive FLS transcript states [K3]. These observations do not establish that the configured inhibitor acts through MerTK, that the jointly labelled Mpos state is independent of CD206, or that the configured transcript endpoint is repair, invasion, or clinical benefit.

The unresolved claim is deliberately narrower:

> In the exact E-MTAB-8873 R1 four-cell design, is the inhibitor-by-Mpos interaction in the FLS harm proxy H materially negative, four-component coherent, and stable under an interpretable same-input shared-state model, with no adverse generic/state bound?

Let

  H_s = mean(z_IL6_s, z_MMP1_s, z_MMP3_s, z_MMP14_s)

using exactly the four RefSeq-like feature identifiers bound below, and let

  Delta_H_R1 = (H_Mpos,Inhibitor - H_Mpos,None)
                - (H_Mneg,Inhibitor - H_Mneg,None).

The directional hypothesis is Delta_H_R1 < 0: inhibitor exposure is associated with a larger reduction of the FLS harm proxy in the jointly MerTK/CD206-labelled Mpos context. A supportive result is only a source-local, assay-level interaction compatible with the hypothesis. It is not MerTK-specific, functional, donor-generalizable, or clinical evidence.

The strongest available evidence supports descriptive state associations and context-sensitive cell communication. The experiment tests the unresolved source-local interaction claim, not those established observations. A negative or rival-dominated result would stop target escalation from this package; it would not prove that MerTK is absent.

## The strongest rival and the substantive advance

The strongest rival is CD206/broader-state encoding: Mpos and Mneg jointly label a macrophage state, so the interaction could be caused by CD206, a correlated state program, contributor composition, or generic perturbation rather than MerTK. A second rival is measurement structure: a fixed mean can appear coherent while one gene, residual covariance, or the single contributor configuration drives the result. Cytokine/FLS context is another ordinary explanation, supported by [K3]. HBEGF is an important biological rival [K2], but HBEGF has no matching R1 feature and is not imputed.

The new scientific information is therefore a predeclared identifiability/decomposition decision, not a better prediction score:

1. Does the exact R1 interaction retain its sign under feature-level leave-one-out and a shared-state/gene-specific decomposition?
2. Is the apparent four-gene coherence distinguishable from a single-gene or residual-covariance artifact?
3. Does any apparent contributor/tier variability exceed what can be identified from the available design, or is it correctly reported as non-identifiable?

A stable negative interaction would justify only the next orthogonal experiment. A shared-state-dominated or unstable interaction would prevent a MerTK-specific prioritization even if the fixed H mean is negative.

## Exact four-source binding and identifiability audit

All source data are read-only. Snapshot boundary: core-molecular-20261003. The catalog is

  SHA-256 162ddf0148975035ee641ae75a2666bf44a7b458b050d79370ee9f550953312f

and the prepared assay registry is

  [private-path]/assay-registry.json
  SHA-256 e959459a88b18aea363570ed029a60199b4415e2fce7ab113bd1a31c77b7f70f.

For every prepared source, join only counts.header.sample_id = design.sample_id and require one-to-one membership for selected rows. Preserve source-local donor/specimen namespaces. Do not join donor IDs across assays, and never pool RefSeq-like E-MTAB-8873 features with Ensembl or GSE symbols. No configured source has a usable longitudinal time field; treatment, condition, cytokine/LPS and protocol labels are assay exposures, not time points.

## Transform, estimand and smallest falsifiable decision gate

First verify nonnegative abundance and the prepared scale for each source. Apply log1p once only if raw nonnegative abundance is verified; otherwise use the documented prepared scale. Record every transform and every missing feature. A missing required feature, non-bijective selected join, or unresolved structural identity returns structural_blocked, not a biological null.

For E-MTAB-8873, fit source-local feature calibration mean/SD within the declared calibration partition, excluding the four locked R1 samples from calibration, model selection and threshold selection. Set M_R1=0.5 source-local SD of H before fitting. The primary interval is a 95% source-conditional interval, using parametric bootstrap from the declared residual model and contributor grouping. It must be labelled non-population-level because R1 contains one contributor configuration; no cell-level t-test and no donor generalization is allowed.

The smallest gate is a single machine-readable row:

- structural_status
- Delta_H_R1 and four Delta_g component estimates
- fixed 95% interval and hierarchical 95% interval
- M_R1
- component_coherent
- leave_one_gene_stable
- shared_state_dominant
- generic_state_warning
- donor_generalizability=not_identifiable
- transferability_status=deferred
- estimability and method_stable
- decision in {supportive_provisional, adverse, inconclusive}
- next_action in {curate_GSE_then_run_transfer_gate, do_not_prioritize_and_review_rivals, resolve_curation_or_defer}

Predeclared flags:

- material_negative iff the upper endpoint of both fixed and hierarchical intervals is below -M_R1.
- component_coherent iff all four Delta_g have negative sign and no required feature is missing.
- leave_one_gene_stable iff removing each H gene in turn leaves the interaction negative; this is a sensitivity, not independent replication.
- shared_state_dominant iff the hierarchical shared-state component accounts for the interaction while gene-specific residual effects are collectively compatible with zero, or the hierarchy's sign differs from the fixed score. This is adverse to a MerTK-specific prioritization, although it may still describe a broader state interaction.
- generic_state_warning iff the six-pair 8316 state panel has a predeclared material coherent shift in at least 5/7 markers in an adverse direction, with donor-cluster uncertainty.
- method_stable iff both intervals are estimable, neither fit has rank/variance-boundary failure, and fixed and hierarchical estimates agree in sign and materiality.
- supportive_provisional requires structural_status=pass, material_negative, component_coherent, leave_one_gene_stable, generic_state_warning=false, shared_state_dominant=false and method_stable=true. It authorizes only curation and a later orthogonal assay; it does not authorize MerTK clinical prioritization.
- adverse requires a material positive/reversal, shared_state_dominant=true with a valid fit, a generic/state rival at least as material as the R1 effect, or a component/contributor audit that reverses the sign.
- every other case is inconclusive, including non-identifiable hierarchy, missing counterparts, a materiality-spanning interval, or unresolved GSE curation. An imprecise null is not refutation.

The gate is intentionally stronger than “Delta is negative”: it asks whether the fixed score contains reproducible information not explained by the alternative. It does not pretend to identify MerTK when Mpos/Mneg are jointly labelled.

## Matched methods before selection

### Transparent fixed-score baseline

Inputs are exactly the selected rows/features above. The baseline computes source-local z features, H, Delta_H_R1 and component effects; paired C_8316(g); and descriptive B_8322 state contrasts. R1 is locked and excluded from nuisance calibration. R2/R5 are grouped tier diagnostics, 8316 pairs remain intact, and 8322 donor/repeated/related units remain intact. No predictive split is meaningful; the design is an estimand partition, not a forecasting task. Use contributor/pair-aware conditional bootstrap and feature leave-one-out sensitivities.

This baseline is auditable and preserves the finite source-local estimand. It loses information about residual covariance, shared versus gene-specific structure, and whether apparent coherence is a shrinkage/measurement artifact.

### Substantive same-input hierarchical/shared-state alternative

On the identical selected inputs, fit separate source-stratified models; no donor, scale, latent factor or parameter is shared across assays. For E-MTAB-8873, use a multivariate model

  y_sg = mu_g + a_g I_s + c_g M_s + delta_g(I_s*M_s) + b_g,k(s) + e_sg,
  delta_g = theta*w_g + u_g,

where w_g are the fixed H weights, k is the contributor/round diagnostic grouping, and the shared theta plus gene-specific u_g decomposition asks whether the interaction is a common state signal or gene-specific residual structure. The single R1 contributor is a fixed/diagnostic level: the model must report contributor variance as not identifiable rather than borrowing it from unrelated assays. R2/R5 may inform only the declared tier sensitivity and cannot create matched R1 replication.

For E-MTAB-8316, fit paired gene contrasts with donor/specimen pair effects and donor-cluster uncertainty. For E-MTAB-8322, fit state contrasts with donor/repeated/related flags; do not use it to estimate treatment response. Use two weakly informative variance specifications fixed before reading Delta, with parametric bootstrap or posterior simulation. Return theta, each delta_g, residual covariance, shared-state fraction, contributor/tier variance share where estimable, interval width, rank, variance-boundary and estimability flags.

The alternative could reveal that the fixed H mean is supported by all four genes, that one gene drives it, or that covariance/shared state explains the mean. It cannot separate MerTK from CD206, create independent donors, recover HBEGF, infer function, or establish mechanism. Selection: retain the fixed score as the primary estimand and the hierarchy as a required scientific sensitivity. Do not choose a neural or high-dimensional predictor because it cannot resolve the central identifiability problem without independently measured markers or a functional endpoint. Revisit that choice only after an independent-donor, protein- and function-anchored dataset exists.

Resource estimate for both methods plus resampling: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, CPU-only, at most 1,200 seconds. This is a planning estimate, not a measured run. The matrices and parameterization are small; a GPU is not scientifically useful. The future solver must report actual runtime and any convergence/variance-boundary failures rather than silently simplifying the model.

## Actual scientific deliverable

Completion requires newly computed, reproducible outputs:

- source_compatibility.json: exact paths/hashes, table names, archive members, selected sample IDs/features, joins, transforms, missing features, namespaces, group keys and GSE deferral reason.
- output/r1_harm_effects.tsv: Delta_H_R1, Delta_g, sensitivity effects and uncertainty.
- output/source_local_bounds.json: 8316 paired marker bound and 8322 descriptive state context.
- output/method_sensitivity.json: fixed versus hierarchical estimates, intervals, shared-state fraction, component/leave-one-gene flags, rank and variance diagnostics.
- output/benefit_harm_gate.json: the single decision row and next action.
- output/decision_trace.md: every scientific conclusion linked to computed output fields.

No biological result is asserted here. A planned check is not an executed result.

## Outcome interpretation and next study

Supportive provisional: the exact R1 source-local harm interaction is negative, coherent, leave-one-gene stable, method-stable and not contradicted by the generic/state bound. This supports curation of GSE95588 and planning—not execution—of an independent-donor orthogonal test.

Adverse: a positive/reversed interaction, a valid shared-state-dominated alternative, an adverse generic marker response, or a composition/contributor audit reversal means do not prioritize MerTK from this package; review CD206/broader-state and other rivals.

Inconclusive: missing joins/features, non-identifiable variance, unstable hierarchy, or a materiality-spanning interval means resolve curation or defer. It does not refute the hypothesis.

Only after a supportive gate and expert curation should the smallest target-specific experiment be run: independent donor blocks with MerTK-selective perturbation versus vehicle crossed with independently measured CD206-high/low macrophages, a matched target-negative perturbation, MerTK/CD206 protein and engagement/proximal readouts, viability, and FLS inflammatory plus invasion/matrix-degradation and repair endpoints. Donor number requires a prospective power calculation. This future experiment is needed for target specificity and function; clinical benefit requires a separate appropriately powered clinical study.

Unavailable essential evidence remains: independent R1 donor replication; independent GSE95588 identity; MerTK/CD206 protein and direct engagement; CD206-independent perturbation; target-negative control; dose-response; viability; functional repair/invasion/matrix endpoints; spatial context; usable longitudinal time; HBEGF in R1; and clinical outcomes. An automatic verifier can check paths, hashes, joins, feature selection, transforms, groupings, thresholds, deferred status, uncertainty plumbing, and conclusion-to-output linkage. It cannot establish mechanism, target specificity, clinical utility, or functional benefit; those require expert adjudication and another study.

## Three inspected works

[K1] Alivernini S, MacDonald L, Elmesmari A, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine (2020). DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Provider full-text response, abstract and relevant displayed passages inspected.

[K2] Kuo D, Ding J, Cohn IS, Zhang F, Zhang F, Wei K, Rao DA, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine (2019) 11:eaau8587. DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587; PMID 31068444; PMCID PMC6726376. Europe PMC metadata/abstract only; publisher full text and supplementary methods were not inspected.

[K3] Smith MH, Gao VR, Periyakoil PK, et al. “Drivers of heterogeneity in synovial fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Immunology (2023). DOI 10.1038/s41590-023-01527-9. Provider full-text response, abstract and relevant displayed passages inspected.

The attached key-references.json contains exactly these three distinct works, and the attached UTF-8 evidence files preserve the inspected excerpts with hashes.

# Episode 14 successor: audited MerTK/CD206 source-local decision gate

Status: planned Harbor experiment only. The source audit below is observed packaging and metadata, not a biological result. No expression effect, model fit, screening result, or target conclusion has been executed.

Parents: candidate-25a7135eee9b29634cbc3329 and candidate-2c9a2b899e2cd850ca8969b9.

## Scientific opening, hypothesis, and advance

The inspected evidence supports a bounded prior, not the proposed conclusion. MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states are associated with remission biology and can induce synovial-fibroblast repair [K1]. HBEGF-positive inflammatory macrophages can promote fibroblast invasiveness through TNF- and EGFR-linked cross-talk [K2]. FLS inflammatory states are shaped by local TNF, IFN-gamma, IL-1beta and spatial context [K3]. These observations make macrophage–FLS target prioritization consequential, but do not establish that the configured “MerTK inhibitor” is MerTK-specific, that Mpos is independent of CD206, or that an H transcript change is functional or clinical.

The exact source-local hypothesis retained here is:

> In the locked E-MTAB-8873 R1 coculture, the macrophage pre-treatment labelled MerTK inhibitor changes the FLS inflammatory proxy H preferentially in the jointly MerTK/CD206-positive context relative to the jointly negative context; for the parent benefit–harm framing, the prespecified expected direction is a material negative interaction. This pattern is useful for target prioritization only if it survives in-assay generic, direct-FLS, component, composition, contributor, and method-stability checks.

This is a finite contrast in one contributing-donor configuration. It is not a MerTK-specific causal effect. The rival explanations are CD206 or broader state encoding, LPS/pre-treatment handling, direct FLS exposure, mixed-cell composition, contributor/round effects, measurement of a nonfunctional transcript program, and the HBEGF/EGFR route.

The substantive advance is an audit-backed minimum gate. The earlier proposals treated GSE95588 as either a deferred transfer test or a possible assay-block comparison. The full catalog shows two GSE prepared matrices plus a previously omitted GSM metadata file: the metadata improves treatment/accession mapping but leaves P1–P4 donor identity unresolved and leaves 23/70 normalized title mappings needing curation. Therefore GSE cannot be promoted to donor validation. The new gate instead uses controls that are actually comparable within E-MTAB-8873: R1 pre-LPS pairs, R1 FLS-only/FLS-inhibitor controls, R2/R5 mixed-composition rows, and contributor/reuse-sensitive rows. GSE remains a separately reported, block-level generic-rival diagnostic, never an R1 validation or cross-source effect.

## Exact estimand and smallest falsifiable decision

For the four exact R1 samples,

[
H_s = (z_{IL6,s}+z_{MMP1,s}+z_{MMP3,s}+z_{MMP14,s})/4
]

using the exact RefSeq-like feature IDs below, and

[
Delta_{R1}=(H_{Mpos,I}-H_{Mpos,N})-(H_{Mneg,I}-H_{Mneg,N}).
]

The expected parent direction is Delta_R1 < -M_R1, with M_R1=0.5 source-local SD of H. The sign is interpreted only as a source-local interaction.

Before fitting, lock nuisance calibration to all eligible E-MTAB-8873 rows except the four R1 primary rows; verify nonnegative abundance and apply log1p exactly once if and only if raw abundance is confirmed. If a feature, exact counterpart, or one-to-one join is missing, return structural_blocked.

The minimum decision gate is:

1. R1 structural checks pass; all four component effects are estimable and at least 3/4 share the expected negative sign.
2. The fixed-score interval and the hierarchical interval both place Delta_R1 below -M_R1. If either interval is not estimable or crosses the materiality boundary, the result is inconclusive.
3. The R1 pre-LPS interaction, defined with the same H and Mpos/Mneg pairing, is not materially negative at the same threshold. This is an in-assay pre-treatment/context rival, not an LPS mechanistic proof.
4. The direct FLS contrast (R1_SA256A_FLS_Inhibitor minus R1_SA256A_FLS_only) is below M_R1 in absolute value. It is a handling control, not a matched macrophage experiment.
5. R2/R5 mixed-composition rows are checked against the predeclared 1/4 and 3/4 Mpos weighted means; a reversal or unexplained non-monotonicity is a composition warning. These rows are sensitivity evidence only because they lack inhibitor-matched Mneg cells.
6. The SA260R contributor reuse check, R2 Mpos preInhibitor pairs, and R5 Mpos preInhibitor pair are reported separately. They cannot create independent R1 replicates. At least one material reversal in a locked contributor/reuse audit is adverse; sparse or non-comparable checks are inconclusive.

Decision:
- supportive_provisional: all six conditions pass, including agreement of fixed and hierarchical intervals. This authorizes curation/review and the future orthogonal target-specific experiment only; it does not prioritize MerTK or claim benefit.
- adverse: Delta_R1 is materially positive, a rival/control is at least as material and compatible, or a locked component/composition/contributor audit reverses the expected pattern. Do not prioritize from this package.
- inconclusive: structural failure, missing counterpart, method instability, materiality boundary crossing, unresolved control comparability, or donor identity limitation prevents discrimination. An imprecise null is not refutation.

The exact output row must be machine-readable with gate_id=R1_MerTK_CD206_audited_minimum_gate_v2, Delta_R1, component effects and intervals, M_R1, preLPS_interaction, direct_FLS_effect, composition_status, contributor_status, fixed/hierarchical estimates, structural_status, estimability, decision, next_action, and donor_generalizability=not_identifiable. No prose may override the row.

## Four source-family audit and binding

This is a packaging observation, not evidence of biological validity.

### E-MTAB-8316: generic/state bound

### GSE95588: overlooked metadata and explicit boundary

There are two prepared assays, not one:

- GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 41c16047ab7e1c8ad2ace7e9b0c6f376fee00afe9bd6b6f360001ed52755eeb0, with design SHA-256 54fb86625bd5982310e14feddb17247ea2daca6ffae2e4c67c7528a1776b6bdc and feature map SHA-256 745f4fb65a6fb643b3edc1a0c6e2d237be38c029e8ade99415061f068a49859a. Its 70 columns are P1–P4 blocks; design donor_id are null/unresolved.
- Previously overlooked prepared/GSE95588.gsm-metadata.json, SHA-256 c6571a8e8bb87553241986a2bcf4c10060d9e23d64b2e0273cee2b6e6bbb7a9c, maps many P titles to GSM accessions and treatment descriptions. The GSE feature maps contain exact source labels MERTK, MRC1, HBEGF, IL6, MMP1, MMP3, MMP14, C1QA, C1QB, C1QC, TREM2, APOE and SPP1, but each is marked source_label_preserved_not_independently_annotated. The GSE samples are macrophage RNA and do not supply an R1-equivalent FLS H endpoint or MerTK perturbation. Therefore report GSE only as a planned block-level generic/context diagnostic after the 23 mappings are expert-curated; do not use it as transferability validation, donor replication, or a pooled rival effect.

## Analysis, uncertainty, and method alternatives

### Transparent fixed-score baseline

Inputs are exactly the selected prepared counts/design rows, exact archive members, feature IDs, and source-specific grouping above. Fit source-local calibration only; calculate H, Delta_R1, the R1 pre-LPS interaction, direct-FLS contrast, composition checks, six paired E-MTAB-8316 contrasts, and descriptive E-MTAB-8322 state summaries. Keep the primary four rows locked out of calibration and selection. Use contributor- or pair-clustered parametric bootstrap; report intervals conditional on the observed contributor structure. No cells are independent replicates and no predictive split is claimed.

This is the selected primary method because it makes the smallest decision auditable and prevents a model from hiding the one-contributor limitation.

### Same-input hierarchical/mechanistic alternative

Fit a source-stratified multivariate hierarchical model to the same selected rows and features, with feature-specific effects, a shared H inflammatory-state component, treatment-by-context terms, contributor/round effects where present, and explicit residual covariance. The model is not allowed to share coefficients, donors, scales, or feature identities across assays. E-MTAB-8873 keeps R1 as a locked estimand and treats R2/R5 as sensitivity groups; E-MTAB-8316 keeps each donor/specimen pair intact; E-MTAB-8322 keeps donor/repeated flags; GSE P1–P4 remain assay blocks and are not fitted as donors.

Target: reproduce the baseline Delta_R1 and control contrasts while decomposing whether the interaction is gene-coherent, covariance-driven, contributor-driven, or unstable. Uncertainty: two predeclared weakly informative variance specifications plus parametric posterior/bootstrap simulation; report rank, variance-boundary warnings, interval width, component loadings and variance shares. Split: no predictive split; the R1 quartet is held out from nuisance calibration, pairs/blocks never cross splits, and no outcome or feature selection follows observed effects.

The hierarchy reveals information the mean loses—whether apparent panel coherence is a single-gene signal or whether contributor/context variance dominates—but cannot separate MerTK from CD206, create donors, prove engagement, or add function. It is retained as a sensitivity and stability test, not selected for predictive superiority. A neural/high-dimensional alternative is deferred because the available outcomes are sparse transcript proxies without an independent functional endpoint; complexity would not resolve the identified rivals.

Planning budget: 4 CPUs, 16,384 MiB RAM, no GPU, at most 1,200 seconds for selected-column transforms, grouped bootstrap and hierarchical sensitivity. This is an unmeasured estimate. The hardware inventory includes A100 GPUs, but this small structured experiment does not need allocation; GPU use would not add scientific information.

## Actual deliverable and outcome interpretation

The future solver must newly produce source_compatibility.json, r1_gate.json, component_and_control_effects.tsv, method_sensitivity.json, e-mtab-8316-bound.json, e-mtab-8322-context.json, and gse-metadata-curation.json. Completion requires reproducible computed estimates, intervals, structural/identifiability flags, and the single decision row; a favorable result is not required.

Supportive provisional evidence means only that the exact R1 pattern is stable against the declared in-assay rivals and merits expert curation followed by an independent-donor factorial with independently measured MerTK and CD206, target-negative perturbation, engagement/proximal readout, viability, FLS inflammatory output, and invasion or matrix-degradation/repair endpoints. Adverse evidence supports deprioritization or revision toward the rival, not proof that MerTK is absent. Inconclusive evidence preserves uncertainty and identifies the missing feature, mapping, donor, or functional evidence.

Clinical benefit, safety, target engagement, protein identity, functional invasion/repair, donor generalizability and clinical efficacy are unavailable and require expert review and another study. Automatic verification can check files, hashes, joins, exact rows/features, transforms, contrasts, grouping, intervals, flags, and conclusion-to-output linkage. It cannot establish mechanistic specificity, clinical utility, or biological validity.

## Three inspected works

[K1] Alivernini S, MacDonald L, Elmesmari A, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020. DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text HTML provider response was inspected for the abstract and relevant passages. It supports remission-associated MerTK-positive states and fibroblast repair, but not the configured inhibitor’s target specificity.

[K2] Kuo D, Ding J, Cohn IS, Zhang F, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019. DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587; PMID 31068444; PMCID PMC6726376. Europe PMC metadata/abstract only was inspected; publisher full text and supplementary methods were not inspected. It supplies the HBEGF/EGFR rival and the missing functional endpoint.

[K3] Smith MH, Gao VR, Periyakoil PK, et al. “Drivers of heterogeneity in synovial fibroblasts in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Immunology, 2023. DOI 10.1038/s41590-023-01527-9. Full-text HTML provider response was inspected for the abstract and relevant passages. It bounds H as context-sensitive FLS transcription rather than functional harm.

No biological result is claimed in this proposal.
