# Episode 19: MerTK authorization under compound-identity uncertainty

Status: planned Harbor experiment. The registry/design audit was executed as a bounded structural check (job-f3f661fccf4cb4a2b6053128); no biological effect, target-engagement result, model fit, therapeutic recommendation or screening result is claimed.

Parent: candidate-bb89ea422cc57f1a0c2b8589.

## Deliverable and scientific opening

The deliverable is an executable source-identity and target-engagement decision contract, not another expression score. A solver must newly compute source-local R1, E-MTAB-8316 and E-MTAB-8322 estimands, uncertainty and controls; compare an auditable fixed-score gate with a source-separated latent-factor/mechanistic sensitivity; and emit an authorization matrix distinguishing therapeutic MerTK priority, an orthogonal MerTK engagement/safety experiment, broad-state/generic-compound redirection and inconclusive/stop.

The key unknown is whether the current two-stage molecular evidence can authorize any MerTK-directed priority decision when the R1 compound identity is unresolved. Registered E-MTAB-8316 perturbation is labelled UNC106238, whereas the R1 E-MTAB-8873 matrix has columns labelled Inhibitor but no configured compound name, identity crosswalk, vendor/lot, or target-engagement measurement. An apparent cross-source pattern cannot be transported as if these compounds were equivalent.

Falsifiable hypothesis:

> Under a prespecified authorization contract, current transcript evidence cannot authorize therapeutic MerTK blockade while R1 compound equivalence, proximal MerTK engagement, viability and functional FLS consequence are unobserved. It can authorize an orthogonal MerTK-specific follow-up only if the source-local R1 gate passes, the E-MTAB-8316 MERTK-versus-broad-state contrast is specific and method-concordant, generic/context controls are non-material, and results are stable to donor-cluster and identity-scenario sensitivity. A broad, generic or method-discordant pattern should redirect the next experiment.

This hypothesis concerns what the available evidence can authorize, not whether MerTK is biologically important. “Protective” means remission-associated proxy direction only. Remission and resistance are not transitions, and no clinical benefit or harm is inferred.

The strongest inspected evidence supports MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets as remission-associated and potentially involved in fibroblast repair [K1]; macrophage state, local TNF and EGFR-linked macrophage–FLS cross-talk as drivers of fibroblast invasiveness and medication response [K2]; and local cytokine exposure as a driver of distinct FLS transcript states [K3]. None establishes that R1 Inhibitor is UNC106238, that either configured perturbation engages MerTK, that E-MTAB-8322 groups are a protective transition, or that R1 transcript change is functional. The advance is to make these missing conditions explicit authorization gates.

## Competing explanations and clinical consequence

The leading interpretation is that a target-selective perturbation of a MerTK-associated macrophage state alters the R1 FLS response. Rivals are:

- compound non-equivalence, undocumented exposure or different potency/selectivity;
- broad macrophage/monocyte state or MRC1/CD206 composition;
- generic compound, dose, LPS, viability, stress or measurement effect;
- local TNF, IFN-gamma, IL-1beta, FLS state, donor composition or contributing-cell configuration;
- E-MTAB-8322 remission/resistant differences caused by selection, age, sampling or treatment history rather than a protective transition.

The discriminating observation is the joint pattern of exact assay identity, source-local paired specificity, R1 conditional separability, generic/context controls, donor-aware uncertainty and external identity/engagement/function status. A coherent expression factor can strengthen a follow-up rationale but cannot fill an identity or engagement field.

Therapeutic MerTK priority is blocked unless identity, target engagement, selectivity, viability and functional consequence are supplied by appropriate evidence; this package cannot supply them. An orthogonal MerTK experiment may be prioritized if the molecular pattern is specific, stable and not explained by generic/context controls. Broad-state/CD206, HBEGF/EGFR or compound-specificity work is prioritized if the pattern is broad, generic or discordant. Structural or uncertainty failure stops target-specific interpretation.

## Authorization matrix

Emit authorization-matrix.json with identity, engagement, function, R1 status, 8316 specificity, generic/context control, 8322 state proxy, method agreement, donor sensitivity and final action. Missing values are unknown, never false and never imputed.

I_identity is confirmed only by external protocol/vendor/chemical evidence mapping R1 to UNC106238. E_engagement is confirmed only by proximal MerTK/TAM engagement in the relevant macrophage context; transcript direction does not count. F_function is confirmed only by independent FLS repair/invasion and viability outcomes; H is not functional.

S8316 is specificity-favoring only if C_spec is informative/material, C_broad is non-material, structural checks pass and both methods agree. G_context is non-material only if direct-FLS, pre-LPS, SA260R and mixed-composition controls do not explain R1. S8322 is a source-local stable aligned/opposed/mixed/uninformative direction annotation. T_donor requires the four-cluster/leave-one-out and donor-stratified sensitivities to be stable. M_agree requires no rank, convergence or variance-boundary failure.

| Conditions | Action | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| I_identity=confirmed, E_engagement=confirmed, F_function=confirmed, R1=pass, S8316=specific, G_context=non-material, T_donor=stable, M_agree=agree | therapeutic MerTK priority may be considered after expert clinical review and external study | Only computationally eligible branch; current configured data cannot fill first three fields |
| Identity or engagement or function unknown, with R1 pass, S8316 specific, context controls non-material, stable donors and method agreement | authorize only orthogonal MerTK engagement/safety experiment | Coherence is a follow-up rationale, not target proof |
| R1 fail, S8316 broad/non-material, context material or methods discordant | redirect to broad-state/CD206, HBEGF/EGFR, cytokine, viability or compound-specificity work | MerTK-specific priority unsupported |
| S8322 aligned or opposed while identity/engagement unknown | retain only as remission-associated direction annotation | No protective disruption or benefit claim |
| Any join/namespace/count/donor/time-boundary/bootstrap/convergence/archive failure | inconclusive/stop target-specific authorization | Wide null is not refutation |
| Any cross-source subtraction, ratio, pooled likelihood or donor join | verifier failure and inconclusive | Forbidden operation |

The first row is a policy counterfactual, not an expected result. Planned current-data output remains therapeutic_priority_blocked unless unavailable external evidence is added; this is a design implication, not a biological result.

## Baseline and substantive alternative

The primary fixed-score baseline performs deterministic source-local filters, one-to-one joins, namespace checks, nonnegative counts, log1p transforms, exact paired/group contrasts, donor/cluster bootstrap intervals, materiality bounds, inherited R1 gate and categorical direction table. Every inclusion, exclusion, formula, seed and flag is emitted. No random train/test split is valid: E-MTAB-8316 has six nested pairs within four FLS clusters and E-MTAB-8322 is a cross-sectional summary. Leave-one-cluster-out is sensitivity. This baseline loses covariance and latent-coherence information but is directly auditable.

The same-input alternative fits E-MTAB-8316 gene-specific paired effects with a shared perturbation factor, gene loadings, MERTK-versus-MRC1 contrast, donor-cluster effects and residual covariance; separately fits E-MTAB-8322 remission/resistant and naïve/resistant effects with donor intercepts, a state factor and loadings. It must emit intervals or posterior sign probabilities, loadings, rank/convergence/boundary diagnostics and the same categorical outputs. It may reveal shared state, MERTK/MRC1 selectivity, one-gene dominance and state heterogeneity; the baseline loses those covariance signals. Neither model can reveal chemical identity, engagement or function from expression alone.

No neural model is selected: the uncertainty is identity and authorization, not representation learning, and 12 treatment samples/25 verified donors cannot justify an unconstrained latent representation. This is a scientific adequacy decision, not a blanket method prohibition.

Planned solver envelope: CPU, 4 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, at most 600 seconds for deterministic calculations, bootstrap and the structured sensitivity model. No GPU is selected because this is a small count-summary/tabular fit without matrix-intensive training. # Episode 19: source identity and MerTK target-engagement contract

Status: planned Harbor experiment and planned orthogonal follow-up. No biological effect, model fit, screening result, target-engagement result, compound-equivalence result, or functional FLS result was computed in this branch. Source files remain read-only.

Parent: candidate-bb89ea422cc57f1a0c2b8589.

## Scientific opening, strongest supported claim, and unresolved hypothesis

The decision is whether to advance a MerTK-blockade programme, defer it pending target-engagement evidence, or redirect toward a broad macrophage-state/CD206, generic-compound, cytokine, or FLS-context explanation. Episode 18 preserved useful R1/8316/8322 expression gates, but interpretation now stops at an unresolved identity dependency: R1 is labelled “MerTK inhibitor,” while E-MTAB-8316 names UNC106238. No inspected configured field establishes that these are the same chemical, and no configured assay measures MerTK protein engagement or FLS function.

The strongest supported claim is bounded. [K1] reports remission-associated MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subpopulations and an in-vitro FLS repair response; [K2] reports an HBEGF-positive macrophage/FLS invasiveness mechanism; [K3] reports cytokine- and context-driven FLS heterogeneity. The configured sources provide an auditable R1 FLS transcript contrast, a source-local UNC106238 paired monocyte contrast, and a cross-sectional remission/resistant macrophage contrast. Together they motivate a target-engagement test, but they do not establish R1 compound identity, selectivity, target engagement, functional FLS harm/repair, a causal protective transition, or clinical utility.

Falsifiable hypothesis:

> The R1-labelled material and UNC106238 are equivalent only if an authoritative chemical record matches their structure/identifier and exposure metadata. If equivalent, a minimal orthogonal cellular experiment will show proximal MerTK engagement by both materials at non-cytotoxic exposure, and MERTK perturbation will reproduce and rescue the relevant FLS functional phenotype. If identity fails, engagement is absent/nonselective, or FLS function does not track MERTK perturbation, the R1 transcript gate must not be interpreted as MerTK blockade causing functional FLS harm or disruption of a protective state.

This is a prospective decision contract, not a biological result. The substantive advance over Episode 18 is a fail-closed source-identity and target-engagement gate plus the smallest orthogonal follow-up, not another pooled expression score.

## Competing explanations and clinical importance

The leading explanation is genuine MerTK perturbation: R1 is UNC106238, both suppress ligand-induced MerTK signalling, and the macrophage perturbation changes a functional FLS endpoint. Alternatives are:

1. R1 is a different compound, or dose, lot, formulation, or exposure differs.
2. A broad macrophage/CD206/MRC1 state, HBEGF, cytokine context, or composition explains the transcript response without selective MerTK engagement.
3. Generic compound, vehicle, dose, LPS, cytotoxicity, or measurement effects explain it.
4. MerTK-positive macrophages are associated with remission/repair, so blockade could disrupt a protective state, but R1 transcripts are not a functional harm endpoint.
5. Contributing-donor selection, timing, or cross-sectional group composition explains the observations.

The discriminating observations are chemical identity, proximal p-MerTK engagement with total protein and viability controls, and a donor-blocked macrophage–FLS functional assay with MERTK loss-of-function and rescue. A positive transcript result without these remains descriptive; engagement without function establishes pharmacology, not clinical harm or benefit.

## Machine-checkable identity and engagement gate

The solver must emit `identity-audit.json`, with each item status PASS, FAIL_CONFLICT, or UNRESOLVED_MISSING_EVIDENCE. The last status blocks any equivalence or on-target claim; it is not a biological null.

For 8316, inspected design fields are `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, and `unit_definition`. Its source metadata names `Factor Value[compound]=UNC106238`, `Factor Value[dose]=250`, and LPS 1 ng/mL. For R1, inspected fields are `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, and `cells`; the relevant treatment text is “macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor.” The R1 design/registry has no verified chemical name, structure, canonical identifier, lot, concentration, or exposure duration. Archive filenames containing `Inhibitor` do not supply those facts. 8322 has group metadata but no treatment compound.

The assay registry can check assay, prepared matrix/design paths, sample and feature counts, donor restrictions, and input hashes. The binding template can check immutable source-to-target archive members and hashes. Neither can establish chemical structure, occupancy, selectivity, protein signalling, viability, or FLS function.

Set `compound_equivalence=PASS` only when an authoritative future record supplies a canonical identifier or exact structure for R1, an exact match to UNC106238 (canonical structure/InChIKey or authoritative cross-reference), matched formulation/lot and concentration/dose units, exposure duration, cell context, and no metadata conflict. Set FAIL_CONFLICT for an authoritative mismatch. Set UNRESOLVED_MISSING_EVIDENCE for the current R1-only label, missing exposure, or inference from filenames, transcripts, or literature. The current Harbor package must emit UNRESOLVED_MISSING_EVIDENCE.

The planned orthogonal assay uses R1 material and UNC106238 side-by-side in primary human monocyte-derived macrophages, with vehicle, a MerTK-specific comparator, and broad-state/generic-compound controls. Lock the R1 concentration and exposure from the authoritative record before testing. Measure ligand-induced phospho-MerTK and total MerTK, with p-AKT/ERK as downstream context, viability/cell number, MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/C1Q/APOE, HBEGF, and compact TNF/IFN-gamma/IL-1beta markers. Include MERTK loss-of-function and, if a functional phenotype appears, MERTK add-back or another validated rescue.

Define engagement PASS before looking at results as reproducible reduction in ligand-induced p-MerTK versus vehicle, total MerTK preserved, viability above the preregistered assay floor, and a 95% interval excluding zero at a source-local materiality bound of 0.5 within-donor SD. If the bound is undefined or underpowered, emit inconclusive. If R1 and UNC106238 diverge despite matched identity, pharmacologic equivalence fails. A target transcript is not an engagement readout.

The functional follow-up uses independent macrophage and FLS donors in a blocked co-culture. Compare vehicle, R1, UNC106238, MERTK loss-of-function, and rescue under the same pre-treatment/washout protocol. Lock a short ligand-stimulation window for engagement, a fixed macrophage pre-treatment interval, and a fixed co-culture interval before execution; deposited matrices have no usable time field, so their labels are not longitudinal evidence. Use one validated FLS function, preferably standardized matrix invasion or an equivalent repair/invasion assay, with FLS viability and the R1 transcript panel secondary. Functional PASS requires a material compound effect phenocopied by MERTK loss-of-function and attenuated by rescue without a viability explanation.

This separates: target-specific blockade (matched identity, proximal engagement, phenocopy and rescue); broad-state (state/cytokine shift without selective engagement); generic compound (R1-only effect or no MERTK phenocopy); and protective-state concern (on-target blockade plus functional loss of repair). None alone proves clinical hazard.

# Episode 20 — MerTK identity, engagement, and protective-state boundary

Status: planned Harbor experiment. No screening, biological effect, model fit, target engagement, compound-equivalence, or FLS functional result was computed. Source files are read-only.

Parent: candidate-ac6c4602043af43a976748e1.

## Deliverable and falsifiable hypothesis

The new scientific deliverable is a reproducible, source-local identity/compatibility analysis: newly computed fixed estimands and a same-input hierarchical/mechanistic sensitivity analysis for R1, E-MTAB-8316, and E-MTAB-8322, plus an explicit identity-audit and decision trace. Completion means the solver emits the required audit, estimates, uncertainty intervals, model diagnostics, branch statuses, and conclusion links. It does not mean that MerTK engagement or FLS function has been demonstrated.

The clinical decision is whether a MerTK-blockade programme should proceed to target-engagement and protective-state functional testing, be deferred pending identity evidence, or be redirected toward a broad macrophage-state/HBEGF or generic-compound explanation.

Falsifiable hypothesis:

> Conditional on an authoritative chemical record establishing that the E-MTAB-8873 R1 material is the same chemical and matched exposure as E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238, its source-local expression pattern is more consistent with a MerTK-selective perturbation than with a broad macrophage-state or generic-compound effect, while the E-MTAB-8322 remission-versus-resistant contrast is a compatible but non-causal protective-state proxy. The hypothesis is not supported as a target-engagement claim unless a future orthogonal assay shows proximal MerTK signalling inhibition with preserved total MerTK and viability. It is adverse to a MerTK-specific programme if identity conflicts, if the expression pattern is broad/nonselective or unstable, or if matched material fails the proximal engagement/functional phenocopy and rescue tests.

The current package must remain UNRESOLVED_MISSING_EVIDENCE for compound equivalence. An expression contrast cannot upgrade that status.

## What is known, what is unresolved, and why it matters

K1 found remission-associated MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets with regulatory signatures and an in-vitro FLS repair response. K2 identified an HBEGF-positive macrophage/FLS invasiveness mechanism, a substantive rival to a MerTK-centered interpretation of FLS inflammatory transcripts. K3 established that arthritis FLS are heterogeneous and can carry distinct inflammatory or tissue-damaging programmes. These works make the target clinically consequential but do not identify the configured R1 chemical or substitute for proximal protein engagement and FLS function.

The configured evidence is narrower. E-MTAB-8873 calls the treatment “macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor” and contains the R1 FLS transcript contrast. E-MTAB-8316 explicitly names UNC106238 and records dose 250 in source metadata for paired monocyte samples. No inspected configured design, registry, catalog, or archive member supplies an R1 chemical structure/canonical identifier, formulation or lot, concentration and units, exposure duration, MerTK occupancy/signalling, viability, or FLS invasion/repair. Therefore “R1 is UNC106238” is an unresolved identity proposition, not an observed fact.

The important unresolved question is whether the R1/8316 expression compatibility is target-specific enough to justify the next experiment, and whether the remission/resistant signal can be used to motivate a protective-state test without being mislabelled as a transition or treatment effect. The answer can change whether a MerTK programme is advanced to target-engagement/functional testing. It cannot by itself establish clinical benefit or harm.

Competing explanations and predictions:

1. MerTK perturbation: after identity is independently passed, the R1 FLS contrast and 8316 paired response should show a coherent MERTK-specific component relative to MRC1 and the broad state panel; the future assay should reduce ligand-induced phospho-MerTK with preserved total protein and viability.
2. Broad state/context: MRC1/TREM2/C1Q/APOE and MERTK move together, or patterns are dominated by LPS, cell composition, donor cluster, or inflammatory context; no selective proximal engagement is expected.
3. HBEGF/FLS alternative: FLS H changes through a macrophage-to-FLS programme not specific to MerTK; engagement may be absent and a functional FLS endpoint may not phenocopy MERTK loss-of-function.
4. Generic material or exposure artefact: R1 differs from UNC106238, or vehicle/dose/cytotoxicity explains the pattern. This predicts identity conflict, divergence between materials, or a viability-associated response.
5. Protective-state association: 8322 remission macrophages differ from resistant macrophages in the seven-gene panel, but this is only a cross-sectional association. A protective-transition or clinical-harm conclusion requires longitudinal paired specimens, cell-state localization, protein/function, and clinical outcomes.

Only an authoritative chemical match can move the identity gate from unresolved to pass. Only a future protein assay can support engagement. Only a donor-blocked macrophage–FLS functional assay with MERTK loss-of-function and rescue can support a functional MerTK mechanism.

## Exact source bindings and temporal/namespace rules

Before estimates, fail closed on declared source hashes, binding-template membership, headers, one-to-one joins, duplicate rows, required fields, nonnegative finite counts, feature identity, namespace labels, and absent time. Emit exclusion reasons; never repair a mismatch silently.

Primary baseline: a deterministic fixed-score analysis using exactly the estimands above. It returns each source-local estimate, interval, materiality comparison, contributor configuration, cluster/donor sensitivity, identity status, and a categorical direction table with states aligned, opposed, mixed, uninformative, or blocked. The 8316 and 8322 intervals are uncertainty/sensitivity summaries, not validation splits. No random split is valid for these nested/cross-sectional data.

Substantive same-input alternative: source-separated hierarchical models using identical rows and metadata. For 8316, fit gene-specific paired effects, a shared treatment factor with gene loadings, the MERTK-versus-MRC1 contrast, four FLS-donor-cluster random effects, and residual covariance. For 8322, fit remission-versus-resistant and naive-versus-resistant effects with donor random effects and a state factor. Keep likelihoods separate; compare posterior/interval sign probabilities and the categorical direction table, never a pooled effect across studies. The alternative can reveal coherent shared-state structure, MERTK/MRC1 selectivity, one-gene dominance, and donor heterogeneity that fixed means lose. It cannot create identity, protein engagement, or function evidence.

Selection: fixed-score is primary because it is transparent and directly auditable with very small nested samples. The hierarchical alternative is retained as a substantive sensitivity, not a predictive contest. A neural model is deferred: the available data have no justified prediction target, have nested/uncertain independence, and added complexity cannot fill the chemical or functional evidence gap. Revisit it only if a verified target-engagement/function-labelled dataset and independent units become available.

Planned future solver envelope: CPU, 4 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, at most 600 seconds for audit, fixed scores, bootstrap and hierarchical sensitivity. This is a planning estimate, not a measured execution. GPU is not selected because the current task is small tabular/count aggregation and uncertainty modeling; GPU methods are not categorically excluded.

Set FAIL_CONFLICT for an authoritative mismatch. A filename, label, transcript, or shared study context is insufficient.

The future orthogonal assay is outside the configured Harbor matrices and is not claimed executed. If identity passes, test R1 and UNC106238 side-by-side in primary human monocyte-derived macrophages with vehicle, a MerTK-specific comparator, broad-state and generic-compound controls. Measure ligand-induced phospho-MerTK and total MerTK, p-AKT/ERK context, viability/cell number, MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/C1Q/APOE, HBEGF, and compact TNF/IFN-gamma/IL-1beta markers. Engagement PASS requires reproducible reduction in ligand-induced p-MerTK versus vehicle, preserved total MerTK, viability above a predeclared floor, and a 95% interval excluding zero at the 0.5 within-donor-SD materiality bound. A target transcript is not engagement.

If a functional phenotype appears, use independent macrophage and FLS donors in a blocked co-culture comparing vehicle, both materials, MERTK loss-of-function, and add-back/rescue under the same protocol. Use one validated FLS function (preferably standardized matrix invasion or repair/invasion equivalent), FLS viability, and the R1 transcript panel as secondary. Functional PASS requires material effect, MERTK phenocopy, rescue attenuation, and no viability explanation.

## Protective-state branch contract

The protective-state branch is admitted only as a conditional, source-local proxy. 8322 can estimate whether remission and resistant macrophage groups differ on the predeclared seven-gene panel after donor exclusions; it cannot tell whether a cell transitioned, whether MerTK caused the difference, whether treatment produced it, or whether it protects FLS. 8316 is a separate UNC106238-versus-none monocyte contrast nested in four FLS-donor clusters. 8873 is a separate R1-labelled FLS transcript condition. Because cell type, donor, specimen, treatment, and time namespaces differ, no arithmetic combination is allowed.

The branch is informative_proxy only when 8322 passes its own source-local gates, has an interpretable donor-level interval and five-of-seven direction result, and the conclusion is worded as a cross-sectional association. It is blocked for identity interpretation whenever R1 equivalence is unresolved, for transition interpretation whenever time/paired specimens are absent, and for protective-function interpretation whenever no FLS function endpoint is measured. Thus the current package must not claim that MerTK blockade disrupts a protective state.

## Falsification and interpretation contract

Supportive Harbor output: valid bindings; no identity conflict; R1 and 8316 source-local patterns are directionally compatible with a selective component; 8322 is an informative but explicitly cross-sectional proxy; and a future authoritative identity record passes. This supports compatibility and justifies an orthogonal engagement study, not engagement, clinical benefit, or protective-state causality.

Adverse output: identity conflict; failed joins or feature identity; an R1 pattern that is broad, composition-driven, or unstable; 8316 lacks MERTK/MRC1 specificity; 8322 contradicts the predeclared proxy; or the hierarchical and fixed analyses disagree materially. These results redirect or revise the target hypothesis; they do not prove MerTK is irrelevant.

Inconclusive output: unresolved identity, missing exposure, wide intervals, insufficient cluster/donor support, method discordance, missing variance, or curation-only GSE95588. An imprecise null is not refutation.

Automatic verification can check source paths, hashes, archive members, columns, joins, feature rows, formulas, source-local estimates, branch statuses, and conclusion-to-output linkage. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for chemical equivalence when records are absent, selectivity, protein occupancy, viability interpretation, FLS repair/invasion, causal protective-state claims, donor generalizability, and clinical utility.

[K1] Alivernini et al. supports the clinical importance of MerTK-positive remission-associated STM and FLS repair, while leaving compound identity and target engagement open.

[K2] Kuo et al. supplies the closest macrophage/FLS invasiveness rival through HBEGF-positive macrophages; it bounds the interpretation of an FLS transcript endpoint.

[K3] Croft et al. supports heterogeneous fibroblast states and limits bulk FLS transcript interpretation; it does not validate the R1 chemical or the Harbor endpoint.

No biological result is claimed.

## Decision contract and scientific opening

The consequential decision is whether a MerTK-directed programme should be advanced to a target-specific functional experiment, redirected toward a broad macrophage-state/CD206 or generic-compound explanation, or deferred until chemical and protein evidence are available.

The strongest inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. [K1] associates MerTK-positive synovial macrophage states with remission biology and reports an in-vitro synovial-fibroblast repair response. [K2] shows that an HBEGF-positive inflammatory macrophage state can promote FLS invasiveness through EGFR-linked crosstalk, providing a consequential broad-state rival. [K3] describes failed resolution as a proposed stromal-myeloid process in which macrophage state and FLS context are reciprocal; it does not establish a MerTK-specific intervention. None establishes that the configured material labelled “MerTK inhibitor” is UNC106238, that either material engages MerTK protein, that the R1 transcript contrast is functional FLS harm, or that a remission-associated state is a causal protective transition.

The unresolved hypothesis is deliberately narrower:

> In the locked E-MTAB-8873 R1 coculture, the exact macrophage pre-treatment labelled “MerTK inhibitor” produces a materially larger FLS inflammatory-transcript interaction in the jointly Mpos/CD206pos context than in the jointly Mneg/CD206neg context, and the same target-specific direction is seen in the source-local E-MTAB-8316 UNC106238 paired contrast. This interpretation is eligible for a MerTK target claim only if an authoritative chemical record proves R1–UNC106238 equivalence and an orthogonal assay shows proximal MerTK engagement. A protective-state claim is eligible only if the source-local remission proxy and a donor-blocked functional FLS assay both support it.

This is an identity-and-function decision, not a claim that MerTK blockade is harmful or that MerTK activation is beneficial.

## Competing explanations and discriminating observations

1. Target-specific blockade: R1 is UNC106238 at a matched exposure, reduces ligand-induced p-MerTK with preserved total MerTK and viability, and MERTK perturbation reproduces the FLS phenotype while rescue attenuates it.
2. Broad state/CD206 explanation: the R1 contrast follows MRC1/CD206, TREM2, C1Q/APOE, cytokine or composition changes without selective proximal MerTK engagement.
3. Generic compound, vehicle, dose, LPS, cytotoxicity or measurement artifact: R1 changes the transcript panel but not p-MerTK selectively, or the effect disappears under direct-FLS, pre-LPS, viability, vehicle, or composition controls.
4. Protective-state explanation: MerTK-positive macrophages are associated with repair/remission, but R1 may not be a MerTK perturbation and the H transcript panel may not be a functional repair/harm endpoint.
5. Selection and timing: the sole R1 contributor configuration, nested E-MTAB-8316 units, cross-sectional E-MTAB-8322 groups, or unrecorded exposure timing explains the apparent direction.

Chemical identity, proximal p-MerTK engagement, total-protein/viability controls, and an independent-donor functional FLS assay discriminate these explanations. Expression concordance alone cannot.

Emit only a curation report; never use it as replication or as a reason to broaden the claim.

## Baseline and substantive same-input alternative

The transparent fixed-score baseline is primary. It audits catalog and binding-template hashes, headers, one-to-one joins, required fields, namespaces, count validity, duplicate rows, absent time fields, exact filters, formulas, materiality bounds and exclusions. It computes only source-local psi_R1, C_8316/C_spec/C_broad/C_panel, and D_8322/N_8322 with contributor-aware or cluster-aware uncertainty. It emits direction categories and identity status, not a cross-source net-benefit score. No random train/test split is valid for these data.

The substantive alternative uses precisely the same source-local rows, features, metadata and grouping. In E-MTAB-8316 it fits gene-specific paired effects with a shared UNC106238 factor, MERTK-versus-MRC1 loading, four-cluster random effect and residual covariance. In E-MTAB-8322 it fits remission/resistant and naive/resistant effects with donor random effects and a shared state factor. R1 is modeled as a finite four-cell conditional interaction with contributor uncertainty, not as a population-generalizable random effect. Likelihoods remain source-separated; the alternative is compared with the baseline only through interval overlap, sign probabilities, coherence, one-gene dominance, contributor/cluster heterogeneity and method-stability flags. It can reveal whether a fixed mean is driven by one gene, whether MERTK and MRC1 separate, and whether state effects are coherent across donors. It cannot manufacture chemical identity, protein engagement, time ordering or FLS function.

Target and split/grouping are fixed before fitting: paired sample units within the six E-MTAB-8316 pairs nested in four clusters; donor-level E-MTAB-8322 groups with SA149 exclusions; R1 contributor configuration with no random split. Uncertainty is four-cluster or donor bootstrap, leave-one-cluster-out sensitivity, and model interval/posterior uncertainty. No cross-source pooled likelihood, donor join, or transferability metric is allowed.

Planned future solver envelope: CPU, 4 CPUs, 16 GiB RAM, up to 600 seconds for audit, fixed scores, bootstrap and hierarchical sensitivity. This is an unverified estimate, not an executed result. GPU is deferred because the actual scientific uncertainty is small structured data plus missing identity/functional evidence; neural or deep models would not answer the target-engagement question and there is no defensible training target or independent validation unit. The hierarchical alternative is retained because it exposes biological coherence and contributor/cluster instability that the fixed score loses, not to chase a small prediction gain. Revisit a larger model only if an independent donor-rich, target-engaged dataset and a prespecified mechanistic prediction become available.

Selection reason: use the fixed-score baseline for the auditable primary decision; retain the hierarchical/mechanistic fit as a sensitivity and explanation layer. Defer both as evidence for MerTK-specific action if identity remains unresolved or uncertainty is non-informative. Do not replace the missing wet-lab experiment with a more complex model.

## Predeclared outcomes and next actions

Supportive Harbor pattern: all structural audits pass; psi_R1 is at least +0.5 H SD with a dual 95% interval excluding zero; R1 nuisance controls stay within 0.2 H SD; C_spec meets the target-compatible negative bound while C_broad is not comparably large; and D_8322 meets the five-of-seven descriptive state rule. This supports a source-local target-compatible pattern and authorizes requesting the smallest orthogonal assay. It does not prove R1 identity, engagement, protective function or clinical utility. If an authoritative identity PASS is not supplied, the final status remains IDENTITY_BLOCKED even under this pattern.

Adverse pattern: an authoritative identity conflict; R1 effect is absent or points opposite the prespecified interaction; R1 effect is broad/composition-driven; C_broad dominates C_spec; direct-FLS/pre-LPS/viability controls explain the response; or the hierarchical alternative shows one-gene/contributor instability incompatible with the fixed-score claim. Redirect toward broad-state or generic-compound testing and do not label MerTK irrelevant without an appropriate target-specific negative study.

Inconclusive pattern: current identity UNRESOLVED_MISSING_EVIDENCE; failed or ambiguous joins/namespaces; missing exposure or time metadata; wide intervals; method disagreement; fewer than five informative E-MTAB-8322 state directions; or no validated functional endpoint. Defer rather than change the population, threshold, outcome or subgroup after inspecting results. A wide null is not refutation.

The current planned package therefore cannot select a MerTK target. Its completion deliverable is a reproducible decision trace showing exact filters, source-local estimates, uncertainty, identity status, branch eligibility and a next action.

## Smallest orthogonal follow-up

Before execution, obtain the authoritative R1 chemical record and lock matched concentration, formulation/lot, exposure and washout. In primary human monocyte-derived macrophages, test R1 and UNC106238 side-by-side with vehicle, a validated MerTK-specific comparator, and a broad-state/generic-compound control. Use ligand stimulation and measure proximal ligand-induced p-MerTK and total MerTK, with p-AKT/ERK as downstream context, viability/cell number, MERTK/MRC1/TREM2/C1Q/APOE, HBEGF and compact TNF/IFN-gamma/IL-1beta markers. Engagement PASS requires reproducible p-MerTK reduction versus vehicle, preserved total MerTK and viability above the preregistered floor, with a 95% interval excluding zero at 0.5 within-donor SD. Divergence between matched R1 and UNC106238 fails equivalence; a target transcript is not engagement.

Only after identity and engagement are informative, use independent macrophage and FLS donors in a donor-blocked co-culture with vehicle, R1, UNC106238, MERTK loss-of-function, and rescue/add-back. Lock a short engagement window, macrophage pre-treatment/washout, and co-culture interval before execution. Use one validated FLS function (standardized matrix invasion or repair assay), with FLS viability and the R1 transcript panel secondary. Functional protective-state PASS requires a material on-target functional effect phenocopied by MERTK loss-of-function and attenuated by rescue, without viability explanation. If engagement passes but function does not, report pharmacology without protective/pathogenic FLS inference. If function changes without engagement, prioritize broad-state/generic explanations.

Configured data cannot provide chemical structure, protein occupancy, selectivity, viability, an independent FLS functional endpoint, MERTK perturbation/rescue, or clinical outcomes. Those claims require expert assay adjudication and another study.

## Automatic checks and unavailable claims

A verifier can check exact source paths, catalog/binding-template membership and hashes, archive members, columns, joins, namespaces, filters, formulas, source separation, uncertainty outputs, identity status, and whether conclusions are linked to computed outputs. It cannot establish chemical equivalence without the missing record, protein engagement, direct selectivity, FLS function, causal protective-state biology, donor generalizability, or clinical utility. Readiness or a successful computation is not a biological result.

[K2] supplies a specific macrophage-state/FLS invasiveness rival but is abstract/metadata-only here.
[K3] bounds protective-state reasoning as a proposed failed-resolution framework; relevant full-text XML was inspected.

# MerTK-conditioned macrophage–fibroblast communication in rheumatoid arthritis

Episode 1; evolved as a targeted repair of expert seed D3-M2. This is a planned Harbor experiment, not an executed biological result.

## Scientific question and hypothesis

Rheumatoid-arthritis (RA) synovium contains macrophage and fibroblast states associated with either destructive inflammation or remission. The strongest inspected evidence supports three separate observations: HBEGF+ macrophages can induce an EGFR-linked inflammatory/invasive fibroblast response in human RA tissue [K1]; MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets are associated with remission and can induce a fibroblast repair response [K2]; and MERTK+ macrophage and fibroblast states are co-enriched in clinically distinct RA synovial tissue contexts [K3]. None of those observations establishes that a MerTK-conditioned macrophage state is the directional driver of a fibroblast transcriptional response, and co-enrichment can reflect shared tissue context or composition.

Hypothesis: among human RA FLS samples cocultured with MerTK/CD206-positive macrophages, macrophage pre-treatment with the recorded MerTK inhibitor will reduce a prespecified coherent inflammatory-FLS program relative to the matched untreated coculture. The reduction should be larger and more coherent than the available MerTK/CD206-negative control, should not be reproduced simply by LPS pre-treatment, and should remain after modeling the contributing FLS/macrophage donors. This is a directional perturbation hypothesis about an in-vitro molecular state, not a claim that MerTK blockade will improve RA clinically.

The key unresolved comparison is:

- MerTK-conditioned communication: Mpos macrophage pre-treatment changes the FLS program in a reproducible direction, with coherent reversal of an inflammatory score.
- Strong rival: generic macrophage activation, donor mixture, FLS composition, batch/cell-number effects, or inhibitor off-target pharmacology explains the same pattern. Those rivals predict no Mpos-specific, donor-consistent reversal or a comparable effect in Mneg/LPS controls.

What would change practice or research is not a small predictive gain. A positive result would justify target-engagement and functional coculture studies aimed at preserving or restoring a pro-resolving macrophage–stromal circuit in difficult-to-treat or relapsing RA. An adverse result would prevent MerTK state association from being promoted to a MerTK-directed fibroblast mechanism.

## Closest inspected work and substantive advance

[K1] established a human RA macrophage–fibroblast communication axis and an EGFR-dependent fibroblast consequence, but it did not test the configured MerTK-pretreated macrophage mixtures. The present experiment adds a matched perturbation boundary and explicitly acknowledges that HBEGF and EGFR are absent from the targeted E-MTAB-8873 panel.

[K2] associated MerTK-positive macrophage subsets with remission and fibroblast repair. The present experiment asks whether a recorded perturbation of the macrophage input changes a prespecified inflammatory FLS output, rather than treating a remission association as a directional mechanism.

[K3] defined clinically meaningful co-enriched MERTK+ macrophage and fibroblast states and candidate communication structure. The present experiment is a small, donor-aware perturbational test designed to distinguish communication from shared tissue context, selection and composition. It does not reproduce K3’s clinical cohort or spatial evidence.

The advance is therefore boundary testing: state association and inferred communication become a falsifiable, bounded perturbation hypothesis, with explicit failure criteria and a direct next experiment.

## Population, temporal boundary, and exact data binding

Primary population: the FLS sample columns in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 targeted matrix. The matrix is a gzipped TSV whose first column is feature and whose remaining 33 columns are the sample_id values in E-MTAB-8873.design.json. It has 445 measured feature rows (446 lines including the header). The design identifies human type-B synovial cells from RA synovial membrane, with condition, treatment, donor_id, donor_status, age, sex, and cells.

Primary matched Mpos inhibitor comparison uses only these design-matrix pairs, because both untreated and pre-inhibitor samples are present for the same recorded contributing-donor mixture:

- R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos vs R1_SA256A_FLS_SA259A_Mpos_Inhibitor; donor string SA256A, SA259A; untreated versus macrophages pre-treated with MerTK inhibitor.
- R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos vs R2_SA257A_FLS_SA266A_Mpos_preInhibitor; donor string SA257A, SA266A.
- R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos vs R5_SA266A_FLS_SA277A_Mpos_preInhibitor; donor string SA266A, SA277A.

The R1 SA256A/SA260R Mpos samples have a conflicting donor representation in the prepared design (SA256A versus SA256A | SA256A, SA260R) and are excluded from the primary matched estimate until the SDRF/protocol resolves the contributing donor. The three mixed Mpos/Mneg samples (R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_1Mpos_SA266A_3Mneg, R2_SA258R_FLS_SA267R_3Mpos_SA266A_1Mneg, and the R5 analogue) are secondary composition controls, not pure Mpos observations. All E-MTAB-8873 records have donor_status=requires_contributing_donor_model; the FLS cells are not independent donors. No claim will call the 33 columns 33 independent biological replicates.

The matrix’s primary prespecified FLS outcome panel is restricted to measured, uniquely identified targeted rows:

- MMP3|NM_002422.4|Reference_end
- MMP9|NM_004994.2|Reference_end
- IL6|NM_000600.4|Reference_end
- IL1B|NM_000576.2|Reference_end
- CXCL8|NM_000584.3|Reference_end
- CCL2|NM_002982.3|Reference_end
- ICAM1|NM_000201.2|Reference_end
- TNFAIP3|NM_001270508.1|Reference_end

MERTK|NM_006343.2|Reference_end, CD163|NM_004244.5|PolyA_1, MRC1|NM_002438.3|Reference_end, APOE|NM_000041.3|Reference_end, ADAM17|NM_003183.5|Reference_end, and the two COL1A1 transcript rows are retained as exploratory context/QC only. The targeted panel does not measure HBEGF, EREG, EGFR, VCAM1, FAP, PDGFRA, PDGFRB or MARCO; their absence is a measurement limitation, not a negative finding.

Exact primary source and prepared paths:

Six none/UNC106238 pairs are present, but repeated contexts occur within four donors. The source records UNC106238 at 250 micromolar in the repository factors. It is an orthogonal donor-paired compound response, not proof that UNC106238 is target-specific or that its monocyte endpoint is the same as the E-MTAB-8873 FLS endpoint.

- Raw E-MTAB-8316 files: [private-path]/repository.json, MK_readcountMatrix.txt.gz, E-MTAB-8316.idf.txt, E-MTAB-8316.sdrf.txt.

All design JSONs expose no numeric sampling-time field or time-course table. The temporal boundary is therefore the recorded endpoint of each culture/pretreatment sample; the study labels do not establish a transition, persistence interval, or clinical follow-up. For completeness, the other two configured datasets remain directly accessible and read-only but are not silently pooled into the primary estimate:

- E-MTAB-8322: raw [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322 with E-MTAB-8322.sdrf.txt and per-sample *.genes.tsv, *.barcodes.tsv, *.matrix.mtx members; prepared matrix [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36, and design [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.design.json, SHA-256 4ef38a7031542ec07551d585e9a2218f2620320018b3d56a86bde5a0b672a3da. It is macrophage-only pseudobulk/single-cell material across healthy, treatment-naive, remission, resistant and undifferentiated RA states; SA149/SA149P are flagged possible related/repeated donors and are excluded from simple independent-donor inference. It can supply a separate macrophage-state context, never a participant join to E-MTAB-8873.
- GSE95588: raw [private-path]/GSE95588; prepared coculture table [private-path]/GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 f6ec16014f3adcadc223a4082620ee32347a5a9bdf4ee7f30903d7a7d258b9b5, with design GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.design.json and unresolved donor IDs; prepared d1–d4 table [private-path]/GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 41c16047ab7e1c8ad2ace7e9b0c6f376fee00afe9bd6b6f360001ed52755eeb0, with design GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.design.json. Its duplicate/date-like gene labels require the registered feature-map JSONs before naming targets, and its donor-column mapping is unresolved; coculture r1/r2 includes earlier GSE57723 lineage and is not independent validation. These files are an exploratory context branch only, not part of the primary inferential package.

## Sampling, preprocessing, analysis, and uncertainty

The solver must first emit a binding audit: each matrix header must join one-to-one to a design sample_id; each primary pair must have exactly one untreated and one pre-inhibitor Mpos sample; all excluded/conflicting and mixed-ratio records must be listed. Source files are read-only and derived matrices/results go to the workspace.

For E-MTAB-8873, apply the documented targeted-matrix convention, preserve the full transcript identifiers, remove no features merely because they are unmeasured, and filter only samples failing the explicit header/design or numeric-value audit. Normalize within matrix using a predeclared library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for score modeling, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. Do not merge duplicate identifiers. Report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count, library size, and all filtering decisions.

Primary outcome is the sample-level inflammatory FLS score: the standardized mean of the eight prespecified row values after normalization, with each gene’s direction fixed before fitting. The primary pairwise effect is delta_k = score(Mpos + MerTK-inhibitor)_k - score(Mpos untreated)_k for the three usable matched mixtures. A supportive direction is negative attenuation in all or nearly all pairs, with a coherent panel-level estimate and uncertainty. Secondary contrasts compare untreated Mpos with untreated Mneg where the FLS donor contribution is recorded; the one available R1 Mneg inhibitor/no-inhibitor pair is a negative-control check, not a stable estimate. LPS-treated Mpos/Mneg records are a generic activation control and are never relabeled as MerTK perturbations.

Fit the simple baseline as a prespecified per-feature donor-aware model (negative-binomial count model or limma-voom equivalent, with size factor, experiment/run and FLS/macrophage contributing-donor terms when identifiable) plus the eight-gene score model. Do not use an ordinary donor t-test on the 33 E-MTAB-8873 columns. With only three usable matched mixtures, report paired estimates, donor/mixture bootstrap or Bayesian posterior intervals, and effect directions; do not manufacture asymptotic p-values or call the result independently replicated.

Fit the substantive alternative on the same inputs: a small hierarchical multivariate latent-factor model in which the eight-gene inflammatory score is a prespecified loading block and the remaining measured 445-feature matrix can contribute only through regularized factors, with random effects for FLS donor, macrophage donor/contributing mixture, and run. The target is coherent FLS-state reversal under inhibitor, not prediction of a clinical label. Fit the alternative only on the training donor clusters and report a leave-one-cluster-out stress test across R1/R2/R5; with three clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare the baseline and alternative on signed paired effect, uncertainty coverage by donor/mixture resampling, coherence of gene-level reversal, and sensitivity to the conflicting donor record. The latent model is scientifically useful because the baseline can hide a distributed, partially correlated state behind noisy per-gene tests; it can also reveal that apparent reversal is driven by one technical module or donor. It is deferred if the sample-level design cannot support partial pooling without unstable factors.

E-MTAB-8316 is analyzed separately as a donor-paired compound-response context: average repeated other_donor_id contexts within each of the four verified donor_id clusters before any exploratory comparison, as required by the dataset guide. Use it to ask whether the compound produces a coherent monocyte transcriptional shift consistent with the proposed macrophage-state perturbation, not to confirm FLS direction or target specificity. E-MTAB-8322 and GSE95588 may be used only for source-specific descriptive context after their own feature/lineage limitations are honored.

No GPU is needed for the planned discovery or solver: the matrices are small enough for CPU linear/multivariate models, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GB RAM allocation should be sufficient; this estimate is reasoned from the 33×445 targeted matrix and is not a measured fit benchmark. The configured planning envelope is 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; it is a future solver envelope, not an instruction to use GPUs. A bounded CPU fit should be under minutes, but convergence and model-library availability remain unverified. No full scientific screen was executed in this episode; only schema/header/design and source-literature inspection were performed.

## Falsification and interpretation

Supportive result: the three usable Mpos matched pairs show a negative inhibitor effect on the inflammatory score, the direction is coherent across the prespecified genes, the effect is not as large in the available Mneg control, donor-aware sensitivity does not erase it, and the multivariate alternative agrees without being driven by an unmeasured feature. This supports a MerTK-conditioned FLS communication hypothesis and justifies independent factorial coculture with target engagement and functional outcomes. It does not prove direct ligand–receptor binding, MerTK target specificity, clinical efficacy, remission causality, or a mechanism involving HBEGF/EGFR.

Adverse result: the score is unchanged or increases under Mpos inhibitor, the sign is inconsistent across matched mixtures, a comparable effect occurs in Mneg or LPS controls, the effect vanishes after donor/run adjustment, or the latent alternative localizes it to a technical/composition factor. This falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific directional interpretation for this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, or assay validity. It does not prove that MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive result: the three matched mixtures cannot be reconciled, the donor contribution is not identifiable, counts are too sparse, the panel is not measured reliably, or UNC106238/“MerTK inhibitor” identity and exposure cannot be verified. The correct action is to obtain protocol/target-engagement information and run a new balanced factorial coculture, not to interpret a null as biological refutation.

Computationally checkable claims are the header/design joins, measured-feature availability, normalization/model execution, paired estimates, uncertainty, sensitivity results, and whether the conclusion matches the prespecified outcome. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for direct target engagement, secreted cytokines, fibroblast invasion/matrix damage, tissue localization, treatment response, flare risk, and patient benefit. The verifier must reject both incorrect computation and unsupported claims that a QA result proves mechanism or clinical efficacy.

## Method alternatives and selection record

The simple donor-aware score/feature model was selected as the primary baseline because it is transparent, aligned to the limited matched design, and gives an interpretable falsification test. The hierarchical multivariate factor alternative is retained because it can reveal distributed state coherence and donor heterogeneity that separate gene tests lose; it is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos pairs and the targeted panel do not support an unconstrained latent model. A mechanistic ligand–receptor mediation model is deferred: the primary targeted matrix is FLS-focused and lacks HBEGF/EGFR, direct ligand abundance, protein secretion, target engagement and a balanced factorial design. Evidence that would justify revisiting it is a verified ligand-containing assay, independent FLS/macrophage donors, vehicle/washout details, direct MerTK engagement, and a functional FLS endpoint.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted, donor-aware estimates of the Mpos inhibitor effect on the prespecified FLS score and feature panel, plus a fitted/assessed multivariate alternative and the binding/QC audit. Completion requires those outputs, uncertainty and the supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification; a readiness package alone is not a biological result.

## Demonstration and seed dispositions

The three clinical demonstrations were treated as ambition references, not topic requirements. Delphi’s learned dated-disease-history method is not pursued because these are molecular endpoint assays without longitudinal EHR histories; its lesson is to compare a substantive learned alternative against a simple baseline, which is applied here with a multivariate FLS-state model. Oncoformer is not pursued because the configured domain has no routine EHR or chest-X-ray modality; its lab-only adaptation would answer a different predictive question, not this mechanism question. ALADYNOULLI is not reproduced because genetic inputs and longitudinal patient trajectories are unavailable; a latent-factor adaptation is retained only as a compact descriptive alternative for the current perturbation question.

D3-M1 is deferred: E-MTAB-8322 is macrophage-only and E-MTAB-8873 is targeted FLS/coculture, so whole-tissue composition versus within-cell regulation cannot be identified without tissue composition or matched whole-tissue data. D3-M3 is deferred as a longitudinal persistence claim: E-MTAB-8322 has cross-sectional treatment-naive, resistant and remission groups and no transition times; it can later support a bounded state comparison, not persistence/remission transition inference. D3-M2 is developed because its MerTK-labeled pre-treatment contrasts provide the clearest bounded perturbation test, while the unresolved target-specific and functional evidence is explicitly retained.

## Key references

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Sci Transl Med. 2019. DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Inspected full-text snapshot excerpt: work/k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nat Med. 2020. DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Inspected full-text snapshot excerpt: work/k2-remission-excerpt.txt.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature. 2023. DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Inspected full-text snapshot excerpt: work/k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt.

# MerTK specificity repair: a donor-blocked macrophage–FLS interaction test

Episode 4 child of candidate-5282fd53c9408f02e8752f4b. This is a planned Harbor experiment. No biological fit or wet-lab experiment was executed here.

## Scientific opening and hypothesis

The clinically important question is unchanged: can a MerTK-associated macrophage state condition rheumatoid-arthritis (RA) fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) behavior in a way that could motivate resolution-restoring therapy for difficult-to-treat or relapsing RA? The strongest inspected evidence is not yet target-specific. [K1] reports an HBEGF+ macrophage–FLS axis with EGFR-dependent fibroblast invasiveness, but it is a different macrophage program. [K2] reports MerTKpos synovial macrophage subsets associated with remission and an in-vitro FLS repair response. [K3] shows that macrophage and fibroblast states are structured within clinically distinct synovial contexts. These observations support a plausible macrophage–FLS mechanism and its clinical importance; they do not establish that a compound-labeled MerTK perturbation changes FLS communication through MerTK.

Hypothesis: in the prepared E-MTAB-8873 endpoint matrix, the recorded inhibitor effect on a prespecified inflammatory FLS program is larger for MerTK/CD206-positive (Mpos) macrophage cocultures than for the matched MerTK/CD206-negative (Mneg) coculture. ## Analysis, baseline and substantive alternative

First produce a binding/QC audit. Require a one-to-one matrix/design join; list every excluded record; verify the three Mpos pairs and the single R1 Mneg pair; preserve the donor conflict and mixed-ratio records; report per-sample cell count, detected-feature count and library size. Do not filter an absent gene into a presumed zero.

Normalize the E-MTAB-8873 matrix with one prespecified library-size/size-factor method, log-transform for the score, and retain raw counts for a negative-binomial sensitivity analysis. The baseline estimates the eight-gene score and each gene with donor-aware paired contrasts. The primary estimand is the signed Mpos delta across the three usable Mpos blocks, summarized by paired values and donor/mixture bootstrap or a weakly informative Bayesian interval. The specificity estimand is the single R1 interaction I_R1; it is reported as a bounded block-level contrast, never as replicated Mneg inference. The LPS contrasts and mixed-ratio samples are prespecified negative/composition checks. There are too few independent blocks for an asymptotic p-value or an independent-replication claim.

The substantive alternative uses exactly the same samples and outcomes: a strongly regularized hierarchical multivariate latent-state model with the eight-gene inflammatory score as an anchored loading block and the remaining measured rows allowed to contribute only through shrinkage-controlled factors. Random effects represent FLS donor, macrophage/contributing mixture and run when identifiable. Its target is an Mpos-by-inhibitor state interaction, not a clinical label. Fit it on donor clusters and run leave-one-cluster-out stress tests across R1/R2/R5; with three usable clusters this is a fragility diagnostic, not external validation. Compare baseline and alternative on signed Mpos delta, the R1 interaction, gene-level coherence, donor/mixture resampling uncertainty, sensitivity to the donor conflict, and whether the alternative's signal is a generic activation or technical factor.

The alternative is scientifically substantive because separate per-gene tests can miss a distributed correlated FLS state and can fail to reveal that a nominal score is carried by one donor or technical module. It is not selected as the sole method because three usable Mpos blocks and one Mneg interaction block cannot support an unconstrained latent model. It is deferred if shrinkage diagnostics or leave-one-cluster-out fits are unstable. A ligand–receptor/mediation model is also deferred: HBEGF/EGFR and direct ligand/protein, secretion, target-engagement and functional data are absent from the primary panel. Evidence to revisit it is a verified ligand-containing assay, balanced independent donors, protocol exposure/washout, direct MerTK engagement and functional FLS endpoints.

Resource estimate: CPU is appropriate. The targeted matrix is only 33 x 445, and a 16-CPU, 32–64 GiB allocation should fit the baseline and small regularized alternative; this is a reasoned estimate, not a measured full fit. No GPU is required. The configured future solver envelope is up to 16 CPUs, 8 GPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds; discovery did not spend that envelope, and no full scientific fit was executed.

Actual scientific deliverable: a completed binding/QC audit; newly fitted donor-aware per-gene and score estimates for the three Mpos pairs; the R1 Mpos-versus-Mneg interaction with uncertainty appropriate to one block; prespecified LPS/mixed-ratio sensitivity outputs; a fitted and stress-tested multivariate alternative or a documented stability deferral; and a supportive/adverse/inconclusive classification tied to those computed outputs. Readiness alone is not completion.

## Interpretation and falsification

Supportive evidence requires all of the following as a pattern, not one favorable gene: (1) negative Mpos inhibitor deltas in all or nearly all usable pairs; (2) coherent negative movement of the fixed eight-gene score; (3) a negative R1 interaction because the Mneg inhibitor effect is smaller, not merely an Mpos change; (4) no comparable signal in LPS-pretreated controls or mixed-ratio composition checks; (5) persistence under donor/run/cell-count/library-size sensitivity; and (6) concordance between baseline and a stable, donor-stressed multivariate alternative. This supports a MerTK-conditioned communication hypothesis for this endpoint and justifies the next wet-lab test. It still does not prove target specificity, direct mechanism or clinical benefit.

Adverse evidence is an absent/inconsistent Mpos effect, a comparable Mneg interaction response, a pattern reproduced by LPS, loss after donor/QC adjustment, dependence on the conflicting R1 record, or a multivariate factor localized to technical/library-size or composition variation. That falsifies the proposed MerTK-specific interpretation of this assay and redirects work toward generic activation, donor-specific biology, compound pharmacology or assay validity. It does not prove MerTK is irrelevant in RA.

Inconclusive evidence includes failure of exact sample/design joins, inability to resolve contributing donors or exposure/vehicle/washout, sparse or unreliable prespecified rows, unstable alternative fits, or absence of target-engagement information. A null from the single R1 interaction is imprecise and is not biological refutation. The next action is protocol recovery and the balanced wet-lab test below, not favorable reclassification.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes and paths, header/design joins, measured-row availability, filtering, normalized values, contrasts, uncertainty, sensitivity outputs, alternative-model stability and whether a conclusion matches the prespecified classification. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for target engagement, direct signaling, secreted mediators, invasion/matrix function, tissue localization, flare, treatment response and patient benefit. A verifier must reject a numerically supportive computation paired with an unsupported claim of MerTK selectivity or clinical efficacy.

## Concrete next wet-lab test

Run the smallest donor-blocked factorial that removes the current ambiguity: the same RA FLS and macrophage donor blocks crossed by macrophage state (Mpos versus Mneg) and macrophage pretreatment (vehicle, UNC106238/recorded inhibitor, orthogonal MerTK perturbation such as MerTK siRNA or a validated blocking antibody, and LPS generic-activation control), with FLS-only wells for baseline. Use at least four independent FLS donors and four independent macrophage donors, randomized/blinded wells and technical replicates nested within donor blocks; do not count wells as independent donors. Record compound identity, concentration, vehicle, pretreatment duration, washout and culture endpoint.

Before interpreting FLS output, verify MerTK surface abundance and pathway engagement (for example, MerTK occupancy or ligand-stimulated phosphorylation with a prespecified assay), macrophage viability and activation. On the same recorded endpoint measure FLS IL-6, CXCL8, MMP3 and MMP9, the eight-gene panel, secreted protein and a functional invasion/matrix assay. The decisive comparison is whether UNC106238 and the orthogonal MerTK perturbation produce the same Mpos-specific interaction while LPS does not and viability/vehicle controls are clean. If pharmacologic and orthogonal effects disagree despite verified engagement, classify the compound response as off-target or non-MerTK until resolved. A rescue or second chemotype is a follow-up, not required for this smallest test.

## Method and branch decisions

Primary baseline chosen: donor-aware fixed score plus per-feature paired interaction, because it is transparent, estimand-aligned and honest about one Mneg block.

Substantive alternative retained: hierarchical anchored multivariate factor model, fitted to the same 33-sample/445-feature input with donor/run shrinkage, leave-one-cluster-out stress testing and uncertainty comparison. It can reveal distributed state coherence and heterogeneity that the baseline loses, but its capacity is intentionally constrained by the sample design.

Not chosen: an unrestricted neural model, ligand–receptor mediation model or cross-dataset classifier. The reason is scientific adequacy, not a blanket complexity or GPU prohibition: the targeted panel lacks ligand/protein/engagement variables and the design cannot identify an unrestricted representation or a clinical prediction target. Evidence for revisiting these choices is the balanced orthogonal wet-lab experiment, verified target engagement, functional FLS outcomes, resolved donor/protocol metadata and independent donor replication.

The three demonstration papers in the research-ambition references were used as ambition context, not as a topic or method list. They are not reproduced here. This proposal is a targeted child repair of the valid parent and does not alter the macrophage–FLS clinical question.

## Key references

[K1] Kuo D et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine, 2019, DOI 10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only inspection in `k1-hbegf-excerpt.txt`.

[K2] Alivernini S et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine, 2020, DOI 10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Full-text HTML inspection of title, abstract and relevant passages in `k2-remission-excerpt.txt`.

[K3] Zhang F et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature, 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Abstract/metadata-only inspection in `k3-ra-subtypes-excerpt.txt`.

These three distinct works support, bound and challenge different parts of the hypothesis; none is treated as proof of MerTK target specificity.
