# D3-M3 successor: coordinated macrophage state or mixture?

Status: planned Harbor experiment. No biological fit, screening result, p-value, interval, wet-lab result, or clinical conclusion has been executed in this branch.

## Scientific opening, strongest evidence, and unresolved claim

The clinically consequential opening is whether remission and treatment resistance mark a reproducible macrophage program that merits prospective state tracking, or merely different mixtures of macrophage states, generic activation, age/treatment selection, or sampling context. [K2] supports remission-associated MerTK-positive synovial macrophage subsets with homeostatic and repair-related biology. [K1] supplies a consequential inflammatory rival: HBEGF-positive macrophages are shaped by fibroblast/TNF context and can promote fibroblast invasiveness. [K3] shows that RA synovium is clinically heterogeneous and contains multiple candidate myeloid states. These works support plausibility and importance; none establishes the exact adjusted E-MTAB-8322 contrast, within-cell coordination, or persistence in the same patient.

The strongest claim currently supported is descriptive: human RA synovium contains remission-associated and inflammatory macrophage states, and macrophage–stromal interactions may matter. The unresolved claim is narrower and falsifiable:

> In the 13 verified remission/resistant E-MTAB-8322 donors, the resistant-minus-remission contrast is a coordinated resident-to-inflammatory transcriptional shift that survives age and measured-cell-count sensitivity, is not explained by the generic-activation axis, and is visible within cells rather than only as a change in the mixture of cell states.

This is a cross-sectional state association. It is not a transition, treatment effect, target-engagement measurement, mechanism, or clinical prediction. The substantive advance over [K2] and [K3] is an attribution test on an independent prepared snapshot: a fixed pseudobulk contrast is challenged by an outcome-blind, donor-held-out cell-distribution model that can distinguish a broad within-cell shift from a composition-shaped signal. The advance over [K1] is that HBEGF is retained as a rival context, not assumed to explain the remission/resistant contrast.

If supportive, the next decision is to fund a prospective repeated-biopsy and orthogonal target-engagement study. If adverse, redirect toward generic activation, composition, age/treatment history, or the HBEGF inflammatory route. If inconclusive, acquire better paired samples rather than treating a null as refutation.

## Population and temporal boundary

Primary population: the 13 E-MTAB-8322 rows whose prepared design records verified macrophages from synovial membrane and whose condition is remission rheumatoid arthritis (7: RemSA132, RemSA160, RemSA161, RemSA174, SA159, SA168, SA225) or resistant to treatment rheumatoid arthritis (6: ResistantSA144, ResistantSA145, ResistantSA151, ResistantSA166, SA222, SA227). The primary unit is donor/sample, not cell. All 13 are female; sex is therefore not estimable. Healthy (4), treatment-naive RA (6), and undifferentiated arthritis (4) rows are boundary inventories only.

Exclude SA149P and UPASA149 from independent inference: the design marks them possible related/repeated donors and their relationship is unresolved. They may be shown one-at-a-time as a descriptive sensitivity, never as independent replication. No donor identifier is joined across sources.

The prepared design has no verified numeric time field, treatment exposure date, repeat-biopsy identifier, drug, dose, duration, adherence, disease-activity score, or flare outcome. The treatment field is null. Remission/resistant labels are cross-sectional clinical-state labels and are not randomized treatment assignments. No statement about persistence, response, resistance onset, flare, or efficacy is identifiable from this snapshot.

## Variables and exact baseline

Use only these 17 Ensembl rows, checked against the E-MTAB-8322 gene map:

- Resident/homeostatic R: MERTK ENSG00000153208; CD163 ENSG00000177575; MRC1 ENSG00000260314; FOLR2 ENSG00000165457; C1QA ENSG00000173372; C1QB ENSG00000173369; APOE ENSG00000130203.
- Inflammatory/tissue-damage I: SPP1 ENSG00000118785; TNF ENSG00000232810; IL1B ENSG00000125538; CXCL8 ENSG00000169429; CCL2 ENSG00000108691; ICAM1 ENSG00000090339; MMP3 ENSG00000149968; MMP9 ENSG00000100985; TNFAIP3 ENSG00000118503; IL6 ENSG00000136244.
- Generic activation A: TNF, IL1B, IL6, CXCL8, TNFAIP3, using the same measured transcript rows already in I.

For the prepared pseudobulk table, normalize each sample as log1p(CPM) over the measured-feature library size. In each fold, standardize each gene using training donors only. The fixed baseline is B_i = mean(I_i) - mean(R_i). Fit the prespecified robust Huber model on the 13 donor rows:
B_i ~ resistant_i + centered age_i + centered log1p(cells_i).
The primary baseline estimand is the resistant-minus-remission coefficient beta_B, with the unadjusted mean difference also reported. The adjustment is descriptive confounding sensitivity, not causal identification. Report the contrast in standardized units with donor-block bootstrap uncertainty; no cell-level p-values or independent-cell intervals.

## Substantive same-input mechanistic alternative

The alternative uses the same 17 feature rows and the same fold-specific normalization, but retains the original cell matrices to test the unit-of-analysis explanation that the pseudobulk baseline cannot see.

For each primary sample and each cell in its original matrix, compute the same R_c, I_c and A_c module scores and D_c = I_c - R_c. Do not assign new biological cell types or call a module a fraction. Aggregate to one donor-level record per sample with predeclared summaries: median(D_c), median(A_c), IQR(D_c), within-sample Spearman correlation of D_c with A_c, and the fraction of cells in the upper training-defined D quartile while A_c is not elevated. The last quantity is a distributional diagnostic, not a measured macrophage fraction.

In each of 13 leave-one-verified-donor-out folds:

1. Fit normalization parameters and the two-component regularized Gaussian mixture in (D_c,A_c) on cells from the other 12 primary donors only, without remission/resistant labels. Use a fixed seed, fixed K=2, at most 50 EM iterations and fixed covariance regularization; orient components only by their predeclared D direction.
2. Transform the held-out donor's cells and record the held-out inflammatory-like component prevalence pi_i, component separation, median D, median A and IQR(D). If the mixture collapses, swaps without an identifiable D orientation, or depends on initialization beyond the prespecified tolerance, mark the alternative non-identifiable rather than choosing a favorable orientation.
3. Fit the same donor-level Huber model to each cross-fitted summary: summary_i ~ resistant_i + centered age_i + centered log1p(cells_i). The primary alternative estimand is beta_D (held-out median D); beta_A and beta_pi are mechanistic diagnostics. Compare beta_D with beta_B, and test whether beta_A accounts for the B contrast and whether beta_pi/IQR changes indicate mixture composition.
4. Use donor-block bootstrap and all 13 held-out donor predictions. Cells are resampling material inside a donor, never independent clinical replicates.

This alternative can reveal information the scalar baseline loses: a coordinated shift should move the within-cell D distribution with little A change and without a large change in mixture prevalence or bimodality; generic activation should move A and leave A-adjusted D weak; composition should primarily change pi, IQR or multimodality while within-component D is stable. These are competing observable patterns, not proof of lineage, mechanism, or direct MerTK action.

## Exact folds, outcomes, and falsification

The 13 folds are leave-one-donor-out, with no donor shared between fit and held-out evaluation. The fold outputs are immutable: training normalization, held-out B/D/A/pi summaries, coefficients, bootstrap draws, mixture convergence/identifiability, all 13 deletion estimates, and feature-deletion results. The exact label-permutation negative fixture uses the same 13 rows and 7-versus-6 labels with a recorded seed; positive and zero-effect synthetic fixtures use the observed feature-wise training distributions and are separate computation checks.

Supportive requires all of the following:

1. beta_B is resistant-higher with standardized magnitude at least 0.5 and the donor-block uncertainty is not wholly on the null side; at least 10/13 leave-one-donor-out baseline contrasts retain that direction.
2. beta_D agrees in direction with beta_B, with at least 10/13 held-out donor summaries retaining direction, and at least two resident and two inflammatory genes contribute in the predeclared direction under one-gene deletion.
3. The mechanistic separation survives the A sensitivity: the A-adjusted D contrast retains at least 75% of the unadjusted D contrast, while beta_A is less than one quarter of the absolute D contrast. This is an attribution gate, not a causal claim.
4. The cell-distribution alternative is identifiable, and the result is not primarily mixture-shaped: the resistant-minus-remission change in pi is below 0.15, no donor's mixture prevalence or IQR change accounts for 40% or more of the cross-sectional contrast, and the held-out D shift is not confined to one fitted component.
5. The exact label permutation is descriptively less extreme than the observed predeclared statistic, while the zero-effect fixture fails the supportive gate and the positive fixture passes the direction/fixture gate.

Adverse means the predeclared state mechanism is not supported when any decisive pattern is replicated across folds: A explains at least 75% of the B separation while A-adjusted D is near zero; beta_D reverses or is unstable in at least 4 donor deletions; |delta_pi| is at least 0.25 with stable mixture/bimodality evidence and little within-component D shift; a single gene or donor drives the contrast; or the adjusted contrast reverses with donor-block uncertainty excluding zero. This redirects the next experiment; it does not show macrophages are irrelevant.

Inconclusive includes missing required feature rows, failed source-internal joins or hashes, non-identifiable mixture, sensitivity envelopes spanning both decision regions, discordant pseudobulk and cell-distribution estimands without a stable pattern, or insufficient clinical metadata to separate age/treatment selection. An imprecise null is not refutation.

## Four-source bindings and provenance

The read-only catalog is datasets/README.md and datasets/disease_mechanisms/README.md, snapshot core-molecular-20261003; catalog SHA-256 7cf76c53840cd6399b217b105279be4937d8c31f289bc3efbbf05a8eb7a8baa0. All joins are source-internal.

### E-MTAB-8322 — primary state contrast

Prepared counts table: [private-path]/E-MTAB-8322.counts.tsv.gz, SHA-256 95bc3a964f3fbc57cde1957ec6637aaac806cedd8dfccc0526158e9068f43f36. It has feature plus 27 source-internal sample_id columns. Raw archive members are GSE95588_coculture_htseq_counts.txt.gz, GSE95588_d1d2d3d4_counts.txt.gz, samples.soft and series.soft. Coculture r1/r2 includes earlier GSE57723 material, so these files are inventory/context, never independent validation and never a donor join.

## Prospective wet-lab decision

A supportive computational result justifies a new study, not a biological conclusion. Recruit independent treatment-naive, stable-remission and resistant/active RA patients with expert rheumatology adjudication. Sample the same patient before treatment and at prespecified follow-up (for example 3, 6 and 12 months), recording drug, dose, duration, adherence, steroids, DAS28/CDAI, imaging, tissue site, batch and flare. Use barcoded single-cell RNA plus surface-protein/composition controls, the 17-gene panel, direct MerTK protein/engagement and a matched macrophage–FLS functional endpoint.

The longitudinal estimand is within-patient change in the state vector and its prospective association with adjudicated response/flare after treatment history and composition adjustment. Same-patient recurrence is not same-cell lineage persistence; lineage/barcoding or validated tracking is needed for that stronger claim. Expert adjudication is essential for clinical labels, tissue quality, cell identity and whether resistance reflects exposure/nonadherence.

## Method alternatives, resources, and scientific deliverable

The selected baseline is the fixed 17-gene pseudobulk score because it is auditable at 13 donors and gives an interpretable primary contrast. The selected alternative is the same-input, outcome-blind two-component cell-distribution model because it adds information the score loses: within-cell coordination, mixture prevalence, dispersion and identifiability. It is a mechanistic attribution alternative, not a neural predictor.

Deferred alternatives are outcome-supervised elastic net/neural prediction (no validated prospective outcome and too few independent donors), unrestricted NMF/PCA or all-gene selection (would mainly add flexibility and label-driven instability), whole-tissue deconvolution (the primary source is macrophage-only pseudobulk and true fractions are unavailable), and pooled cross-source fitting (incompatible namespaces and unresolved donors). Revisit them only with a larger repeated-donor cohort, validated cell composition and a clinical endpoint. No GPU is scientifically required; the planned fit is approximately 4 CPU cores, 8–16 GiB, under 30 minutes for the prepared audit plus 13 raw triplet transformations (estimate, not measured). Future solver packaging may use 4–8 CPU cores and 16–32 GiB; this discovery design does not launch it.

Actual scientific deliverable: newly fitted fold-normalized baseline and cell-distribution alternative; the 13 held-out donor score records; beta_B, beta_D, beta_A and beta_pi with donor-block uncertainty; mixture identifiability/convergence; within-sample distribution diagnostics; all gene/donor deletions; source/hash/join audit; negative and positive fixture decisions; and a decision JSON linking each conclusion to computed outputs. Completion is these outputs, not confirmation of the hypothesis.

## Claim boundaries

Computationally checkable: source hashes, table schemas, exact joins, condition counts, feature availability, fold normalization, baseline/alternative fits, donor-held-out summaries, mixture diagnostics, age/cell-count sensitivity, fixture behavior and decision-gate execution.

Not established by this experiment: MerTK protein or engagement, direct macrophage lineage, cell-state causality, HBEGF mediation, macrophage–FLS causality, treatment response, clinical benefit, flare prediction, or individual state persistence. Those require orthogonal assays, prospective repeated patients, wet-lab perturbation and expert clinical adjudication.

## Compact bibliography

[K1] Kuo D, Ding J, Cohn IS, et al. “HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness.” Science Translational Medicine (2019), 11(491):eaau8587. DOI:10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Abstract-only evidence attached.
[K2] Alivernini S, MacDonald L, Elmesmari A, et al. “Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis.” Nature Medicine (2020), 26:1295–1306. DOI:10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8.
[K3] Zhang F, Jonsson AH, Nathan A, et al. “Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes.” Nature (2023), 620:137–145. DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y.

Evidence files and key-references.json are attached separately. No biological result is claimed.

# Episode-20 child: non-circular attribution of the E-MTAB-8322 remission/resistance contrast

This is a planned Harbor experiment. The source audit and literature inspection were executed; no biological fit, state assignment, treatment effect, or clinical result was executed.

## Successor purpose and substantive repair

The selected parent asks whether the terminal E-MTAB-8322 remission-versus-treatment-resistant contrast is composition, within-state regulation, generic activation, or measurement/depth. Its cell-level alternative defines resident-like and inflammatory-like states from the same 17 genes used to quantify within-state change. That makes a within-state result partly tautological: a cell can be assigned to a state because it has the tested expression pattern.

This child makes one scientific repair. It predeclares two complementary, disjoint feature partitions. In each partition, state labels are computed from one set of measured genes and the within-state readout is computed only from the other set. The label/readout split is repeated in the complementary direction, while donor-held-out normalization and donor-level inference are retained. This tests whether the attribution survives an outcome-independent molecular definition rather than merely adding model complexity.

The repair does not create cell identity. A state remains an expression-defined transcriptional stratum, not a protein- or lineage-validated macrophage subtype. If the two feature partitions disagree materially, the correct conclusion is that the available 17-gene panel cannot identify the requested within-state estimand.

## Scientific opening, strongest supported claim, and unresolved claim

[K1] reports remission-associated synovial macrophage heterogeneity and MerTK-positive programs in a different study, with fibroblast-repair and flare associations in that study. [K2] reports an HBEGF-positive inflammatory macrophage context and fibroblast invasiveness, supplying a consequential inflammatory rival. [K3] shows that RA synovial tissues contain multiple cell-abundance and cell-state contexts and that multimodal protein/transcript data help distinguish them. These works support the importance of separating state composition, within-state expression, and generic activation. They do not establish that the E-MTAB-8322 resistant-minus-remission contrast is a within-cell transition, a treatment effect, a MerTK mechanism, or a persistent lineage.

The unresolved question is:

> Among the 13 terminal E-MTAB-8322 RA macrophage donors, does the resistant-versus-remission association in a fixed macrophage transcriptional readout persist after composition standardization using state labels built from disjoint measured genes, and is it distinguishable from generic activation and library/cell-depth artifacts?

The hypothesis is that a reproducible resistant-higher association remains in the disjoint held-out readout after standardizing state proportions, while composition and the generic activation axis do not account for most of the contrast. The rival explanations are: (1) a different mixture of cells or sampling fractions; (2) a broad activation/depth response that moves all inflammatory genes together; (3) expression-defined state circularity; and (4) donor, related-donor, or technical measurement structure.

The substantive advance is an identifiable, falsifiable attribution check at the level actually available: a cross-fitted expression-defined state/readout contrast. A supportive result would justify a prospective study with independent protein/composition labels and longitudinal sampling. It would not show causality, target engagement, same-cell persistence, treatment response, or clinical benefit.

## Population and temporal boundary

Primary population: the 13 verified E-MTAB-8322 terminal synovial-membrane macrophage samples, seven remission and six treatment-resistant:

- remission: RemSA132, RemSA160, RemSA161, RemSA174, SA159, SA168, SA225;
- resistant: ResistantSA144, ResistantSA145, ResistantSA151, ResistantSA166, SA222, SA227.

The source design audit verified 27 rows with fields `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `source_name`, and `cells`. The primary rows are macrophage, synovial membrane, verified donors, all female; `treatment` is null. Healthy (4), treatment-naive RA (6), and undifferentiated arthritis (4) are descriptive context only and do not enter the primary estimand.

The independent unit is donor, not cell. All cells from a donor stay together in every leave-one-donor-out fold. SA149/SA149P relatedness is unresolved; related samples are excluded from the primary independent-donor analysis and included one at a time only as sensitivity analyses. No donor or patient identifier is joined across assays.

The temporal boundary is the single terminal sample. No verified numeric time field is available. “Remission” and “treatment-resistant” are cross-sectional clinical-state labels, not randomized treatment assignments. The analysis cannot estimate a transition, treatment effect, persistence, flare risk, or response prediction.

## Exact measured panel and non-circular feature partitions

Use only these 17 Ensembl rows, after verifying each row in each source gene map. No external markers, pathway-selected genes, PCA/NMF factors, outcome-selected genes, or whole-tissue deconvolution are allowed.

Resident block R:
`MERTK ENSG00000153208`, `CD163 ENSG00000177575`, `MRC1 ENSG00000260314`, `FOLR2 ENSG00000165457`, `C1QA ENSG00000173372`, `C1QB ENSG00000173369`, `APOE ENSG00000130203`.

Inflammatory block I:
`SPP1 ENSG00000118785`, `TNF ENSG00000232810`, `IL1B ENSG00000125538`, `CXCL8 ENSG00000169429`, `CCL2 ENSG00000108691`, `ICAM1 ENSG00000090339`, `MMP3 ENSG00000149968`, `MMP9 ENSG00000100985`, `TNFAIP3 ENSG00000118503`, `IL6 ENSG00000136244`.

The source audit must confirm the exact feature identifiers; the proposal does not treat a gene symbol alone as a valid join.

Predeclared split A:

- state panel: R_A = MERTK, MRC1, FOLR2, C1QA; I_A = SPP1, TNF, IL1B, CXCL8, CCL2;
- held-out readout panel: R'_A = CD163, C1QB, APOE; I'_A = ICAM1, MMP3, MMP9, TNFAIP3, IL6.

Predeclared split B is the complement:

- state panel: R_B = CD163, C1QB, APOE; I_B = ICAM1, MMP3, MMP9, TNFAIP3, IL6;
- held-out readout panel: R'_B = MERTK, MRC1, FOLR2, C1QA; I'_B = SPP1, TNF, IL1B, CXCL8, CCL2.

The generic activation panel is `A = TNF, IL1B, IL6, CXCL8, TNFAIP3`. For split A, the held-out generic-activation readout is IL6/TNFAIP3; for split B it is TNF/IL1B/CXCL8. Thus every primary within-state readout gene is absent from the state panel in the same split. The two splits are not independent replications; they are a sensitivity pair that tests feature dependence.

For each fold and split, normalize each cell using its own measured total and `log1p(CPM)`. Estimate centering/scaling parameters from training donors only, then apply them to the held-out donor. Compute fixed scores:

`D_state = mean(I_state) - mean(R_state)`;

`B_readout = mean(I'_readout) - mean(R'_readout)`;

`A_readout = mean(A'_held-out)`.

Use the fixed thresholds `D_state <= -0.25` resident-like, `D_state >= 0.25` inflammatory-like, and otherwise ambiguous. These labels are descriptive molecular strata. Never call them validated resident or inflammatory cell types.

A primary sample is flagged if more than 50% of its cells are ambiguous or if either non-ambiguous state has fewer than 30 cells and 5% of that sample. ## Fixed baseline

The baseline uses the prepared E-MTAB-8322 counts table and the same 17 measured rows, with columns `feature` plus the 27 source-internal sample IDs. For each donor, compute the sample-level fixed module score:

`B_all = mean(I) - mean(R)`.

Fit a donor-level robust Huber regression within the primary 13 donors:

`B_all = intercept + group + centered age + centered log1p(cells)`.

All centering and fitting is inside each donor-held-out fold. The primary baseline output is the resistant-minus-remission group coefficient and its 13 held-out donor projections. This is an adjusted cross-sectional association, not a predictive clinical model.

## Substantive alternative and primary estimand

For each split, assign cells using the state panel only. For donor d and state s in {resident-like, inflammatory-like}, compute `pi_ds`, the state proportion, and `mu_ds`, the donor's mean held-out `B_readout` among cells in s. Exclude ambiguous cells from state-specific means but retain an overall readout summary for reconstruction.

Let `w_s` be the fixed pooled proportion of state s across the 13 primary donors, calculated once from observed state proportions and not fitted to the outcome. Construct each donor's composition-standardized held-out readout:

`Y_within_d = sum_s w_s * mu_ds`.

The primary alternative estimand for split k is the resistant-minus-remission coefficient `theta_within,k` from the donor-level robust model:

`Y_within_d = intercept + group + centered age + centered log1p(cells)`.

This estimates the group association in held-out expression after replacing each donor's observed state mixture by the same pooled mixture. The alternative is informative because it separates a composition-sensitive `B_all` from a composition-standardized readout, while the readout genes were not used to define states.

For interpretation, compute the observed total donor mean `Y_total_d = sum_s pi_ds * mu_ds`, the composition component using pooled state-specific means `mu_s^0`, and the residual interaction. Report the exact reconstruction identity:

`Y_total_d - Y_within_d = sum_s (pi_ds - w_s) * mu_ds`.

Do not force the composition and within-state terms to sum if missing-state guards or normalization create a residual; report it. Compute the group coefficient for the held-out generic activation readout `A_readout` under the same state standardization. The primary comparison is:

2. cross-fitted disjoint-readout `theta_within,A` and `theta_within,B`;

4. held-out reconstruction error and residual.

State-specific group coefficients are secondary descriptive outputs; they are not used to select a split, threshold, or outcome.

Predeclared negative and artifact controls:

1. Enumerate all `choose(13,7)=1716` remission-label permutations, preserving the 7/6 allocation, and rerun the donor-level estimand and fold bookkeeping. The primary negative-control statistic is `theta_within`; report its empirical rank, not a model-based p-value.
2. Permute state labels within each sample while preserving the sample's cell count and held-out readout values. Supportive requires all of the following:

- both splits pass the stability diagnostic;

# Episode-20 child: non-circular attribution of the E-MTAB-8322 remission/resistance contrast

This is a planned Harbor experiment. The source audit and literature inspection were executed; no biological fit, state assignment, treatment effect, or clinical result was executed.

## Successor purpose and substantive repair

The selected parent asks whether the terminal E-MTAB-8322 remission-versus-treatment-resistant contrast is composition, within-state regulation, generic activation, or measurement/depth. Its cell-level alternative defines resident-like and inflammatory-like states from the same 17 genes used to quantify within-state change. That makes a within-state result partly tautological: a cell can be assigned to a state because it has the tested expression pattern.

This child makes one scientific repair. It predeclares two complementary, disjoint feature partitions. In each partition, state labels are computed from one set of measured genes and the within-state readout is computed only from the other set. The label/readout split is repeated in the complementary direction, while donor-held-out normalization and donor-level inference are retained. This tests whether the attribution survives an outcome-independent molecular definition rather than merely adding model complexity.

The repair does not create cell identity. A state remains an expression-defined transcriptional stratum, not a protein- or lineage-validated macrophage subtype. If the two feature partitions disagree materially, the correct conclusion is that the available 17-gene panel cannot identify the requested within-state estimand.

## Scientific opening, strongest supported claim, and unresolved claim

[K1] reports remission-associated synovial macrophage heterogeneity and MerTK-positive programs in a different study, with fibroblast-repair and flare associations in that study. [K2] reports an HBEGF-positive inflammatory macrophage context and fibroblast invasiveness, supplying a consequential inflammatory rival. [K3] shows that RA synovial tissues contain multiple cell-abundance and cell-state contexts and that multimodal protein/transcript data help distinguish them. These works support the importance of separating state composition, within-state expression, and generic activation. They do not establish that the E-MTAB-8322 resistant-minus-remission contrast is a within-cell transition, a treatment effect, a MerTK mechanism, or a persistent lineage.

The unresolved question is:

> Among the 13 terminal E-MTAB-8322 RA macrophage donors, does the resistant-versus-remission association in a fixed macrophage transcriptional readout persist after composition standardization using state labels built from disjoint measured genes, and is it distinguishable from generic activation and library/cell-depth artifacts?

The hypothesis is that a reproducible resistant-higher association remains in the disjoint held-out readout after standardizing state proportions, while composition and the generic activation axis do not account for most of the contrast. The rival explanations are: (1) a different mixture of cells or sampling fractions; (2) a broad activation/depth response that moves all inflammatory genes together; (3) expression-defined state circularity; and (4) donor, related-donor, or technical measurement structure.

The substantive advance is an identifiable, falsifiable attribution check at the level actually available: a cross-fitted expression-defined state/readout contrast. A supportive result would justify a prospective study with independent protein/composition labels and longitudinal sampling. It would not show causality, target engagement, same-cell persistence, treatment response, or clinical benefit.

# Episode-20 child: non-circular attribution of the E-MTAB-8322 remission/resistance contrast

This is a planned Harbor experiment. The source audit and literature inspection were executed; no biological fit, state assignment, treatment effect, or clinical result was executed.

## Successor purpose and substantive repair

The selected parent asks whether the terminal E-MTAB-8322 remission-versus-treatment-resistant contrast is composition, within-state regulation, generic activation, or measurement/depth. Its cell-level alternative defines resident-like and inflammatory-like states from the same 17 genes used to quantify within-state change. That makes a within-state result partly tautological: a cell can be assigned to a state because it has the tested expression pattern.

This child makes one scientific repair. It predeclares two complementary, disjoint feature partitions. In each partition, state labels are computed from one set of measured genes and the within-state readout is computed only from the other set. The label/readout split is repeated in the complementary direction, while donor-held-out normalization and donor-level inference are retained. This tests whether the attribution survives an outcome-independent molecular definition rather than merely adding model complexity.

The repair does not create cell identity. A state remains an expression-defined transcriptional stratum, not a protein- or lineage-validated macrophage subtype. If the two feature partitions disagree materially, the correct conclusion is that the available 17-gene panel cannot identify the requested within-state estimand.

## Scientific opening, strongest supported claim, and unresolved claim

[K1] reports remission-associated synovial macrophage heterogeneity and MerTK-positive programs in a different study, with fibroblast-repair and flare associations in that study. [K2] reports an HBEGF-positive inflammatory macrophage context and fibroblast invasiveness, supplying a consequential inflammatory rival. [K3] shows that RA synovial tissues contain multiple cell-abundance and cell-state contexts and that multimodal protein/transcript data help distinguish them. These works support the importance of separating state composition, within-state expression, and generic activation. They do not establish that the E-MTAB-8322 resistant-minus-remission contrast is a within-cell transition, a treatment effect, a MerTK mechanism, or a persistent lineage.

The unresolved question is:

> Among the 13 terminal E-MTAB-8322 RA macrophage donors, does the resistant-versus-remission association in a fixed macrophage transcriptional readout persist after composition standardization using state labels built from disjoint measured genes, and is it distinguishable from generic activation and library/cell-depth artifacts?

The hypothesis is that a reproducible resistant-higher association remains in the disjoint held-out readout after standardizing state proportions, while composition and the generic activation axis do not account for most of the contrast. The rival explanations are: (1) a different mixture of cells or sampling fractions; (2) a broad activation/depth response that moves all inflammatory genes together; (3) expression-defined state circularity; and (4) donor, related-donor, or technical measurement structure.

The substantive advance is an identifiable, falsifiable attribution check at the level actually available: a cross-fitted expression-defined state/readout contrast. A supportive result would justify a prospective study with independent protein/composition labels and longitudinal sampling. It would not show causality, target engagement, same-cell persistence, treatment response, or clinical benefit.

## Population and temporal boundary

Primary population: the 13 verified E-MTAB-8322 terminal synovial-membrane macrophage samples, seven remission and six treatment-resistant:

- remission: RemSA132, RemSA160, RemSA161, RemSA174, SA159, SA168, SA225;
- resistant: ResistantSA144, ResistantSA145, ResistantSA151, ResistantSA166, SA222, SA227.

The source design audit verified 27 rows with fields `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `other_donor_id`, `age`, `sex`, `tissue`, `cell_type`, `condition`, `treatment`, `source_metadata`, `source_name`, and `cells`. The primary rows are macrophage, synovial membrane, verified donors, all female; `treatment` is null. Healthy (4), treatment-naive RA (6), and undifferentiated arthritis (4) are descriptive context only and do not enter the primary estimand.

The independent unit is donor, not cell. All cells from a donor stay together in every leave-one-donor-out fold. SA149/SA149P relatedness is unresolved; related samples are excluded from the primary independent-donor analysis and included one at a time only as sensitivity analyses. No donor or patient identifier is joined across assays.

The temporal boundary is the single terminal sample. No verified numeric time field is available. “Remission” and “treatment-resistant” are cross-sectional clinical-state labels, not randomized treatment assignments. The analysis cannot estimate a transition, treatment effect, persistence, flare risk, or response prediction.

## Exact measured panel and non-circular feature partitions

Use only these 17 Ensembl rows, after verifying each row in each source gene map. No external markers, pathway-selected genes, PCA/NMF factors, outcome-selected genes, or whole-tissue deconvolution are allowed.

Resident block R:
`MERTK ENSG00000153208`, `CD163 ENSG00000177575`, `MRC1 ENSG00000260314`, `FOLR2 ENSG00000165457`, `C1QA ENSG00000173372`, `C1QB ENSG00000173369`, `APOE ENSG00000130203`.

Inflammatory block I:
`SPP1 ENSG00000118785`, `TNF ENSG00000232810`, `IL1B ENSG00000125538`, `CXCL8 ENSG00000169429`, `CCL2 ENSG00000108691`, `ICAM1 ENSG00000090339`, `MMP3 ENSG00000149968`, `MMP9 ENSG00000100985`, `TNFAIP3 ENSG00000118503`, `IL6 ENSG00000136244`.

The source audit must confirm the exact feature identifiers; the proposal does not treat a gene symbol alone as a valid join.

Predeclared split A:

- state panel: R_A = MERTK, MRC1, FOLR2, C1QA; I_A = SPP1, TNF, IL1B, CXCL8, CCL2;
- held-out readout panel: R'_A = CD163, C1QB, APOE; I'_A = ICAM1, MMP3, MMP9, TNFAIP3, IL6.

Predeclared split B is the complement:

- state panel: R_B = CD163, C1QB, APOE; I_B = ICAM1, MMP3, MMP9, TNFAIP3, IL6;
- held-out readout panel: R'_B = MERTK, MRC1, FOLR2, C1QA; I'_B = SPP1, TNF, IL1B, CXCL8, CCL2.

The generic activation panel is `A = TNF, IL1B, IL6, CXCL8, TNFAIP3`. For split A, the held-out generic-activation readout is IL6/TNFAIP3; for split B it is TNF/IL1B/CXCL8. Thus every primary within-state readout gene is absent from the state panel in the same split. The two splits are not independent replications; they are a sensitivity pair that tests feature dependence.

For each fold and split, normalize each cell using its own measured total and `log1p(CPM)`. Estimate centering/scaling parameters from training donors only, then apply them to the held-out donor. Compute fixed scores:

`D_state = mean(I_state) - mean(R_state)`;

`B_readout = mean(I'_readout) - mean(R'_readout)`;

`A_readout = mean(A'_held-out)`.

Use the fixed thresholds `D_state <= -0.25` resident-like, `D_state >= 0.25` inflammatory-like, and otherwise ambiguous. These labels are descriptive molecular strata. Never call them validated resident or inflammatory cell types.

A primary sample is flagged if more than 50% of its cells are ambiguous or if either non-ambiguous state has fewer than 30 cells and 5% of that sample. The fold is then inconclusive for the state-conditional estimand rather than rescued by changing thresholds. Record the cell counts, proportions, and threshold decisions.

## Fixed baseline

The baseline uses the prepared E-MTAB-8322 counts table and the same 17 measured rows, with columns `feature` plus the 27 source-internal sample IDs. For each donor, compute the sample-level fixed module score:

`B_all = mean(I) - mean(R)`.

Fit a donor-level robust Huber regression within the primary 13 donors:

`B_all = intercept + group + centered age + centered log1p(cells)`.

All centering and fitting is inside each donor-held-out fold. The primary baseline output is the resistant-minus-remission group coefficient and its 13 held-out donor projections. This is an adjusted cross-sectional association, not a predictive clinical model.

## Substantive alternative and primary estimand

For each split, assign cells using the state panel only. For donor d and state s in {resident-like, inflammatory-like}, compute `pi_ds`, the state proportion, and `mu_ds`, the donor's mean held-out `B_readout` among cells in s. Exclude ambiguous cells from state-specific means but retain an overall readout summary for reconstruction.

Let `w_s` be the fixed pooled proportion of state s across the 13 primary donors, calculated once from observed state proportions and not fitted to the outcome. Construct each donor's composition-standardized held-out readout:

`Y_within_d = sum_s w_s * mu_ds`.

The primary alternative estimand for split k is the resistant-minus-remission coefficient `theta_within,k` from the donor-level robust model:

`Y_within_d = intercept + group + centered age + centered log1p(cells)`.

This estimates the group association in held-out expression after replacing each donor's observed state mixture by the same pooled mixture. The alternative is informative because it separates a composition-sensitive `B_all` from a composition-standardized readout, while the readout genes were not used to define states.

For interpretation, compute the observed total donor mean `Y_total_d = sum_s pi_ds * mu_ds`, the composition component using pooled state-specific means `mu_s^0`, and the residual interaction. Report the exact reconstruction identity:

`Y_total_d - Y_within_d = sum_s (pi_ds - w_s) * mu_ds`.

Do not force the composition and within-state terms to sum if missing-state guards or normalization create a residual; report it. Compute the group coefficient for the held-out generic activation readout `A_readout` under the same state standardization. The primary comparison is:

1. fixed all-17-gene `B_all` baseline;
2. cross-fitted disjoint-readout `theta_within,A` and `theta_within,B`;
3. composition and activation components;
4. held-out reconstruction error and residual.

State-specific group coefficients are secondary descriptive outputs; they are not used to select a split, threshold, or outcome.

## Dependence, uncertainty, and negative controls

The solver must save all 13 donor deletions, not cell-level p-values. In each fold, held-out donor cells never contribute to normalization, state-panel scaling, pooled weights, or model fitting. Report donor-level coefficient, direction, state proportions, ambiguous fraction, reconstruction residual, and baseline/alternative RMSE and MAE. Use a whole-donor block bootstrap only as a sensitivity envelope; with 13 donors it is not a population confidence interval.

Predeclared negative and artifact controls:

1. Enumerate all `choose(13,7)=1716` remission-label permutations, preserving the 7/6 allocation, and rerun the donor-level estimand and fold bookkeeping. The primary negative-control statistic is `theta_within`; report its empirical rank, not a model-based p-value.
2. Permute state labels within each sample while preserving the sample's cell count and held-out readout values. This breaks state/readout assignment while preserving sequencing depth and composition counts. A large unchanged within-state effect indicates that the decomposition is not identifying the intended structure.
3. Evaluate pseudo-outcomes `log1p(cells)`, measured total, ambiguous fraction, and the held-out state-panel score. A group contrast that is reproduced in these controls is an artifact warning.
4. Verify exact disjointness of state and readout row identifiers in every fold. A deliberate leakage fixture that reuses one readout gene in state construction must be reported separately and cannot be used for inference.
5. Repeat without `log1p(cells)`, with the prespecified age-by-group interaction, and after removing each R, I, and A gene family in turn. These are sensitivity analyses, not opportunities to select the most favorable result.
6. Repeat with SA149P and UPASA149 one at a time only as related-donor sensitivity. Do not treat them as independent donors.

A necessary identifiability diagnostic is agreement between the two complementary partitions. Report cell-level agreement among non-ambiguous labels and per-sample absolute differences in resident-like and inflammatory-like proportions. If non-ambiguous agreement is below 0.60 or either state proportion differs by more than 0.25 in any primary sample, classify the state attribution as inconclusive. This is a predeclared warning about the limited panel, not evidence against macrophage biology.

Required fields include source-internal `sample_id`, `donor_id`, `donor_status`, `condition`, `source_metadata`, and `mapping_note`; donor/GSM mapping is unresolved, so these tables are inventory/rival context only and cannot validate this child. Preserve duplicate/date-like feature rows.

## Alternatives and resource selection

The simple baseline is the fixed 17-gene module score on donor-level pseudobulk. Its information is transparent and low variance at n=13, but it cannot tell whether a group contrast is due to a changed mixture, a state-conditional shift, or generic activation.

The selected alternative is the cross-fitted, disjoint-feature state/readout decomposition above. It adds state proportions, within-stratum readout, composition, activation, split agreement, and reconstruction residuals on identical cells, genes, donors, nuisance fields, and leave-donor-out folds. It is scientifically substantive because these outputs answer a different attribution question, not because it is a better predictor.

Deferred alternatives are unrestricted NMF/Gaussian mixtures, supervised elastic-net or neural prediction, external-reference deconvolution, and pooled inference across the four assays. NMF/mixtures would add latent structure but would worsen identifiability at 13 donors and would not cure same-input circularity. Supervised prediction optimizes classification rather than attribution. Deconvolution requires unmeasured reference markers. Pooling violates source-specific identity and design limits. Revisit them only with independent markers/proteins, verified donor mapping, or a prospective outcome.

The future solver should use CPU, approximately 4 cores and 8–16 GiB RAM, with a 30–120 minute envelope for sparse extraction, 26 donor-held-out split fits, 1,716 label permutations, and cell-label controls. This is a planning estimate, not a measured full-study runtime. The source metadata audit job used 1 CPU and completed in 0.56 seconds, but that does not benchmark matrix extraction or the scientific computation. GPU is not appropriate: the workload is a 17-feature sparse tabular calculation with 13 donor units, and GPU overhead would not answer a scientific uncertainty. This is a workload choice, not a categorical exclusion of neural methods.

## Actual scientific deliverable

Completion requires new output files containing:

1. source/hash audit, exact feature-map validation, archive-member checks, and counts/design joins;
2. donor-level baseline `B_all`, both feature-split state assignments, held-out readouts, state proportions, ambiguous fractions, and state stability;
3. `theta_within`, composition, activation, and reconstruction residual outputs for each split and all 13 donor deletions;
4. the complete 1716-label permutation distribution and within-sample cell-label negative control;
5. pseudo-outcome, family-deletion, age/cell-count, and related-donor sensitivity outputs;
6. a decision JSON linking each supportive/adverse/inconclusive rule to exact output rows.

No readiness or source audit output counts as a biological result. Claims beyond computation require expert review, orthogonal protein/composition measurement, direct target-engagement assays, and a new longitudinal study. The next study should recruit treatment-naive RA, stable remission, and active/resistant RA with exact drug/dose/adherence history, repeated synovial sampling, cell hashing, RNA plus surface protein, validated macrophage composition markers, and prespecified clinical/imaging outcomes. Same-patient recurrence would not establish same-cell persistence without lineage or validated tracking.
 
## Compact bibliography

[K1] Alivernini S et al. Distinct synovial tissue macrophage subsets regulate inflammation and remission in rheumatoid arthritis. Nature Medicine. 2020. doi:10.1038/s41591-020-0939-8. Abstract/HTML passage inspected.

[K2] Kuo D et al. HBEGF+ macrophages in rheumatoid arthritis induce fibroblast invasiveness. Science Translational Medicine. 2019;11:eaau8587. doi:10.1126/scitranslmed.aau8587. Europe PMC abstract inspected.

[K3] Zhang F et al. Deconstruction of rheumatoid arthritis synovium defines inflammatory subtypes. Nature. 2023. doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06708-y. Abstract and selected HTML passages inspected.

Evidence files, retrieval limits, and receipt-linked hashes are in `key-references.json` and the three `evidence-k*.txt` attachments.

# Episode 20 independent branch — resident-anchor attribution without cell-level independence

Status: planned Harbor experiment. No biological fit, screening job, effect estimate, p-value, interval, or clinical conclusion has been executed.

Parent: candidate-c52b870e210dcb9102c3c3c6. This branch preserves its terminal cross-sectional question but repairs the most consequential identifiability weakness: the parent both assigned state and measured the state contrast with the same 17 genes, and its cell-label permutation could be mistaken for an inferential null. Here state assignment and inflammatory readout use disjoint measured panels; cells are summarized within source sample and donor, and every uncertainty calculation resamples donors rather than cells.

## Scientific opening, evidence, and unresolved claim

[K1] reports multiple synovial macrophage subsets, including MerTK-positive remission-associated signatures and fibroblast repair observations. [K2] reports an HBEGF-positive inflammatory macrophage state shaped by fibroblast/TNF context and an EGFR-dependent fibroblast invasiveness assay. [K3] describes several synovial composition categories and coexisting resident-like MERTK/CD163/CD206, HBEGF/IL1B, and SPP1 myeloid axes. These inspected works establish why macrophage heterogeneity and tissue context matter; they do not establish that this E-MTAB-8322 remission-versus-treatment-resistant difference is within-state, treatment-caused, persistent in the same cells, or target-engaged.

The unresolved question is:

> In the terminal E-MTAB-8322 macrophage samples, does the remission-versus-treatment-resistant inflammatory RNA contrast remain within a fixed resident-anchor stratum after donor-level composition and generic-activation checks, or is it explained by the proportions of expression-defined strata, activation/depth, or unmeasured clinical/technical selection?

The falsifiable hypothesis is that the resistant-minus-remission difference in a predeclared ten-gene inflammatory readout is positive and donor-robust within resident-anchor-high/low strata, with a non-dominant composition component and a non-dominant generic-activation component. The strongest supported claim is only an adjusted cross-sectional association among measured macrophage RNA profiles. A supportive result does not prove a macrophage lineage, mechanism, treatment effect, target engagement, same-cell persistence, flare prediction, or clinical benefit.

The decision affected is whether to invest in an independent repeated-patient study with validated protein/composition, spatial or lineage evidence, direct target engagement, and adjudicated treatment exposure. A composition-dominant result redirects that effort toward sampling/composition measurement; a generic-activation result redirects it toward the competing inflammatory context; an inconclusive result supports only better-powered orthogonal measurement.

## Population and temporal boundary

The primary estimand uses exactly 13 E-MTAB-8322 samples: remission rheumatoid Arthritis (7) versus resitant to treament rheumatoid Arthritis (6), retaining the source spelling of the condition labels. Primary sample IDs are:

- RemSA132 (SA132), RemSA160 (SA160), RemSA161 (SA161), RemSA174 (SA174), SA159 (SA159), SA168 (SA168), SA225 (SA225);
- ResistantSA144 (SA144), ResistantSA145 (SA145), ResistantSA151 (SA151), ResistantSA166 (SA166), SA222 (SA222), SA227 (SA227).

The prepared design has 27 rows: Healthy control 4, Na\u00efve to treament rheumatoid Arthritis 6, remission 7, resistant 6, and Undifferentiated arthritis 4. Healthy, treatment-naive, and undifferentiated rows are reference/descriptive context, not additional observations in the primary effect. The design audit found 25 rows with donor_status=verified and two rows marked possible_related_or_repeated_donor_exclude_inference: SA149P and UPASA149. The primary donor IDs are unique across the 13 primary rows; SA149P/UPASA149 are excluded from independent-donor inference and included only one at a time in sensitivity analyses.

Use source-internal sample_id as the sole counts/design join key. Preserve donor_id, donor_status, other_donor_id, age, sex, tissue, cell_type, condition, treatment, source_metadata, source_name and cells. In the primary group all sex values are female; sex is not estimated. treatment is null in the relevant design rows; detailed drug, dose, adherence, prior-treatment, severity and exposure timing are unavailable. No verified numeric time field exists. The labels are not randomized assignments. The boundary is terminal and cross-sectional: no transition, treatment effect, longitudinal persistence, flare prediction, or clinical response claim is permitted.

## Exact measured inputs and identifiability repair

Use only these 17 measured Ensembl rows, with no outcome-selected genes, PCA/NMF, unrestricted pathway search, external deconvolution references, or latent factors:

- Resident anchor panel R (state assignment only): MERTK ENSG00000153208; CD163 ENSG00000177575; MRC1 ENSG00000260314; FOLR2 ENSG00000165457; C1QA ENSG00000173372; C1QB ENSG00000173369; APOE ENSG00000130203.
- Inflammatory readout I (baseline and alternative outcome): SPP1 ENSG00000118785; TNF ENSG00000232810; IL1B ENSG00000125538; CXCL8 ENSG00000169429; CCL2 ENSG00000108691; ICAM1 ENSG00000090339; MMP3 ENSG00000149968; MMP9 ENSG00000100985; TNFAIP3 ENSG00000118503; IL6 ENSG00000136244.
- Generic activation subscore A, a prespecified subset of I: TNF, IL1B, CXCL8, TNFAIP3, IL6.
- Tissue-damage/inflammatory subscore D, the complementary subset of I: SPP1, CCL2, ICAM1, MMP3, MMP9.

The source audit must verify every identifier against each included sample’s gene map before fitting. The common frozen map is SA220.genes.tsv; all 27 sample gene maps are expected to match its bytes. Normalize every cell and prepared sample by its own measured total to CPM and apply log1p. For each leave-one-primary-donor-out fold, estimate gene centering/scaling from training data only. The primary alternative’s state assignment uses R only; I, A and D are never used to define the state. Thus a within-stratum I result cannot be a tautology caused by using the I readout to assign the stratum. This is an operational expression stratum, not a validated cell type.

The read-only gene-map audit confirmed CXCL8 is ENSG00000169429 (and verified the other 16 requested symbols/IDs in SA220.genes.tsv). The solver must assert the same mapping and classify inconclusive on any source-map mismatch rather than silently substituting a symbol or row.

## Fixed baseline

For each prepared sample, compute the sample-level inflammatory score I_total = mean(log1p(CPM) for the ten I genes). The fixed baseline fits, on donor-level sample summaries only, a robust Huber regression:
I_total = intercept + group + centered age + centered log1p(cells).

The estimand is the resistant-minus-remission adjusted contrast. Report the unadjusted donor-level contrast as context, the adjusted contrast, standardized donor difference, all 13 leave-one-donor-out projections, and a donor-block bootstrap sensitivity envelope. cells is a measured number of captured cells, not a measured fraction of resident or inflammatory cells and not a cure for composition confounding.

The baseline is intentionally simple and auditable at n=13. It answers whether there is an overall inflammatory association but loses state proportions and within-stratum information.

## Substantive cell-level alternative on the identical measured inputs

The alternative is a reference-anchored, disjoint-panel decomposition, not a flexible classifier.

1. In each leave-one-primary-donor-out fold, normalize cells from the original sparse archive and compute only R cell scores after training-only gene centering/scaling. Use healthy and treatment-naive reference samples to define the fold’s fixed anchor threshold: resident-anchor-high is R_score >= 0 after reference centering; resident-anchor-low is R_score < 0. Do not use remission/resistant labels to choose the threshold. Record the threshold, cell counts and the fraction in each stratum for every sample. If a training reference has no variance or a primary sample has fewer than 5% of cells in either stratum, flag the fold/sample and do not interpret its primary decomposition.
2. For each sample, summarize I_total, A and D separately within the two strata, and record stratum proportions pi_high and pi_low. No cell is an inferential replicate. Cell-level values are reduced to one summary per source-internal sample and the primary uncertainty unit is donor.
3. Estimate a two-stratum counterfactual decomposition of the resistant-minus-remission I_total contrast using donor/sample summaries:
   - Delta_comp changes pi_high/pi_low while holding pooled stratum-specific I means fixed.
   - Delta_within changes stratum-specific I means while holding pooled stratum proportions fixed.
   - Delta_total is the direct observed I_total contrast; report the reconstruction residual and never force components to sum.
   - Report the analogous A and D decompositions separately. A is a rival/pseudo-outcome, not an additive proof of mechanism.
4. Fit training-only state-stratum sample-level models with group, age and log1p(cells), then generate held-out sample summaries. Compare alternative held-out reconstruction error for I_total with the fixed baseline’s held-out prediction error. The same primary donors, folds, covariates and measured genes are used in both methods.
5. As a non-inferential aggregation diagnostic, deterministically split each sample by a recorded barcode hash into two halves. Recompute pi and state-specific means in each half. A large state-proportion discrepancy or a direction reversal is an instability flag, not evidence based on extra replicates.

This alternative reveals composition and within-stratum information the baseline loses, while making the state/readout separation auditable. It still cannot distinguish true lineage, protein state, spatial localization, treatment action, or a biological mechanism.

## Dependence, uncertainty, and falsification

The fixed split is leave-one-primary-donor-out, with every cell from the held-out donor kept together. Report all 13 held-out donor projections, median and range, not cell-level p-values. Use a donor-block bootstrap stratified by clinical label only as a small-sample uncertainty envelope, explicitly not a population confidence interval. Run all 1,716 assignments of 7 remission and 6 resistant labels across the 13 primary donors, holding each donor’s cells and all covariates together and recomputing the full donor-level contrast/decomposition. The primary permutation statistic is the median held-out Delta_within; report its exact rank and distribution.

Mandatory sensitivity and negative controls:

- With and without age and log1p(cells); age-by-group interaction is prespecified. If a linear age term is visibly inadequate, report a labeled exploratory sensitivity rather than silently fitting a spline.
- Treat library size and cells as pseudo-outcomes. A group separation tracking these signals is an artifact warning.
- Exclude SA149P and UPASA149 from the primary analysis and include each singly as a related-donor sensitivity; a material change is dependence evidence.
- Delete each R gene and each I gene in turn; no one-gene result may be silently retained. Delete A genes as a family for the generic-activation control.
- Compare barcode-half summaries as measurement stability only; do not treat halves as independent donors.
- A within-sample random permutation of state labels may be used only as a code/aggregation diagnostic: it should disrupt the decomposition, but it is not a valid biological null or p-value. The donor-label permutation is the inferential negative control.
- Verify raw archive dimensions, barcode uniqueness, gene-map identity, nonnegative counts, finite normalization, prepared counts/design join completeness and exact source hashes before any fit.

Fixtures required in the executable package:

1. Fixed-seed donor-label-shuffled fixture preserving the 13 donor blocks, 7/6 group sizes, all cells, covariates and missingness. It must not satisfy the supportive gate.
2. Composition-only synthetic fixture with identical within-stratum I/A/D distributions but a prespecified resistant-versus-remission difference in pi_high. It must trigger composition/adverse, not within-state support.
3. Within-state positive synthetic fixture with identical pi distributions but a prespecified multigene resistant increase in disjoint I/D values, while R is unchanged. It must trigger the within-state direction checks.
4. A zero-effect fixture preserving the observed R/I covariance and cell-count distribution but no clinical-label effect. It must fail support.

Fixtures validate computation and interpretation gates, not biological truth.

## Predeclared decision gates

All thresholds below are planned rules, not observed results.

Supportive for the cross-sectional within-state hypothesis requires all of:

- baseline adjusted resistant-minus-remission I_total is positive, standardized donor difference >=0.5, and its donor-block 95% sensitivity envelope excludes zero;
- at least 10 of 13 leave-one-donor-out projections retain the baseline direction;
- median held-out Delta_within is positive and contributes at least 50% of |Delta_comp|+|Delta_within|;
- the median reconstruction residual is no more than 20% of the absolute observed I_total contrast, and alternative held-out RMSE is no worse than baseline RMSE by >10%;
- the generic activation contrast is less than 75% of the total inflammatory contrast in absolute value, while D retains the prespecified direction in at least 10 of 13 donor deletions;
- the observed median Delta_within is in the upper 5% of the fixed 1,716 donor-label permutation distribution;
- barcode-half stability and R/I one-gene deletion checks do not reverse the conclusion.

Adverse to the within-state hypothesis is triggered by any reproducible, donor-robust pattern of: composition explaining >=75% of the total while Delta_within is near zero; A explaining >=75% while D/within-state effects vanish; reversal/near-zero baseline in at least 4 donor deletions; alternative held-out RMSE >10% worse than baseline; or a composition-only fixture falsely passing the within-state gate. This redirects the next experiment; it does not show macrophages are irrelevant.

Inconclusive includes a missing/mismatched required feature or archive member, incomplete sample_id join, failed source hash, absent/unstable R stratum, barcode-half instability, reconstruction residual >20%, bootstrap envelope spanning the decision regions, discordant components, unresolved related-donor dependence, or any result that depends on unavailable treatment/time/clinical adjudication. An imprecise null is not refutation.

Computationally checkable: source hashes and archive members; 27-row design and 27-column count audit; exact feature availability; donor/sample joins; normalization; baseline contrast; fold outputs; donor-held-out stability; state proportions; disjoint-panel decomposition; permutation distribution; sensitivity and fixture behavior.

Not computationally established: true macrophage lineage or state identity; MerTK protein abundance/engagement; direct target selectivity; treatment exposure/adherence or causal treatment effect; clinical remission/resistance adjudication; same-cell persistence; spatial localization; macrophage–FLS causality; flare, response or benefit. These require expert clinical/pathology review, validated surface/protein and spatial assays, target-engagement measurements, and a prospective repeated-patient study.

## Method alternatives, choice, and compute

Alternative 1, selected baseline: fixed ten-gene inflammatory score with donor-level robust regression. Inputs, target, splits and uncertainty are above. It is low variance and transparent at n=13, but cannot separate composition from within-stratum expression.

Alternative 2, selected substantive alternative: disjoint resident-anchor state assignment plus donor-level two-stratum decomposition of the same ten inflammatory genes, with A/D subreadouts, held-out donor folds, barcode-half stability and exact donor permutations. It can reveal whether equal overall I scores arise from different proportions or different I expression within the same operational stratum. It is selected because that information changes the next experiment; it is not selected for predictive gain or model complexity.

Deferred methods: unrestricted neural models, supervised classifiers, whole-transcriptome clustering, external-reference deconvolution and pooled cross-assay prediction. Readiness validates packaging and limited probes only; it is not a biological result. No conclusion may be written without a computed output and uncertainty reference.
