### Deterministic follow-up readiness gate

Before any cohort fitting:

1. Verify each exact path, source ID, catalog table ID, SHA-256, namespace, key uniqueness, and required column list.
2. Inspect the frozen source README, catalog metadata and the relevant outcome-source documentation for an explicitly stated outcome-ascertainment cutoff `tau_source`, including its calendar date and provenance. A file mtime, campaign date, current date, observed maximum event date, or undocumented interpretation of `20191-0.0` is not `tau_source`.
3. If no such documented cutoff exists, emit a readiness failure with the missing evidence and stop before fitting. Do not report a null, a cohort result or a five-year estimate.
4. If a cutoff is documented, apply the same cutoff to all death/cancer ascertainment fields. For each case, require `t0 + DateOffset(years=h) <= tau_source` for h=1, 3 and 5; use an explicit leap-day rule and report the rule. The five-year primary analysis uses only cases satisfying h=5.
5. Report the observed maxima separately as an audit: in this snapshot, death dates observed in `40000-0.0/1.0` reach 2022-12-19 and cancer dates in `40005-*.0` reach 2022-06-01. These maxima do not establish completeness.

## 3. Population, paired outcomes and estimand

Set `b_i = 53-0.0` and retain assessment dates from 2006-01-01 through 2010-12-31. A cancer record is valid only if the same slot has a parseable `40005-k.0` date and a trimmed uppercase ICD-10 `40006-k.0` code. Report malformed, unpaired and discordant slots; never repair them by borrowing a neighboring slot. Exclude participants with any valid paired C00–C97 record on or before `b_i`.

For incident CRC, select the earliest valid post-`b_i` C18, C19 or C20 date as `t0_i`. Retain all tied earliest slots and use the lowest slot, then lexicographically smallest normalized code, only for deterministic subsite labeling. A source audit using this rule found 6,094 assessment-window participants with a valid paired cancer on/before assessment, 2,219 post-assessment CRC cases with no such prior cancer, and 329/493/1,397 of those cases in the 0–<2, 2–<5 and >=5-year diagnosis-lag strata. These are screening counts before reserve completeness and documented follow-up gating, not fitted estimates.

Primary eligibility is diagnosis lag `t0_i-b_i >= 730` days, valid reserve exposure under the prespecified missingness rule, and documented five-year follow-up support. The primary timing window is 2–<5 years plus >=5 years; the 0–<2-year stratum is an adverse reverse-causation check, and >=5 years is a prespecified durable-timing sensitivity, not a replacement for the primary.

Death must use the paired slot `40000-j.0` date and `40001-j.0` underlying cause. Parse valid dates, retain only deaths after `t0_i`, choose the earliest date, and on a date tie prefer a usable ICD-10 cause then the lowest slot while recording all tied slots. Unknown means missing, malformed or non-ICD-10 cause. Classify first death as: CRC-specific C18/C19/C20; other cancer C00–C97 excluding C18–C20; non-cancer outside C00–C97; or unknown. Unknown is a separate competing event in the primary analysis. Sensitivities classify unknown as non-cancer and censor at unknown death. V01–Y89 external-cause death is a separately reported endpoint-specific negative control, not automatically folded into target non-cancer death. Death on/before `t0_i` is an impossible ordering: exclude it from primary and report it.

The primary estimand is the adjusted five-year cumulative-incidence differential:
`Delta5 = [CIF_nonCRC(R=Q25) - CIF_nonCRC(R=Q75)] - [CIF_CRC(R=Q25) - CIF_CRC(R=Q75)]`,
with other-cancer and unknown death competing, Q25/Q75 fixed from training data, and standardization over the locked eligible population. Report the one-, three- and five-year CIFs, `Delta5`, and the difference between cause-specific reserve log-effects; use 95% participant-bootstrap intervals. A positive `Delta5` supports the stated differential association. These are standardized prognostic associations, not causal effects. Fine–Gray and cause-specific estimates are descriptive sensitivity parameterizations, not interchangeable causal estimands.

## 4. Exposure and covariates

Set `grip_max = max(46-0.0, 47-0.0)`, using one side if the other is absent and missing if both are absent. The four primary reserve components are grip_max, albumin `30600-0.0`, creatinine `30700-0.0` and cystatin C `30720-0.0`. Fit transformations and scaling within training data only: sex-stratified standardization of grip, log(albumin), negative-log creatinine and negative-log cystatin C. Primary R is the mean of available standardized components when at least three of four are present; record component count and every missingness indicator. Complete-four, grip-only, laboratory-only, and training-median-plus-indicators versions are mandatory sensitivities. Call R “measured reserve,” never validated biological reserve.

Adjustment uses age at diagnosis derived from `21022-0.0` plus exact assessment-to-diagnosis interval under a documented convention, sex `31-0.0`, BMI `21001-0.0`, smoking `20116-0.0`, diagnosis calendar year, CRC subsite, and a dated pre-`t0` Charlson count from `41270-*`/`41280-*`, excluding the incident CRC. No post-diagnosis variable is allowed. Townsend deprivation, ethnicity, centre, stage, grade, TNM, treatment, toxicity, performance status, recurrence, histology, validated frailty, adjudicated causes and external validation are not in the verified binding. In particular, do not relabel diagnosis-array occurrences of 189 as deprivation.

## 5. Baseline versus learned alternative

Both models use the identical participant split, outcome construction, covariates, reserve components, missingness indicators and diagnosis anchor. The comparison tests whether reserve is adequately represented as an approximately linear scalar or instead has stable thresholds/component combinations; it is not a leaderboard exercise.

- **B0/B1 interpretable baseline:** one-year discrete-time cause-specific complementary-log-log hazards for CRC, non-cancer, other-cancer and unknown death through five years. B0 contains age using prespecified restricted cubic-spline knots, sex, BMI, smoking, calendar year, Charlson count, subsite and interval. B1 adds one linear one-SD R term and its pre-specified missingness indicators. Convert hazards to CIFs by the competing-risk recursion. Freeze B0/B1 before inspecting test predictions.
- **B2 learned alternative:** CPU gradient-boosted multinomial discrete-time hazard model over the same person-period rows and four outcome states, with the same B1 inputs plus the four reserve components, interval and prespecified reserve-by-diagnosis-lag interactions. Use a small fixed grid (200/400 trees, depth 2/3, learning rate 0.03/0.05) chosen on validation integrated Brier score only. Report endpoint-specific permutation importance and held-out accumulated-local-effect curves; do not treat them as mechanisms.

Use a fixed participant-level 70/15/15 train/validation/locked-test split, seed 36, assigned by deterministic eid hashing and stratified only after participant assignment by event type and diagnosis year. No person-period rows may cross splits. Fit scaling, imputation, tuning and Q25/Q75 on training/validation only; read the locked test once.

Report cause-specific CIF calibration intercept/slope, one/three/five-year and integrated IPCW Brier scores, time-dependent AUC, one-SD reserve effects, `Delta5`, event counts, model coefficients, learned effect tables and paired participant-bootstrap uncertainty with at least 500 resamples. Treat an absolute locked-test integrated-Brier improvement of 0.01 with an interval above zero as a pre-specified practically meaningful predictive improvement, but do not require B2 improvement to support a descriptive association if B1 is stable. A predictive improvement without a stable reserve endpoint contrast is only a prediction result.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted and output-linked: (1) cohort-flow and one-row-per-participant table with `b_i`, `t0_i`, lag, paired-record audit, reserve components, missingness, covariates, `tau_source`, support and exclusion reason; (2) fitted B0/B1/B2 objects and effect tables; (3) locked-test CIF, calibration, Brier/AUC and bootstrap outputs; and (4) a falsification report labeling the evidence supportive, adverse or inconclusive. No fitted result is asserted in this child.

## 6. Falsification and interpretation

Run each check once under a frozen specification and retain all adverse results.

1. **Occult timing:** repeat 0–<2, 2–<5 and >=5-year lag strata. A signal confined to 0–<2, or absent at >=5, is adverse to durable prediagnostic reserve and supports occult disease/observation timing.
2. **Age/comorbidity:** compare the prespecified flexible-age/Charlson model with age-only, age-plus-comorbidity, and age-band analyses (40–59, 60–69, >=70 where supported). Large attenuation or a reserve-by-age reversal indicates confounding or effect heterogeneity, not a host-reserve mechanism.
3. **Missingness/selection:** compare complete-four, min-three, imputed-indicator, grip-only and laboratory-only R. Model availability of complete R from assessment age, sex, BMI and smoking among all assessment-window participants; apply stabilized inverse-probability-of-observation weights only as a sensitivity and report overlap/extreme weights. Compare included incident cases with assessment-window participants and report missingness by event/lag. This tests measured availability selection; it cannot remove UKB volunteer selection or MNAR bias.
4. **Coding:** report every unpaired/malformed cancer or death slot, tie, unknown cause and impossible ordering. Compare paired `40005/40006` diagnosis anchoring with the earliest concordant pre-`t0` C18–C20 `41270/41280` occurrence where date/code are both usable. Material instability is adverse to the coding interpretation.
5. **Competing-risk and cause:** compare CRC, non-cancer, other-cancer, unknown and external-cause patterns; compare diagnosis-anchored competing-risk CIFs with naive censoring of competing deaths. A matching external-cause signal or CRC-dominant pattern weakens the proposed differential reserve interpretation.
6. **Leakage/permutation:** shuffle R within sex once, permute outcomes once with fixed seed, and run fixed exposure/outcome permutation probes. Retained held-out signal indicates leakage or coding contamination and invalidates the corresponding result.
7. **Stage/treatment boundary:** do not proxy stage or treatment with death cause, diagnosis lag, comorbidity or reserve. If the result is CRC-specific, disappears after timing checks, or differs by subsite, label stage/treatment as unresolved and do not reinterpret it as biology.

**Supportive:** readiness passes; in the >=2-year primary cohort lower R yields positive `Delta5` with an interval excluding zero; direction is compatible in >=5 years; the contrast is not reproduced for CRC death; cause, coding, missingness-weighted and complete/imputed analyses are materially consistent; and no matching external-cause signal or permutation leakage appears. This supports a robust prognostic regularity only. B2 may add evidence of stable nonlinear reserve patterns, but its predictive gain alone is not support.

**Adverse:** `Delta5` is zero/reversed, CRC death is at least as strongly associated, the effect is timing-only, it is driven by missingness or one assay, it tracks age/comorbidity, is unstable under paired coding/unknown-cause rules, or matches external-cause/permutation signals. Report which rival this supports and abandon the durable-reserve interpretation.

**Inconclusive:** readiness fails; deaths/events are sparse; clinically important intervals are wide; causes or coding are unstable; test calibration fails; or weighted analyses lack overlap. Do not call this a null. Continuing requires documented linkage completeness, expert outcome review, stage/treatment linkage or an independent cohort.

Computationally checkable claims are source binding, paired parsing, cohort flow, lag counts, model outputs, calibration, uncertainty and interpretation-to-output consistency. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for histologic confirmation, cause-of-death validity, stage, treatment, recurrence, treatment tolerance, mechanism, causality and generalizability outside UKB.

## 7. Alternatives and resource decision

The CPU baseline is retained because it directly estimates the differential competing-risk estimand and makes age/comorbidity and cause contrasts inspectable. The CPU boosted alternative is retained because it can reveal clinically meaningful reserve thresholds or component combinations that a scalar R erases while remaining feasible on the same inputs and split. A transformer/sequence model is deferred: no validated dated repeated reserve/laboratory trajectory is bound, and it would add representation complexity without separating a distinct rival explanation. A mechanistic renal-muscle model is deferred because validated mechanistic labels and treatment outcomes are absent. Revisit these alternatives only if repeated dated measures, stage/treatment evidence or an independent cohort is admitted, or if B2 shows stable nonlinear patterns requiring external mechanistic testing.

The measured discovery audit used a short CPU Parquet scan (about 11 seconds for selected columns on the available shell); full fitting, 500 bootstrap resamples and calibration are unmeasured. Plan 4–8 CPUs, 16–32 GiB RAM and under two hours as a provisional CPU estimate, subject to a readiness probe; the future solver envelope remains up to 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds. GPU is not needed for these tabular models. No fitted model or solver result is claimed here.

## 8. Three inspected works

All three works were inspected through the attached Europe PMC metadata/abstract snapshots only; no full text or supplement is claimed.

[K1] Zhou H, Li W, Liu S, Zhang H, Huang Y, Hu Y, Hu Y. “Pre-frailty and frailty as predictors of mortality among colorectal cancer survivors: Evidence from the National Health Interview Survey (1997-2018).” *Medicine*, 2026. PMID 41686585. Supports post-diagnosis frailty/mortality association; does not test prediagnostic competing-risk reserve.

[K2] Zhao D, He F, Liu H, Qing X. “Impact of preoperative handgrip strength and frailty on early postoperative loss of independence in patients with colorectal cancer.” *Frontiers in Oncology*, 2026. PMID 42459304. Supports perioperative handgrip/frailty vulnerability; does not establish long-term or prediagnostic timing.

[K3] García-Aranda M et al. “Ten-Year Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer-Competing Risks and Patient Vulnerability: A Prospective Multicenter Observational Study.” *Journal of Clinical Medicine*, 2026;15:4389. PMID 42279250. Supports competing-risk separation and highlights stage/treatment as a consequential unresolved rival.

# UKB-03 repaired proposal: MRI thigh fat infiltration and same-visit functional limitation

Status: delivery-ready hypothesis and Harbor experiment specification; not fitted. This is a repaired child of expert seed candidate-b8b73c60f7e389c61d45a2f7. It does not inherit the prior UKB-36 outcome question or use any non-Assessment_Center outcome linkage.

## 1. Scientific opening and actual deliverable

The clinically unresolved boundary is whether MRI-derived thigh muscle fat infiltration measures lower-limb muscle quality that is functionally informative beyond muscle quantity and hand-grip strength, or whether it is simply another correlate of age, body size, low grip and existing disability. This matters because a clinician deciding whether a patient with apparently preserved muscle mass needs additional functional assessment needs evidence that composition adds information rather than another measurement of the same reserve construct.

The strongest inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. A UK Biobank study reports that higher MRI-measured thigh muscle fat infiltration (TMFI) is associated with mortality and system-specific disease, but its abstract does not establish functional validity beyond quantity or grip [K1]. A review of imaging studies links myosteatosis with gait, balance, strength and physical function, while emphasizing depot definitions, cross-sectional confounding and the need for standardized imaging [K2]. The EWGSOP2 consensus treats strength as central, muscle quantity/quality as confirmatory, and poor physical performance as severe disease, motivating joint measurement but not proving incremental value for this specific MRI field [K3].

The unresolved claim is therefore:

> At the same Assessment_Center visit, among UKB participants with complete instance-2 MRI thigh measurements, posterior-thigh muscle fat infiltration has a positive, clinically material adjusted association with slow usual walking pace after muscle quantity, grip strength, age, BMI and body-fat percentage are accounted for; a concordant but secondary association is expected for any fall in the prior year.

This is a cross-sectional, descriptive/prognostic information claim about current or recalled functional limitation. It is not a causal effect, a diagnosis of sarcopenia, a claim about future falls, a treatment rule, or a mechanism.

Actual scientific deliverable: newly fit B0/B1/B2 interpretable models and B3 learned models on the locked participant split; output the cohort-flow and complete-case/missingness table, the MFI incremental risk contrast, calibration and held-out uncertainty for walking pace and falls, the instance-3 unpooled sensitivity, and the frozen falsification report. Completion requires output-linked estimates and uncertainty; no fitted result is asserted in this proposal.

## 2. Why this advances inspected work

[K1] establishes broad health relevance of TMFI in UK Biobank but leaves functional incremental validity open. [K2] motivates composition as potentially informative for function, yet notes that myosteatosis is heterogeneous and often confounded by age, disease, disuse and body size. [K3] gives a clinical framework that combines strength, quantity/quality and performance, but its consensus recommendation is not an empirical test of whether the additional MRI measure changes functional classification.

This experiment adds a deliberately narrow, falsifiable boundary test: identical-visit posterior-thigh MFI, bilateral thigh fat-free volume and bilateral grip are entered in nested models for two clinically interpretable outcomes. The key contrast is not a small predictive score improvement; it is the adjusted absolute risk difference for slow pace when MFI is set to the training-derived 75th versus 25th percentile, with quantity and grip retained. A null result would be useful: it would argue that, for this population and measurement, quantity and grip capture most of the available same-visit functional information. A positive result would justify external validation and prospective functional testing, not immediate clinical use.

Leading explanation: MFI reflects lower-limb muscle quality and retains a residual relationship with functional limitation after quantity and grip adjustment. Strong rivals are: (1) quantity/body-size confounding, so MFI attenuates after fat-free volume, BMI and body-fat adjustment; (2) common age, disease, inactivity, pain or neurologic limitation, so the association is non-specific or disappears in age/body-composition sensitivity analyses; (3) measurement/selection, because MRI attendees with complete fields differ from the broader cohort; and (4) hand-grip mismeasurement, because upper-limb pain or neuropathy makes grip an imperfect comparator. Same-visit data cannot separate MFI causing disability from disability/disuse causing MFI, and no bound field provides pain, physical activity, neurologic examination or raw-image QC.

## 3. Exact read-only source binding

The full catalog snapshot is ukb-completed-subset-20261002, catalog SHA-256 6834d79f6da16d271bd2f4e017feff3648babeb8e3ea41122015757f0adedf32. The dataset README lists 61 read-only source files. This proposal uses one table only:

| join | none; every required field is in this table; do not join ukb671626, Olink, dta or any other namespace |

Primary instance 2 fields and their roles:

- Visit/time: eid and 53-2.0.
- MRI MFI: 23355-2.0 (posterior thigh MFI left), 23356-2.0 (right).
- MRI muscle quantity: 22403-2.0/22405-2.0 (anterior thigh fat-free muscle volume right/left) and 22404-2.0/22406-2.0 (posterior thigh fat-free muscle volume right/left).
- Grip: 46-2.0 and 47-2.0.
- Primary functional outcome: 924-2.0, usual walking pace.
- Secondary functional outcome: 2296-2.0, falls in the last year.
- Same-visit adjustment: 21003-2.0 age at assessment, 21001-2.0 BMI, 23099-2.0 body-fat percentage.
- Sensitivity adjustment: 21085-2.0 visceral fat volume.

The table has exact MRI/outcome counterparts at instance 3: 53-3.0, 23355-3.0/23356-3.0, 22403-3.0 through 22406-3.0, 46-3.0/47-3.0, 924-3.0, 2296-3.0, 21003-3.0, 21001-3.0 and 23099-3.0. Instance 3 is an unpooled later-visit sensitivity only. The complete source audit and all observed overlap counts are in source-schema-audit.json.

Same-visit means all fields use the same instance and the participant's Assessment_Center date. No within-day timestamps or raw images are bound, so the experiment must not claim finer temporal ordering.

## 4. Population, timing and missingness

Primary population: one row per unique eid with a parseable 53-2.0 date from 2014-01-01 through 2023-12-31, valid numeric values for both MFI sides, all four thigh fat-free-volume fields, both grip fields, age, BMI and body-fat percentage, and a valid walking-pace response. The audit observed dates from 2014-04-30 through 2023-03-12. There is no future follow-up window and no incident disease selection.

MFI_mean is the arithmetic mean of 23355-2.0 and 23356-2.0 after training-only scaling; thigh_quantity is the sum of the four fat-free-volume fields after training-only scaling; grip_max is the maximum of 46-2.0 and 47-2.0. The primary complete-case model requires all source components rather than silently substituting one side. Prespecified sensitivities use one-side-available MFI and grip, complete-four versus minimum-three MRI components, left/right MFI separately, and MFI side difference.

Walking pace is coded as slow (924 = 1) versus average/brisk (924 = 2 or 3) for the primary binary estimand; an ordinal 1<2<3 model is secondary. Falls is any fall (2296 = 2 or 3) versus none (2296 = 1); the ordinal three-level coding is secondary. Codes -7/-3 and nulls are missing and excluded from the primary outcome, not encoded as healthy or impaired.

Primary instance-2 audit facts: 39,443 complete for the six MRI fields; 38,070 complete for MRI plus both grip sides; 39,145 with MRI plus walking pace; 39,177 with MRI plus falls; and 37,830 with MRI, both grips and both functional outcomes. Instance 3 has 816 complete MRI records and 808 with both grips and both outcomes. These are source audit counts, not study results.

Missingness is part of the result. Report a flow diagram from all table rows to dated instance-2 rows, complete MRI, complete comparator, complete covariates, and each outcome. Compare included versus excluded participants on available same-visit age, BMI, body fat, visit date and field availability. As a sensitivity, model probability of complete MRI/comparator availability from those observed fields and use stabilized inverse-probability-of-observation weights only with adequate overlap; report extreme weights. Do not impute a missing outcome in the primary analysis. Multiple imputation of covariates is a secondary analysis only, with imputation fitted within training data.

## 5. Estimand and analysis

For the primary slow-pace outcome Y, let C be age, BMI, body-fat percentage and visit calendar year, Q be thigh_quantity, G be grip_max, and M be MFI_mean. The primary standardized information contrast is:

Delta_MFI = E[ P(Y=1 | M=Q75, Q, G, C) - P(Y=1 | M=Q25, Q, G, C) ],

where Q25 and Q75 are calculated from the training split only and the expectation averages over the locked eligible population's observed Q, G and C. This is a model-standardized association contrast, not an intervention effect. Report Delta_MFI in percentage points with a 95% participant-bootstrap interval and the corresponding B1-to-B2 contrast. The secondary estimand repeats this for any fall. Report one-SD MFI contrasts as well because quartile contrasts are scale-dependent.

Models are:

- B0: age, BMI, body-fat percentage and calendar year, with prespecified restricted cubic splines for age and BMI.
- B1 baseline: B0 plus thigh_quantity and grip_max. This is the quantity/grip comparator.
- B2 primary incremental model: B1 plus linear MFI_mean.
- B3 learned alternative: a shallow gradient-boosted binary model using the identical participants, split and information set, represented by the raw bilateral MFI, four quantity, two grip, age, BMI, body fat and calendar-year fields plus deterministic summaries. A fixed small grid is selected on validation log loss/Brier score only. It can reveal stable MFI thresholds, side asymmetry or interactions with quantity/grip that B2 erases; effect plots are descriptive and not mechanisms.

All models use a deterministic eid-hash 70/15/15 participant split into train/validation/locked test, with event/date-stratum balance only after participant assignment. No participant may contribute to more than one split. Scaling, spline fitting, quartiles, imputation, tuning and thresholds use training data only. The locked test is read once. Fit and report both outcomes under the frozen specification; do not select the primary endpoint after viewing results.

Report event counts and prevalence, complete-case flow, B1/B2 coefficients and standardized contrasts, B3 held-out calibration intercept/slope, Brier score and AUROC, and paired participant-bootstrap intervals (at least 500, preferably 1,000). A 0.01 Brier change is secondary and is not clinical evidence without a stable MFI contrast. Repeat the frozen analysis at instance 3 without pooling or retuning; because it may reuse participants and has only 808 fully observed rows, it cannot serve as independent validation.

## 6. Falsification and interpretation rules

Run once under the frozen specification and retain adverse results.

1. Quantity/grip attenuation: if MFI loses direction or material size after Q and G are added, the claim that MFI adds information is not supported.
2. Body-composition sensitivity: compare B2 with and without body-fat percentage and, where overlap permits, visceral fat volume. Large attenuation identifies body-composition confounding or overadjustment as unresolved; it does not prove a mechanism.
3. Age and calendar sensitivity: compare flexible age with age bands and visit-year adjustment. A signal confined to one age band or date period is a boundary/selection finding, not a general functional marker.
4. Measurement structure: compare bilateral mean, each side, side difference, complete-four and minimum-three rules. A signal driven by one side or one missingness rule is adverse to a stable MFI interpretation.
5. Comparator limitation: repeat with grip_max, both grips, and grip residualized on age/body size. A large change shows that grip is an imperfect or collinear comparator; it does not prove lower-limb biology.
6. Outcome coding: repeat binary versus ordinal walking pace and falls coding, retain -3/-7 exclusion counts, and report whether the same direction appears for the two distinct outcomes. A pace-only result is not evidence for falls.
7. Selection: compare complete MRI attendees with all dated instance-2 rows and apply the observation-weight sensitivity. Failure of weight overlap or material instability makes the result inconclusive for the source population.
8. Leakage/permutation: shuffle MFI within age/BMI strata and permute outcomes once with fixed seeds. Any retained locked-test signal invalidates the corresponding computational result.
9. Later visit: repeat at instance 3 as a sensitivity. Concordance is supportive of transport across visit instances but is not independent replication; discordance is a reason to investigate selection and measurement timing.

Supportive result: in the locked instance-2 analysis, Delta_MFI for slow pace is positive with a 95% interval excluding zero and the prespecified point estimate reaches at least 5 percentage points (a planning threshold for clinical materiality, not a validated MCID); the direction is not removed by quantity/grip/body-composition/missingness sensitivities; no permutation signal appears; and the secondary falls result is directionally compatible or explicitly reported as null. B3 may reveal stable nonlinear structure, but predictive improvement alone cannot turn an adverse B2 result into support.

Adverse result: Delta_MFI is zero/reversed, below the planning materiality threshold, is explained by quantity/grip or missingness, is confined to a coding/side/date subgroup, or the same signal appears under permutation. This supports the rival that MRI MFI is redundant, confounded or selected, and the incremental-functional-information claim should be abandoned or narrowed.

Inconclusive result: wide intervals, too few falls, failure of source/date or overlap checks, unstable coding, non-overlapping observation weights, or inability to verify MFI measurement validity. An imprecise null is not a refutation. Continuing would require expert review of MRI segmentation/QC and functional coding, validated clinical assessments, or an external cohort. Clinical adjudication is required for disability severity, physical examination, pain/neurologic causes, raw-image measurement validity and generalization. The computation can check source binding, same-instance joins, cohort flow, model outputs, uncertainty and whether conclusions match those outputs; it cannot establish causality, mechanism, future falls risk or treatment benefit.

## 7. Alternatives, compute and limits

The interpretable nested models are retained because they directly answer the incremental question and expose attenuation after quantity and grip. The learned alternative is retained because threshold and component interactions are scientifically substantive possibilities: a linear mean MFI term can lose a high-risk tail or side-specific pattern. Both use the same source fields, participant split, targets and uncertainty evaluation. A transformer/sequence model is deferred because this is a one-visit question and no repeated dated trajectory is needed. A mechanistic model is deferred because raw images, histology, physical activity, pain, neurologic findings and treatment are unavailable. Revisit either only after those dependencies are admitted and the question changes.

The measured audit was CPU-only and completed in seconds for selected columns. Full model fitting and bootstrap are unmeasured; plan 4-8 CPUs, 16-32 GiB and under two hours, within the future solver planning envelope of 16 CPUs, 262,144 MiB and 28,800 seconds. No GPU is required or scientifically justified for these tabular models.

## 8. Three inspected works

Exactly three distinct works are attached through key-references.json and the three UTF-8 evidence snapshots:

[K1] Zhang Y et al. “Integrative Analysis Uncover the Effects and Multi-Omics Features of Thigh Muscle Fat Infiltration.” Aging Cell. 2026;25(9):e70690. PMID 42675546, DOI 10.1111/acel.70690. Abstract-only inspection. Supports broad UKB TMFI-health association; does not establish incremental same-visit function beyond quantity/grip.

[K2] Roe LS, Zmuda JM, Miljkovic I. “Myosteatosis: an emerging biomarker of aging.” Frontiers in Aging. 2026;7:1868010. DOI 10.3389/fragi.2026.1868010. Relevant full-text passages inspected from the frozen provider source. Supports the plausible composition-function link and explicitly bounds it with depot, confounding, cross-sectional and standardization limitations.

[K3] Cruz-Jentoft AJ et al., Writing Group for EWGSOP2. “Sarcopenia: revised European consensus on definition and diagnosis.” Age and Ageing. 2019;48(1):16-31. PMID 30312372, DOI 10.1093/ageing/afy169. Abstract-only inspection. Supports the clinical framework of strength plus quantity/quality plus physical performance; does not test this MRI incremental estimand.

# UKB-03 repaired direction: MRI muscle fat infiltration and same-visit functional discordance

Status: delivery-ready design, not fitted. This is an independent evolution of expert seed UKB-03, with the prior outcome-ascertainment branch retained as context only.

## Recommendation

Make the cross-sectional imaging-visit question primary. Use the first repeat-imaging change question only as a prespecified secondary, visit-ordered sensitivity. The reason is scientific and data-bound: instance-2 complete overlap is large (37,778 records with all MRI, bilateral grip, walking pace and falls fields), whereas only 765 participants have all of those fields at both instances 2 and 3. Instances 2 and 3 are explicitly the imaging visit and first repeat imaging visit in the UKB field definitions, but this derivative has no nonmissing 53-2.0 or 53-3.0; therefore repeat changes cannot be converted into a rate or exact elapsed-time effect.

## Opening, supported claim and unresolved hypothesis

The strongest inspected evidence supports a bounded association: MRI-derived adverse muscle composition, usually combining low muscle quantity with high fat infiltration, is associated with poorer self-reported function in a CKD-focused UKB imaging analysis [K1]. UKB MR/observational evidence also links anterior and posterior thigh MFI with grip strength [K2]. A consensus statement says imaging is complementary to grip and gait/function, not a replacement for those assessments [K3]. None of these establishes that MFI supplies clinically meaningful information beyond thigh muscle quantity and grip for a broader imaging population, and none turns walking pace or falls at an imaging visit into future outcomes.

The falsifiable hypothesis is:

> Among UKB participants at the instance-2 imaging visit with usable bilateral thigh MRI composition, bilateral grip, usual walking pace and falls responses, higher posterior-thigh MFI is associated with worse same-visit functional status after adjustment for thigh muscle quantity and grip, age, sex, BMI and smoking; specifically, adding MFI to the quantity-plus-grip model produces a prespecified clinically meaningful increase in the standardized probability of slow usual walking pace.

Primary outcome: the UKB ordinal usual-walking-pace response 924-2.0, retaining its documented categories and excluding only special/missing codes. The primary clinical contrast is the standardized probability of slow pace for MFI at the training-set 90th versus 10th percentile, with a 5-percentage-point absolute difference prespecified as clinically meaningful. Secondary outcomes are the full 2296-2.0 falls-response distribution and a binary any-fall contrast only after the UKB coding table is bound and its positive category is verified. These are responses about the visit, with falls referring to the last year; they are not prospective falls outcomes.

This is a descriptive/prognostic cross-sectional association, not a causal effect, diagnostic claim, validated sarcopenia phenotype or mechanism. A positive result would justify external validation against objective gait and adjudicated falls and could inform whether MRI composition deserves consideration when function and grip appear discordant. It would not justify screening, treatment, or inferring that fat infiltration causes weakness.

## Why this is an advance

The closest UKB study [K1] asks about a combined adverse-composition phenotype in a CKD-enriched comparison. This experiment asks whether MFI itself adds functional information once quantity and grip are already known, in the available general imaging cohort, and defines a clinically interpretable discordance contrast. [K2] supports MFI–grip relevance but does not test walking pace/falls conditional on grip and quantity. [K3] identifies the unresolved measurement boundary; the proposed nested models test it directly. Thus the advance is not another association or a small leaderboard gain: it tests whether composition measures a distinct functional dimension that would remain visible when conventional quantity and strength measures are already available.

## Exact population and data construction

Use only the ukb672073 namespace and join on eid. Sources are read-only.

This is a coarse pre-imaging disease-history sensitivity, not complete disease adjudication.

The fourth configured source, ukb_a19465be8f90accc_parquet / UKB/ukb672073_Biological_Samples.csv (Parquet), remains accessible read-only but is not required: no blood biomarker is needed to answer this functional-information question. Do not join it merely to use all sources.

Exclude special values such as -1, -3, blank and nonnumeric strings. Do not replace missing MFI with zero. Require both sides for primary bilateral MFI and grip; report complete-case flow and retain one-sided/single-component analyses as sensitivity only. Define:
- MFI_post = mean(23355-2.0, 23356-2.0), after unit/finite-value checks; report left-right difference.
- Q_thigh = (22403+22404+22405+22406)/(50-2.0 squared), with volume units verified from the field metadata; report total, anterior/posterior and left/right components as sensitivity.
- grip_mean = mean(46-2.0, 47-2.0); grip_max is a sensitivity.
- Preserve raw 924-2.0 and 2296-2.0 codes and use the public coding table before mapping labels. The bounded audit found the following core counts: instance-2 MRI complete 39,443; MRI+grip 38,070; MRI+grip+walking+falls 37,778; adding instance-2 BMI, smoking and age leaves 37,558. Walking pace observed codes were 1:3,554, 2:33,037, 3:28,219 and -7:45; falls observed codes were 1:52,779, 2:8,712 and 3:3,329. These are source audit counts, not fitted results.

## Models and estimand

Freeze a participant-level hash split (70% train, 15% validation, 15% locked test; seed 36), stratified after assignment by walking-pace category, falls category and sex. No participant may contribute to more than one split.

B0 is an interpretable ordinal logistic model for walking pace with age spline, sex, BMI, smoking, and Q_thigh plus grip. B1 adds standardized MFI_post. Standardization, imputation and the MFI 10th/90th percentiles are fit on training data only. Estimate the standardized 90th-versus-10th MFI slow-pace probability difference over the locked test covariate distribution, with participant bootstrap 95% intervals. Report odds ratios only as secondary summaries; the primary scale is absolute standardized probability. Repeat B0/B1 for the falls response as ordinal/multinomial outcome; do not collapse codes without verified code meanings.

B2 is a small CPU gradient-boosted multiclass/ordinal-compatible model using exactly the B1 inputs and split, with fixed shallow-tree settings selected on validation ordinal log loss. Its substantive purpose is to reveal stable nonlinear MFI thresholds or MFI-by-quantity/grip regions that the linear MFI term erases, especially high-MFI/normal-quantity or high-MFI/preserved-grip discordance. Report held-out ordinal log loss, Brier score, calibration, category-specific discrimination, permutation importance and held-out partial-dependence/effect tables. These curves are descriptive, not mechanisms. A B2 predictive gain without a stable B1 standardized contrast is not evidence that MFI adds clinically meaningful information.

Supportive primary evidence requires: (a) B1’s locked-test 90th-versus-10th MFI slow-pace contrast is at least 5 percentage points with a 95% interval excluding zero; (b) the direction is stable under bilateral/volume-indexing and disease-history sensitivities; (c) the effect is not explained by a matching grip/quantity permutation or by a large complete-case weighting correction; and (d) B2, if used, shows reproducible nonlinear/interaction structure rather than only an unstable test-score gain. Adverse evidence is a reversed/near-zero contrast, a contrast confined to one side or missingness pattern, disappearance after age/sex/disease adjustment, or a matching signal after MFI permutation. Inconclusive evidence is a wide interval, sparse valid outcome categories, unstable code interpretation, inadequate overlap for observation weights, or inability to bind disease timing.

Computationally checkable outputs are source hashes and columns, participant flow, raw-code distributions, derived variables, nested model fits, locked-test predictions, standardized contrasts, calibration and uncertainty. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for objective gait, validated functional testing, fall adjudication, pain/neurologic disease severity, treatment status, causality, mechanism, external validity and a clinical decision threshold.

## Rival explanations and falsification

- Selection: MRI attendance and complete MFI/function fields select healthier volunteers. Compare included participants with all instance-2 MRI participants on age, sex, BMI and smoking; model observation probability and apply stabilized inverse-probability weights as one sensitivity. Report extreme weights and overlap; this cannot remove UKB volunteer bias.
- Age and sex: MFI, quantity and function are age/sex patterned. Use flexible age, sex adjustment and prespecified sex-stratified estimates. Do not interpret residual association as biology.
- Medical disease: CKD, diabetes, obesity, pain and neurologic/musculoskeletal disease could cause both MFI and poor function. Use the paired pre-2014 ICD-10/date sensitivity above, plus BMI and smoking, and report how much the MFI contrast attenuates. No claim of complete disease control is allowed.
- Measurement: outcomes are self-report; falls is a last-year recall field and walking pace is a questionnaire category. Report code frequencies, special codes, left-right MFI agreement, implausible/extreme values and grip side discordance. Repeat imaging is not a replacement for objective performance.
- Timing: instances 2 and 3 are imaging visits by UKB field definitions, but no participant-level 53-2.0/53-3.0 values exist in this Parquet. Do not infer dates from file metadata, instance labels or current date.
- Leakage: permute MFI within sex once, permute outcome once, and rerun the locked pipeline. Any retained signal invalidates the corresponding computation.
- Disease-history negative control: compare the MFI contrast before and after pre-2014 disease adjustment; a large attenuation is evidence that disease composition, not an independent MFI dimension, may explain the association.

## Repeat-imaging secondary, not primary

For the 765 participants with complete MRI, grip, walking pace and falls at both instances 2 and 3 (756 after the listed instance-specific covariates), compute Delta_MFI, Delta_Q, Delta_grip, and visit-ordered changes in the walking/falls responses. Fit a paired ordinal transition model or change-score regression adjusted for baseline values, sex and baseline age. Report direction, paired uncertainty and missingness; do not estimate a rate, causal change effect or future outcome because exact dates are unavailable. The instance-3 complete sample has age-at-recruitment median 49 versus 55 for the instance-2 complete sample, demonstrating selection/composition differences. Treat this analysis as supportive only if it is directionally compatible and sufficiently precise; otherwise it is inconclusive, not a refutation of the cross-sectional question.

## Alternatives and resource choice

The simple baseline is retained because it directly tests the conditional estimand on an absolute probability scale and makes age, sex, quantity, grip and disease attenuation auditable. The learned alternative is retained because it can reveal threshold/interaction structure—such as high MFI despite preserved volume or grip—that a single linear MFI coefficient loses. Both use the identical participant split, fields, outcome construction and uncertainty evaluation. A transformer or mechanistic muscle model is deferred: no image payload, histology, objective gait, inflammatory mechanism, exact imaging dates or intervention labels are available. Revisit it only after objective functional validation or richer longitudinal dates are admitted. Planned future fit: CPU, 4–8 cores, 16–32 GiB RAM, under two hours provisionally; the bounded selected-column audit took about 15 seconds on 2 CPUs/8 GiB. No GPU is needed for these tabular fits and no scientific fit has been executed here.

## Actual deliverable

Completion requires newly fitted B0, B1 and B2 objects and output-linked tables: deterministic cohort flow; one-row participant analysis table with raw codes, derived MFI/quantity/grip, covariates, source audit and exclusion reason; locked-test predictions and calibration; standardized slow-pace and falls contrasts with participant-bootstrap intervals; repeat-change table; and the frozen falsification report. The present note asserts no fitted result.

## Key references

See the attached key-references.json and evidence snapshots for exactly three inspected works: [K1] Indurain et al. (full-text relevant passages), [K2] Taylor et al. (abstract only), and [K3] Wang et al. (full-text relevant passages). Field timing/coding checks were obtained separately from the public UKB field pages and are not counted as the three key works.

# UKB prediagnostic measured reserve and CRC competing mortality — follow-up provenance repair

Status: proposed, not fitted. Parent: candidate-2b202f4d99e86bdc347d56e0. This child preserves the incident C18–C20 question and makes one consequential repair: the primary target is explicitly non-cancer death (not the ambiguous shorthand “non-CRC”), and five-year eligibility is defined from a documented outcome-ascertainment date rather than an observed maximum or an invented administrative cutoff.

## 1. Opening, supported evidence, and unresolved hypothesis

The closest inspected evidence supports associations but leaves a clinically meaningful timing boundary unresolved. [K1] reports an abstract-only association between post-diagnosis frailty/pre-frailty and all-cause mortality among CRC survivors. [K2] reports an abstract-only association between preoperative handgrip/frailty and early postoperative loss of independence. [K3] reports an abstract-only competing-risk distinction in which CRC-specific mortality is related to tumor factors while non-CRC mortality is related to patient vulnerability. None tests an objectively measured reserve profile before diagnosis, restricts diagnosis to a durable prediagnostic window, or asks whether reserve is more strongly associated with non-cancer than CRC-specific death.

The strongest supported claim is therefore that vulnerability measures around or after CRC diagnosis can be prognostically associated with adverse mortality or recovery, and that CRC-specific and other-cause mortality may have different predictors. The unresolved claim is narrower:

> Among UKB participants assessed from 2006-01-01 through 2010-12-31, free of a valid paired C00–C97 cancer record at assessment, who subsequently develop an incident C18, C19 or C20 cancer at least 730 days after assessment, is lower assessment-time measured reserve associated with a larger five-year cumulative-incidence increase in non-cancer death than in CRC-specific death, after prespecified age, sex, BMI, smoking, diagnosis year, prediagnosis comorbidity and CRC subsite adjustment?

This is a standardized prognostic association conditional on later incident CRC. It is not a causal reserve effect, a treatment-tolerance rule, a validated frailty construct, a mechanism, or evidence that reserve changes CRC biology.

The leading rival is occult-cancer timing: low reserve close to diagnosis may record cachexia, early illness or intensified observation. Other rivals are age/comorbidity confounding, UKB volunteer and exposure-availability selection, cancer/death coding, and unmeasured stage, grade, treatment, recurrence and deprivation. [K3] makes stage and residual disease a consequential rival, but the verified UKB binding does not contain those variables.

## 2. Exact read-only source bindings

All joins use only participant namespace ukb672073 and exact key eid. No source-specific IDs are cross-joined, and no /data alias or inferred crosswalk is allowed. The inherited source-schema audit and compile audit verified the selected columns, unique non-null eid keys, table IDs, archive members and hashes; its JSON is attached as source-schema-audit.json.

| role | exact source path and SHA-256 | catalog table / archive member | required columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| assessment exposure/covariates | [private-path]/ukb_d61ec821b81b9034.parquet; e69705f71f6a4f263371bec081d50a7d9482291d73cde09873634b327936a841 | UKB/ukb672073_Assessment_Center.csv (Parquet), table-6fc0a334db7f533b; ordinary file | eid; 53-0.0; 46-0.0, 47-0.0; 21001-0.0; 20116-0.0 |
| demographics | [private-path]/ukb_ce68812c3a782e09.parquet; d446c8288dfe59abc97e44a43027628aa7221a60f307d4da879a7c491b930299 | UKB/ukb672073_Population_Characteristics.csv (Parquet), table-674bd55f4152a860; ordinary file | eid; 31-0.0; 34-0.0; 21022-0.0 |
| laboratory reserve | [private-path]/ukb_a19465be8f90accc.parquet; 9a62c73361094f4e12045082d8872efa84933e7bb86f596e9e8a49fc162a4ab0 | UKB/ukb672073_Biological_Samples.csv (Parquet), table-50f94f98137a2d88; ordinary file | eid; 30600-0.0 albumin; 30700-0.0 creatinine; 30720-0.0 cystatin C |
| outcomes/diagnoses | [private-path]/ukb_e53f1b242ccf9047.parquet; 36d0e32efc608dd0e324a6e66fd4211813e7542ec08b78213488ab8f52874ad8 | UKB/ukb672073_Health_Related_Outcomes.csv (Parquet), table-03f57283ab9ae48b; ordinary file | eid; 40000-0.0/1.0 and 40001-0.0/1.0; 40005-0.0..21.0 and 40006-0.0..21.0; 41270-0.0..258 and 41280-0.0..258 |
| follow-up provenance audit only | [private-path]/ukb_c9f8c514956c9481.parquet; 42c0e50e9b3e270bb578a4c56f0d753c9a794ad69e56a221bae940dd9060b1d5 | UKB/ukb672073_Online_Follow_up.csv (Parquet), table-99ff3ee72fc4030a; ordinary file | eid; 20191-0.0 |

The full catalog snapshot is ukb-completed-subset-20261002, SHA-256 6834d79f6da16d271bd2f4e017feff3648babeb8e3ea41122015757f0adedf32, covering 61 source files. Each of the five listed derivatives has 502,370 rows in the inherited audit. The follow-up derivative contains only eid and 20191-0.0; the verified audit found that field to be integer/code-like rather than a parseable ascertainment date. It is never used as an outcome date.

## 3. Non-negotiable follow-up readiness gate

The scientific design remains executable only conditionally. With the currently verified snapshot, tau_source is not documented, so a solver must emit an inconclusive pre-fit readiness result and must not fit the cohort. This is a scientifically meaningful boundary, not a null finding.

Before any cohort fitting, the solver must:

1. Verify every exact source path, SHA-256, catalog table ID, ordinary archive member, namespace, eid uniqueness/non-nullness and required column list.
2. Read the frozen dataset README/catalog and relevant outcome-source documentation. Find an explicitly documented calendar cutoff tau_source for completeness of absence as well as presence in the 40000/40001 death and 40005/40006 cancer fields, with provenance and scope. A file mtime, campaign date, current date, observed maximum event date, or interpretation of 20191-0.0 is invalid.
3. If no common documented cutoff covers all fields, write readiness_status=inconclusive_pre_fit, list the missing source and scope, and stop before fitting, reporting a null or reporting a five-year estimate. If field-specific cutoffs are documented, tau_source is their minimum only when the documentation establishes a common completeness interpretation; otherwise the gate fails.
4. If the gate passes, record tau_source and its source locator in every output manifest. Use a single explicit leap-day rule: anniversary dates use calendar DateOffset(years=h), with February 29 anniversaries mapped to February 28 in non-leap years.
5. For h=1, 3 and 5 years, include a diagnosis at t0 only when t0 + DateOffset(years=h) <= tau_source. The primary five-year cohort therefore has documented support for the complete five-year risk window. Deaths are counted through t0+h and otherwise censored at tau_source. Observed maxima (death 2022-12-19; cancer 2022-06-01) are reported only as audits and never prove completeness.

Thus the current verified provenance supports a readiness package and a conditional study specification, but not a fitted five-year result. Missing tau_source cannot be repaired by selecting a shorter arbitrary horizon because that would change the stated clinical estimand; a future Lead decision could define a new horizon only as a new scientific child.

## 4. Population and deterministic outcome construction

Use baseline date b_i=53-0.0 and retain b_i in the specified 2006–2010 interval. A cancer slot is valid only when the same k has a parseable 40005-k.0 date and trimmed uppercase ICD-10 40006-k.0 code. Record malformed, unpaired and discordant slots; never borrow a date or code from an adjacent slot. Exclude any participant with a valid paired C00–C97 record on or before b_i.

Define t0_i as the earliest valid post-b_i paired C18/C19/C20 diagnosis date. Retain tied earliest slots for audit, then choose the lowest slot and lexicographically smallest normalized code for deterministic subsite labeling. To keep “incident CRC” distinct from a later recurrence/second primary, exclude a participant from the primary cohort if any other valid paired C00–C97 diagnosis lies strictly between b_i and t0_i; report that count and repeat without this exclusion only as a labelled sensitivity. The inherited screening audit found 6,094 baseline cancer records, 2,219 post-assessment CRC cases without baseline cancer, and lag counts 329 (0–<2 years), 493 (2–<5 years), and 1,397 (>=5 years). These are source screening counts before reserve completeness, the no-intervening-cancer rule and readiness gating, not fitted results.

Primary participants require t0_i-b_i >=730 days, valid reserve exposure, no intervening cancer under the primary rule, and five-year support after the readiness gate. The 0–<2-year stratum is a reverse-causation check; 2–<5 years and >=5 years are prespecified timing strata. The >=5-year stratum is a sensitivity boundary, not a replacement chosen after seeing results.

For death, use each paired 40000-j.0 date with the same-slot 40001-j.0 underlying-cause code. Retain valid deaths after t0_i and before or at tau_source, choose the earliest date, and on date ties prefer a usable ICD-10 cause then the lowest slot while recording all tied slots. Classify the first death as CRC-specific (C18/C19/C20), non-cancer (outside C00–C97), other cancer (C00–C97 excluding C18–C20), or unknown (missing, malformed or non-ICD-10 cause). Unknown is a fourth competing event in the primary analysis. Sensitivities classify unknown as non-cancer and censor at unknown death. V01–Y89 external-cause death is reported as a negative-control endpoint, not silently merged into non-cancer. Death on or before t0_i is an impossible ordering: exclude from the primary and report.

## 5. Exposure, adjustment and estimand

Set grip_max=max(46-0.0,47-0.0), using one available side and missing only when both are unavailable. The four measured-reserve components are grip_max, albumin, creatinine and cystatin C. Within training data only, standardize grip by sex, use log(albumin), negative-log creatinine and negative-log cystatin C. Define R as the mean of available standardized components when at least three of four are present; retain component count and every missingness indicator. Mandatory sensitivities are complete-four, grip-only, laboratory-only and training-median-plus-indicators. Call this “measured reserve,” never validated biological reserve.

Adjustment uses age at diagnosis derived from age field 21022-0.0 plus the exact b_i-to-t0_i interval under a documented convention, sex 31-0.0, BMI 21001-0.0, smoking 20116-0.0, diagnosis year, CRC subsite and a dated pre-t0 Charlson count from 41270/41280, excluding the incident CRC. No post-diagnosis variables enter. Townsend deprivation, ethnicity, centre, stage, grade, TNM, treatment, toxicity, performance status, recurrence, histology, validated frailty, adjudicated causes and external validation are unavailable in the verified binding; diagnosis-array values must not be relabelled as deprivation.

The primary estimand is the standardized five-year differential:
Delta5 = [CIF_NC(R=Q25) - CIF_NC(R=Q75)] - [CIF_CRC(R=Q25) - CIF_CRC(R=Q75)],
where NC is non-cancer death, CRC is C18/C19/C20 death, other cancer and unknown are competing events, Q25/Q75 are training-derived, and standardization averages predictions over the locked eligible population. Report one-, three- and five-year cause-specific CIFs, Delta5, cause-specific reserve log-effects, event counts and 95% participant-bootstrap intervals. This is a descriptive prognostic association. Fine–Gray and cause-specific hazard parameterizations are sensitivity descriptions, not interchangeable causal effects.

## 6. Baseline versus learned alternative

Both alternatives use the same eligible participants, t0, paired outcomes, covariates, reserve components/missingness audit, split and uncertainty procedure. The scientific comparison asks whether a scalar reserve summary is adequate or whether component thresholds/lag interactions materially change the cause-specific contrast; predictive gain alone is not clinical evidence.

Baseline B0/B1: one-year discrete-time cause-specific complementary-log-log hazards for CRC, NC, other cancer and unknown through five years. B0 contains prespecified restricted cubic splines for age, sex, BMI, smoking, diagnosis year, Charlson count, subsite and time interval. B1 adds one linear one-SD R term and prespecified missingness indicators. Convert the four hazards to CIFs by competing-risk recursion. Freeze B0/B1 before locked-test predictions.

Learned B2: CPU gradient-boosted multinomial discrete-time hazard model on the same person-period rows, with B1 inputs plus raw reserve components, their missingness indicators, interval and prespecified reserve-component-by-lag interactions. Choose only from 200/400 trees, depth 2/3 and learning rate 0.03/0.05 by validation integrated IPCW Brier score. Fit transformations, imputation, tuning and Q25/Q75 on training/validation only. Use a participant-level 70/15/15 split, seed 36, assigned by deterministic eid hash and stratified only after assignment by event type and diagnosis year; no person-period rows cross splits; read the locked test once.

Report endpoint-specific calibration intercept/slope, one/three/five-year and integrated IPCW Brier scores, time-dependent AUC, Delta5, one-SD effects, coefficients, learned effect tables, permutation importance and accumulated-local-effect curves with >=500 participant bootstrap resamples. A locked-test integrated-Brier improvement of 0.01 with an interval above zero is a practical predictive threshold, not a clinical threshold. B2 improvement without a stable NC-versus-CRC contrast is only a prediction result.

The actual deliverable is newly fitted and output-linked if readiness passes: (a) cohort-flow and one-row-per-participant table with b_i, t0_i, lag, paired-record audit, reserve fields, covariates, tau_source and exclusions; (b) B0/B1/B2 objects and effect/CIF tables; (c) locked-test calibration, Brier/AUC and bootstrap output; and (d) a falsification report explicitly labelled supportive, adverse or inconclusive. If readiness fails, the only valid deliverable is the readiness report and no fitted objects.

## 7. Falsification and interpretation

Run the following once under the frozen specification, retain adverse results and do not select a stratum or endpoint after inspection:

1. Timing: report 0–<2, 2–<5 and >=5 years. A signal confined to 0–<2, or absent at >=5, is adverse to durable prediagnostic reserve and supports occult timing/observation.
2. Age/comorbidity: compare flexible age/Charlson, age-only, age-plus-comorbidity and supported age bands (40–59, 60–69, >=70). Strong attenuation or reserve-by-age reversal indicates confounding or heterogeneity, not mechanism.
3. Availability/selection: compare complete-four, minimum-three, imputed-indicator, grip-only and laboratory-only definitions; model reserve availability from assessment age, sex, BMI and smoking in all assessment-window participants; use stabilized inverse-probability-of-observation weighting only as a sensitivity with overlap/extreme-weight reporting. This cannot remove UKB volunteer or MNAR bias.
4. Coding: enumerate malformed/unpaired slots, ties, unknown causes and impossible orderings; compare paired 40005/40006 anchoring with the earliest concordant pre-t0 41270/41280 C18–C20 occurrence where both date and code are usable. Instability is adverse to the coding interpretation.
5. Cause/competing risk: compare CRC, NC, other-cancer, unknown and external-cause patterns and compare competing-risk CIFs with naive competing-death censoring. A matching external-cause pattern or CRC-dominant pattern weakens the proposed differential interpretation.
6. Leakage: shuffle R within sex and permute outcomes once with fixed seeds. Any held-out signal under permutation invalidates the corresponding computation.
7. Stage/treatment boundary: never proxy stage or treatment with lag, death cause, comorbidity or reserve. A CRC-specific result, timing-only result or subsite divergence remains unresolved for stage/treatment and must not be narrated as biology.

Supportive requires a passed provenance gate; in the >=2-year cohort a positive Delta5 with an interval excluding zero; compatible direction in >=5 years; no comparable CRC-specific contrast; stability across cause/coding/missingness sensitivities; no external-cause match; and no permutation leakage. This supports only a robust prognostic regularity. B2 may reveal stable nonlinear component patterns, but does not convert the association into mechanism or causality.

Adverse means Delta5 is zero/reversed, CRC death is at least as strongly associated, the pattern is confined to the 0–<2-year window, is driven by one assay/missingness, is removed by age/comorbidity, is coding-unstable, or matches external-cause/permutation patterns. Report the rival supported and abandon or narrow the durable-reserve interpretation.

Inconclusive means the provenance gate fails, deaths/events are sparse, intervals are clinically wide, cause/coding is unstable, calibration fails, or observation weights lack overlap. Do not call this a null. Continuing would require documented linkage completeness, expert cause/stage/treatment review, or an independent cohort. Computation can verify bindings, parsing, cohort flow, model outputs, uncertainty and conclusion-to-output consistency; it cannot establish cause-of-death validity, stage, treatment, recurrence, mechanism, causal effects or external generalizability.

## 8. Alternatives, compute and decision

The interpretable baseline is retained because it directly estimates Delta5 and exposes cause and confounding contrasts. The CPU boosted alternative is retained because stable component thresholds or combinations could be clinically relevant information lost by R, while remaining feasible on the same split and outcome. A sequence model is deferred because no dated repeated reserve/laboratory trajectory is verified. A multi-omics/mechanistic model is deferred because stage, treatment, validated molecular labels, histology and external validation are unavailable. The exact inputs, fitting target, split, uncertainty, baseline comparison, resource estimate and revisit conditions are recorded in method-alternatives.md.

The inherited selected-column Parquet audit is a short CPU operation; full fitting/bootstrap is unmeasured. Plan 4–8 CPUs, 16–32 GiB RAM and <=2 hours, within the future solver envelope of up to 16 CPUs, 262144 MiB and 28800 seconds. GPU is neither required nor a blanket exclusion for this tabular question.

## 9. Three inspected works

Exactly three distinct abstract-only works are attached with byte-matching receipts in key-references.json and evidence-K1-zhou-abstract.txt, evidence-K2-zhao-abstract.txt and evidence-K3-garcia-aranda-abstract.txt.

[K1] Zhou H et al. Medicine. 2026. DOI 10.1097/MD.0000000000047702. Post-diagnosis frailty/mortality association; no prediagnostic competing-risk test.

[K2] Zhao D et al. Frontiers in Oncology. 2026. DOI 10.3389/fonc.2026.1878444. Perioperative handgrip/frailty vulnerability; no long-term prediagnostic mortality test.

[K3] García-Aranda M et al. Journal of Clinical Medicine. 2026;15:4389. DOI 10.3390/jcm15114389. Competing CRC/non-CRC mortality and stage/vulnerability distinction; no UKB prediagnostic reserve test.

No fitted scientific result is asserted in this proposal.

# UKB-672073 diagnosis-anchored child: prediagnostic reserve and near-term CRC presentation

Status: proposed, not fitted. Parent: candidate-2b202f4d99e86bdc347d56e0. This child is a targeted repair of the parent’s follow-up gate. It does not claim a mortality or incidence result.

## 1. Scientific opening and hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports three bounded observations. A mixed oncology cohort containing colorectal-cancer patients found that a patient-reported/comorbidity frailty index was associated with survival [K1]. A longitudinal immune study found physiological change up to four years before some cancer diagnoses, making occult disease timing a serious rival [K2]. A Swedish register study demonstrates that prediagnostic exposures can be related to CRC outcomes, but its stage, treatment and follow-up infrastructure are not present in the verified UKB binding [K3]. None tests whether objectively recorded preassessment reserve is associated with how soon a recorded CRC diagnosis follows assessment, or whether that pattern is CRC-specific.

The parent’s five-year competing-risk mortality question cannot pass its required readiness gate on the present snapshot: the registered Online_Follow_up derivative has only `eid` and `20191-0.0`, and the catalog/source notes do not document an outcome-ascertainment cutoff `tau_source`. Observed maxima are not completeness. Therefore this child will not use absence of a cancer/death record as survival, censoring or a five-year risk endpoint.

Hypothesis:

> Among UKB participants with a valid assessment in 2006–2010 who have a subsequently recorded incident cancer diagnosis, lower assessment-time measured reserve is associated with a greater probability that the first recorded CRC diagnosis occurs within 730 days of assessment rather than 730–1825 days, relative to the analogous timing contrast for non-CRC cancers.

This is a case-only, diagnosis-anchored prognostic/descriptive association. It asks whether reserve can discriminate a near-assessment CRC presentation among people whose cancer is recorded. It is not an incidence, screening-performance, stage, treatment, mortality, causal or mechanistic claim. It remains clinically useful as a boundary test for whether a baseline reserve signal could identify a short diagnostic window for future validation; it cannot justify changing screening or treatment.

The leading rival is occult-cancer timing/measurement: low reserve may be an early manifestation of an already developing cancer or may increase healthcare contact and recording. Run each check once under the frozen specification and retain adverse results.

1. **Occult timing:** repeat short-lag cutoffs 365 and 1460 days and report continuous `L`. A reserve signal confined to the shortest window, especially if it disappears at 730–1825 days, supports occult disease/diagnostic proximity rather than durable reserve.
2. **Cancer specificity:** compare CRC with non-CRC overall and separately with other digestive and non-digestive cancers when event support permits. A similar contrast in non-CRC weakens a CRC-specific interpretation.
3. **Age/comorbidity:** compare age-only, age-plus-Charlson and flexible-age models; report age bands. Large attenuation or reversal is evidence of confounding/heterogeneity, not mechanism.
4. **Measurement/selection:** compare complete-four, min-three, grip-only and laboratory-only reserve; report component availability by cancer class and lag; model availability using assessment age, sex, BMI and smoking as an observation-weight sensitivity. 5. **Coding:** report every paired/unpaired/malformed slot and tie. Compare paired `40005/40006` anchoring with the earliest concordant C18–C20 or comparator occurrence in `41270/41280` where both code and date are usable. Material instability is adverse to the coding interpretation.
6. **Negative controls and leakage:** permute reserve once within sex and permute outcome labels once with fixed seeds. Report a non-CRC outcome contrast and a lag threshold that was fixed before test inspection. Any retained permutation signal invalidates the corresponding result.
7. **Follow-up boundary:** record that `tau_source` failed for mortality/incidence. **Adverse:** `D_short` is null/reversed, is equally strong for non-CRC, disappears after age/comorbidity or missingness handling, is driven by one assay, is coding-unstable, or occurs only in the shortest lag window. This supports nonspecific selection, measurement or occult timing and abandons a durable CRC-reserve interpretation.

**Inconclusive:** sparse cases, wide intervals, unstable paired records, inadequate overlap, poor calibration, or materially divergent coding definitions. This is not a null. Continuing requires an outcome-complete linkage source, stage/treatment data, clinical adjudication or an independent cohort.

Computationally checkable claims are source hashes/columns, paired parsing, case flow, lag categories, fitted model outputs, calibration, uncertainty and whether conclusions match outputs. Clinical adjudication or another study is required for true diagnosis date validity, stage, treatment, symptoms, healthcare-seeking, mechanism, causality and generalizability.

A simple case-only lag regression is retained as the minimum adequate design. The learned B2 alternative is retained because it can reveal component-specific thresholds or interactions that a scalar R loses; it is not selected for complexity or predictive gain.

Future solver estimate: CPU, 2–4 cores, 8–16 GiB RAM, under 20 minutes after selected-column Parquet reads; measured source audit and overlap evidence are available, but this fit-time estimate is unverified. GPU is unnecessary for the proposed tabular models. Revisit the deferred mortality/incident branches only if a documented linkage cutoff and relevant clinical evidence are admitted.

# Diagnosis-anchored CRC timing after an ascertainment repair

Status: proposed, not fitted. Parent: candidate-7508a649e73cc544ca5959e0. This is a substantive child: it keeps the recorded-case timing question and exact UKB binding, but promotes healthcare-contact/recordability selection to a prespecified estimand and falsification rather than a peripheral sensitivity.

## 1. Scientific opening, supported claim, and unresolved hypothesis

The inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. [K1] reports an association between frailty categories and mortality among people already identified as CRC survivors. [K2] supports the clinical relevance of handgrip/frailty for CRC vulnerability in a postoperative cohort. [K3] reports that tumor-related and patient-vulnerability correlates can differ for CRC-specific versus non-CRC mortality when stage and follow-up are available. None tests whether measured reserve before a recorded cancer diagnosis is associated with when that diagnosis is recorded, and none resolves whether such a pattern is CRC biology/timing or the joint result of healthcare contact, coding, and case selection.

The strongest available claim is therefore only that reserve-like measures can prognostically associate with outcomes in selected, already recorded CRC populations. The unresolved claim is:

> Among UKB participants assessed in 2006–2010 who have a subsequently recorded first cancer diagnosis within 1,825 days, lower assessment-time measured reserve is associated with a larger probability of a CRC diagnosis within 730 days rather than 730–1,825 days than the corresponding timing association for non-CRC cancer, after standardizing for age, comorbidity, and a baseline coded-recordability proxy.

This remains a recorded-case, descriptive/prognostic association. It is not cancer incidence, screening sensitivity, stage, mortality, causal effect, mechanism, or a treatment rule.

The leading explanation is a CRC-specific timing process in which lower reserve components are associated with near-assessment presentation differently for CRC than for other cancers. The consequential rival is generic ascertainment: people with lower reserve may have more clinical encounters or coded diagnoses, and people with more pre-existing coded healthcare history may be more likely to have any cancer recorded promptly. A further rival is occult disease: the shortest lag may represent already developing cancer, not a durable reserve state. These explanations differ on a concrete comparison: the CRC-versus-non-CRC contrast should persist across low/high baseline recordability strata and lag cutoffs if it is CRC-specific; a contact/recording explanation predicts a common or stratum-dependent timing pattern across cancer classes, especially among people with more prior coded records or only when the cancer diagnosis is corroborated in a clinical-code channel.

The advance over the parent is not a larger model. It is an explicit observation-process check that says what can and cannot be learned after conditioning on a recorded cancer case. [K1] and [K2] motivate reserve components; [K3] motivates separating tumor-class and vulnerability contrasts, while also showing why unavailable stage/treatment cannot be silently inferred here.

## 3. Population, timing, reserve, and recordability proxy

Set b_i=53-0.0; retain 2006-01-01 through 2010-12-31. A cancer record is valid only when the same slot has a parseable date in 40005-k.0 and a trimmed uppercase ICD-10 code in 40006-k.0. Report malformed, unpaired, duplicate-date, and discordant slots; never borrow a neighboring slot.

This is a proxy for prior coded healthcare-record opportunity, not a measure of visits, symptoms, access, or contact. Missing, malformed, and discordant pairs are a separate audit category and are not reclassified as zero.

Also derive a sensitivity-only channel_concordance: whether a usable 41270/41280 code-date occurrence of the same broad cancer class is within ±90 days of the selected 40005/40006 date. The field families have different source roles and are not assumed interchangeable. Concordance is an observation-model check, not a replacement diagnosis.
