## 3. Population and two locked outcome clocks

Let b_i be the parsed `53-0.0` date. Construct the full baseline population U before scanning post-assessment events:

- one unique `eid`;
- (2006	ext{-}01	ext{-}01le b_ile2010	ext{-}12	ext{-}31);
- valid `31-0.0`, `21022-0.0`, `21001-0.0`, and `20116-0.0`;
- at least three available baseline components among maximum grip (`46-0.0`/`47-0.0`), albumin `30600-0.0`, creatinine `30700-0.0`, and cystatin C `30720-0.0`;
- no observed valid paired C00–C97 cancer code/date on or before b_i in either cancer source.

This is no observed pre-assessment cancer record, not biological cancer-free status.

### Baseline full-cohort anchor

Source D's primary outcome (Y^0), for every U row, is the first valid paired source-D event in (W^0_i=(b_i,b_i+1825	ext{ days}]). Categories are CRC-near, CRC-late, other-cancer-near, other-cancer-late, non-cancer-near, non-cancer-late, no qualifying recorded event, and multi-class same-date tie. Near is 0 < L < 730 days and late is 730 <= L <= 1825 days. A tie is retained as its own category. Source C supplies the analogous cancer-only CRC/other-cancer target and cannot create a non-cancer event. Dates beyond 1825 days are descriptive only.

Reserve (R_0) is the training-fitted mean of four transformed components: sex-stratified maximum grip, log albumin, negative-log creatinine, and negative-log cystatin C. Component count and missingness are retained; no missing component is silently imputed as normal.

For model (m), standardize predicted full-cohort probabilities over the fixed locked-test distribution of age, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year, dated history state, and component availability. Define
[
T^0_{g,D,m}=[p(Y^0=g,mathrm{near}mid R_0=Q25)-p(Y^0=g,mathrm{late}mid R_0=Q25)]-[p(Y^0=g,mathrm{near}mid R_0=Q75)-p(Y^0=g,mathrm{late}mid R_0=Q75)].
]
Report (D^0_{NC}=T^0_{CRC,D}-T^0_{non	ext{-}cancer,D}), (D^0_{OC}=T^0_{CRC,D}-T^0_{other	ext{-}cancer,D}), and (D^0_{comp}=T^0_{CRC,D}-0.5(T^0_{non	ext{-}cancer,D}+T^0_{other	ext{-}cancer,D})), plus source-C (D^0_C=T^0_{CRC,C}-T^0_{other	ext{-}cancer,C}). These are absolute recorded-event probability contrasts, not incidence, hazard, survival, encounter, or causal effects.

### Repeat landmark R and its support decision

Let r_i be the parsed `53-1.0` date, strictly after b_i. The primary repeat landmark R requires membership in U, 731 <= r_i - b_i <= 1825 days, at least one repeat grip value among `46-1.0`/`47-1.0`, at least two of `30600-1.0`, `30700-1.0`, `30720-1.0`, and no observed valid paired C00–C97 event in either cancer source in (b_i, r_i]. The 731-day lower bound is locked because the bounded audit found no 30–730-day repeat support; no short interval stratum will be invented. Participants with valid repeat dates beyond 1825 days are reported in an audit but excluded from the primary trajectory estimand because their outcome and measurement windows are not comparable.

The repeat outcome (Y^1) starts at r_i, not b_i: first valid source-D event in (W^1_i=(r_i,r_i+1825	ext{ days}]), with early 0 < L <= 365, intermediate 365 < L <= 730, and late 730 < L <= 1825. Retain CRC-early/intermediate/late, other-cancer-early/intermediate/late, non-cancer-early/intermediate/late, no qualifying recorded event, and multi-class same-date tie. Source C repeats the cancer-only outcome. The full-U baseline anchor is never replaced by this selected panel.

The observed bounded readiness audit, before exact U and through-repeat filtering, found 18,856 nonmissing `53-1.0` dates, 18,785 rows with repeat grip, 16,577 with at least two repeat labs, 16,504 with date/grip/lab support after a 30–3,650-day proxy interval check, median interval 1,617 days, and no 30–730-day support. These are not fitted results, not event counts, and not the final R denominator. The solver must recompute them after exact pair parsing, cancer exclusions, and participant splitting. Exact outcome support is a pre-fit gate.

## 4. Reserve change, selection tests, and estimands

On training rows only, apply the same transformations to baseline and repeat components. Define
[
Delta R_i=(R_{1i}-R_{0i})/((r_i-b_i)/365.25),
]
with separate Delta R_lab from the three laboratory components and Delta R_grip from maximum grip. Retain interval, repeat year, component counts, and field missingness. Training-derived Q25/Q75 define low/high trajectory contrasts.

The primary repeat contrast is T^1_{g,I-L,m}, the standardized probability difference between intermediate and late source-D outcome bands under low versus high trajectory. Report CRC, other-cancer, non-cancer, no-event and tie probabilities and denominators. The scientific incremental estimand is
[
I_{Delta,m}=D^1_{comp,m}(Delta R	ext{ included})-D^1_{comp,m}(R_0	ext{ only}),
]
with lab- and grip-specific increments. Positive I_Delta means the observed trajectory contributes CRC-specific recorded-timing information conditional on this selected landmark; it does not prove biology.

Repeat selection is handled as a test, not hidden in the estimand. Report U-to-R flow separately for date availability, acceptable interval, grip, two-lab support, and no recorded cancer through repeat. Compare baseline reserve, missingness, age, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year, dated history state, baseline outcome, and source capture among U participants with and without each selection stage. Fit a prespecified two-stage selection model using only baseline variables to estimate repeat-date/measurement availability and remaining recorded-event-free-through-repeat; use stabilized inverse-selection weights only if positivity holds. Report unweighted R, weighted R, and a model-dependent U-standardized transport estimate with effective sample size. The conditional R result is primary for the trajectory question; transport is secondary and is not a counterfactual claim.

Transport/selection gates are mandatory: every required baseline selection stratum has repeat support; stabilized weights have ESS >=500, <=1% above 10 before truncation, and no unexplained extreme-weight concentration; primary R CRC and other-cancer class/lag cells have >=30 participants overall and >=10 per split, non-cancer cells >=100 overall and >=20 per split; source-C CRC/other-cancer cells have >=30 overall and nonempty splits. If any gate fails, do not merge classes or intervals after seeing outcomes. Report the baseline anchor but mark the repeat trajectory estimand unresolved/deferred.

## 5. Models and concrete alternative reasoning

Use one deterministic participant split: hash `eid` with seed 1414 into 70% train, 15% validation, and 15% locked test. All rows for an `eid` stay in one split. Event construction is date/code based, but transformations, imputation if any, reserve quantiles, weights, splines, tuning, and thresholds use train/validation only. No test outcome may influence a choice.

B0 is the CPU baseline: interpretable additive multinomial logistic regression for the full-U outcome and, separately, the repeat-landmark outcome, with age spline, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year, baseline reserve, component count/missingness, and dated pre-baseline history. The repeat B0 adds interval and selection indicators but not within-person slopes for the nested baseline-only comparison.

B1 is the substantive learned alternative on the same rows, target, features, and split: shallow gradient-boosted multinomial probabilities with fixed validation grid of 200/400 trees, depth 2/3, and learning rate .03/.05. For the trajectory test B1 receives the same baseline features plus (Delta R,Delta R_{lab},Delta R_{grip}), baseline-by-slope and slope-by-class/lag terms; B0 has a matched trajectory-feature version for a method comparison, while the nested B0 baseline-only fit estimates the information added by change. B1 can expose thresholds or reserve-by-history-by-class interactions that additive terms lose; it is not justified by a small predictive gain. Select by validation multiclass log loss and Brier score, then evaluate locked-test Brier/log loss, calibration by class/lag, all recorded-timing estimands, and bootstrap uncertainty. The learned model is retained only if it changes the prespecified trajectory-versus-baseline scientific decision and remains stable across falsification checks.

CPU is selected for both: 4–8 cores, 16–32 GiB RAM, and at most 2.5 future-solver hours for selected-column reads, paired-event parsing, fits, locked evaluation, and 500 participant-bootstrap replicates. This is a planning estimate; the bounded repeat audit is the only measured feasibility evidence. GPU and sequence models are deferred because they cannot supply missing encounter provenance or adjudicated onset. Revisit them only with a new validated data dependency or reproducible nonlinear trajectory pattern. This is a resource tradeoff, not a blanket exclusion of neural or structured methods.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted, output-linked evidence: immutable source/schema/hash audit; U and R flow; exact interval and missingness tables; full-U B0/B1 contrasts; repeat B0 baseline-only versus trajectory contrasts; weighted/transport sensitivity and ESS; lab/grip decomposition; source-C replication; calibration; 500 participant-bootstrap intervals; and locked falsification outputs. Every conclusion must point to computed files and uncertainty intervals. No fitted result is claimed in this proposal.

## 6. Falsification and interpretation

Lock these checks before fitting:

- **Generic recorded timing:** if non-cancer or other-cancer tilts track CRC, or (D^0_{comp}) or (D^1_{comp}) is near zero, the information is generic recorded-health/recordability rather than CRC specificity.
- **Reverse timing:** compare early, intermediate, and late repeat-clock bands and repeat the trajectory contrast after excluding events in the first 90 days after r_i. An early-only effect, or strong attenuation after accounting for valid events in (b_i, r_i], is adverse to an independent warning interpretation. It is compatible with reverse causation but cannot prove occult disease.
- **Selection:** compare unweighted, weighted and transported estimates; show baseline distributions and event capture across U-to-R stages. Positivity failure, unstable weights, or large movement means repeat selection prevents resolution.
- **Interval and measurement:** report (731	ext{–}1460) versus (1461	ext{–}1825) only when each has support; compare complete-four versus minimum-three baseline components, grip-only, laboratory-only, and missingness strata. No 30–730 comparison is possible. Instability is a measurement/selection finding, not a mechanism.
- **Source/date:** replicate cancer contrasts in source C; report exact paired-date agreement and a prespecified +/-30-day concordance sensitivity. Opposite source directions or date instability are adverse.
- **Coding:** once within history state and lag band, permute event classes; separately permute source labels among paired cancer records. A non-null specificity result after permutation invalidates that computation.
- **Calendar and capture:** report assessment/repeat year tables and inherited all-U source capture categories; do not use `20191-0.0` as follow-up. A reserve/selection gradient confined to a calendar or capture category is adverse to source-independent interpretation.

Supportive results require the full-U anchor gates, repeat R support gates, positive CRC-specific trajectory increment with a 95% interval excluding zero, comparator contrasts positive, agreement of unweighted/weighted/source results, adequate calibration, no permutation signal, and persistence beyond the early band. This would justify expert clinical adjudication or prospective repeat-reserve ascertainment. It would not justify a clinical warning rule, causal intervention, or onset claim.

Adverse results include comparator-matched change, attenuation from trajectory to baseline-only, early-only change, strong interval or component dependence, source disagreement, capture gradients, unstable weights, or a permutation signal. These favor generic recordability, selection, measurement, coding, or reverse-timing artifacts and should abandon the CRC-specific trajectory interpretation.

Inconclusive results include failed R support, sparse class/lag cells, no interval overlap, failed positivity/ESS, malformed pairs, failed calibration/bootstrap, or intervals spanning both the decision regions. An imprecise null is not refutation. If R cannot pass its predeclared gates, retain only the full-U baseline anchor and explicitly defer the within-person question rather than changing the population, clock, or categories.

## 7. Clinical limits and evidence requiring another study

The data lack verified encounter dates, healthcare-contact intensity, symptoms, screening/referral, stage, histology, treatment, mortality, pathology, adjudicated onset, assay quality/fasting metadata, complete observation boundaries, and an external clinical validation cohort. The repeat date is an assessment date, not necessarily a clinically identical visit. No recorded cancer through repeat is not absence of disease. Conditioning on repeat participation and recorded-event-free-through-repeat can induce selection or collider bias. Adjustment or a nonlinear model cannot identify a mechanism. Any stronger clinical or causal claim requires clinical adjudication, validated linkage with complete follow-up and ascertainment, or a prospective study.

## 8. Alternatives not chosen and revisit evidence

The chosen CPU pair is additive multinomial B0 versus shallow boosted B1 on identical rows and splits because the scientific uncertainty is whether baseline reserve versus within-person change and class/lag interactions alter CRC specificity, not whether a black-box score wins a metric. A survival model is deferred: the available endpoint is a first recorded event with uncertain observation completeness and explicit no-event/tie categories, so survival censoring would add assumptions without resolving the opening. Sequence or GPU models are deferred because there is only one laboratory repeat instance and no encounter provenance; revisit only if a validated new time series or a stable B1 nonlinear trajectory pattern appears. A repeat component is deferred entirely if its exact landmark/outcome support, interval strata, or selection gates fail.

## 9. Three inspected works

[K1] Mathew D, Lane H, Ward D, Saunders R, Millar L, Etherton-Beer C. “Development and application of a frailty index derived from patient-reported outcome measures and comorbidities in oncology patients.” Internal Medicine Journal, 2026. DOI 10.1111/imj.70599. Abstract-only Europe PMC inspection. It supports clinical relevance of frailty-like constructs but does not establish prediagnostic CRC timing, repeat change, onset, or recordability.

[K2] Chen G et al. “Age-dependent cytokine surge in blood precedes cancer diagnosis.” Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2025. DOI 10.1073/pnas.2420502122; PMID 40117305; PMCID PMC11962427. Abstract-only Europe PMC inspection. It supports a prediagnostic systemic-physiology/occult-disease rival but does not validate these UKB fields, CRC specificity, or clinical onset.

[K3] Lu SSM et al. “Prediagnostic Prescription Antibiotics Use and Survival in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: A Swedish National Register-Based Study.” Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 2023. DOI 10.1158/1055-9965.epi-23-0340; PMID 37490284; PMCID PMC10543975. Abstract-only Europe PMC inspection. It bounds the stage, treatment, survival, and register provenance needed for stronger prediagnostic CRC interpretation, none of which is available here.

The attached `key-references.json` contains exactly these three distinct works. The attached K1/K2/K3 files are frozen Europe PMC metadata/abstract responses; no inaccessible full text or supplementary methods is claimed.

It is compatible with reverse causation but cannot prove occult disease.

Adverse results include comparator-matched change, attenuation from trajectory to baseline-only, early-only change, strong interval or component dependence, source disagreement, capture gradients, unstable weights, or a permutation signal. These favor generic recordability, selection, measurement, coding, or reverse-timing artifacts and should abandon the CRC-specific trajectory interpretation.

Inconclusive results include failed R support, sparse class/lag cells, no interval overlap, failed positivity/ESS, malformed pairs, failed calibration/bootstrap, or intervals spanning both the decision regions. An imprecise null is not refutation. If R cannot pass its predeclared gates, retain only the full-U baseline anchor and explicitly defer the within-person question rather than changing the population, clock, or categories.

The data lack verified encounter dates, healthcare-contact intensity, symptoms, screening/referral, stage, histology, treatment, mortality, pathology, adjudicated onset, assay quality/fasting metadata, complete observation boundaries, and an external clinical validation cohort. The repeat date is an assessment date, not necessarily a clinically identical visit. No recorded cancer through repeat is not absence of disease. Conditioning on repeat participation and recorded-event-free-through-repeat can induce selection or collider bias. Adjustment or a nonlinear model cannot identify a mechanism. Any stronger clinical or causal claim requires clinical adjudication, validated linkage with complete follow-up and ascertainment, or a prospective study.

## 8. Alternatives not chosen and revisit evidence

The chosen CPU pair is additive multinomial B0 versus shallow boosted B1 on identical rows and splits because the scientific uncertainty is whether baseline reserve versus within-person change and class/lag interactions alter CRC specificity, not whether a black-box score wins a metric. A survival model is deferred: the available endpoint is a first recorded event with uncertain observation completeness and explicit no-event/tie categories, so survival censoring would add assumptions without resolving the opening. Sequence or GPU models are deferred because there is only one laboratory repeat instance and no encounter provenance; revisit only if a validated new time series or a stable B1 nonlinear trajectory pattern appears. A repeat component is deferred entirely if its exact landmark/outcome support, interval strata, or selection gates fail.

## 9. Three inspected works

[K1] Mathew D, Lane H, Ward D, Saunders R, Millar L, Etherton-Beer C. “Development and application of a frailty index derived from patient-reported outcome measures and comorbidities in oncology patients.” Internal Medicine Journal, 2026. DOI 10.1111/imj.70599. Abstract-only Europe PMC inspection. It supports clinical relevance of frailty-like constructs but does not establish prediagnostic CRC timing, repeat change, onset, or recordability.

[K2] Chen G et al. “Age-dependent cytokine surge in blood precedes cancer diagnosis.” Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2025. DOI 10.1073/pnas.2420502122; PMID 40117305; PMCID PMC11962427. Abstract-only Europe PMC inspection. It supports a prediagnostic systemic-physiology/occult-disease rival but does not validate these UKB fields, CRC specificity, or clinical onset.

[K3] Lu SSM et al. “Prediagnostic Prescription Antibiotics Use and Survival in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: A Swedish National Register-Based Study.” Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 2023. DOI 10.1158/1055-9965.epi-23-0340; PMID 37490284; PMCID PMC10543975. Abstract-only Europe PMC inspection. It bounds the stage, treatment, survival, and register provenance needed for stronger prediagnostic CRC interpretation, none of which is available here.

The attached `key-references.json` contains exactly these three distinct works. The attached K1/K2/K3 files are frozen Europe PMC metadata/abstract responses; no inaccessible full text or supplementary methods is claimed.

# Full-cohort recorded-CRC specificity with a gated instance-1 reserve trajectory

Status: substantive crossover successor of `candidate-be2d73bd0508251fa8cbf015` and `candidate-28c77cf68b97ec3d05953fa4`. This is a source-bound, unfitted design. The repeat audit is readiness evidence only; no association, model fit, or clinical conclusion is claimed.

## 1. Scientific opening and falsifiable hypothesis

The strongest supported claim is limited: in an eligible UKB assessment cohort, baseline reserve can be compared with the timing and class of a subsequently *recorded* first diagnosis, using same-source non-cancer and other-cancer records as specificity comparators. The full-cohort design makes “no qualifying recorded event” and same-date class ties explicit rather than selecting only CRC cases. This does not establish incidence, true onset, encounter timing, symptoms, screening, referral, stage, treatment, mortality, mechanism, causality, or clinical utility.

The unresolved claim is whether a verified repeat reserve measurement at Assessment Center instance 1 adds information about the CRC-versus-comparator recorded-timing contrast beyond a baseline reserve snapshot. A stable low baseline may represent longstanding vulnerability or generic recordability. A within-person decline might be a proximal prediagnostic signal, but it might instead reflect repeat-assessment selection, a long and heterogeneous measurement interval, field-specific missingness, or disease already being recorded between assessments.

Hypothesis H_change: among the baseline-eligible cohort, the CRC-versus-comparator contrast in the lag of the next recorded event is larger for participants with a lower annualized reserve change between baseline and a verified instance-1 assessment than for participants with a higher change, after baseline reserve, dated pre-baseline recorded history, interval, repeat-selection variables, and laboratory-versus-grip slope decomposition are accounted for. The trajectory contrast must remain for the repeat-landmark outcome after the repeat clock begins, must exceed non-cancer and other-cancer comparator tilts, and must not disappear under prespecified selection, interval, source-concordance, or reverse-timing checks.

This is a descriptive recorded-event hypothesis. It is not a claim that reserve decline causes CRC, identifies occult disease, measures onset, or is a warning rule.

[K1] supports the clinical relevance of measuring frailty-like reserve in oncology but is post-diagnosis and does not test prediagnostic recorded timing. [K2] makes prediagnostic systemic change a serious reverse-causation rival, but does not validate these UKB fields or distinguish onset from first record. [K3] bounds stronger prediagnostic CRC interpretations by showing the value of register provenance and outcome context unavailable here. Participants with valid repeat dates beyond 1825 days are reported in an audit but excluded from the primary trajectory estimand because their outcome and measurement windows are not comparable.

The repeat outcome (Y^1) starts at r_i, not b_i: first valid source-D event in (W^1_i=(r_i,r_i+1825	ext{ days}]), with early 0 < L <= 365, intermediate 365 < L <= 730, and late 730 < L <= 1825. Retain CRC-early/intermediate/late, other-cancer-early/intermediate/late, non-cancer-early/intermediate/late, no qualifying recorded event, and multi-class same-date tie. Source C repeats the cancer-only outcome. The full-U baseline anchor is never replaced by this selected panel.

The observed bounded readiness audit, before exact U and through-repeat filtering, found 18,856 nonmissing `53-1.0` dates, 18,785 rows with repeat grip, 16,577 with at least two repeat labs, 16,504 with date/grip/lab support after a 30–3,650-day proxy interval check, median interval 1,617 days, and no 30–730-day support. These are not fitted results, not event counts, and not the final R denominator. The solver must recompute them after exact pair parsing, cancer exclusions, and participant splitting. Exact outcome support is a pre-fit gate.

## 4. Reserve change, selection tests, and estimands

On training rows only, apply the same transformations to baseline and repeat components. Define
[
Delta R_i=(R_{1i}-R_{0i})/((r_i-b_i)/365.25),
]
with separate Delta R_lab from the three laboratory components and Delta R_grip from maximum grip. Retain interval, repeat year, component counts, and field missingness. Training-derived Q25/Q75 define low/high trajectory contrasts.

The primary repeat contrast is T^1_{g,I-L,m}, the standardized probability difference between intermediate and late source-D outcome bands under low versus high trajectory. Report CRC, other-cancer, non-cancer, no-event and tie probabilities and denominators. The scientific incremental estimand is
[
I_{Delta,m}=D^1_{comp,m}(Delta R	ext{ included})-D^1_{comp,m}(R_0	ext{ only}),
]
with lab- and grip-specific increments. Positive I_Delta means the observed trajectory contributes CRC-specific recorded-timing information conditional on this selected landmark; it does not prove biology.

Repeat selection is handled as a test, not hidden in the estimand. Report U-to-R flow separately for date availability, acceptable interval, grip, two-lab support, and no recorded cancer through repeat. Compare baseline reserve, missingness, age, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year, dated history state, baseline outcome, and source capture among U participants with and without each selection stage. Fit a prespecified two-stage selection model using only baseline variables to estimate repeat-date/measurement availability and remaining recorded-event-free-through-repeat; use stabilized inverse-selection weights only if positivity holds. Report unweighted R, weighted R, and a model-dependent U-standardized transport estimate with effective sample size. The conditional R result is primary for the trajectory question; transport is secondary and is not a counterfactual claim.

Transport/selection gates are mandatory: every required baseline selection stratum has repeat support; stabilized weights have ESS >=500, <=1% above 10 before truncation, and no unexplained extreme-weight concentration; primary R CRC and other-cancer class/lag cells have >=30 participants overall and >=10 per split, non-cancer cells >=100 overall and >=20 per split; source-C CRC/other-cancer cells have >=30 overall and nonempty splits. If any gate fails, do not merge classes or intervals after seeing outcomes. Report the baseline anchor but mark the repeat trajectory estimand unresolved/deferred.

## 5. Models and concrete alternative reasoning

Use one deterministic participant split: hash `eid` with seed 1414 into 70% train, 15% validation, and 15% locked test. All rows for an `eid` stay in one split. Event construction is date/code based, but transformations, imputation if any, reserve quantiles, weights, splines, tuning, and thresholds use train/validation only. No test outcome may influence a choice.

B0 is the CPU baseline: interpretable additive multinomial logistic regression for the full-U outcome and, separately, the repeat-landmark outcome, with age spline, sex, BMI, smoking, assessment year, baseline reserve, component count/missingness, and dated pre-baseline history. The repeat B0 adds interval and selection indicators but not within-person slopes for the nested baseline-only comparison.

B1 is the substantive learned alternative on the same rows, target, features, and split: shallow gradient-boosted multinomial probabilities with fixed validation grid of 200/400 trees, depth 2/3, and learning rate .03/.05. For the trajectory test B1 receives the same baseline features plus (Delta R,Delta R_{lab},Delta R_{grip}), baseline-by-slope and slope-by-class/lag terms; B0 has a matched trajectory-feature version for a method comparison, while the nested B0 baseline-only fit estimates the information added by change. B1 can expose thresholds or reserve-by-history-by-class interactions that additive terms lose; it is not justified by a small predictive gain. Select by validation multiclass log loss and Brier score, then evaluate locked-test Brier/log loss, calibration by class/lag, all recorded-timing estimands, and bootstrap uncertainty. The learned model is retained only if it changes the prespecified trajectory-versus-baseline scientific decision and remains stable across falsification checks.

CPU is selected for both: 4–8 cores, 16–32 GiB RAM, and at most 2.5 future-solver hours for selected-column reads, paired-event parsing, fits, locked evaluation, and 500 participant-bootstrap replicates. This is a planning estimate; the bounded repeat audit is the only measured feasibility evidence. GPU and sequence models are deferred because they cannot supply missing encounter provenance or adjudicated onset. Revisit them only with a new validated data dependency or reproducible nonlinear trajectory pattern. This is a resource tradeoff, not a blanket exclusion of neural or structured methods.

The actual scientific deliverable is newly fitted, output-linked evidence: immutable source/schema/hash audit; U and R flow; exact interval and missingness tables; full-U B0/B1 contrasts; repeat B0 baseline-only versus trajectory contrasts; weighted/transport sensitivity and ESS; lab/grip decomposition; source-C replication; calibration; 500 participant-bootstrap intervals; and locked falsification outputs. Every conclusion must point to computed files and uncertainty intervals. No fitted result is claimed in this proposal.

## 6. Falsification and interpretation

Lock these checks before fitting:

- **Generic recorded timing:** if non-cancer or other-cancer tilts track CRC, or (D^0_{comp}) or (D^1_{comp}) is near zero, the information is generic recorded-health/recordability rather than CRC specificity.
- **Reverse timing:** compare early, intermediate, and late repeat-clock bands and repeat the trajectory contrast after excluding events in the first 90 days after r_i. An early-only effect, or strong attenuation after accounting for valid events in (b_i, r_i], is adverse to an independent warning interpretation. It is compatible with reverse causation but cannot prove occult disease.
- **Selection:** compare unweighted, weighted and transported estimates; show baseline distributions and event capture across U-to-R stages. Positivity failure, unstable weights, or large movement means repeat selection prevents resolution.
- **Interval and measurement:** report (731	ext{–}1460) versus (1461	ext{–}1825) only when each has support; compare complete-four versus minimum-three baseline components, grip-only, laboratory-only, and missingness strata. No 30–730 comparison is possible. Instability is a measurement/selection finding, not a mechanism.
- **Source/date:** replicate cancer contrasts in source C; report exact paired-date agreement and a prespecified +/-30-day concordance sensitivity. Opposite source directions or date instability are adverse.
- **Coding:** once within history state and lag band, permute event classes; separately permute source labels among paired cancer records. A non-null specificity result after permutation invalidates that computation.
- **Calendar and capture:** report assessment/repeat year tables and inherited all-U source capture categories; do not use `20191-0.0` as follow-up. A reserve/selection gradient confined to a calendar or capture category is adverse to source-independent interpretation.

Supportive results require the full-U anchor gates, repeat R support gates, positive CRC-specific trajectory increment with a 95% interval excluding zero, comparator contrasts positive, agreement of unweighted/weighted/source results, adequate calibration, no permutation signal, and persistence beyond the early band. This would justify expert clinical adjudication or prospective repeat-reserve ascertainment. It would not justify a clinical warning rule, causal intervention, or onset claim.

Adverse results include comparator-matched change, attenuation from trajectory to baseline-only, early-only change, strong interval or component dependence, source disagreement, capture gradients, unstable weights, or a permutation signal. These favor generic recordability, selection, measurement, coding, or reverse-timing artifacts and should abandon the CRC-specific trajectory interpretation.

Inconclusive results include failed R support, sparse class/lag cells, no interval overlap, failed positivity/ESS, malformed pairs, failed calibration/bootstrap, or intervals spanning both the decision regions. An imprecise null is not refutation. If R cannot pass its predeclared gates, retain only the full-U baseline anchor and explicitly defer the within-person question rather than changing the population, clock, or categories.

## 7. Clinical limits and evidence requiring another study

The data lack verified encounter dates, healthcare-contact intensity, symptoms, screening/referral, stage, histology, treatment, mortality, pathology, adjudicated onset, assay quality/fasting metadata, complete observation boundaries, and an external clinical validation cohort. The repeat date is an assessment date, not necessarily a clinically identical visit. No recorded cancer through repeat is not absence of disease. Conditioning on repeat participation and recorded-event-free-through-repeat can induce selection or collider bias. Adjustment or a nonlinear model cannot identify a mechanism. Any stronger clinical or causal claim requires clinical adjudication, validated linkage with complete follow-up and ascertainment, or a prospective study.

## 8. Alternatives not chosen and revisit evidence

The chosen CPU pair is additive multinomial B0 versus shallow boosted B1 on identical rows and splits because the scientific uncertainty is whether baseline reserve versus within-person change and class/lag interactions alter CRC specificity, not whether a black-box score wins a metric. A survival model is deferred: the available endpoint is a first recorded event with uncertain observation completeness and explicit no-event/tie categories, so survival censoring would add assumptions without resolving the opening. Sequence or GPU models are deferred because there is only one laboratory repeat instance and no encounter provenance; revisit only if a validated new time series or a stable B1 nonlinear trajectory pattern appears. A repeat component is deferred entirely if its exact landmark/outcome support, interval strata, or selection gates fail.

## 9. Three inspected works

[K1] Mathew D, Lane H, Ward D, Saunders R, Millar L, Etherton-Beer C. “Development and application of a frailty index derived from patient-reported outcome measures and comorbidities in oncology patients.” Internal Medicine Journal, 2026. DOI 10.1111/imj.70599. Abstract-only Europe PMC inspection. It supports clinical relevance of frailty-like constructs but does not establish prediagnostic CRC timing, repeat change, onset, or recordability.

[K2] Chen G et al. “Age-dependent cytokine surge in blood precedes cancer diagnosis.” Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2025. DOI 10.1073/pnas.2420502122; PMID 40117305; PMCID PMC11962427. Abstract-only Europe PMC inspection. It supports a prediagnostic systemic-physiology/occult-disease rival but does not validate these UKB fields, CRC specificity, or clinical onset.

[K3] Lu SSM et al. “Prediagnostic Prescription Antibiotics Use and Survival in Patients with Colorectal Cancer: A Swedish National Register-Based Study.” Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention, 2023. DOI 10.1158/1055-9965.epi-23-0340; PMID 37490284; PMCID PMC10543975. Abstract-only Europe PMC inspection. It bounds the stage, treatment, survival, and register provenance needed for stronger prediagnostic CRC interpretation, none of which is available here.
